title: Path-bar switcher search field cannot be reached or held by the keyboard
reason: Citation is accurate and the primary mechanism reproduces in source. src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:328-336 renders the search input verbatim as quoted; every menu row has tabIndex={-1} (lines 201, 233), making the input the only tabbable node in the open menu; focusMenuOption (422-431), moveMenuFocus and the typeahead all address only menuOptions() ([role="menuitem"|"menuitemcheckbox"|"menuitemradio"] per menuKeyboard.ts:13), and the input has no role; and there are FOUR Tab handlers, not one — the menu container (258) plus all three openers (516, 551, 618) — each closing the menu, with .sync-path-menu[hidden]{display:none} (App.css:3080) pulling the input out of the focus order on the same synchronous commit, before the browser's default Tab action. No onFocus/focusin/autoFocus/ref-focus exists in the file. So no pure-keyboard path reaches the field. However three sub-claims are wrong: (1) the Enter-takes-first-match branch (267-272) is NOT dead code — the input is mouse-focusable and click-then-type is the ordinary path, so `typing` (264) and its Enter/Arrow branches run routinely; (2) the field CAN be "held" by the keyboard once focused — line 273 returns early for every key but Enter/ArrowDown/ArrowUp while typing, so characters, Home/End and Backspace all reach it and focus is retained; (3) the Shift+Tab sequence is backwards — keydown closes the menu before focus moves, so the input never momentarily receives focus, and the browser's sequential-focus starting point normally lands on the opener rather than "<body>"/the top of the document. Severity is medium, not high: all switch targets remain reachable by Arrow/Home/End and by the label typeahead (167-195), and since no query can be set by keyboard the list is never filtered down, so switching is not blocked — only the substring filter convenience is lost. A related defect the finding missed: a bare <input> is an invalid child of role="menu", so a screen reader in menu mode may not expose it even after focus is fixed.
correction: The path-bar switcher's filter field (SyncPathBar.tsx:328-336, shown when a switcher has >= 6 targets) can be focused only with the mouse. Every menu row is tabIndex={-1}, and the four Tab handlers (menu container at 258; openers at 516, 551, 618) close the menu on keydown — before the browser's default focus move — so no keyboard path lands on the input. Once focused by click it works correctly: typing, Home/End and Enter-takes-first-match (267-272) are live, not dead, code. Impact is limited to losing the substring filter: all targets stay reachable via Arrow/Home/End and label typeahead, and the list is never filtered while the query is empty. Fix by focusing the input first when `searchable` and letting Tab move between the input and the list (closing only on real focusout); separately, an <input> is an invalid child of role="menu", so the field needs to move out of the menu container or the container needs a different role.

title: Path-bar switcher search field cannot be reached or held by the keyboard
reason: No functionality is lost and the behaviour is a documented, deliberate choice. (1) The search pill is an additive pointer affordance layered over a fully keyboard-operable menu: SyncPathBar.tsx:283-300 implements a 500ms type-ahead that focuses the next row whose label starts with the typed prefix (cycling on a repeated first letter), on top of moveMenuFocus's Arrow/Home/End roving over every [role="menuitem"] — which includes all "Switch to" targets. A keyboard user with 20 projects presses "h" and lands on HorrorGame; when no query is typed every target row is rendered, so the whole list is reachable. WCAG 2.1.1 asks that the function (pick a project) be keyboard-operable, and it is. (2) Tab closing the menu is the WAI-ARIA menu-button behaviour and an explicit decision stated in the file ("Tab is not menu navigation: the menu steps aside and the bar's own tab order continues wherever the browser takes it", SyncPathBar.tsx:245-247), applied identically at all four openers; the shipped design record for this switcher specifies the same contract verbatim ("ArrowDown/Up step into the list, Enter activates the first .target, typeahead skips the input"). Special-casing Tab for searchable switchers would break the pattern the other menus keep. (3) The claimed focus-loss mechanism is sequenced wrong: the keydown handler closes first and React 18 flushes discrete-event state before the browser performs Tab's default action, so the container is already `hidden` and the input is never focused-then-dropped; whatever focus the browser then resolves is the same for every menu in the bar, so the search field introduces nothing new. (4) The Enter-takes-first-match branch is not dead code — it serves the ordinary path of opening the menu with the mouse, clicking the field, typing and pressing Enter, which is exactly the interaction the field was drawn for. (5) The proposed fix would also worsen the ARIA picture the file already flags: a text input is not an allowed child of role="menu", so making it the first focus stop and trapping Tab inside pushes further from the menu pattern rather than toward it. Residual gap is at most an enhancement: keyboard users get prefix type-ahead rather than the field's substring match.
correction: Precise residual statement: in a switcher with 6+ targets, keyboard-only users cannot focus the filter field (Tab closes the menu by design), so they narrow the list with prefix type-ahead instead of the field's substring match. This is a convenience gap, not a loss of function — every target stays reachable via Arrow/Home/End and type-ahead — and the field remains fully usable on the pointer-opens/keyboard-types path that its Enter-activates-first-match branch was written for.

title: Escape discards the prepared Push review from anywhere, including inside the Logs drawer
reason: Reproduced in source. (1) PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:417-423 holds the quoted effect verbatim on `window`, and its `busy` prop is `busy || projectContentLoading` (ProjectSync.tsx:3408), false during normal review — so the Escape branch is live. (2) `onClose` at ProjectSync.tsx:3395-3402 is `if (busy) return; setPendingPush(null); setPushError(null); setPushProjectContentRemovals(new Set()); setPushWarningAcknowledgements(new Set());` with no confirm and no undo; `pendingPush` is built at ProjectSync.tsx:1903+ from a backend `context` (thread_comparison + project_files inventory), so it is genuinely backend-prepared. (3) ActivityLogDrawer.tsx contains no keydown/Escape handling whatsoever; its root is `role="region" tabIndex={-1}` and takes programmatic focus via `logDrawerRef.current?.focus()` (ProjectSync.tsx:3679) when opened, so Escape pressed on the drawer region has no local consumer. (4) LogPanel stops Escape only for an open type filter (LogPanel.tsx:180-192) and a non-empty search input (LogPanel.tsx:307-312), both with comments naming this exact hazard — Level select, Manage logs, Close, Load older and the region itself all fall through to window. (5) Reachability confirmed rather than refuted: ProjectSync.tsx:3667 passes `busy={busy || !!inlineStorageReview}` to ProjectSidebar to seal nav during a review, and Storages/Settings/Projects all carry `disabled={busy}` (ProjectSidebar.tsx:713/721/729/737), but the Logs trigger at ProjectSidebar.tsx:741-748 has no `disabled` — so the drawer is openable exactly while a review is up. (6) No higher layer intercepts: ProjectSync.tsx:1318, SyncPathBar.tsx:405, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1278, ProjectActivityPage.tsx:182/878, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:234/398/955 each call stopPropagation() on document-level listeners with the same "must not also close and discard the whole review" comment. The house pattern is applied at seven sites; the drawer region is the hole in it. Severity lowered to medium because the loss is in-progress review work that is fully recoverable by re-running Push — nothing on disk or in remote storage is destroyed.
correction: The impact statement's reset list is slightly off. `onClose` clears `pendingPush`, `pushError`, `pushProjectContentRemovals` and `pushWarningAcknowledgements` — that is one error reset plus two review-decision sets, not "three selection resets". `pushSelected` (the ticked conversations/files) is NOT cleared by `onClose`; it survives in state but is unconditionally overwritten with `new Set(projectDefaults)` on the next prepare at ProjectSync.tsx:1922, so the ticks are still lost on reopen, just by a different mechanism. Everything else in the finding — the citation, the line number, the drawer's total absence of an Escape handler, and the reachability of the drawer during a review — is accurate. Worth adding to the fix note: the codebase already has an established remedy pattern for exactly this (a document-level keydown listener that calls stopPropagation, used at seven other sites); the minimal fix is to apply that pattern in ActivityLogDrawer.tsx rather than rescoping the review's window listener.

title: Escape discards the prepared Push review from anywhere, including inside the Logs drawer
reason: Refuted on three independent grounds. (1) INTENTIONAL DESIGN: the window-level Escape listener is a consciously maintained repo-wide contract. Eight sites carry the verbatim comment "This layer consumed Escape; the Push/Pull review listens on window and must not also close and discard the whole review" (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:184,880; SyncPathBar.tsx:407; StorageCatalogPage.tsx:235,399,957; ProjectSync.tsx:1320; ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1270; LogPanel.tsx:184), and LogPanel.tsx:303-306 names the drawer-over-review case explicitly. The author audited this layer by layer and drew the boundary where the finding says there is a gap: sub-layers that genuinely close on Escape swallow it, drawer chrome does not. (2) FALSE PREMISE: the Logs drawer has no Escape-to-close behavior in ANY context in this app — it is a docked non-modal panel with a Close button. No user can have learned "Escape closes the drawer" here, so the "expecting the drawer to close" scenario is imported from elsewhere. The proposed fix (drawer closes on Escape) is a new feature, not a bug fix, and rescoping the review listener to a subtree would silently break the eight stopPropagation call sites built against the window contract. (3) NOT DESTRUCTIVE, AND ALREADY ACCEPTED: onClose (ProjectSync.tsx:3396-3402) only nulls client state — no write, delete, remote mutation, or backend corruption (the plan id lives in memory and a lost review fails closed). pendingPush is derived from an idempotent preparePushReview re-run with one click, and ProjectSync.tsx:1920 restores the identical recommended selection via setPushSelected(new Set(projectDefaults)); only deviations from the default are lost. The drawer's own "Manage logs" button already discards the prepared push on a plain click (openSettings:1496 -> closeWorkspaceSettings:1430 -> setPendingPush(null)), as does any sidebar navigation — the codebase treats a prepared review as disposable navigation state by design. The one genuinely irreversible state, a running push, is already sealed by "&& !busy" in the handler and "if (busy) return" in onClose, with a live region explaining why.
correction: If restated at all, it is a keyboard-ergonomics nit, not a destructive-safety defect: "Escape pressed while focus is in the Logs drawer chrome closes the underlying Push review instead of the drawer. No data is lost — the review is re-prepared with one click and the recommended selection is restored identically; only manual deviations from the default selection are discarded, and the same discard already happens when the drawer's own Manage logs button is clicked."

title: Logs drawer resize separator is mouse-only
reason: Citation verified verbatim at src/components/project-sync/ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:190-198 (div opens line 191). The separator really does carry only role/aria-label/aria-orientation/onMouseDown/onDoubleClick — no tabIndex, no key handler. Traced every path to the height: a repo-wide grep finds logHeight only in ProjectSync.tsx (useState(240) at :398, window-fit at :589, drag move at :676, double-click reset at :3883); the onStartResize prop is startLogResize (ProjectSync.tsx:665), ReactMouseEvent-typed with document mousemove/mouseup, so it is genuinely mouse-only with no global shortcut, guard, or fallback. The sibling contract does exist as claimed at ProjectSync.tsx:3694-3709 and ProjectSidebar.tsx:663-683 (dividerProps). Defect reproduced in source. But the claimed impact overstates it on three counts, so severity drops to low: (1) logHeight is ephemeral state initialized to 240 and persisted nowhere, so a keyboard user is never handed a mouse-set value — the only shrinking force, the window-fit effect at ProjectSync.tsx:584-593, floors at 140px; (2) a non-focusable role="separator" is a VALID static separator under ARIA and requires no aria-valuemin/max/now — those become required only once tabIndex={0} is added, so their absence is not itself a defect; (3) LogPanel's body (bodyRef, .log-panel-body at App.css:731) is its own keyboard-scrollable region with tail-following, so no log content is unreachable. This is a missing resize enhancement (WCAG 2.1.1 on the resize function), not a drawer that strands a keyboard user.
correction: The log drawer's resize separator (src/components/project-sync/ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:191) is mouse-only: it has no tabIndex and no onKeyDown, and its handler startLogResize (ProjectSync.tsx:665) binds document mousemove/mouseup, so the resize and double-click-reset functions are unavailable to keyboard users — a WCAG 2.1.1 gap on that function. It diverges from the sidebar separator (ProjectSync.tsx:3694-3709) and the sidebar section gutters (ProjectSidebar.tsx:663-683), which both ship tabIndex={0}, the three aria-value attributes, and a key handler. Impact is limited, not a lock-out: logHeight is non-persisted state defaulting to 240px with a 140px floor (ProjectSync.tsx:398, :589), and LogPanel's body is independently keyboard-scrollable, so all log content stays reachable. Note also that the missing aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuenow are not a defect in the current markup — a non-focusable role="separator" is a valid static separator; those attributes become required only as part of the fix, once tabIndex={0} makes it a widget.

title: Focus indicators on the thread-status badge and metric readouts fall below 3:1
reason: Independently reproduced. The quoted CSS exists verbatim at the stated lines in <repo>/src/App.css (5215 outline:none inside .sync-thread-sync-indicator, 5279 the 35% box-shadow, 5367 outline:none inside .sync-history-thread-metric, 5450 the 45% box-shadow), and ProjectActivityPage.tsx:602/670/701-706 all carry tabIndex={0} on non-interactive spans. I recomputed the ratios myself: the backdrop is --surface-row (set on .sync-history-thread-card at App.css:9839); color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 35%, transparent) is accent at alpha 0.35, giving L=0.4246 over #fdf9f3 = 2.109:1 light and 2.833:1 dark for the badge, and 2.723:1 light for the metric at 45% — all below the 3:1 SC 1.4.11 floor. However the finding is imprecise in three verifiable ways (see correction), most importantly that App.css:9940 (.sync-history-commit > .sync-history-thread-list .sync-thread-sync-indicator { box-shadow: none }) is specificity (0,3,0) and later in source, so it beats the (0,2,0) :focus-visible rule and removes the badge ring entirely for every commit row — the timeline's dominant case. That makes the defect worse than stated there, not absent, so the finding stands.
correction: Corrected statement: (1) The badge's low-contrast ring only exists in the `flat` lists (uncommitted, storage-only, review). For sessions rendered under a commit — `div.sync-history-thread-list` is a direct child of `li.sync-history-commit` (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1937 -> 1970) — App.css:9940 `.sync-history-commit > .sync-history-thread-list .sync-thread-sync-indicator { background: transparent; box-shadow: none; }` has specificity (0,3,0) against the (0,2,0) of `.sync-thread-sync-indicator:focus-visible` and comes later, so the focus ring is suppressed outright, not merely dimmed. (2) The metric ring fails in light only: 45% #efe7d4 over #14120f measures 3.90:1, which passes; light is 2.72:1. (3) The proposed fix's first branch is wrong — there is no global `--focus-ring` outline to fall back to. The only global focus rules are App.css:38-41 and 8526-8531, which match button/input/select/summary/textarea, never a `<span tabindex="0">`; deleting `outline: none` would restore only the UA default ring. The workable fix is the second branch (opaque `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--focus-ring)`), which must additionally override App.css:9940 or that rule will keep zeroing it in commit rows. Mitigating context the finding omits: both classes reveal an opaque tooltip on :focus-visible (App.css:5273-5277, 5444-5448) with --surface-popover fill and a --border-strong border, so focus position is not wholly invisible — though a tooltip is not a conforming focus indicator for the control.

title: Every custom radiogroup ignores arrow keys and makes each radio a separate tab stop
reason: Independently reproduced at all five sites. BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:123 matches the quoted evidence verbatim (container `role="radiogroup" aria-label="Available remote repos"` wrapping `matches.map` over `<button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked={active}>`), and the four secondary line numbers are exact: SettingsPage.tsx:391 (src/components/project-sync/), StorageSettings.tsx:230 (src/components/project-sync/), ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:905, AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:228 (src/components/storage-catalog/). No guard or fallback was missed: grep for `onKeyDown|keydown|Arrow|tabIndex` across all five files returns zero hits, so there is no roving tabIndex and no arrow handling anywhere in them. There is no shared helper in src/hooks, src/lib, or src/utils, and none of the eleven app-wide document/window keydown listeners touches arrows or `[role=radio]` — they are all Escape/close handlers in unrelated components. The buttons are disabled only transiently (busy/working/storageTypeLocked), so each is a live tab stop in normal state. Corroboration that this is a genuine omission rather than a pattern implemented elsewhere: the same codebase does supply the roving contract for its tablist at src/components/sync-review/SyncReviewTabs.tsx:78,82 (`tabIndex={active ? 0 : -1}` plus `onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}` on role="tab"), so the pattern is known and was simply never applied to the radiogroups. Existing tests only assert the role's source text (settings-page.integration.test.tsx:45, storage-catalog.integration.test.tsx:537), pinning the ARIA without covering behavior.
correction: The defect and all five citations hold as stated; two details in the impact claim are overstated. (1) "The arrows then do nothing" is true in focus/forms mode, but in a screen reader's browse mode arrows still move the reading cursor — the precise defect is that the declared radiogroup role promises an arrow-driven selection model that is never delivered, not that arrow keys are globally inert. (2) This is not a clean WCAG 2.1 AA failure: SC 2.1.1 Keyboard is satisfied because every option remains reachable by Tab and operable by Enter/Space. The issue is a role/behavior mismatch (SC 4.1.2 adjacent) plus the extra tab stops, which in BundleConnectionDialog scale with the number of remote repos in the storage.

title: Focus indicators on the thread-status badge and metric readouts fall below 3:1
reason:
REFUTED — the ring is not the focus indicator, and the claimed consequence does not occur.

1. Focus opens an opaque, high-contrast popover. Three lines above the quoted rule, App.css:5273-5277 says `.sync-thread-sync-indicator:hover::after, .sync-thread-sync-indicator:focus-visible::after { opacity: 1; visibility: visible; }` (same for the metric at 5444-5448). That `::after` is a filled box: App.css:10297-10303 gives the badge tooltip `background: var(--surface-popover)`, `border-color: var(--accent)`, `box-shadow: var(--shadow-popover)`; the metric's own `::after` (5395-5402) gets `background: var(--surface-popover)` and `border: 1px solid var(--border-strong)`. Border-vs-row contrast is ~14:1 (accent) and ~6:1 (border-strong). So tabbing a session list pops a bordered box carrying that element's own text at every stop. "A keyboard user cannot see where they are" is false; SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible is met emphatically.

2. The premise about the global rule is wrong. App.css:38-42 is element-scoped — `button:focus-visible, input:focus-visible, select:focus-visible, summary:focus-visible`. These are `<span>`s (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:597-604, 701-706), so no global `--accent` outline ever applied and `outline: none` "drops" nothing. The primary proposed fix (delete `outline: none`, let the global outline apply) therefore yields the UA default `outline: auto` — system blue in dark mode, the exact regression App.css:30-35 documents and fixes for checkboxes ("the only cool colour on a sepia page").

3. Deliberate and actively maintained. `git blame`: the soft ring dates to 2026-07-20 (88e19094 / 3282d280); e7c1d60 (2026-08-26) and 52c15a0a (2026-08-29) were explicit passes that *added* `:focus-visible` reachability to these hover-only readouts and kept the tint; today's uncommitted tree adds `border-radius: 8px` (5211) and `border-radius: var(--r)` (5366) so the 2px shadow follows the chip shape. This author measures contrast in comments when it matters — App.css:5285-5290 records "3.31:1 light, 3.75:1 dark, both clear of the 3:1 WCAG 2.2 bar" for the glyph. Softness here is a choice, not an oversight.

4. The codebase already suppresses the ring on purpose. App.css:9940-9943 `.sync-history-commit > .sync-history-thread-list .sync-thread-sync-indicator { box-shadow: none; }` is specificity (0,3,0) and beats `.sync-thread-sync-indicator:focus-visible` (0,2,0), so in the main timeline the ring never paints at all — and focus still reads fine via the tooltip. That confirms the ring is decorative reinforcement, not the affordance.

5. Scope. These are non-interactive readouts — the code comment at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:683-685 says "Readouts only — everything in here is hovered, nothing is clicked." No role, no handler, no activation. `tabIndex={0}` is an accessibility *addition* layered over `aria-label`, which every one of them already carries (601, 670, 701-706), so screen-reader users get the content without focus styling. SC 1.4.11 governs UI components and their states; a static chip is at the margin of that scope.

Remaining nit: yes, the 35%/45% tint alone measures ~2.11:1 light (I reproduced the blend over `--surface-row` #fdf9f3). Making it opaque would put a near-black 2px ring on 5-6 chips per row in a dense list — the visual noise the design's own comments work hard to avoid — for a criterion already satisfied. Also note `--focus-ring: var(--accent)` (8070/8182), so the suggested "opaque ring" is the same hue the rule already uses.
correction: Accurate statement: the supplementary `:focus-visible` box-shadow tint on `.sync-thread-sync-indicator` (App.css:5279) and `.sync-history-thread-metric` (5450) measures below 3:1 against `--surface-row` on its own. It is not the focus indicator — focus reveals an opaque bordered tooltip popover (5274, 5445, backed by 10297-10303 and 5395-5402) whose border clears 3:1 in both themes — and the tint is suppressed entirely in the main timeline by App.css:9940. No global outline is being overridden; App.css:38-42 matches only button/input/select/summary, and these are spans. Optional polish, not a defect.

title: Logs drawer resize separator is mouse-only
reason: The code fact is right (src/components/project-sync/ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:190-198 has no tabIndex/onKeyDown, unlike ProjectSync.tsx:3694-3709 and ProjectSidebar.tsx:663-682), but both concrete harms are unreachable in this app. (1) "Stuck at whatever height was last set with a mouse" is false: logHeight is `useState(240)` at ProjectSync.tsx:398 with no persistence — unlike sidebarWidth, which reads storedSidebarWidth() and writes PROJECT_SIDEBAR_WIDTH_KEY at line 537. Every launch starts at the 240px default, so a keyboard-only user never inherits a mouse-shrunk drawer. (2) "On a short window only a couple of log lines visible" is impossible: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json pins minHeight 560, and the fit effect (ProjectSync.tsx:588) clamps to Math.min(current, Math.max(140, innerHeight-120)) = min(240, >=440) = 240 at the smallest allowed window; the 140 floor is only reachable by a deliberate mouse drag. (3) Nothing is gated behind the resizer: .log-panel-body is overflow-y:auto (App.css:731) with tail-follow and a focusable "Load older" button (LogPanel.tsx:333-341), and the panel's filters, search, manage and close controls are all ordinary focusable elements, so all log functionality and content remain operable. (4) The ARIA half of the claim is not a defect: a non-focusable role="separator" is the valid static structural separator; aria-valuemin/valuemax/valuenow are required only for the focusable widget form, so the current markup is conforming and would only become non-conforming if tabIndex were added without them. (5) The proposed fix would not deliver the claimed benefit anyway — the drag ceiling is Math.min(520, innerHeight-120), roughly doubling visible lines against MAX_LOG_LINES = 2000, so resizing is not a path to log history under any input method. What remains is a consistency nit: one cosmetic pane-sizing convenience is pointer-only while two siblings are not. No user or maintainer loses access to anything by hitting it.
correction: Accurate residual: the log drawer's resize handle is the one pointer-only separator among three in the app, so keyboard users cannot fine-tune the drawer's height. It is a comfort/consistency gap only — the drawer always opens at its unpersisted 240px default, the window cannot be short enough for the auto-fit clamp to reduce that, and all log content and controls stay reachable via the scrolling body and its focusable buttons. The missing aria-value* attributes are not themselves a defect while the separator is non-focusable.

title: Every custom radiogroup ignores arrow keys and makes each radio a separate tab stop
reason:
The code is as described — all five sites declare role="radiogroup"/role="radio" on plain <button>s with no roving tabIndex and no arrow handling (BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:123, SettingsPage.tsx:391, StorageSettings.tsx:230, ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:905, AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:228). But no user-visible capability is lost, and the claimed impact overstates what actually happens.

1) Nothing is unreachable or unoperable. Every option is a real <button>: Tab reaches it, Enter/Space activates it, and <repo>/src/App.css:38-43 paints a global 2px accent `:focus-visible` outline on every button, so the Tab path is visibly tracked. WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.1 (Keyboard) passes; SC 4.1.2 passes too — role and aria-checked are correctly exposed and the state is settable from the keyboard. Arrow-key navigation inside a radiogroup is an ARIA Authoring Practices *authoring pattern*, not any WCAG A/AA success criterion. This is a conformance-to-APG polish item, not a defect a user hits.

2) The "one tab stop per option, sitting between the dialog's other controls" cost is bounded and small. Real option counts: Storage type = 2, Theme = 3 (THEME_CHOICES), Resource kind = 4 (CATALOG_KINDS in src/components/storage-catalog/model.ts is a fixed four-element list), Repo identity = 1 + the storage's repos, Bundle dialog = the storage's matching repos. In the bundle dialog the tab order is close button → N cards → footer; N is a handful of repos per storage. Tabbing through a card list of 2-5 items is a coherent interaction, not an obstacle.

3) The screen-reader narrative is platform-mismatched. "Announces radio group, 1 of N and switches to arrow-key mode" is NVDA/JAWS browse-vs-forms-mode behavior on Windows. This is a Tauri desktop app whose whole surface is macOS-shaped (WKWebView, ~/.mallard, Codex/Claude CLI homes, Darwin dev), where the realistic AT is VoiceOver — which has no browse/forms mode switch and navigates any focusable element with VO+arrows or Tab. There, each option being individually tabbable is more navigable, not less.

4) The codebase demonstrably knows the pattern and applied it where it judged it warranted: SyncReviewTabs.tsx:78-82 implements exactly the roving `tabIndex={active ? 0 : -1}` + onKeyDown for role="tablist" (where APG's single-tab-stop is genuinely load-bearing). BundleConnectionDialog also deliberately uses native <dialog>+showModal() for focus trap/Escape/inert (comment at line 38-39). The a11y attention here is selective and considered, not absent — the radiogroups are a keep-the-button-list-tabbable choice, not an oversight that strands anyone.

5) As a finding it is one lint-shaped pattern observation restated across five sites, none of which produces a wrong outcome, a stuck state, or an unreachable control. "Medium" is inflated for a best-practice deviation with zero functional loss on the app's actual platform.
correction: What actually holds: the five custom radiogroups follow the ARIA button-list convention rather than the APG radiogroup keyboard pattern — every option remains Tab-reachable, focus-ringed and Enter/Space-activatable, so no functionality is lost and no WCAG 2.1 A/AA criterion fails. The only genuine (narrow) mismatch is a Windows NVDA/JAWS forms-mode user pressing arrows inside the group and finding them inert; on the app's macOS/VoiceOver target this does not arise. Worth queuing as a shared roving-tabindex helper for consistency, not as a medium-severity accessibility defect.

title: Branch picker reimplements the shared menu keyboard helper and leaves every option a tab stop
reason: Reproduced in source. ProjectActivityPage.tsx:242-256 contains the quoted handler verbatim (line number exact) and it is a line-for-line duplicate of moveMenuFocus in src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts:22-35. title: Agent-setup split menu declares role="menu" with no name, no keyboard contract and no focus move
reason: I tried to refute this and could not — the codebase itself documents the exact defect. src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts:1-9 states the house rule verbatim: the keyboard half is "shared by every popup that declares one. Declaring the role without this is a promise the widget does not keep: a screen reader switches to menu navigation and the arrow keys then do nothing (or scroll the page)." So this is the opposite of an intentional design decision; the intent record points the other way. The code is as described: the div at :2044 carries role="menu" with no aria-label, no onKeyDown, and no focus move, and the effect at :1272-1289 handles outside-press/Escape only. It is on a live route (ProjectSync.tsx:3797), and four of the five sibling menus already carry aria-label (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:239 "Branches", ProjectSync.tsx:2780 "App actions", SyncPathBar.tsx:252, files-selection-mockup.tsx:436) with three of them implementing full arrow/Home/End handling — this site is the outlier, not the convention. What I do refute is the severity and part of the impact. The consequence is friction, not a block: the menu items are real <button> elements rendered inline immediately after the trigger, so Tab reaches and activates every one of them — WCAG 2.1.1 is satisfied and no function is unreachable. The APG roving-focus pattern is best practice, not a WCAG 2.1 AA success criterion, and role="menu" has no required accessible name. The path is also low-traffic: it appears only while creating an S3/R2 storage draft, only when a launcher is detected, and is exercised once per storage. Medium is inflated; this is a low-severity conformance/consistency gap on a one-time setup surface.
correction: Two claims in the impact are overstated, and the proposed fix carries a regression hazard. (1) "Nothing announced" is wrong — the trigger sets aria-expanded (line 2037) and is named "More agent setup routes" (line 2038), so a screen reader announces the expanded state on Enter; what is missing is the focus move into the menu, not the announcement. (2) The menu is not keyboard-inaccessible — its items are plain <button>s in DOM order right after the chevron, so Tab reaches them today; the real defects are (a) role="menu" puts a screen reader into menu-navigation mode where ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End do nothing, (b) the popup has no accessible name, and (c) Escape (or an outside press) unmounts the menu while focus may be inside it, dropping focus to <body> instead of returning it to the chevron. (3) The proposed tabIndex={-1} on the items must land only together with the moveMenuFocus/focusMenuEdge handler — applied on its own it would remove the Tab access that currently works and turn a low-severity gap into a genuine keyboard trap. Scope note: ProjectSync.tsx:2780 ("App actions") declares role="menu" with an aria-label but likewise no arrow handling, so the correct framing is a small pattern-level cleanup across the two remaining non-conforming menus rather than a single-site medium defect.

title: Three menus that close by `hidden` drop focus to <body> on Escape
reason: The primary citation is exact. src/components/storage-catalog/StorageCatalogPage.tsx:955-961 contains the quoted handler verbatim, and line 585 is verbatim `ref={(node) => focusMenuEdge(node, "first")}`. focusMenuEdge (src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts:37-42) calls options[0].focus() over `[role="menuitem"|"menuitemcheckbox"|"menuitemradio"]`, and the options at line 599 are `role="menuitemcheckbox"`, so focus is genuinely inside the menu after open. ResourceCard holds no trigger ref; the only `.focus()` in the whole file is line 212, which belongs to InfoMenu's own closeMenu(restoreFocus). Focus therefore falls to <body>. The cited correct-pattern sites are also real: InfoMenu in the same file (209-214, 239), SyncPathBar.tsx:405-412 (openerRefs lookup then opener?.focus()), ProjectActivityPage.tsx:163-166. I could not reproduce at runtime because tests/frontend/ uses renderToStaticMarkup only (no jsdom, react-dom/client or testing-library anywhere in the repo), so this is source-traced. The finding is nonetheless imprecise in scope and impact, which the correction narrows.
correction: Only one of the three cited menus loses focus on the ordinary path. Restated: the Catalog Pull review's local-action menu (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:577-615, closed at 955-961) focuses its first option on open and unmounts it on Escape without restoring focus to the chevron trigger, so activeElement becomes <body>. The title's "close by `hidden`" is wrong for it and for ProjectLinksWorkspace (both conditionally unmount); only ProjectSync's app-actions menu uses `hidden={!appMenuOpen}` (line 2782). Neither ProjectSync's menu nor ProjectLinksWorkspace's agent menu (2018-2078) moves focus into itself on open — no focusMenuEdge, and ProjectLinksWorkspace has no menu onKeyDown at all — so opening by click or Enter leaves focus on the trigger and Escape loses nothing; focus only drops there if the user first Tabs into a menu item. The impact claim "next Tab restarts at the top of the page" overstates it: browsers keep a sequential focus navigation starting point when the focused node is removed, so Tab resumes near the removed menu. Fix is the one proposed, but only StorageCatalogPage.tsx:955-961 needs it on the primary path.

title: Agent-setup split menu declares role="menu" with no name, no keyboard contract and no focus move
reason: Reproduced in source. src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2044 is verbatim `<div className="sync-path-menu end" role="menu">` with no aria-label; `grep -n onKeyDown` over the entire 3368-line file returns zero hits, and the only keyboard listener is the document-level Escape closer in the effect at lines 1271-1289, which does no focus management. menuKeyboard.ts exists at src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts and is imported only by SyncPathBar.tsx:3 and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:13. All other role="menu" sites in src/ are named; only 2044 is not. It is shipped code, pinned by tests/frontend/storage-settings.integration.test.tsx:1019. Two parts of the impact statement are wrong, however: the trigger at 2036-2038 does carry aria-label="More agent setup routes" plus aria-expanded, so the expanded state is announced (not "nothing announced"); and the menu items are plain buttons with no tabIndex, so they remain in the natural tab order and every route is reachable and activatable with Tab+Enter. correction: The split-button popup at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2044 declares role="menu"/role="menuitem" but keeps none of that contract: no accessible name on the container, no ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End handling (the file contains no onKeyDown at all), and no focus move on open — the only keyboard code is the document-level Escape closer at lines 1271-1289. It is the sole role="menu" in src/ without a name, and the same `sync-path-menu end` widget in StorageCatalogPage.tsx:583 does implement the full contract via the shared menuKeyboard.ts helper. Impact is a screen-reader-experience defect, not a keyboard block: the trigger is named ("More agent setup routes") and exposes aria-expanded, and the menu items are ordinary buttons with no tabIndex, so they stay in the tab order and every route is still reachable via Tab+Enter. Fix accordingly: add aria-label, focusMenuEdge on open, the moveMenuFocus onKeyDown, and Escape focus-restore — and add tabIndex={-1} to the items only together with the focus move, never on its own, or the routes become unreachable.

title: Three menus that close by `hidden` drop focus to <body> on Escape
reason: One of the three sites is real; the other two are mischaracterized, and the severity is inflated. StorageCatalogPage.tsx:585 genuinely puts focus inside the menu on open (focusMenuEdge is a synchronous ref callback that focuses options[0], for mouse-opens too) and the menu is conditionally rendered, so the Escape handler at :955 unmounts the focused button and Chromium drops activeElement to <body> on a realistic path (Pull review row with >1 action, open chevron, press Escape). But ProjectSync.tsx:1318 and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1278 never move focus on open — the app-actions menu is rendered with hidden and `.storage-link-actions-menu[hidden]{display:none}` (App.css:3804) keeps its one item out of the tab order, and the agent split menu has no autofocus and no roving-focus handler. In both, opening by click or Enter leaves focus on the trigger, so Escape already ends with focus exactly where the proposed fix would put it; a drop requires the user to first Tab off the trigger into the menu and only then press Escape, and for ProjectLinksWorkspace that is on the one-time storage-creation form. The consequence even at the live site is that the next Tab restarts at the top of the document: recoverable, no state corruption, nothing inoperable, no screen-reader trap, DOM order unchanged. No test covers it and no doc or commit states focus-return as a global contract (only the openerRefs comment at SyncPathBar.tsx:145-147, from a15687a), so this is a consistency cleanup against an established-but-undocumented pattern rather than a medium defect.
correction: Only StorageCatalogPage.tsx:955 drops focus on a realistic path, because its menu is the one of the three that programmatically focuses its first option on open (focusMenuEdge at line 585) and unmounts on close. ProjectSync.tsx:1318 and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1278 leave focus on their trigger button when the menu opens, so Escape there preserves focus correctly; they lose focus only if the user deliberately Tabs into the open menu first. The fix is still worth making for consistency with SyncPathBar.tsx:410 and ProjectActivityPage.tsx:163, but the impact is a keyboard user's next Tab restarting at the top of the page, at one site.

title: Branch picker reimplements the shared menu keyboard helper and leaves every option a tab stop
reason: Both load-bearing impact claims are contradicted by the actual code. (1) "Every option is a tab stop / Tabbing off the trigger walks the branch list": the menu is `hidden={!open}` (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:241) and App.css:4939 carries an explicit `.sync-history-branch-menu[hidden] { display: none; }` rule, so a closed menu's options are display:none — unfocusable and out of the tab order entirely. Tabbing off the trigger goes straight to the next path-bar control. The tab stops exist only while the menu is open, and opening it already moves focus inside (focusOption, lines 144-162). (2) "The menu stays open under Tab": refuted by the document `focusin` guard at lines 178-180, which closes the menu the moment focus lands outside rootRef — so Tab past the last option closes it. The branch picker is in fact the only one of these menus with a focus-out auto-close. (3) "Unlike every other menu in the app": false. `tabIndex={-1}` appears at exactly two sites in the whole repo, both in SyncPathBar.tsx (201, 233). StorageCatalogPage.tsx:583-611 — which does import moveMenuFocus and does handle Tab — has no tabIndex={-1} on its menuitemcheckbox buttons; ProjectSync.tsx:2776 and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2044 have neither roving tabindex nor a Tab handler. The branch picker matches the app's norm; SyncPathBar (the one menu with a search field and typeahead) is the outlier. The role="menu" contract the shared helper's doc-comment names as load-bearing — arrows do something, Home/End, Escape, focus-on-open, focus restore to trigger — is fully implemented here. No focus trap, no dead end, no lost focus. What survives is that lines 242-257 hand-copy moveMenuFocus with byte-identical behavior (no functional drift): a code-reuse nit, not a keyboard-accessibility defect, and worth at most a two-line swap.
correction: The inline handler at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:242-257 duplicates `moveMenuFocus` (sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts:22-35) with identical behavior — a DRY/consistency cleanup under code-reuse, not a11y-keyboard. The only real ergonomic wrinkle is that while the menu is already open, Tab steps option-by-option before the focusin guard closes it, instead of leaving immediately as in SyncPathBar; adopting roving tabindex would be a refinement, but two of the app's three other menus behave the same way and none of the claimed consequences (tab stops reachable from the closed trigger, a menu left open behind the user) actually occur.

title: Path-bar crumb menus open on Enter/Space without moving focus into the menu
reason: Verified against the real file, not the quoted evidence. Line 514 is verbatim the cited onClick; the onKeyDown at 515-524 returns early for every key except Tab/ArrowDown/ArrowUp, so Enter (keydown) and Space (keyup) fall through to native button activation and reach only `setOpenMenu(...)`. The same shape is at 541-548 (non-split crumb) and 616 (overflow). I looked for the guards a refutation would need and found none: PathBarMenu (247-305) is a plain `<div role="menu" hidden={!open}>` with no mount/open autofocus, every item is tabIndex={-1} (201, 233) so Tab cannot reach them, and the trigger's Tab branch closes the menu anyway. The only useEffects (394-396, 398-420, 432-440) handle stale-menu cleanup, outside-click/Escape, and the external openMenuRequest prop -- none fires on click. focusMenuOption (422-430) is invoked only from the arrow-key branches and the openMenuRequest effect. The codebase's own sibling menu at src/components/storage-catalog/StorageCatalogPage.tsx:585 does `ref={(node) => focusMenuEdge(node, "first")}`, focusing the first item on open regardless of pointer or key, so SyncPathBar is the inconsistent one and the proposed fix matches house convention.
correction: Two corrections. (1) "Only the Arrow-key open path calls focusMenuOption" is slightly wrong: the openMenuRequest effect at lines 432-440 also calls focusMenuOption(menuId, "first") when an outside control asks for a menu. The click path is still the gap. (2) The menu is not unreachable. Because focus never leaves the trigger, the trigger's own onKeyDown stays live, so ArrowDown/ArrowUp after an Enter/Space open still focuses the first/last item, and Escape (lines 405-413) closes and returns focus to the opener. So this is a deviation from the APG menu-button pattern ("Enter/Space opens the menu and places focus on the first item") and an inconsistency with StorageCatalogPage.tsx:585, not a WCAG 2.1 AA failure or a keyboard trap -- hence low rather than medium. Also note the proposed fix's "and a mouse click" clause goes beyond APG (pointer activation need not move focus), though it does match what StorageCatalogPage.tsx already does.

title: Pull review has no Escape handler, but its own status copy tells the user Escape closes it
reason:
The finding's headline claim is factually wrong, and the residual is a stale code comment, not a keyboard-accessibility defect.

1. No user-visible copy mentions Escape. The `role="status"` string at <repo>/src/components/project-sync/RestorePlanView.tsx:672 reads in full: "A running pull finishes or fails whole — it can’t be cancelled midway." Escape appears only in the source comment on lines 666-671, which no user ever sees. So "its own status copy tells the user Escape closes it" is not true of the shipped UI — the announcement itself is accurate (a running pull genuinely has no mid-write abort) and does not promise anything about Escape.

2. Neither review is a modal, so no Escape contract is owed. Both are mounted as `inlineStorageReview` — an inline, in-page surface (ProjectSync.tsx:3385 for push, :3465 for pull), not a `<dialog>`/`showModal()` overlay (the app's real modals, ProjectBindingEditor.tsx:90 and BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:38, use native `<dialog>` and get Escape from the platform). WCAG 2.1 AA requires Escape only as an escape from a keyboard trap or modal; there is none here.

3. The Pull review is not keyboard-trapped and loses no function. Its header carries a real focusable `<button class="btn btn-ghost sync-inline-action-close">` with `aria-label="Close pull review for {projectName}"` (RestorePlanView.tsx:547 → SyncReviewSelectionBar.tsx:71-78), reachable by Tab alongside the tabs and footer. A keyboard user closes the review the same way in both flows.

4. Realistic encounter rate is near zero and the failure is the mildest possible. Nothing in either UI advertises Escape; a user can only learn it by accident on Push, and the "consequence" is pressing a key and nothing happening while a labelled close button sits in the same header. No data loss, no dead end, no missing announcement.

5. The asymmetry is arguably safer, not broken, which makes it a design question rather than a defect. The Push listener (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:417-423) is a bare `window` keydown that discards an entire curated review with no confirmation — which is precisely why five unrelated layers must defensively `stopPropagation` to stop their own Escape from nuking it (SyncPathBar.tsx:407, LogPanel.tsx:184, ProjectActivityPage.tsx:182 and :878, ProjectSync.tsx:1319, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:234). Pull holds a hand-built restore selection; not wiring the same instant-discard hazard into it is a defensible choice, and the finding's own fix admits the alternative resolution is to delete the Push listener. Long-standing too: the Push handler dates to a very early commit and Pull has never had one across ~15 subsequent commits to this file, with no doc or test asserting the contract (no `Escape` assertion exists anywhere in tests/frontend, and docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md's keyboard section flags menus, never the reviews).

What is actually true is much smaller: the comment at RestorePlanView.tsx:666-671 was copied from Push and asserts an Escape behaviour Pull does not have. That misleads a maintainer reading the file; it is invisible to users.
correction: Accurate statement: the source comment at src/components/project-sync/RestorePlanView.tsx:666-671 is stale — copied from PushResourceWorkspace.tsx, it cites "Escape no longer closing the review" as a justification, but RestorePlanView registers no Escape handler and no ancestor closes the Pull review on Escape. The user-visible `role="status"` text on line 672 says nothing about Escape and is correct as written. Fixing the comment (or, separately, deciding whether Push's window-level Escape-to-discard should exist at all) is a code-hygiene/design item, not a keyboard-accessibility defect: the Pull review is non-modal, untrapped, and closable via a labelled focusable button at line 547.

title: Pull review has no Escape handler, but its own status copy tells the user Escape closes it
reason: The code facts are independently reproducible. RestorePlanView.tsx:672 holds the quoted span verbatim (comment at 667-671, one line off from the cited 666). The file registers no keydown listener at all — its useEffects are at 321/323/359/392/398 and none touch the keyboard — and its only close affordance is the selection bar at line 547 (close={{ ariaLabel: `Close pull review for ${projectName}`, onClose: onBack }}). No ancestor supplies Escape: the pull review is mounted as inlineStorageReview.content into a plain div (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:3227, className "sync-storage-inline-review", not a <dialog>, so no native Escape), and the only keydown listeners above it (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1284 agent menu, ProjectSync.tsx:563 sidebar shortcut, ProjectSync.tsx:1327 app menu) never call inlineStorageReview.onClose(). PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:417-422 is indeed the only review-closing Escape in the tree, and the pull comment is a condensed copy of PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:866-874 that dragged along a clause true only on Push. HOWEVER the finding's framing is wrong in two ways, so it stands only in corrected form: (1) no user-visible copy mentions Escape — the announced sentence is "A running pull finishes or fails whole — it can't be cancelled midway"; the false Escape claim lives only in a source comment; (2) this is not an a11y-keyboard defect — the panel is non-modal inline content with a keyboard-reachable, aria-labelled close control, so no functionality is keyboard-unreachable and no WCAG criterion (2.1.1/2.1.2) is implicated. What remains is a stale comment plus an undocumented shortcut inconsistency, and the questionable side is arguably Push, whose unscoped window listener discards an entire review on Escape irrespective of focus. No test in tests/frontend asserts Escape behaviour on either review.
correction: RestorePlanView.tsx:667-671 carries an inaccurate comment copied from PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:866-874: it cites "Escape no longer closing the review" as a reason for the busy-time announcement, but Escape never closed the Pull review — RestorePlanView registers no keydown listener and its container (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:3227) is a plain div, not a dialog. The user-facing status text itself says nothing about Escape, and the review remains fully keyboard-operable via the labelled close button at line 547, so this is a stale-comment and shortcut-consistency issue (Push closes on Escape at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:417-422, Pull does not), not an accessibility defect. Fix by correcting the comment and picking one Escape contract across both reviews — noting that Push's unscoped window-level Escape, which discards a whole review regardless of focus, is the more questionable of the two.

title: Path-bar crumb menus open on Enter/Space without moving focus into the menu
reason:
The code reads as described (SyncPathBar.tsx:514, 541-548, 616 toggle `openMenu` only; only the Arrow path at 520-524 / 555-559 / 622-626 calls `focusMenuOption`), but there is no real user-visible consequence, and the claimed impact overstates what actually happens.

1. No dead end and no focus loss. After Enter/Space the menu is open, focus sits on a visible, correctly-labelled trigger with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded={true}` and `aria-controls={menuId}` (lines 511-513). The very next key a menu-button user presses — ArrowDown — is handled on the *trigger* (520-524) and lands focus on the first item whether the menu was already open or not. So Enter-then-ArrowDown works, Escape returns focus to the opener (405-413), Tab deliberately steps the menu aside (516-518, and the mirrored comment at 256-258). There is no state from which the menu's contents are unreachable.

2. No WCAG criterion fails. 2.1.1 Keyboard is met (every item is operable via ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End/type-ahead through `menuKeyboard.ts`); 4.1.2 is met (`aria-expanded` tracks state accurately); 2.4.3 is met (focus never moves anywhere unexpected — it does not move at all). "Enter/Space opens the menu and focuses the first item" is APG *guidance*, not a normative requirement. This is pattern polish, not a defect.

3. "Hears nothing further / has to guess ArrowDown" is inflated. The trigger announces as a collapsed/expanded menu popup button, which is exactly the affordance that trains ArrowDown; and because `PathBarMenu` is rendered as a plain DOM sibling inside the same `<li>` (580-592), not a portal, the un-hidden menu also sits immediately next in reading order.

4. The proposed fix would introduce a worse defect than it removes. Routing `focusMenuOption(key, "first")` through `onClick` also fires it for **mouse** opens. The outside-click handler (400-404) then hides the menu (`hidden={!open}`) while focus is inside it, so focus drops to `<body>` — precisely the failure the `openerRefs` comment at lines 385-387 exists to prevent. It would also land past the search field on switcher menus that render one (`searchable`, line 174/328-337), since `focusMenuOption` only walks `[role=menuitem*]`. Any correct fix has to be keyboard-only and search-aware, which the finding does not account for.

Not covered by intent docs either way (no test in tests/ presses ArrowDown at all, and the switcher-menu memory note documents only the Arrow/Enter-in-search contract), so I am not calling it deliberate — but on impact it is a low-severity APG-alignment nit on a fully operable control, not a medium keyboard-access defect.
correction: Accurate statement: the path-bar menu triggers follow the WAI-ARIA menu-button pattern for ArrowDown/ArrowUp but not for Enter/Space, which open the menu while leaving focus on the trigger. All menu items remain reachable (one ArrowDown), aria-expanded stays accurate, and Escape restores focus, so no WCAG criterion fails — this is APG-alignment polish. A fix must move focus only on the keyboard-activation path (mouse opens must keep focus on the trigger, or the outside-click close will drop focus to body) and must target the search input rather than the first menuitem on switcher menus that render one.

title:
Empty switcher result uses a

inside role="menu" and is never announced
reason:
No real user-visible consequence, and both halves of the claim overreach. (1) The `

` is not an outlier: this `role="menu"` already ships a banner div, an `aria-current` header div, and an `` as non-menuitem children — a deliberate, documented shape (the file's own comment at the banner reasons explicitly about SC 4.1.3 and the menuitem family). The premise that AT "drops" such children would make the search input itself unreachable, which it demonstrably is not; Chromium/WebKit expose them as static text. (2) Keyboard behavior is unaffected: menuKeyboard.ts's MENU_OPTION_SELECTOR matches only role=menuitem/menuitemcheckbox/menuitemradio, so the `

` cannot enter or disturb the roving order, and the Enter-in-search handler targets `.target` rows only. (3) The empty row is unreachable without a query — `lists` derives from `populated`, which already filters out zero-item groups, and the search field only renders at >=6 switch targets — so it can only appear while focus is in the search input, in response to the user's own keystroke, with the AT in forms mode echoing what they typed. The finding itself concedes the user learns the menu is empty; the only missing datum is the "why", which is the filter they just typed, and the absence is confirmable by arrowing (only footer verbs/tails remain as menuitems). SC 4.1.3 scopes status messages to changes not driven by the user's own focus/input, and nothing else in this app announces filter results, while live regions are used consistently for genuinely async outcomes (StartupLoadingScreen, ProjectActivityPage refreshStatus, StorageSettings progress, SyncOutcomeNotice) — so this is app-consistent policy, not an omission. (4) The aria-label sub-claim is factually right but consequence-free: in switcher mode the group label is deliberately not drawn for sighted users either (only headerless menus render .sync-path-menu-label), so dropping it is exact parity with the visual design; adding role="group" would give AT users a name no one else gets. What remains is a cosmetic parity nit on a narrow path, not a defect.
correction: Accurate but inconsequential: `aria-label` on the role-less group `<div>` is inert, and "No match." is not spoken. Neither costs the user information — the switcher intentionally hides group labels from everyone, and the empty state is a self-authored, immediately-inferable result of the user's own typing.

title:

inside role="menu" and is never announced
reason:
Citation is accurate (SyncPathBar.tsx:343-345, parent role="menu" at :252), but all three claimed mechanisms fail. (1) "role=menu drops or flattens a

title: The switcher's search field can never receive keyboard focus — every route to it closes the menu
reason:
The mechanics are accurate but the impact is not. The switcher is fully operable from the keyboard without the search field, and skipping the input is a documented, chosen design.

1. Keyboard users are not stranded — the menu has its own typeahead. With 20 projects a keyboard user presses "h","o" and lands on "HorrorGame", then Enter. Arrows/Home/End wrap over the same set (moveMenuFocus), and Esc returns focus to the opener (line 405-414). The claim "they can only arrow through the unfiltered list" is false: the narrowing affordance exists, is the WAI-ARIA menu-pattern one, and costs fewer keystrokes than the text filter would. The switching task — the whole point of the widget — is completable by keyboard end to end.

2. It is intentional, and stated at ship time. The shipping note for this exact feature (~/.claude/projects/-Users-hequ-Desktop-project-mallard-app/memory/switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md, "IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-01)") specifies: "a search pill ... appears once a menu has ≥ SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR (6) targets, filters on label+detail, ArrowDown/Up step into the list, Enter activates the first .target, typeahead skips the input." The comment at lines 265-266 therefore does not document unreachable behaviour — it documents what happens once the caret is in the field, which a pointer user reaches by clicking, and it is exercised on that path.

3. The proposed fix would regress the chosen behaviour. Auto-focusing the input on open would swallow the typeahead keystrokes (every letter becomes a filter character instead of a jump) and would change what ArrowDown-to-open means, i.e. it reverts two decisions the user made when picking direction B.

4. The role="menu" content nit is known and accepted here, not novel: the banner and the current-object header row are also non-menuitem children, and the file's own comment at lines 306-309 says so explicitly ("A `role=\"menu\"` admits only the menuitem family"). The input carries an aria-label, so it is announced where a reader does surface it.

5. Residual delta is narrow: a keyboard-only user gets label-prefix matching instead of label+detail substring matching, and cannot filter by path fragment. That is a convenience gap in a secondary affordance, not a blocked workflow, no dead-end, no data consequence — and the app is a mouse-first macOS Tauri shell where the switcher is normally opened by clicking a chevron. "High" is inflated by an order of magnitude; this is a low-severity a11y enhancement at most, and one the author would likely decline as written.

The real gap is only that a keyboard-only user cannot use the substring/path matching the field offers — a convenience delta in a secondary affordance, severity low.

title: Switch targets drop their path line, so same-named projects and storages render as identical rows
reason:
The code is as quoted (SyncPathBar.tsx:190-192, :202), but this is not a regression — it is the shipped design the user explicitly chose, and the user-visible consequence is far narrower than claimed.

1) DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED, USER-PICKED. Calling the intended effect of a chosen redesign a "regression" mislabels it. The reviewer's proposed fix is literally direction A ("the least change"), which the user rejected.

2) THE PATH IS NOT GONE. The current object keeps its full path as a visible mono second line (header row, :316-327 — `detailIsPath` is honored there and never suppressed). The crumb itself carries `title: "<name> · <path>"` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2345, :2294; StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1277). And the switcher's search field, which appears once a list reaches SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR = 6 targets, filters on **label AND detail** (:176-178) — i.e. typing a path fragment disambiguates precisely in the crowded lists where collisions are most likely.

3) THE COLLISION PRECONDITION IS MOSTLY SELF-INFLICTED AND FIXABLE IN THE SAME MENU. Storage rows are labelled `storage.name` — a name the user types when adding the storage (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2302, :1714); two identically-named storages is the user's own naming, not an app-generated collision, and the icon still separates local (drive) from S3 (cloud). Catalog rows are labelled `${kind.plural} · ${profile.display_name}` (model.ts:44-50) — kind already differentiates, and profile names are user-set with "Rename profile…" in the same menu. Only projects derive their label from the folder basename (service.rs:13894-13899), and `projectLabel` prefers `local_alias`, with "Rename project…" sitting in the same switcher's verb strip as the intended disambiguator.

4) THE CONSEQUENCE IS A REVERSIBLE NAVIGATION. Selecting a switch target calls `onSelectProject` / `onOpenStorage` / `onOpenScope` — navigation only, no mutation, no destructive side effect. If you land on the wrong "app", the reopened switcher header shows that project's full path and one click returns you. That is nowhere near "high".

5) THE ROW-HEIGHT COMPLAINT IS A STYLE PREFERENCE, and the rule it objects to is coherent by design: paths (mono) go to the tooltip, prose qualifiers ("Bucket · …", an agent profile, a disabled reason) stay visible as `.phrase` (App.css:9094-9105, comment: "Paths keep the mono face above; a phrase … is prose").
correction: Precise residual, stated correctly: switch targets deliberately move a path detail into the native `title` (a user-chosen design, direction B). The one genuine narrowing is that below the 6-target search floor there is no filter field, so two projects sharing a folder basename with no alias set are separated only by hover tooltip — and because `title` is not surfaced on keyboard focus, the button's accessible name loses the path it previously carried. That is a low-severity scannability/a11y polish item (fix by folding the path into `aria-label`, or by lowering the search floor), not a regression to revert.
