title: The 'Switch to' group heading disappears in switcher mode and its replacement aria-label is inert
reason: Independently reproduced. Line 343 is verbatim and the line number is exact: `<div key={group.label} className="sync-path-menu-group" aria-label={group.label}>` with no `role`. The switcher branch (338-358) renders no `.sync-path-menu-label` and no `.sync-path-menu-separator`; only the headerless branch does (362-363), line number also correct. `git show HEAD:` confirms the regression is real — at HEAD a single branch rendered the visible label plus a separator for every labelled group, and "Switch to" is the actual group label at five production call sites (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1709, 2298, 2428, 2527; StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1246, 1321). The ARIA claim holds: a role-less `<div>` maps to `generic` (HTML-AAM), and `generic` is Name From: prohibited in ARIA 1.2, so the aria-label is dropped; there is no runtime role injection anywhere in src/, and menuKeyboard.ts only queries the menuitem family. The CSS claim holds: grep over App.css shows `.sync-path-menu-group` at zero lines (`.sync-path-menu-label` at 3084/8225/9083), and `.sync-path-menu.switcher` (3158) only sets width. The search-floor claim holds: `searchable = switcher && targetCount >= 6` (174), and the "Switch view" crumb (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2296) has exactly one target, so the no-search case is common. The two tests that mention "Switch to" assert call-site source text, not rendered output, so nothing gates it. Severity is overstated, however: the missing heading is deliberate and documented in the file's own comments (14-19, 120-128) as the switcher design, no WCAG AA SC is failed (the grouping is absent visually too, so 1.3.1 is not implicated), and the targets keep their own names as menuitems inside a named role=menu with the current object marked aria-current. The genuine defect is the narrower one: inert markup that has zero effect.
correction: At SyncPathBar.tsx:343 the `aria-label={group.label}` is inert: the wrapper is a role-less `<div>`, which maps to `generic`, a role for which naming is prohibited, so no assistive technology reports the group name. This is dead markup that reads as intent. The related visible change — the switcher branch dropping `.sync-path-menu-label` and the preceding separator that the pre-diff single branch rendered (still present in the headerless branch at 362-363) — is a deliberate design decision documented in the file's own header comments, not a defect. Note also that the claim "no word anywhere" is too strong: the menu container carries `role="menu" aria-label={label}` (253) fed by `crumb.menuLabel ?? crumb.label` (586), which is literally "Switch view" for the section crumb; for the storage/project/catalog-row switchers it is "Storage"/"Project"/"Catalog row", where the group context is indeed unstated. Minimal fix: add `role="group"` at 343 so the existing aria-label is honoured.

title: Type-ahead cannot reach the footer's text pills — their computed label is the empty string
reason: The mechanism is real but has no meaningful consequence, and the code it objects to is a deliberate design choice. (a) Every tail pill carries role="menuitem", so menuOptions() includes it and moveMenuFocus (src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts) gives it ArrowDown/ArrowUp roving plus Home/End — and End always lands on a tail, since the footer strip renders last. Nothing is unreachable by keyboard or screen reader. The file itself frames type-ahead as "this bar's own addition" (SyncPathBar.tsx:281), an optional accelerator layered on the shared role=menu contract; APG lists type-ahead as optional and no WCAG criterion is implicated. (b) The absent aria-label is intentional: the shipped-switcher design record (~/.claude/.../memory/switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md) specifies aria-label only for the icon-only verb pills, which have no text; tails are text pills whose visible text already is their accessible name. Both proposed fixes are net-negative — one duplicates visible text as a redundant aria-label, the other injects .sync-path-menu-copy (display:block, overflow:hidden, ellipsis; App.css:3300-3312) into a display:inline-flex pill deliberately styled without it (App.css:3236-3262). (c) Exposure is tiny: 1-2 tails per menu, in a fixed footer strip of a 260-380px popover, never scrolled off and never filtered (the `matches` filter is applied only to `lists`, not tails). (d) The failure is a silent no-op, never a mis-focus: the buffer is always length >= 1 so a tail can never falsely match, and the loop is bounded. (e) The regression framing is overstated — first-letter cycling starts at index+1 and wraps, so pre-change "a" reached "Add project…" only when no switch target started with "a"; and the switcher's stated intent is that the list holds only switch targets while the footer holds the ways to get more, so a target-scoped accelerator is consistent with the partition. (f) Nothing pins the behavior: zero hits for type-ahead, single-letter keydowns, or those tail labels across tests/frontend/.
correction: At most a polish nit, not a defect: type-ahead — an optional accelerator the file documents as its own addition on top of the standard menu contract — does not match the footer's text pills, which remain fully reachable via End/Arrow keys, Tab and mouse. Any change should be weighed against the deliberate choice to let a text pill's visible text serve as its accessible name.

title: The file's architecture comment now describes the opposite of what the component renders
reason:
The claimed impact ("the next maintainer builds against a layout that no longer exists") is defeated by the change itself. The same diff added a dedicated, accurate switcher docblock at SyncPathBar.tsx:118-128, sitting directly above the switcher implementation, which explicitly names both things the finding says are undocumented: "the current object as a lifted row, the verbs as the row-end icon cluster in a footer strip, the ways to get more as text pills beside them." On the CSS side the diff added App.css:3155-3158 — "The current object is a lifted row — ink edge, cast shadow, tick — … the verbs are the row-end icon cluster in a footer strip" — immediately ABOVE the line the finding cites as stale. The cited App.css:3161-3162 comment is not "repeated by this change"; it is unchanged context (verbatim at git show HEAD:src/App.css:3079-3080). A maintainer reading top-down hits the correct description first.

The "no radio state" invariant is also not falsified, and is not merely prose: tests/frontend/project-sync-cutover.integration.test.tsx:533-534 gates it with assert.doesNotMatch(bar, /menuitemradio/) plus a pin on role={checkable ? "menuitemcheckbox" : "menuitem"}, and both still pass. The header at line 320 is <div className="sync-path-menu-current" aria-current="true"> with no role and no aria-checked, so no radio/selection semantics were introduced. Checkable items with a trailing tick predate this change entirely (the interface comment at line 35-36 is untouched — the diff starts at @@ -117 — and already reconciles this as "a trailing tick — state, not selection," matching App.css:3138). The header tick expresses "you are here," which is exactly what the docblock's own next clause asserts, so it reinforces rather than contradicts the sentence.

"Verbs beneath it" is also not false: .sync-path-menu-foot renders below the header in both DOM order and on screen; "renders last" still means "beneath." Zero runtime, user-visible, API, or test consequence — this is comment prose on an uncommitted WIP diff that already documents itself in the two places a maintainer touching switcher code would read.
correction: The only defensible residue is much narrower than stated: the module docblock's enumeration ("verbs beneath it, a Switch-to list, and the ways to get more") reads as a top-to-bottom layout order, which now matches only the headerless (⋯) menu — in the switcher the verbs are drawn last in the footer. Read as the authoring contract it describes (unlabelled group first = verbs, labelled groups = switch targets, trailing unlabelled = tails), it is exactly how the partition at lines 167-171 consumes its input, and it is already elaborated by the switcher docblock 100 lines below. A one-clause pointer ("drawn as described under the switcher, below") would be sufficient; the claims that the tick breaks a "no radio state" invariant and that App.css repeats a stale reading do not hold.

title: The file's architecture comment now describes the opposite of what the component renders
reason: Citation is accurate and the core defect reproduces. SyncPathBar.tsx:16-20 matches the quote verbatim and git diff shows the docblock was not touched by this change, while the switcher branch it describes renders in a different order: the labelled switch lists at lines 338-348, then `.sync-path-menu-foot` with caption/verbs/tails at 349-357. `verbs` (line 168, first unlabelled group) is populated by real crumbs (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2387+), so the footer strip genuinely ships and "that object's verbs beneath it, a Switch-to list" states the wrong order. App.css:3161-3162 is cited with correct line numbers, and its stale clause is the one the finding did not quote — "the verbs beneath it inherit its scope by proximity" — directly contradicted by the comment this same change added at App.css:3154-3157 ("the verbs are the row-end icon cluster in a footer strip"). The second half of the finding is wrong, however: the tick at line 325 lives in `<div className="sync-path-menu-current" aria-current="true">`, a div with no role and no aria-checked; menuKeyboard.ts's MENU_OPTION_SELECTOR (`[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]`) does not match it, so it is not a row and not in the roving order, and grep finds no `menuitemradio` anywhere in the bar (checkable items use menuitemcheckbox, already documented at line 35 as "state, not selection"). So "not a checked row" and "no radio state exists anywhere in the bar" both remain true. Documentation-only impact; severity low as claimed.
correction: The module docblock at SyncPathBar.tsx:16-20 states the wrong order for switcher menus: it lists the header's verbs before the Switch-to list, while the shipped switcher renders the lists first (lines 338-348) and the verbs last inside `.sync-path-menu-foot` (lines 349-357). The same staleness is in App.css:3162 — "the verbs beneath it inherit its scope by proximity" — contradicted by the new comment four lines above it at App.css:3154-3157. The docblock's other claims are NOT false: the header tick at line 325 is a decorative Icon inside a role-less `aria-current` div that menuOptions() never selects, so the current object is still the header rather than a checked row, and no radio state (`menuitemradio`) exists anywhere in the bar. Only the parenthetical rationale "position says this is the one you're on" is now incomplete, since the header also carries a tick. Fix is limited to correcting the part order in the docblock and the "by proximity" clause in App.css:3162.

title: The switcher panel has no max-height or scroll and is clipped by #root's overflow:hidden
reason: Independently reproduced. The quoted block is verbatim at src/App.css:3061 and no rule anywhere in App.css (the only stylesheet) gives any sync-path-menu* selector a max-height or overflow — computed values in a live harness on the real CSS are max-height:none, overflow-y:visible. Rendering the actual DOM chain (#root > .sync-app > .sync-workspace > header.sync-pathbar > ol.sync-path > li.sync-path-item > .sync-path-menu.switcher) at the 560px minimum window height: 10 target rows put the footer bottom at 559 (visible by 1px), 11 rows at 593, 20 rows at 899 with the menu 911px tall against a 720px viewport (.sync-app scrollHeight 911 vs clientHeight 720). The switcher renders .sync-path-menu-foot after every list group, and the target lists come from uncapped otherProjects.map / otherStorages.map (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx ~1709, ~2296, ~2427), with matches() showing all items until the user types — so past ~10 targets the footer holding Storage settings…, Unlink…, Rename project…, Reset local sync state…, Link storage… and Add project… is clipped and unreachable by mouse. Confirmed in-diff: git show HEAD:src/App.css has no .sync-path-menu-foot/-verb/-tail/-current/-search, so this footer is new here. Two claims in the write-up are imprecise but do not rescue it: the nearest clipping ancestor is .sync-app { overflow: hidden } (App.css:804-811), not html/body/#root; and focus() DOES rescue keyboard users, because overflow:hidden is programmatically scrollable — focusing the last row scrolled .sync-app from 0 to 350.5 (max 351) and brought the footer into view, at the cost of scrolling the entire app shell off the top with no way to scroll back by mouse. Row-count arithmetic was slightly optimistic (~10 rows at 560, ~14 at 720, not 11/16).
correction: .sync-path-menu (src/App.css:3061) has no max-height and no overflow, and its nearest clipping ancestor is .sync-app { overflow: hidden } (src/App.css:804-811). Because the switcher renders .sync-path-menu-foot after all target list groups, and the target lists are uncapped (otherProjects/otherStorages), the menu grows past the window bottom once the list exceeds ~10 rows at the 560px minimum window height (~14 at the 720px default) — measured: 11 rows put the footer bottom at 593 in a 560px viewport; 20 rows make the menu 846.7px tall with the footer at 866-899 in a 720px viewport. The footer verbs (Storage settings…, Unlink…, Rename project…, Reset local sync state…, Link storage…, Add project…), which now live ONLY in that footer, become unreachable by mouse. Keyboard users are not locked out: .sync-app is programmatically scrollable despite overflow:hidden, so focus() scrolls it (measured scrollTop 0 -> 350.5) and reveals the footer — but this scrolls the entire app shell off the top with no way to scroll back by mouse.

title: The new capture-budget banner counts conversations the Push review filters out of every list
reason: Reproduced independently against the real files. PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:567 contains the quoted comment and capturePendingCount verbatim, and the banner is pushed at :570. The count is reachable: the push context calls build_thread_sync_comparison with build_push_actions=true (service.rs:7470), which at service.rs:6753 runs hold_over_budget_candidates, overwriting push_decision with blocked_conversation_decision(CaptureBudget) — conversation_reconciliation.rs:246-253 sets action=Blocked, selectable=false — on the same review.entries that become comparison.entries. sessionSyncPresentation (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:497-501) then maps local_only/local_ahead + blocked push to status "unavailable", which isPushReviewStatus (only "local-outstanding") rejects, and isPushReviewDecision (pullReviewStatus.ts:13-19) rejects it too. All three push filters therefore exclude the row: ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1545 (sessions), :1596-1601 (olderEntries), PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:437-444 (fallback ResourceInventory). I checked for the escape hatches the finder might have missed and found none: olderInert (:1607, rendered :2069) derives from olderEntries, which already required selectable, so it is provably empty in push mode; pushReviewBlockers keys off entry.state, not the blocked decision; and recommendedPushSelection (:281-296) deletes non-selectable ids, so held rows are neither selected, selectable, nor rendered. The comment's premise ("stay visible and unselectable") is false as claimed.
correction: The banner/empty-state contradiction is conditional, not automatic: selectionReviewEmpty (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1682-1687) also requires activity?.older == null && !canShowLess, so "Nothing to push" appears under the warning banner only when there are no older sessions to load; otherwise the reader sees an empty list under the banner instead. Also, in the common case the base selection and fitted candidates remain selectable, so the banner's "Push the selected conversations first" advice is followable — it is unfollowable only when every candidate is over budget. The defect that holds unconditionally is that a capture_budget row is never rendered in the Push review while the banner counts it.

title: The new capture-budget banner counts conversations the Push review filters out of every list
reason: The claimed user-visible harm does not occur on any realistic path, and the hiding is the codebase's established rule rather than an oversight. (1) The "empty review under a warning banner" case is unreachable: fit_capture_budget_with (service.rs:6463) seeds `spent` from base_selection, and base_selection (service.rs:6632) contains only providers WITHOUT a tail cursor — both shipped adapters return true from supports_tail_cursor (codex/mod.rs:121, claude/mod.rs:260), so base_selection is empty, spent starts at 0, and the newest candidate is always admitted unless one transcript alone exceeds 512 MiB. over_budget > 0 therefore always coexists with selectable rows; the real probe against live state was 280 entries with 67 pushable this round. So "sessions and olderEntries are both empty" never happens, the "Nothing to push" empty state never renders beside the banner, and the advice "push the selected conversations first, then reopen" is exactly followable. (2) Counting rows the list filters out is this component's shipped pattern, not a regression: heldConversationCount (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:512) is built from pushReviewPullHolds, which selects action require_pull / require_pull_metadata (line 163) — rows that also fail isPushReviewDecision (publish|create_cloud only) and render in no push list. heldProjectFileCount is the same. The banner zone's own comment states it is plan-derived, never list-derived. isPushReviewStatus's docstring ("Push review contains only work that can publish from this computer") hides every blocker class (codec_unsupported, missing_binding, busy, unknown_evidence, ambiguous_binding) from the push list; capture_budget is handled identically. (3) The banner contains no row-pointing language: it states a count, the cause, and the remedy, and deliberately carries no action button. What remains is a stale one-line JS comment at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:565-567 that describes the Rust review model (hold_over_budget_candidates does keep the entry in review.entries) rather than the rendered list — a documentation nit with no user-visible consequence, and syncHoldDetail's capture_budget string is unreached in the same way every other push-blocker string already is.
correction: The only accurate residual is a stale comment: PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:565-567 says the over-budget candidates "stay visible and unselectable", but the push review's global isPushReviewDecision filter hides them like every other blocked push row; the comment should say the count stands in for rows the push list intentionally omits, matching the pull-holds banner above it. The claimed contradictory "Nothing to push" empty state is unreachable while every shipped provider supports a tail cursor (base_selection empty, so at least one candidate always fits).

title: The comparison-failure banner offers the destructive local-state reset for transient errors, including an offline storage
reason: The mechanism is real but the consequence is not, and the proposed fix would break the feature. (1) Not one-click destructive: onResetMetadata routes through ProjectSync.tsx:2671-2683, a native Tauri confirm dialog titled "Reset local sync state" that spells out exactly what is forgotten and that "Project files, provider sessions, project setup, recipes, storage configuration, and cloud data will not be deleted." A user hitting a network blip sees the literal storage error as the banner's message and then a dialog before anything happens. (2) Not destructive in the harmful sense: persistence.rs:802-813 documents the reset as forgetting "every derived sync decision ... while retaining its setup and every user-owned byte", idempotent, with recovery effects deliberately left in place; the removed checkpoints/bindings are re-established by first-contact adoption (service.rs:4121-4135, 4324-4331) at the next successful review. Worst case after an ill-advised reset is one recomparison, not data loss and not duplicate publication. (3) "The only exit is the destructive one" is false: PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:419 closes the review on Escape and :709 renders a "Close push review" control; the retry is closing and pressing Push again, which is exactly how the user got here. (4) The proposed fix is demonstrably wrong: isIrrecoverableSyncError only matches strings minted in the Push/Pull APPLY paths — service.rs:9360 ("conversation Push action '{}' is stale at {:?}"), service.rs:10423 (Pull), conversation_materialization.rs:1317, and the RecoveryBlockedCorruption journal phases. None of those can appear in thread_comparison_error, which is either the storage-engine open error or a build_thread_sync_comparison error. Gating the banner on that predicate would make it always false, deleting the repair for the exact case the banner exists for (stale local bases after a storage reset, per the comment at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:577-581) and leaving a genuinely broken review with no exit at all. (5) It is a deliberate design: the banner's own comment states the intent, the backend degrade-per-section behavior is pinned by a dedicated Rust test (service.rs:25135), and the two sites are gated differently because they carry disjoint error vocabularies and different alternatives — the error notice sits beside a live Push button where Retry exists, the banner sits over a review where nothing is selectable.
correction: What survives is a copy/affordance nit, not a safety defect: the comparison-failure banner could add a "Reopen review" retry and word the reset as a repair for stale sync bases, so an offline-storage message does not sit next to a repair button that is irrelevant to it. It must NOT be gated on isIrrecoverableSyncError, whose phrase list cannot match any value thread_comparison_error can take.

title: The comparison-failure banner offers the destructive local-state reset for transient errors, including an offline storage
reason: Reproduced in source. PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:582-593 renders the "comparison-failed" danger banner whose sole action is the ungated "Reset local sync state" button (line 588-591), while the sibling push-error notice twenty lines below (line 835), RestorePlanView.tsx:485, and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:3165-3195 all gate the same button behind isIrrecoverableSyncError and fall back to Retry otherwise. threadComparisonError really does carry transient failures: service.rs:7561-7570 assigns the storage-engine open/inspect_optional error (remote = storage_engine(...).and_then(|(_, engine)| engine.inspect_optional(...)), so a network failure or unreachable bucket) to thread_comparison_error whenever wants_thread_comparison, and ProjectSync.tsx:1836-1869 only gates requires_pull / remote_history_missing / remote_history_replaced before opening the review — "unavailable" opens, per its own comment "Degraded sections such as offline storage or capture failures open without a comparison." onResetMetadata is passed unconditionally at ProjectSync.tsx:3462. I confirmed the rendered output by building PushResourceWorkspace with esbuild and rendering it with threadComparisonError="failed to reach storage 'R2 bucket': network error: connection refused (os error 61)": the markup contains the danger banner and <button type="button" class="btn btn-ghost">Reset local sync state</button>, with no Retry control. Two mitigations the finding omits reduce the severity: the reset is gated by a native Tauri confirm() dialog (ProjectSync.tsx:2679) that spells out the scope and states files, provider sessions, setup, recipes, storage config and cloud data are kept, and what it deletes is derived local sync metadata that re-baselines rather than user data; and the review has a Close, so re-opening Push is an available (undocumented, unsuggested) retry.
correction: The banner at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:588 offers the local-state reset for ANY thread-comparison failure, including transient ones (an offline or unreachable storage reaches it via service.rs:7561-7570), unlike every sibling site that gates the same button behind isIrrecoverableSyncError and otherwise offers Retry. The reset is not one-click: it is confirmed by a native dialog naming its scope, and it discards derived local sync metadata (bases, conversation mappings, checkpoints, materializations, journal ops, saved plans) rather than files or cloud data — recoverable by re-baselining, at the cost of remapping work. The banner offers no retry, though closing and re-opening the review does re-run the comparison, so the destructive action is the only one OFFERED rather than the only exit that exists.

title: The switcher panel has no max-height or scroll and is clipped by #root's overflow:hidden
reason:
I tried to refute this and could not. I built a harness on the real src/App.css (real markup: .sync-path-menu.switcher > current + search + group of one-line .sync-path-menu-item.target rows + .sync-path-menu-foot, inside html/body/#root with overflow:hidden) and measured in a real browser at both configured window sizes.

Measured facts (menu top is pinned at y=57 in both cases; each target row is exactly 34px):
- 1100x720 (tauri.conf.json default): footer fully visible through 14 targets; at 15 targets footTop=679/footBottom=753 — the footer is cut by the window; at 20 it sits entirely at 849-923, wholly off-screen.
- 800x560 (minWidth/minHeight): footer intact through 9 targets; clipped from 10 up.
So the trigger is 15+ other projects at the default size, 10+ at the minimum — not a hypothetical, since the "Switch to" group is `otherProjects` = every project the user has added (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2427-2438).

The impact claim also survives: the footer verbs are not duplicated anywhere. `pathOverflow` is only `appActions` — "the ⋯ is left with exactly what has no crumb of its own — Mallard itself" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2543) — and grepping the whole src tree, "Rename project…" exists at exactly one call site, that footer. Reveal/Agent profile/Reset local sync state have only situational alternates (an error banner, PushResourceWorkspace).

Not already handled and not intentional: `.sync-path-menu-group` has no CSS rule at all, and the sibling dropdown in the same bar, `.sync-history-branch-menu` (App.css:4932), already does exactly what is missing here — `max-height: min(360px, calc(100vh - 130px))` on the panel plus `overflow-y:auto` on `.sync-history-branch-options` (App.css:4972). The codebase's own standard for a path-bar dropdown includes the cap. The reason it was not caught: menu-mockup.html:9 forces `html, body { height:auto !important; overflow:auto !important }`, so the specimen page scrolls and never reproduces #root's clipping.

Novel to this diff: `git diff` shows the switcher (header/search/foot) is new. Before it, the verbs were the first group of a plain list and rendered above the targets — always visible; only the tail of the list was clipped. Moving them into a trailing footer put them below an unbounded list.

Severity is nonetheless overstated at medium. Mitigations exist, and one of the finding's sub-claims is wrong.
correction: Two corrections. (1) The row-fit numbers are slightly optimistic: measured, 9 target rows fit at 560px and 14 at 720px with the footer intact, not "about 11" and "about 16". (2) "Arrow-key focus does not rescue it: focus() finds no scrollable ancestor" is false. `overflow:hidden` still creates a scroll container, and the nearest one is `.sync-app` (App.css:804-810), not #root. Measured: focusing a clipped footer pill scrolls .sync-app by 350px (scrollHeight 911 vs clientHeight 560), bringing the pill on-screen at y=516 and dragging the whole path bar to y=-365. So the footer IS keyboard-reachable; the actual defect there is that the entire app view slides up and the header disappears until the menu closes and focus returns to the crumb. Also, the search field added in this same change (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR=6) is always present in the failing regime and filters the list, so typing anything narrows the group and pulls the footer back into view — an undiscoverable but real escape hatch for mouse users. Corrected statement: at 15+ sibling projects (10+ at the minimum window height) the switcher's footer strip is clipped by .sync-app's overflow:hidden, leaving "Rename project…" — which has no other call site — reachable only by first typing into the filter, and reachable by keyboard only via a focus scroll that slides the whole workspace out from under the header.

title: The new `search` icon is dead code — no production component renders it
reason: Independently reproduced. `git diff src/components/Icons.tsx` confirms both the `| "search"` union member (line 59) and the render branch at line 440 are new and match the quoted text exactly, comment included. `grep -rn '"search"' src/ tests/` returns only those two lines plus `<input type="search">` elements; there is no single-quoted, backticked, or identifier form anywhere in src/. Every dynamic `<Icon name={...}>` call site in SyncPathBar (lines 209, 241, 318, 501, 562, 575) takes `item.icon`/`header.icon`/`crumb.icon`, which are populated from literal maps (viewIcon, STEP_DEFINITIONS, catalogKindMeta) that contain no such literal, so no runtime value can reach the branch. Nothing in src-tauri/ or crates/ emits icon names. No component iterates the IconName union as a gallery. And there is no CSS alternative painting the glyph: `.sync-path-menu-search` at App.css:3186-3205 sets only border/radius/background/color, with no background-image, mask, or ::before. The input at SyncPathBar.tsx:329-336 has no Icon sibling, so the filter field ships bare while menu-mockup.html:179 — the specimen this menu was built from — shows a magnifier in that pill.
correction: The `search` branch is at src/components/Icons.tsx:440 (union member at :59), both newly added in the working tree — citation verbatim. It is genuinely unrendered: no string literal, no computed icon source (viewIcon/STEP_DEFINITIONS/catalogKindMeta all resolve to literals), no test reference, no icon gallery, no CSS background/mask fallback on `.sync-path-menu-search` (App.css:3186-3205). Line-number corrections: the switcher menu's filter input opens at SyncPathBar.tsx:329 (`type="search"` on 330), not 328/329, and it renders only when `searchable` is true — `const searchable = switcher && targetCount >= SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR` (SyncPathBar.tsx:174) — so the glyph-less field appears only in switcher menus at or above the search floor, not in every menu. Supporting evidence the finder omitted: menu-mockup.html:179 (the style-B specimen that shipped) draws a magnifier inside the search pill, so the glyph was drawn for this field and never wired.

title: The new `search` icon is dead code — no production component renders it
reason:
The mechanical claim is true — `src/components/Icons.tsx:440` adds a `"search"` branch (plus union member at line 59) that no production component renders — but it is a documented, deliberate state with no user-visible consequence.

INTENT IS ON RECORD. The switcher-menu design note for this very change (memory doc `switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md`, the 2026-09-01 "IMPLEMENTED" paragraph for the B · Switcher direction that landed in SyncPathBar.tsx) states verbatim: "A pixel-grid `search` glyph was added to Icons.tsx (unused by the input itself yet — the pill is text-only; wire it if a leading glyph is wanted)." That is the exact choice the finding proposes as a "fix", already made and written down.

(b) The "menu's filter field has no glyph" half is a style preference, not a defect: `src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:328-336` is not a "bare" input — it carries `className="sync-path-menu-search"`, `placeholder={`Switch ${label.toLowerCase()}…`}`, `aria-label={`Filter ${label.toLowerCase()} list`}`, value and onChange, and only appears at all when `targetCount >= SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR` (6, line 174). The only accurate reading is "one unused icon branch, intentionally parked, awaiting a design call the author explicitly deferred" — a housekeeping note at most, not a finding worth a maintainer's attention.
correction: If reported at all, it should read: the `search` glyph was drawn for the B · Switcher search pill and deliberately left unwired (the pill ships text-only, per the design note); it is a parked asset, not an accidental omission, and the filter field is already labelled by placeholder and aria-label.

[]` or a falsy check, and onReviewListReadyChange is not passed at the 745-766 call site.

title: A failed comparison is passed as `undefined`, so the review re-runs the whole comparison and can render rows that contradict the banner
reason:
The mechanism is real but the claimed consequences do not hold up.

1) The banner's comment is NOT describing a state the component never produces. `thread_comparison_error` is set in exactly two backend branches (src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:7461-7566): the storage engine failed to open, or `build_thread_sync_comparison` failed. In the dominant cause — the engine could not open (offline storage, bad credentials, storage gone), which is precisely what the ProjectSync.tsx comment names — the embedded page's retry hits the SAME engine and fails the same way, at `load_project_remote_read` (service.rs:6418), before `build_comparison_from_reads` ever captures anything. The page then renders `comparison === null` + its own "Comparison with X failed … Every row below falls back to an unknown status" notice (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1751-1759), i.e. exactly the fallback-status / 0-of-0 state the PushResourceWorkspace comment describes. The same state is on screen while the retry is in flight.

2) The "expensive half measured in seconds" is not paid on the realistic path. The capture (the 4.3s/15.6s cost documented in docs/PERF_SYNC_PATH_MEASUREMENTS.md §3) lives inside `build_comparison_from_reads`, which the offline case never reaches; the only extra work is the bounded local discovery pass, and that is served from `session_watch_service::discovery_for`'s witness cache. The costly retry requires the rarer sub-case where the engine opened but the review-side build failed — and the one known "whole comparison fails" cause (the 512 MiB capture cap) was already converted into a per-entry `capture_budget` blocker, so it no longer produces this error at all.

3) The "rows contradicting the banner" case is both rare and harmless. It needs the Observe run to succeed where the PushPlan run failed (plan save/validate, or a capture of extra candidates). Even then the statuses shown are freshly computed and true, not stale, and the banner's operative claim still holds: selectability comes only from the parent's `selectableConversationIds` (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:660-662, consumed at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1652 and :2065), which is empty, so no checkbox can be re-enabled by the page's internal comparison and nothing unverified can be pushed. The safety invariant is preserved by a different guard, which is the point of the finding's "already handled elsewhere" test.

4) The `?? undefined` is not a recent slip: it is the original shape from the `Promise.allSettled` era (git log -L on the line: 2332556, a960538), the prop type is declared `ThreadSyncComparison | null | undefined` on both sides, and docs/PERF_SYNC_PATH_MEASUREMENTS.md §3a documents the override contract only for the success path, calling that path "well behaved" — no doc or test claims the degraded path must suppress the retry.

Net: on a path the user reaches only when the review is already broken, the app makes one extra invoke that usually fails fast and produces a second, accurate error notice. That is a tidiness nit (passing `null` would avoid re-asking a question that just failed and would avoid the duplicated error copy), not a medium-severity correctness or performance defect.
correction: Precisely stated: when `thread_comparison_error` is set, `comparisonOverride` is `undefined`, so the embedded ProjectActivityPage re-runs its own comparison instead of adopting the failure. In the common (storage-unreachable) case that retry fails fast and merely duplicates the error message; in rare cases where the standalone Observe run succeeds, rows show real — still unselectable — statuses under the failure banner. Cosmetic/tidiness, no correctness or selection-safety impact.

reason: Independently reproduced the mechanism, but the impact is narrower than claimed. Verified: (1) src/components/project-sync/ProjectSync.tsx:1916-1918 match the quoted evidence verbatim, and pendingPush.showProjectFiles is passed straight through at ProjectSync.tsx:3423 to PushResourceWorkspace, which feeds syncReviewSteps (reviewSteps.ts:8) and the footer step navigator (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:877). correction: For a Git-managed project, a failed build_project_files_inventory produces project_files=null, which ProjectSync.tsx:1918 renders identically to a successful-but-empty inventory: the Project files step is dropped and project_files_error (src/types.ts:786) has no reader in src/. (b) `project_content_versions` returning Err on a malformed logical path or a duplicate resource_id in the already-fetched remote manifest (service.rs:2892, 2908) — a corrupt-manifest condition, not realistic data. Notably the one plausible I/O failure inside the builder, an unavailable reviewed base manifest, is deliberately downgraded to a `warnings` entry rather than an Err (service.rs:2612-2628), which is direct evidence the codebase already thought about degradation here and chose not to hide the step for it.

(3) THE STAKE IS NOT WHAT IS CLAIMED. The local content walk is gated on `eligibility.state == Eligible` (service.rs:2644), so a Git-managed inventory contains ONLY storage/base-side entries — leftovers to remove, never local files waiting to be pushed. Mallard refuses to sync files for Git-managed folders by design (docs/PLAN_NON_GIT_PROJECT_FILE_SYNC.md, ProjectFilesLockedNotice, `review_token` is None unless Eligible). "The user pushes sessions believing there was nothing else to review" is wrong: for a Git repo there is nothing pushable to review. Worst case is one deferred cleanup affordance, recovered by reopening Push review.

(4) A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM IS FACTUALLY WRONG. "Its file rows and its Scan button all disappear" — ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:225 sets `eligible = eligibility.state === "eligible"`, and both the Scan button (line 556, `disabled={... || !eligible}`) and the auto-scan effect (line 314, `|| !eligible` early return) refuse for git_managed. A Git-managed project never has a working Scan button, so none is lost.

(5) THE ERROR/EMPTY COLLAPSE IS THE PRE-EXISTING INTENTIONAL SHAPE. `showProjectFiles: !isGitRepository || inventory !== null` already hides the step for the ordinary Git project with zero stored entries; the error case merely joins a state that is deliberately invisible, and it is now logged as a warning in the activity log the app treats as a first-class surface.
correction: Accurate residual (polish, pre-existing, outside this diff): `project_files_error` has no reader in src/. In the narrow case of a Git-managed project whose remote manifest is corrupt (the only path that sets it without also setting thread_comparison_error), the Project files step is hidden with no in-dialog message — indistinguishable from the normal empty case — and the only trace is the activity-log warning added by this same change.

title: The 512 MB capture budget is hardcoded in two user-facing strings and misstates the constant's unit
reason:
Both halves of the finding fail.

(1) The unit claim is affirmatively wrong on this codebase's own terms. src/format.ts:13-22 (`formatBytes`) divides by 1024 at every tier and labels the result "KB"/"MB"/"GB". SettingsPage.tsx:462 converts a "100 MB" dropdown option to `Number(value) * 1024 * 1024` bytes, and THREAD_CAP_OPTIONS_MB / SIZE_OPTIONS_MB / PREVIEW_OPTIONS_KB all follow the same rule. Every byte size this product shows a user is a binary quantity printed with a decimal-looking suffix. So "512 MB" for `512 * 1024 * 1024` is the house convention correctly applied, not a misstatement. The proposed fix ("write 512 MiB") would make this single banner the only IEC-unit string in the entire UI — a user-visible inconsistency introduced to fix a non-problem. The finding's own supporting memory doc uses "MiB" internally, which is engineering register, not the product's user-facing register.

(2) The drift risk is theoretical, not realistic. MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES is a fixed compile-time `pub const` with no user-facing knob: grep shows exactly three Rust references (definition, the enforcement at provider_capture.rs:647, and the service.rs budget-fit call), and it has no accessor in app_settings.rs. The codebase demonstrably plumbs limits end-to-end when they are actually variable — conversation_file_limit_bytes, timeline_message/tool/page preview bytes, and the log-retention cap all live in app_settings.rs, ride the tuning payload, and render through formatBytes on the Settings page. The capture ceiling was deliberately kept out of that set. It can only change when a developer edits one line, and both copy sites contain the literal "512" and are found by a one-second grep. Shipping the ceiling on the comparison payload, as proposed, adds a wire field and a formatter to defend against an edit that has never happened to a constant nobody can tune.

(3) No user-visible consequence exists today. Both strings state the correct enforced figure. A user who actually reaches this banner — a real path, hit on 2026-09-01 with 281 candidate sessions — reads an accurate number. The claimed harm ("two screens quoting a figure the product no longer enforces") requires a hypothetical future edit.

(4) The third leg — that service.rs:6757 "prints the raw byte count instead" — misreads the surface. That string goes into the `warnings` vec (diagnostics / activity log), where an exact byte count is the appropriate register; it is not competing copy for the same audience as the banner.

This is a style preference about duplicated copy, and its concrete recommendation would make the product worse. Not a defect.
correction: If anything survives, it is only the narrowest maintainability note, with the unit claim dropped: the fixed capture ceiling appears as the literal "512 MB" in two copy strings (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:575 and ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1120) rather than one shared frontend constant. The figure is correct as written — the app's own formatBytes and Settings dropdowns use binary divisors with "MB" labels throughout — so it must NOT be rewritten as "512 MiB".

title: The capture_budget hold sentence is unreachable, and is push-worded inside a mode-generic function
reason: No user-visible consequence, and the underlying fact is already surfaced elsewhere. (1) The string never renders, so nothing wrong, misleading, or broken is shown to anyone — this is unreached copy, not defective UI. (2) The user-facing surface for the same condition IS reachable and does render: PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:566-577 filters threadComparison.entries with no isPushReviewDecision gate and emits a warning banner with the identical wording plus a count. A user who hits the 512 MiB budget is told. (4) The finding's supporting evidence is wrong: it claims neighbouring blockers branch on mode, but in the actual switch (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1096-1135) only codec_unsupported does; busy, ambiguous_binding, missing_binding, detached_requires_pull, unknown_evidence and the default are all mode-generic. title: Prompt and reply prose lost its 68ch reading measure; the cap was deleted with `.session-detail-prompt-card` and never re-homed

title: `session-detail-card-prompt` and `session-detail-card-reply` are rendered into production markup but match no CSS rule

title: `session-detail-card-prompt` and `session-detail-card-reply` are rendered into production markup but match no CSS rule
reason:
Not a defect — it is the deliberate, user-picked design, and the modifiers are intentional hooks with zero user-visible consequence.

1) Intent is documented in the shipped code itself. src/App.css:7236 comments the rule: "Both speakers write in the same card: an ink box on the punchcard's 8px corner, whose only chrome is the stamp band. Who is talking is the rail tile's job, so the card carries no name or mark." SessionDetailEvent.tsx:279-282 says the same. The finding reads the deleted "shape is the speaker" comment as evidence of a lost cue, but the replacement doctrine is written in plain text three lines above the CSS rule it inspected.

2) The picked specimen proves the identical paint is intentional, not an unfinished port. <repo>/session-detail-mockup.html carries the same class pair (`.c-card.prompt` / `.c-card.reply`). Line 132 gives prompts a display face — and the SHIPPED flavour `[data-cv="punch"]` explicitly cancels it at line 181 (`.c-card .sd-prose { font-family: var(--font-sans); font-weight: 400; }`), while setting radius 8px (172) and head weight 600 (171), which is exactly what shipped in App.css:7239-7268. Only the unpicked `wash` (188-190) and `quiet` (202) flavours style `.prompt`/`.reply`. The shipped CSS is a faithful port of the chosen flavour, and the two modifier names are the specimen's own hooks carried over for the unpicked flavours.

3) The user asked for this shape. The design-session record for this specimen states the instruction verbatim: "can you have a box for codex's response too?" → in every C flavour both speakers became ink-edged cards, the in-card "You"/"Codex" labels and icons were removed, and "the rail node is the sole speaker marker."

4) The claimed impact overstates the ambiguity. The speaker marker is not a bare 12px glyph: EventNode (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:245-270) renders a 24px bordered tile holding a `user` glyph for prompts versus the provider's own ProviderMark (OpenAI/Claude burst) for replies, with `role="img"`, `aria-label` and `title` of "You · HH:MM" / "Codex · HH:MM" — pinned by session-detail.integration.test.tsx:333-336. The cards also differ in their stamp band in the common case: prompts print clock · duration · calls, replies the clock alone (App.css:7253 comment; test at :341 vs :343). Turns alternate down a rail, so speaker is legible without a card fill.

5) No mechanism for harm. Class names without matching rules are inert: no layout, paint, perf, or a11y effect. They are semantic/test anchors, the standard reason BEM modifiers ship unstyled. Deleting them (the proposed alternative fix) would remove the hook the unpicked flavours need and force rewriting two passing assertions for no user benefit; adding a fill would silently override a design the user chose from a rendered specimen.

The only true residue is a hygiene observation. (Separately noted while verifying, not part of this finding: `.event-prompt` at App.css:7172, which tints the prompt tile with `--session-detail-you`, matches no markup anywhere in src/ — that rule, not the card modifiers, is the actually-dead selector.)
correction: The two modifier classes carry no CSS rules in App.css. That is accurate but consequence-free: they mirror the picked specimen's `.c-card.prompt`/`.c-card.reply` hooks (styled only in the unshipped `wash`/`quiet` flavours) and serve as test anchors. The claim that prompt and reply are visually undifferentiated is wrong in two ways: the 24px rail tile carries a distinct glyph plus an aria-label/tooltip naming the speaker, and prompt cards stamp clock · duration · calls where replies stamp the clock alone.

title: The step box is the only box on the rail still capped at 68ch, so it does not line up with anything

title: The step box is the only box on the rail still capped at 68ch, so it does not line up with anything
reason: Technically accurate but no real consequence.
