title: Every markdown link in session prose renders an invalid `node="[object Object]"` attribute
reason:
The mechanism is real — I reproduced it against the installed packages (react-markdown 10.1.0 sets `passNode: true` at node_modules/react-markdown/lib/index.js:355; hast-util-to-jsx-runtime/lib/index.js:339 attaches `node` to any non-string component type), and rendering the same component shape emits `<a node="[object Object]" href="src/App.css">`. But the finding fails the impact bar, so it should not be reported as a defect.

There is no realistic path on which anyone hits it:
- Rendering/layout/styling: `node` is an unknown attribute; browsers ignore it. I grepped src/App.css and tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx for `[node]`/`node=` selectors — zero hits, so nothing in the cascade keys off it.
- Accessibility: assistive tech ignores unknown attributes. The `a` branch already sets a real `aria-label` for project links (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:178).
- Console: React 19 passes unknown props through without warning. My dev-mode render (NODE_ENV unset) printed no warning at all, so there is no diagnostic noise for a maintainer to trip over.
- Behavior: `href`, `className`, `rel`, and both `onClick` handlers are all written explicitly after the spread; the stray prop changes nothing about link handling.
- Cost: `String(node)` hits Object.prototype.toString and returns a constant — no traversal, no measurable render cost on a page whose expensive work is markdown parsing (documented at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:102-105).

The three claimed harms do not exist in this codebase. This is a Tauri desktop WebView, not a scraped page — nothing scrapes it. "Copied selection of the DOM" does not apply either: the only clipboard path in the app is src/components/sync-review/clipboard.ts, which is `navigator.clipboard.writeText` (plain text, no HTML flavor), and I found no `outerHTML`/`innerHTML` use anywhere in src/. "Invalid HTML in the inspector" is a validator-conformance observation, not a user or maintainer consequence.

It also breaks no existing gate: tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:797 asserts `/href="https:\/\/example\.com\/docs"/` and the image assertions use `[^>]*` spacers, so the extra attribute passes cleanly today and would keep passing.

The one-token fix is harmless and I would not object to it landing opportunistically, but as a review finding it is hygiene, not a defect — no user or maintainer will ever observe it.
correction: The mechanism is accurate; the impact statement is not. Corrected: "The hast `node` prop is spread onto the rendered `<a>`, producing a non-conforming `node="[object Object]"` attribute. It is inert — no CSS selector, assistive-technology behavior, click handling, React warning, clipboard output (the app copies plain text only), or test assertion depends on it. Cosmetic hygiene, no user-visible effect."

title: Every markdown link in session prose renders an invalid `node="[object Object]"` attribute
reason:
Verified in the real source and reproduced against the installed packages. CITATION IS EXACT. /src/components/project-sync/session-detail/SessionDetailEvent.tsx:158 is verbatim `a: ({ href, children, ...props }) => {`, inside the `useMemo` at line 119, and the returned `` is at 172-173. The `img` component at :120 destructures `{ src, alt }` and spreads nothing, as claimed. MECHANISM CONFIRMED. Installed react-markdown is 10.1.0; node_modules/react-markdown/lib/index.js:355 sets `passNode: true`. hast-util-to-jsx-runtime 2.3.6, lib/index.js:339 `addNode()`: `if (typeof type !== 'string' && type !== state.Fragment && state.passNode) props.node = node`. The custom `a` is a function, so it receives the hast Element as `node`; `node` is not destructured, so it lands in `...props` and is spread onto the DOM ``. REPRODUCED. Bundled the actual SessionDetailEvent.tsx with the repo's own esbuild and rendered `SessionDetailMarkdown` (react 19.2.7 / react-dom 19.2.7): input: "See [the file](src/App.css) now.\n\nAnd [ext](https://example.com/x) too." output:

See the file now.

And ext too.

CLIENT PATH TOO, not just SSR. node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js `setValueForAttribute` drops only undefined/function/symbol/non-data-non-aria-boolean; everything else goes through `node.setAttribute(name, "" + value)`. `node` is a safe lowercase attribute name, so React 19 coerces the object and emits it silently — no dev warning. NO GUARD MISSED. Nothing later strips it: `className` and `href` are re-specified after the spread but `node` is untouched, and there is no CSS/DOM cleanup anywhere. All three call sites (lines 315, 354, 489 — prompt/reply cards and intermediate step prose) pass through this same memoized `components` object. PROPOSED FIX IS VALID. `node` is part of react-markdown's `ExtraProps`, so `a: ({ href, children, node: _node, ...props }) =>` type-checks. Impact is cosmetic: an invalid attribute in the DOM/inspector and in copied or scraped markup; no functional, layout, or security effect. "low" is the right severity.
correction: "Every link" is slightly overstated: links whose href fails `safeMarkdownUrl` (line 159-160) and project links reached without an `onOpenProjectPath` handler (line 163) return a bare `{children}` with no prop spread, so those carry no `node` attribute. Every link that actually renders as an `` — external links and openable in-project links, in every prompt, reply, and step body — carries `node="[object Object]"`.

title: The new card's `overflow: hidden` clips the in-project file-path tooltip out of existence
reason: Citation verified verbatim: <repo>/src/App.css:7239-7245 is `.session-detail-card { overflow: hidden; border: var(--box-border); border-radius: 8px; … }`, with `overflow: hidden` on line 7240 exactly as quoted, and the tooltip rule at 7368 (`position: absolute; z-index: 60; bottom: calc(100% + 8px); left: -10px; max-width: min(520px, calc(100vw - 48px))`) with `position: relative` on the link itself at 7363. SessionDetailEvent.tsx:303 and :346 do render `session-detail-card`, and the project link (line 169) is minted inside `.session-detail-event-copy` inside that card, so the tooltip's containing block is inside the clip box. I searched the rest of the file for an escape and found none: no later rule sets `overflow` on `.session-detail-card` (the retro block at 10964 only repaints `background`), and no ancestor (`.session-detail-event`, `.session-detail-event-list`) clips. Regression claim also holds: at HEAD, `.session-detail-prompt-card` (7023) and `.session-detail-response-prose` (7048) carry no `overflow`, and neither does the retro block at 10664. I then measured it live — served a probe using the real App.css and computed the tooltip box from `getComputedStyle(link, '::after')` against the card rect: a first-line link with a wrapping absolute path loses 21.8px of a 53.6px tooltip (41%, first line of the path gone); a reply card rendered without a clock (timestamp is optional, src/types.ts:1159, so `.session-detail-card-head` is absent) loses 46.6px of 53.6px (87%); a link 614px into a 760px card loses 364px of its 520px width at the right border. A forced-visible screenshot shows exactly that. The proposed fix's caveat is also right: the head paints `--surface-subtle` with square corners under an 8px card radius, so dropping `overflow: hidden` does need `.session-detail-card-head` to round its top corners.
correction: The clipping is positional, not total — the finding overstates it. A link below the first text line is unaffected (0px clipped, tooltip overlays the prose above), and a first-line link on a card that has a stamp band with a short single-line path loses only ~5px of a 36.8px tooltip (the top border and a sliver of padding; the path text stays readable). The real damage is in three cases I measured: a first-line link whose path wraps to two lines loses 41% (the first line of the path is cut); a reply card rendered without a clock has no stamp band, so a first-line link loses 87% and the tooltip is unreadable; and any link past roughly the card's left half has its 520px tooltip shaved at the right border (364px cut at a 614px offset in a 760px card). The `aria-label="Open <displayPath>"` on the same anchor still carries the path to assistive tech, so the screen-reader route is not dead — only the visual `:focus-visible` reveal is clipped, identically to hover.

title: Prompt and reply prose lost its 68ch reading measure; the cap was deleted with `.session-detail-prompt-card` and never re-homed
reason: Independently reproduced in source and in a live browser. Citation is verbatim and line numbers are exact: src/App.css:7226 declares `.session-detail-event-copy { max-width: 68ch }` under the comment "Hold prose to a readable 45-75-character measure"; 7239 `.session-detail-card` has no max-width; 7247 `.session-detail-card > .session-detail-event-copy { max-width: none }` overrides it (0,2,0 specificity AND later source order, so it wins unambiguously). `68ch` now appears exactly ONCE in the whole 11k-line file (7227). The modifier classes `.session-detail-card-prompt` / `.session-detail-card-reply` used at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:303 and :346 have zero CSS rules anywhere; the RetroTheme layer at 10964 sets only `background`; no max-width exists on `.session-detail-event-body` (7202), `.session-detail-timeline` (6940), or any ancestor below `.session-detail-page` (6842, max-width 1380px). Live measurement against the real App.css served over localhost, page forced to its 1380px cap: `.session-detail-card` computes `max-width: none` and renders 1342px; the inner `.session-detail-event-copy` computes `max-width: none` and renders 1338px (~1314px content box) = ~152 zero-glyph widths per line. Decisive control: `.session-detail-intermediate-prose` (step notes, NOT a `.session-detail-card` child) still computes `max-width: 556.816px` and renders 550px — the 7226 rule is alive and intended, and only the card path escapes it. Regression against HEAD confirmed: `git show HEAD:src/App.css` line 7023 had `.session-detail-prompt-card { max-width: 68ch }`, and HEAD's SessionDetailEvent.tsx rendered prompts in that card (:302) and responses as bare `.session-detail-event-copy` (:439), so both speakers were capped before the cutover. No guard, fallback, later rule, or call-site condition rescues it. The container query at 7862 relaxes only `.session-detail-event-copy`, which is already `none` inside cards, so it is now a no-op for the card path — the proposed fix correctly notes the card must be re-added there. --type-lg resolves to 0.875rem (7921) against `html { font-size: 100% }` (8198) = 14px, as claimed.
correction: The impact is real but the character estimate is imprecise. Measured at the 1380px page cap: card renders 1342px, prose content box ~1314px, which is ~152 zero-glyph widths per line (the "~170 characters" figure is an unmeasured estimate; proportional lowercase runs somewhat above the digit-width count). Either way it is roughly double the stated 45-75 character measure, and at the 1100px default window it still clears the 75-character bar. Add: the cap survives only on `.session-detail-intermediate-prose` step notes, so the page is now internally inconsistent — narrow step notes beside full-bleed prompt and reply prose.

title: The new card's `overflow: hidden` clips the in-project file-path tooltip out of existence
reason:
I could not refute the mechanism: `.session-detail-card` at src/App.css:7240 really does set `overflow: hidden`, HEAD's `.session-detail-prompt-card` (7023) and `.session-detail-response-prose` (7048) set no clipping, and `.session-detail-project-link[data-tooltip]::after` is an abspos whose containing block (the link, `position: relative`) sits inside the new clip box — so the clip is a genuine regression, not a style preference. I verified it empirically: served a harness page against the real App.css, rendered `.session-detail-card > .session-detail-event-copy` with a `session-detail-project-link`, forced the `::after` visible and screenshotted. A link on the card's first body line (link top = card top + 40px) with a real absolute display path yields a 520x54px two-line tooltip of which the top 22px is cut — the first line of the path is gone from the painted box while the second line stays readable. So there is a real, reproducible user-visible loss, and I cannot honestly call it theoretical.

But the impact as written is inflated on four counts, which is why I drop the severity from high to low:

1. "No longer shows the resolved absolute path" / "most or all of the ~40px tooltip is cut away" is wrong. Measured on a 1100px viewport: first-line prompt-card link = 22px clipped of 54px (41%), the box still appears and its lower line is legible. The claimed ~40px tooltip height is also wrong — `overflow-wrap: anywhere` feeds into max-content sizing, so real paths render as a 520px two-line box, not a one-liner.

2. It is confined to the top of a card. Measured link at card top +96px: clipTop = 0. Link at +153px: clipTop = 0. Every link past roughly the second body line is completely unaffected, which is most links in a multi-paragraph message.

3. The "~12px on a reply card with no timestamp band" case (30px of 37px clipped, i.e. the near-total loss the title leans on) requires an event with `event.timestamp == null` — SessionDetailEvent.tsx:347 renders the stamp band whenever a clock exists, so that is the rare path, not the common one.

4. "The keyboard route to the path is dead too" overstates it: the same partial clip applies, and the anchor still carries `aria-label={`Open ${displayPath}`}` (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:178), so assistive tech still gets the full path. The primary affordance — click to open the file via `onOpenProjectPath` — is untouched, and the link text in Claude transcripts is normally the file name itself.

I also could not confirm the horizontal half of the claim. My right-edge probe measured clipRight = 0 because the tooltip is left-anchored at `left: -10px` and the link had wrapped to the start of a line; a link genuinely sitting in the right half of an 820px card would overflow, but the finding presents that as observed when it is not.

One correction that matters to whoever fixes this: the proposed primary fix (delete `overflow: hidden`) is not free. The rule is load-bearing for the punchcard design — `.session-detail-card-head` (7253) paints `background: var(--surface-subtle)` with square corners and relies on the card's clip to sit inside the 8px radius. The finding's own fallback (round the head instead) is the correct fix; the headline fix would regress the shipped card corners.
correction: `.session-detail-card`'s new `overflow: hidden` (src/App.css:7240) clips the top of the `.session-detail-project-link` tooltip for links in roughly the first two lines of a card: measured, a first-line link on a prompt card loses 22px of a 520x54px two-line tooltip, hiding the leading segments of the path while the rest stays readable. Links deeper in the body are not clipped at all (clipTop = 0 at +96px and +153px from the card top), the click-to-open action and the `aria-label` path are unaffected, and the near-total clip described applies only to a reply card rendered without a timestamp band. Fix by rounding `.session-detail-card-head`'s top corners rather than dropping `overflow: hidden`, which the stamp band depends on.

title: A lower-bound tool count prints in the singular: "1+ call"
reason:
The code is as quoted (src/components/project-sync/session-detail/SessionDetailEvent.tsx:309, formatSessionCount at sessionDetailModel.ts:178-182, tool_quality wired through claude/history.rs:668-703 and codex/history.rs:1033-1068), and yes, a degraded session whose turn has one indexed call renders "1+ call". But the load-bearing claim of the finding — that this "reads as an exact count of one" — is false, and with it the impact.

1. The lower-bound signal is printed and is not the noun. "1+" cannot be read as exactly one; the "+" is right there and it is this app's established lower-bound glyph, used identically for the header token chip (SessionDetailHeader.tsx:84-87, formatCompactCount). Pluralising the noun adds nothing a reader is missing; the fact is already on screen.

2. The partialness is surfaced elsewhere, more loudly. On a degraded session the header prints the token count inside `<code class="quality-lower_bound">` (amber, App.css:7028) with `detail.tokens.explanation` as its tooltip; the toolbar filter counts carry an "At least N" title (SessionDetailToolbar.tsx:49, sessionCountQualityLabel); events wear a "Partial" chip with a visually-hidden explanation (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:212-228). No user learns "this count is a floor" from the plural of "call".

3. The card head is deliberately quality-agnostic. The stamp band is documented as "clock · duration · calls" (comment at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:280-284, the C2 Punchcard design shipped in 722ebf1); unlike the header and toolbar it applies no quality class and no tooltip at all. Agreement with the known value is the shipped rule, and it is pinned by an existing test — session-detail.integration.test.tsx:405-410, "A single loaded call still pluralises honestly", asserting `1 call`. One loaded call in a truncated transcript is still one loaded call; the "+" carries "there may be more". The current output is consistent with that stated intent rather than a violation of it.

4. Every other pairing of a count with a noun in this feature uses a fixed plural ("tokens") or no noun at all, so there is no cross-surface inconsistency to fix here either — this is the only site that inflects.

What is left is a one-word English-usage preference ("1+ calls" is more idiomatic than "1+ call") on a card in an already-degraded rendering, where no number is wrong and no fact is hidden. That is style, not a defect; the claimed misreading does not occur.
correction: If reported at all, the accurate statement is narrower: "In a degraded session (degraded_all/degraded_tools), a turn with one indexed call renders '1+ call'; '1+ calls' would be the more idiomatic phrasing." The count, the '+' and the lower-bound meaning are all correct as rendered — nothing reads as an exact count of one. Note also that the proposed fix would break the pinned test's intent only if applied carelessly: `quality === "inferred"` with value 1 would start printing "1 calls".

title: Tool calls now default off, so a turn whose last event is a tool call loses its duration stamp
reason:
Refuted on three independent grounds: intent, pre-existing contract, and negligible impact.

(1) DELIBERATE. `toolCalls: false` is not an oversight. The same diff rewrites the function's doc comment from "Tool calls default on: the punchcard rows are the transcript's account of the work" to "The conversation is what opens by default: prompts and replies. Steps and tool calls… stay behind SHOW › Steps and SHOW › Tool calls until asked for, so a long session reads as an exchange first and a log second." The change is pinned by a test written in the same change (tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:185-197): `assert.deepEqual(includedSessionEventKinds(filters), ["prompt","response","checkpoint"])`, `assert.equal(filters.toolCalls, false)`, under the comment "the punchcard rows — steps and tool calls — wait behind their SHOW toggles until asked for." The filter drives the *server query* (`included_event_kinds` on the paged timeline command, page size 50), so this is a load-budget decision as much as a visual one.

(2) NOT A REGRESSION IN CONTRACT. Turn duration has always been an optional stamp measured over the loaded page, and both doc comments saying so are present unchanged at HEAD: SessionDetailEvent.tsx:26 "This event's turn duration, shown on prompt cards once a later event of the turn has loaded", and sessionDetailModel.ts:295-298 "Spans grow as pages load; a turn whose only loaded event is the prompt has no extent yet and yields no duration — measured, never promised." The same absent-stamp state is already reachable at HEAD by (a) the 50-event page boundary splitting a turn, (b) `intermediateSteps: false`, which was ALREADY the default at HEAD — a turn of prompt + steps only already printed no duration — and (c) the user simply unchecking Tool calls, a one-click labelled toggle that prints the kind's count beside it. The finding therefore describes a pre-existing, documented, user-reachable state, not a new defect.

(3) NO REAL DEGRADATION. The scenario requires an interrupted turn: prompt, then tool calls, and no response/checkpoint at all. On such a turn the old number measured "prompt until the interruption", which is not a turn duration in any meaningful sense. What remains on the card is clock + "N calls" — and that count comes from `event.turn_tool_summary`, computed server-side per turn and attached to the turn's leading NON-tool-call event (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/providers/claude/history.rs:686-700). It is filter-independent by construction: it is precisely the summary designed to stand in for rows that are not loaded, so "points at rows that are not on screen" describes the feature working, not failing. The claim that the card "degrades to a bare clock, indistinguishable from a reply card's" is factually wrong: the prompt card keeps its calls chip, its `.session-detail-card-prompt` class, and its rail `EventNode` (ReplyCard, SessionDetailEvent.tsx:345-352, renders a clock and nothing else in `.session-detail-card-reply`). Session-level start and length are unaffected — they are header fact chips read from `detail` (SessionDetailHeader.tsx:70-83), never from the filtered page.

The proposed fix is also contrary to intent: keeping `toolCalls: true` "for the span computation" would re-request every tool call from the backend and spend the 50-event page budget on rows the change deliberately stopped loading, reintroducing the exact cost the default was changed to avoid.
correction: If anything survives, it is a cosmetic nicety, not a defect: on an interrupted turn (prompt followed only by tool calls, no response) the prompt card's optional duration stamp is now absent by default, as it already was for prompt+steps-only turns at HEAD and as the "measured, never promised" contract states. The card still shows the clock and the filter-independent per-turn call count, and the session's own start/length chips are unaffected.

title: A lower-bound tool count prints in the singular: "1+ call"
reason: Independently reproduced. The citation is exact: SessionDetailEvent.tsx:309 contains the quoted line verbatim, and sessionDetailModel.ts:181 appends "+" for lower_bound as claimed. The full chain holds: claude/history.rs:668-672 and codex/history.rs:1033-1037 compute one session-wide tool_quality = LowerBound whenever degraded_all || degraded_tools, and pass it straight into each per-turn tool_calls count (claude:696, codex:1062 — both line numbers correct); claude_count (:727) passes quality through untouched. mark_tools_lower_bound / mark_all_lower_bound have ~15 real call sites, so the degraded state is live, not dead code. tools_by_turn counts ToolCall events per turn, so a turn with one surviving call gives value:1 with quality LowerBound. I specifically checked the likeliest missed guard — the validation layer at session_detail.rs:520 and :581 — and it only validates summary.tool_calls.value against the de-duplicated call count and the turn-id pairing; quality is never inspected or rewritten. The page mapper (claude/history.rs:1564-1579, above the #[cfg(test)] boundary at :1627; codex:2506-2521) clones the summary through unchanged and deliberately attaches it to a non-ToolCall event, i.e. the prompt. speakableCount (:274) filters only null values and "unsupported", so lower_bound passes; serde(rename_all = "snake_case") on SessionCountQuality (traits.rs:186) makes the wire literal "lower_bound", matching the TS union in types.ts:1067. PromptCard renders on event.kind === "prompt" (:469), exactly where the summary lands. Running the real logic confirms the render: {value:1, quality:"lower_bound"} produces "1+ call" while value 2 produces "2+ calls". Severity low is right — a copy defect confined to truncated/degraded transcripts on turns with exactly one known tool call.
correction: The finding stands as stated, but its proposed fix is wrong in one respect. Gating on `callCount.quality === "exact"` would regress the "inferred" case: formatSessionCount prints a bare "1" for inferred (no "+"), so that branch would render the ungrammatical "1 calls". Pluralise on the same fact that adds the "+": `callCount.value === 1 && callCount.quality !== "lower_bound" ? "call" : "calls"`. (Latent today — tool_quality is only ever Exact or LowerBound in both providers — but it keeps the plural tied to the rendered string rather than to a whitelist of qualities.)

title: Event anchors, `tabIndex={-1}` and the event focus ring are plumbing nothing reaches
reason: Reproduced from source. SessionDetailEvent.tsx:439-445 matches the quoted evidence verbatim (id at 440, tabIndex at 444). A repo-wide grep for the literal "session-event-" (excluding node_modules/.git/target/dist) returns exactly ONE hit — the template inside eventAnchorId at sessionDetailModel.ts:232 — so no code, markup, doc, or fixture anywhere ever names such an id. eventAnchorId has four call sites: definition, import, the JSX at 440, and tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:326, which only asserts the id is present in the rendered HTML. There is no scrollIntoView call anywhere in src/, no location.hash use, and the only getElementById calls are document.getElementById("root") in main.tsx and mockup entry points. SessionDetailPage's props are localProjectId, projectRoot, resourceId, occurrenceKey, onHeaderChange — no target-event parameter — and its only programmatic focus is headingRef.current?.focus() at line 197, which targets the visually-hidden h1#session-detail-heading in SessionDetailHeader.tsx, not an event. data-event-id has no reader either. git blame shows the id/tabIndex pair landed in 96e1e41 (2026-08-09) and was never wired. The finding's two imprecisions do not change the verdict: the CSS lines are 7147/7150 rather than 7157/7161, and scroll-margin is not provably unreachable (a click focuses a checkpoint article via tabindex=-1, and focus-triggered scroll-into-view does honor scroll-margin), but the focus ring genuinely cannot appear since :focus-visible does not match pointer focus on a generic container.
correction: Corrected line numbers: the CSS rules are at src/App.css:7147 (scroll-margin: 80px 0) and src/App.css:7150 (.session-detail-event:focus-visible), not 7157/7161. Corrected behavior claim: the :focus-visible ring is genuinely unreachable (nothing focuses the article programmatically, and pointer focus on a tabindex=-1 container does not match :focus-visible), but scroll-margin is not strictly inert — clicking a checkpoint focuses it via tabindex=-1, and the browser's focus-triggered scroll-into-view honors scroll-margin, so a checkpoint clicked within 80px of the scrollport edge can shift the list. Deleting the plumbing also requires updating the id assertion at tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:326.

title: Portalled role="dialog" popovers never take focus and close on focus-out, so their controls are keyboard-unreachable
reason: The citation is accurate but the behavioral claim is wrong. The finder read only the trigger's onClick and concluded "opening moves no focus"; the focus move lives in the shared hook these popovers all use. src/components/sync-review/debugPopoverPlacement.ts:99-104 runs `useEffect(() => { if (!open || !placement) return; panelRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>("button:not([disabled])")?.focus(); }, [open, panelRef, placement])` — its doc comment says "Once placed, the first enabled action receives focus." Real sequence on open: setOpen(true) renders the panel with hidden=false, the useLayoutEffect measures and calls setPlacement, the re-render replaces the `visibility: hidden` style with real top/left/width/maxHeight, then the passive effect focuses the first Copy button. The focusin that fires has event.target inside panelRef, so `inside()` is true and closeMenu() is NOT called; Tab from there walks the remaining Copy buttons and Copy all inside the panel. All three cited sites use this same hook — ProjectFileDetailsMenu.tsx:44, ProjectActivityPage.tsx:817, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:215 — so the proposed fix is already implemented in the one shared place. A pinned source gate at tests/frontend/project-activity.integration.test.tsx:1439-1442 asserts that exact focus() call, and a loop at :1450-1459 asserts the shared hook plus `panelRef.current?.contains(target)` across all three pages. The controls are therefore keyboard-reachable, the role="dialog" announcement does place the user inside, and Escape's closeMenu(true) restores focus to the trigger. Tab-out dismissal is ordinary non-modal popover behavior, not the claimed defect.
correction: At most a residual nit, not the reported defect: these role="dialog" popovers are non-modal (no aria-modal, no focus trap, Tab off the last control leaves and dismisses). That is a defensible pattern for an info popover, and focus is placed inside on open and restored to the trigger on Escape.

title: Event anchors, `tabIndex={-1}` and the event focus ring are plumbing nothing reaches
reason: Refuted on three grounds. (1) Deliberate, documented design: docs/PLAN_PROVIDER_NEUTRAL_SESSION_DETAIL.md §4.4 ("Selecting a checkpoint") specifies exactly this quartet — "scrolls the workspace's single scroll root to the stable event anchor" and "moves programmatic focus to the checkpoint heading without trapping focus". tabIndex={-1} is the canonical idiom for focusable-but-not-tabbable; scroll-margin: 80px offsets the fixed path bar; the :focus-visible ring matches a codebase-wide convention (62 such rules in App.css). §4.3 repeats the intent. This is spec'd scaffolding, not accidental plumbing. (2) The evidence's central claim is factually wrong: the grep was scoped to src/ only. tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:17 imports eventAnchorId and :326 asserts `id="${eventAnchorId("tool-1")}"` is rendered. The anchor is a test-pinned contract, which inverts the claimed impact — a maintainer will not keep it alive by mistaken assumption; a green gate holds it on purpose, and the proposed deletion breaks that test. (3) Already triaged: docs/BACKEND_OVERENGINEERING_AUDIT_2026-08-21.md D2 catalogs the sibling backend anchor_event_id plumbing as known P2 speculative plumbing with the UI mode deliberately deferred. Consequence check: an unused id attribute, an unused tabindex="-1", and two CSS rules that never paint — no wrong pixel, no wrong data, no perf cost, no keyboard or screen-reader regression (the checkpoint's <a> sha link at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:384 stays tabbable). No user or maintainer reaches this on any realistic path at any window size. The only true observation is that the checkpoint-selection entry point is not yet built in SessionDetailPage.tsx, which makes this an unfinished spec'd feature rather than dead UI — the correct response is finishing the plan's step 4, not deleting the scaffolding the plan names.
correction: Precise statement: the checkpoint-selection flow specified in docs/PLAN_PROVIDER_NEUTRAL_SESSION_DETAIL.md §4.4 is not yet wired in SessionDetailPage.tsx, so its DOM scaffolding (stable event anchor id, checkpoint tabIndex={-1}, scroll-margin, :focus-visible ring) is currently dormant. It is not unread — tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:326 asserts the anchor id — and it should not be deleted; the gap is the missing entry point, tracked alongside BACKEND_OVERENGINEERING_AUDIT_2026-08-21.md D2.

title: Portalled role="dialog" popovers never take focus and close on focus-out, so their controls are keyboard-unreachable
reason: Factually wrong: the claimed missing behavior is already implemented, in the shared hook all three popovers use. src/components/sync-review/debugPopoverPlacement.ts:99-104 contains `useEffect(() => { if (!open || !placement) return; panelRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>("button:not([disabled])")?.focus(); }, [open, panelRef, placement])`, and the hook's docstring states the intent explicitly: "Once placed, the first enabled action receives focus." All three sites the finding names call it with the same panelRef bound to the portalled role="dialog" div — ProjectFileDetailsMenu.tsx:44, ProjectActivityPage.tsx:817, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:215. The open sequence is therefore: click -> setOpen(true) -> useLayoutEffect measures and sets placement (pre-paint, so the panel is neither `hidden` nor `visibility:hidden` by then) -> passive effect focuses the panel's first Copy button. That button satisfies `panelRef.current?.contains(target)` in the components' own `inside()` predicate, so the document `focusin` listener sees it as inside and does NOT close the panel; the components even carry a comment at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:865-866 explaining that panelRef must count as inside precisely because the panel is portalled. From there Tab walks the panel's own Copy buttons, which are contiguous in the DOM at the end of document.body, and Escape closes with `closeMenu(true)` restoring focus to the trigger. The claimed impact — "Every Copy / Copy all button inside is therefore reachable by mouse only" and "a screen-reader user is never placed inside" — does not occur on any realistic path. The finding was evidently written from the JSX and the onClick handler alone without following useDebugPopoverPlacement, the same hook whose returned `placement` value it quotes in its own evidence block. The only residue is a style-level quibble (role="dialog" on a non-modal popover with no aria-modal and no focus trap, and tab-out-closes as dismissal), which is a conventional non-modal popover pattern here, not a defect.
correction: No correction preserves the finding: the focus-on-open behavior it asks for already ships in src/components/sync-review/debugPopoverPlacement.ts:99-104 for all three popovers. At most, a low-severity note remains that role="dialog" is a heavy role for a non-modal, tab-out-dismissed info popover.

title: Tool calls now default off, so a turn whose last event is a tool call loses its duration stamp
reason: Citation is verbatim and the line number is exact: sessionDetailModel.ts:94 reads `toolCalls: false,` in createDefaultSessionDetailFilters, and `git diff HEAD` shows the single behavioral change `toolCalls: sessionCountSupported(counts.tool_calls)` -> `toolCalls: false` (intermediateSteps was already false at HEAD, so tool calls were the only work-rows the old default loaded). The chain reproduces in source: SessionDetailPage.tsx:111/145 seeds `filters` solely from createDefaultSessionDetailFilters with no persistence or override; SessionDetailPage.tsx:229 sends `included_event_kinds: includedSessionEventKinds(activeFilters)`, and includedSessionEventKinds (model:162-172) pushes "tool_call" only when filters.toolCalls is true; the backend enforces the exclusion rather than leaking extras (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/session_detail.rs:1514 rejects the page if an event's kind is not in included_event_kinds). SessionDetailTimeline.tsx:58 computes sessionTurnSpans(events) over exactly that loaded array, sessionTurnDurationLabel (model:316-319) returns null when span.ended <= span.started, and SessionDetailTimeline.tsx:135-138 passes it to PromptCard, whose head (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:303-311) then prints the clock alone. The affected turn shape is real for Claude: providers/claude/history.rs:571-598 classifies an assistant group with tool use as IntermediateStep (also off) and drops empty-text groups entirely, so a turn interrupted mid-tool-use has no Response event; tool calls carry a timestamp and share the prompt's turn id (add_prompt sets current_turn_id = claude:turn:{uuid}; add_tool stores it, history.rs:382/1097/525), so they were exactly the extent that used to yield the duration. sessionTurnDurationLabel has only that one call site — no guard, fallback, or server-side turn duration exists.
correction: Accurate on the mechanism, overstated on two secondary points. (1) Only the stamp band degrades to a bare clock; the cards themselves remain distinguishable via `session-detail-card-prompt` vs `session-detail-card-reply` and the rail node's speaker glyph (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:346). (2) The "N calls" chip is not newly broken by this change: it reads the server-computed `event.turn_tool_summary` (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:300), attached to the turn's leading non-tool event in history.rs:672-690, so it is filter-independent by design and summarizing off-screen rows is its purpose. Corrected statement: with tool calls now off by default, a turn that records no `response` event (Claude interrupts mid-tool-use, where the trailing assistant groups become hidden intermediate_step rows or are dropped for empty text) loads only its prompt, so sessionTurnSpans yields a zero-width span and the prompt card's duration chip disappears where the previous default printed the real elapsed time. No wrong value is shown, and sessionTurnSpans' own contract already declares duration to be measured from loaded extent ("measured, never promised").

title: All five role="radiogroup" widgets omit roving tabindex and arrow-key selection
reason: Reproduced in source. The quoted evidence at src/components/project-sync/SettingsPage.tsx:391 matches verbatim, and all four secondary citations are exact: StorageSettings.tsx:230 ("Storage type"), AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:228 ("Resource kind"), BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:123 ("Available remote repos"), ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:905 ("Repo identity for this project"). Each is a role="radiogroup" container whose children are <button type="button" role="radio" aria-checked={...} onClick={...}>. The grep claim holds: ArrowRight|ArrowLeft|ArrowUp|ArrowDown|tabIndex|onKeyDown|onKeyUp|roving returns zero hits across all five files. No shared roving-tabindex helper exists anywhere in src/, and none of the eleven document/window keydown listeners in the tree handles radiogroups (they are Escape-close handlers, a sidebar-width shortcut, and activity-page handlers). Decisively, the codebase implements this exact pattern elsewhere: src/components/sync-review/SyncReviewTabs.tsx uses tabIndex={active ? 0 : -1} (line 78) and onKeyDown={handleKeyDown} (line 82) with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End wrapping plus a requestAnimationFrame focus move for its role="tablist" — so the pattern is known in-repo and simply absent from every radiogroup. No guard, fallback, wrapper, or call-site condition compensates. Two claims in the finding are inaccurate but not fatal, addressed in the correction: the severity is overstated, and the "only way to set theme" assertion is false.
correction: All five role="radiogroup" widgets (SettingsPage.tsx:391, StorageSettings.tsx:230, AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:228, BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:123, ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:905) omit roving tabindex and arrow-key selection, breaking the keyboard contract the radio role advertises. Two corrections to the finding as written. (1) Severity is medium, not high: every radio is a native <button type="button"> with an onClick, so it sits in the tab order at default tabIndex 0 and Enter/Space fire the handler. No option is unreachable or unsettable by a keyboard-only user, so WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard is satisfied; the real failure is 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — the announced radio role promises arrow-key selection the widget does not deliver — plus tab-order bloat (n stops per group instead of 1). Nothing is blocked, so this is a role-contract and efficiency defect rather than a functional barrier. (2) The claim "This is the only way to set theme" is wrong: ProjectSync.tsx:2758 renders a titlebar theme toggle, a plain correctly-labeled button with aria-label="Switch to {light|dark} theme", reachable from any screen. Only the "System" choice is exclusive to the SettingsPage radiogroup. The proposed fix is otherwise sound, and SyncReviewTabs.tsx:78-82 already supplies an in-repo reference implementation of the roving-tabindex handler to copy.

title: Sidebar exposes no aria-current for the active destination or the open project/Catalog/storage row
reason:
Refuted on novelty and impact, not on code facts (the aria-current absence is real).

(1) ZERO NOVELTY — already documented and deliberately deferred. This is a re-report of finding M05 in <repo>/docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md, which cites the same component at ProjectSidebar.tsx#L698 (the <nav> open tag two lines above the quoted button), states the same claim nearly verbatim ("Persistent sidebar destinations and selected project, Catalog, and storage rows use CSS only and do not expose `aria-current`"), and prescribes the same repair ("Apply `aria-current` to the persistent sidebar destination and selected object"). title: All five role="radiogroup" widgets omit roving tabindex and arrow-key selection
reason:
The markup is exactly as quoted at all five sites (SettingsPage.tsx:391, StorageSettings.tsx:230, AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:228, BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:123, ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:905), and none of the five files contains onKeyDown/tabIndex. But the claimed impact does not hold.

1. Every one of these controls is keyboard-operable today. They are native `<button type="button">` elements, so Tab reaches each and Space/Enter fire onClick. WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard, Level A) is satisfied — no task is blocked. The claim that an AT user is "left guessing that Space/Enter is the substitute" inverts reality: Space is the same key a user presses to select a native radio, so the primary muscle-memory key works unchanged. Only the Arrow shortcut is inert.

2. Roving tabindex + arrow selection is an ARIA Authoring Practices Guide *pattern*, not a normative requirement. No WCAG 2.1 A or AA success criterion mandates arrow-key navigation inside a composite widget. The criterion that does apply, 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value, is fully met here: group role + aria-label, per-option role=radio, correct aria-checked that flips on selection, and an accessible name from the visible label. So this is an APG-conformance polish item, not an accessibility failure.

3. The extra-Tab-stops cost is negligible at real sizes: Theme = 3 options, Storage type = 2, Catalog kind = 4 (CATALOG_KINDS in storage-catalog/model.ts), Repo identity = 1 + typically 1-2 remote bundles, BundleConnectionDialog = the match list the user opened the dialog specifically to pick from. Nobody tabs past a long roster. In the two card-shaped lists a Tab stop per option is arguably better than roving focus, since each option carries multi-line content (display name, bundle id, revision, resource count, relative time) an AT user wants read.

4. It is a deliberate house pattern, not an oversight. The identical `<button role="radio">` + `.sync-bundle-radio` construction is repeated across five components with matching CSS classes, docs/PLAN_STORAGE_SCOPED_CODEX_CLAUDE_CATALOG.md:1051 refers to reusing "the current row-local radiogroup", and tests/frontend/settings-page.integration.test.tsx:45-46 pins the `role="radiogroup" aria-label="Theme"` and `<button role="radio" aria-checked="true">` markup by source text. The proposed primary fix (native `<input type="radio">` in a `<fieldset><legend>`) would break that pinned gate and require re-doing five widgets' card layouts — icon slot, bold title, description line, right-hand meta column — for a shortcut key.

5. Platform context further deflates it: this is a Tauri desktop app, so the real AT surface is VoiceOver in WKWebView, where navigation is VO+arrow and activation is VO+Space regardless of page-level roving tabindex.

Also, the "only way to set theme" framing overstates the stakes — the shipped default is System, which follows macOS, so a user who never touches that segment still gets the correct appearance.
correction: Accurate restatement: the five radiogroups implement the ARIA radio *roles and states* correctly but not the APG keyboard *pattern* — Arrow/Home/End do nothing and each option is its own Tab stop instead of the group being one. All options remain reachable by Tab and selectable with Space/Enter (native button behavior), so no task is blocked and WCAG 2.1 A/AA is met. This is a keyboard-efficiency and APG-conformance polish item on a deliberate, test-pinned house pattern, best addressed with a shared roving-tabindex hook if picked up at all — not the "high" severity claimed.

title: Four main views have no h1; their first heading is an h2 (or there is no heading at all)
reason:
The structural facts check out, but the claimed impact does not survive contact with the code, and the item is neither novel nor a defect.

1. Page identity is already exposed programmatically on every view named. SettingsPage.tsx:384 `<section className="profile-links-section" aria-label="Settings">`; StorageIndexPage.tsx:101 `aria-label="Storages"`; CatalogIndexPage `aria-label="Catalog resources"`; StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1969 `aria-label={label}` (the scope label); and the project workspace's `<main>` at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2741 carries `aria-label={projectLabel(workspaceProject)}` — the project name, on the landmark itself. The proposed hidden h1 would duplicate a string the landmark already announces. On top of that, SyncPathBar renders a `<header>` containing `<ol aria-label="Settings path" | "Storages path" | …>` whose leaf crumb carries `aria-current="page"` on all three crumb branches (lines 488, 537, 571). A screen-reader user reaching any of these views hears the page name on entry and can reach it with one landmark keystroke (VO rotor / D). "The heading list gives no page identity" is true; "the page has no identity" is not.

2. No WCAG criterion is failed. There is no A/AA success criterion requiring an h1 or requiring the first heading to be h1. axe's `page-has-heading-one` and `heading-order` are both tagged best-practice, not wcag2a/aa. This is a polish item, not a conformance defect, and the finding is filed as if it were the latter.

3. The "lands nowhere" claim is overstated. Four of the five surfaces do have headings (SettingsPage h2 groups, StorageCatalogPage h2s at 1978+, ProjectActivityPage h2s at 1876/1895/2007/2021) — H navigation lands on them and works. Only StorageIndexPage and CatalogIndexPage have zero headings, and those are flat single-list index screens: one labelled region containing one list of buttons. There is nothing for heading navigation to move *between* there, so a heading would add a landing pad, not navigation.

4. It is a deliberate decision of this codebase, pinned by a test. tests/frontend/project-activity.integration.test.tsx:1152-1154 asserts the activity page does NOT print the storage alias, with the comment: "The alias is the path bar's to say. The list used to print it again as an `<h1>` directly under the crumb that already carried it." An h1 naming the page was removed from the activity page on purpose and locked with `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /Mallard local/)`. The doctrine — the bar owns the title, identity lives in the crumb — is consistent across the app. The one counter-example the finding cites as precedent, SessionDetailHeader.tsx:47, is not a page-identity convention: that h1 carries `tabIndex={-1}` and a `headingRef`, i.e. it exists as a focus anchor for focus-on-navigation, a different job.

5. Zero novelty. This is already written up in the repo's own audit as M05, committed in f2cdac4: docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md:184-188 — "Settings, Storages, Catalog list, and Catalog reviews do not have a page-level `h1`… Repair: Give each main view one `h1`, visible or visually hidden" — with the same file-and-line evidence (SettingsPage.tsx#L372, StorageIndexPage.tsx#L43, StorageCatalogPage.tsx) and the same proposed fix, down to the wording. Line 431 repeats it for Settings. The maintainers triaged it to step 6 of an 8-step repair order. Re-reporting a two-day-old tracked audit item as a new medium finding adds nothing.

Realistic-path check: this is a single-window Tauri app whose AT pairing is VoiceOver over WKWebView. The browse-mode quick-key model the impact statement leans on ("pressing H or 1") is an NVDA/JAWS-in-a-browser idiom that does not exist in this shell; the rotor exposes landmarks and headings equally, and the landmarks are named.

Residual value: giving the two flat index pages a heading is a mild orientation nicety, and normalizing rank order is reasonable housekeeping. That is low severity, already tracked, and deliberately deferred.
correction: Accurate restatement: no main view renders an h1 naming the page, so the heading outline of each view starts at h2 (or is empty on the two flat index pages). This is a best-practice gap, not a WCAG failure — page identity is already carried accessibly by the named content region (`aria-label` on the section/main, equal to the string the proposed h1 would hold) and by the path bar's `aria-current="page"` leaf crumb. It duplicates tracked audit item M05 in docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md:184-188, and the app's "the bar owns the title" doctrine — under which an h1 was deliberately removed from the activity page and the removal pinned by tests/frontend/project-activity.integration.test.tsx:1152 — means any fix should add visually-hidden headings only, never restore a visible title.

title: R2 agent-setup menu declares role="menu" with no name, no aria-controls, no arrow keys, and loses focus on Escape
reason: Independently reproduced in source. src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2044 is verbatim `<div className="sync-path-menu end" role="menu">` with no id, no aria-label/aria-labelledby, and no onKeyDown; the trigger at 2033-2042 matches the quoted evidence exactly and has no aria-controls; the two role="menuitem" buttons (2049-2071) carry no tabIndex; the wrapping `<div className="sync-r2-split" ref={agentSplitRef}>` at 2018 has no key handling either. The block is live: it renders when creatingStorage && storageDraft.kind === "s3" and agentLaunchers is non-empty, and both the claude and codex provider descriptors ship cli_launcher. No guard, override, CSS rule, or call-site condition rescues it.
correction: The contract break is real, but "a screen-reader user is stuck" overstates it. Because the menuitems are left at the default tabIndex 0, they stay reachable by Tab and activatable by Enter/Space, so the popup is operable — it just violates the role="menu" contract it declares. title: R2 agent-setup menu declares role="menu" with no name, no aria-controls, no arrow keys, and loses focus on Escape
reason: The code is as quoted (src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2033-2077): the split-arrow trigger carries aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-label but no aria-controls, and the popup is `<div className="sync-path-menu end" role="menu">` with no id, no aria-label, and no onKeyDown. The Escape path is real too: closeOnEscape at line 1277 unmounts a conditionally-rendered node, so focus inside it falls to body. The fix is still the right one — import moveMenuFocus/menuOptions, add id + aria-controls + aria-label, and refocus agentSplitRef's arrow button before closing — but this is a low-severity polish item on a two-item popup, not a medium-severity keyboard trap.

Name-from-label never runs for the input, so nothing is "folded in". `<button>` is a labelable element, so with no `htmlFor` the label's labeled control is the FIRST labelable descendant in tree order — the HelpButton, which precedes the input. `input.labels.length === 0`. The field is therefore never announced as "S3 API URL How to find the Cloudflare R2 S3 API URL"; it is announced from the placeholder alone.

The underlying defect is real, is at exactly the cited lines, has exactly the cited cause (HelpButton inside the implicit label), and the proposed fix (move the button out of the label, associate input via id/htmlFor) is the correct remedy — so I am not refuting the finding, only its mechanism and severity framing.
correction:
Corrected statement: the HelpButton inside each implicit `<label>` does not pollute the field's accessible name — it STEALS the label outright. `<button>` is a labelable element, so for a `<label>` with no `htmlFor` the labeled control is the first labelable descendant in tree order, which is the HelpButton at lines 334/363/380/397/414, not the input that follows it. Verified in Chromium: `label.control` is the BUTTON and `input.labels.length` is 0 for all five R2 fields.

Two consequences, both reproduced:
1. All five R2 inputs (S3 API URL, Bucket name, Account ID, Access Key ID, Secret Access Key) have NO programmatic label. Chrome falls back to the placeholder, so the a11y tree reports the S3 API URL field as textbox "Example: https://9cc0c910ec***41511aca1.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/agent" and the Secret Access Key field as "Stored — type to replace" / "Example: a1B2…x9Y0". That is a WCAG 2.1 A failure (1.3.1 Info and Relationships, 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value), not merely a verbose name.
2. It is also a pointer bug for every user, not just screen-reader users: because the label's control is the help button, clicking the visible field text forwards activation to it. In the probe, clicking `.sync-field-name` incremented the button's click counter and moved focus to the BUTTON. In the app that handler is `onClick={() => void openExternalUrl(url)}`, so clicking "Secret Access Key" launches an external browser to the Cloudflare docs instead of focusing the field.

The proposed fix stands and is the right one: render `.form-label-row` (name + HelpButton) as a sibling of the input rather than inside the label, and bind the input with an explicit id/htmlFor pair. The alternative offered in the finding — keeping the layout and adding `aria-label` to each input — patches only consequence 1 and leaves consequence 2 (label click opening an external URL) in place, so it should not be taken.

title: Logs drawer resize separator is not focusable and carries no aria-value* state
reason: The code is as quoted (ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:190-197), and the keyboard half of the claim is real: there is genuinely no keyboard path to change the drawer height, while the sibling sidebar separator (ProjectSync.tsx:3694-3708) shows the codebase's own intended pattern, added in f956ad8 with no doc, specimen, or commit evidence that the drawer was deliberately exempted. So it is not a fabrication and not an intentional design decision. But the impact is far smaller than "medium" implies, on two counts. First, the ARIA half is misstated: aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax are applicable to role="separator" only when the separator is focusable; a non-focusable separator is a spec-valid static structural element, and because it is absent from the focus order a screen-reader user is never parked on an inert control — there is no "reads a control it cannot operate" failure here. Second, nothing is gated behind the resize. App.css:731-734 gives .log-panel-body overflow-y:auto (LogPanel.tsx:333 wires the scroll container), "Load older" is a real button, and the drawer opens at a fixed, usable 240px that is clamped to 140…min(520, innerHeight-120) and refit on window resize. logHeight is plain useState(240) with no persistence, so the height resets every mount for mouse users too — the resizer only buys a transient, per-session comfort adjustment. A keyboard-only user reads every log line, applies every filter, and pages older entries at the default height; the sole loss is an optional, non-persisted visual preference in a developer-facing log drawer of a single-user desktop app. Real, worth a one-line fix by copying the sidebar contract, but polish-tier rather than a functional block.
correction: The log drawer's resize separator is mouse-only: a keyboard user cannot adjust the drawer height, unlike the sidebar separator at ProjectSync.tsx:3694-3708 which has tabIndex={0}, aria-value*, and onKeyDown. Drop the aria-value* half of the claim — those properties are required only for a focusable separator, so as authored the element is a valid non-focusable structural separator and screen readers do not surface it as an operable control. No log content or control is unreachable: .log-panel-body scrolls, "Load older" is a button, and the drawer opens at a fixed 240px height that is not persisted for any user. The gap is an unavailable optional size preference, not lost functionality.

title: Switcher menus drop the "Switch to" group caption from both the render and the accessibility tree
reason: The visible caption's removal is a deliberate, user-selected design, not an oversight. Four path-bar menu directions were built as a static specimen (menu-mockup.html) and the user picked "B · Switcher"; the "SWITCH TO" caption belonged to the rejected directions A and D. B's grammar is explicitly positional and is documented three times in the code itself: the component doctrine comment at SyncPathBar.tsx:16-21 ("a header block naming the object the menu acts on… The current object is the header, not a checked row — position says 'this is the one you're on'"), the switcher comment at App.css:3153, and the memory record switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md (implemented 2026-09-01, 269/269 + tsc green). The predicted confusion ("no caption saying these rows switch rather than act") cannot occur: in switcher mode the verbs are no longer rows — every unlabelled group is rendered as icon/text pills inside a separately shaded, border-topped .sync-path-menu-foot strip — so the only menuitem rows in the body ARE the switch targets, sitting directly under a visually lifted current-object header (2px ink border, shadow-card, trailing check, aria-current="true"). Menus with ≥6 targets also gain a search pill whose placeholder literally reads "Switch <scope>…". The accessibility-tree half is not a regression either: the pre-change caption was a plain div with no role="group" and no aria-labelledby, so AT never received a group name in this bar in either mode, and arrow-key navigation inside role="menu" does not announce intervening static text — a screen-reader user heard nothing before and hears nothing now. What is announced remains sufficient (crumb button "<name>. Project menu", the menu's own aria-label from menuLabel ?? crumb.label, then each target's name). No WCAG SC is implicated; group captions inside a menu are optional per the ARIA APG, and no axe/a11y linter runs in this repo. The only real residue is that aria-label on a role-less div is inert — dead markup, costing no user anything.
correction: Only a narrow, non-user-facing part of the finding holds: the aria-label on the role-less .sync-path-menu-group div at SyncPathBar.tsx:343 is discarded (naming is prohibited on the generic role), so it is dead markup that should either be removed or paired with role="group". It is not a regression in what AT announces (the pre-change visible caption was likewise never programmatically associated with the group), and re-rendering the caption would reverse a design direction the user explicitly chose.

title: R2 credential fields inherit the help button's aria-label into their own accessible name
reason: The mechanism is real but the consequence is verbosity, not a defect, and the severity is inflated. (1) No WCAG SC is violated: each input still has a unique, correct accessible name that BEGINS with the exact visible label text, so 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value passes and 2.5.3 Label in Name passes (visible text is contained in, and leads, the computed name). The appended string is an accurate, topical help sentence — it does not misidentify the field, and it is announced once on focus, not "doubled". (2) The aria-label being blamed is a deliberate project rule, not an oversight: the codebase requires icon-only controls to carry accessible names (docs/PLAN_PROVIDER_NEUTRAL_SESSION_DETAIL.md:456, "Icon-only actions retain accessible names and tooltips"), and the adjacent CSS comment at src/App.css:416 ("the hit area meets the 24px minimum") shows the same button was authored with a11y in mind. Stripping the aria-label would also not fix anything — the button's "?" text content would still fold into the label subtree as "S3 API URL ?" — so the finding penalizes the a11y measure rather than the structural choice. (3) Realistic exposure is tiny: five fields confined to the one-time Cloudflare R2 storage-setup panel of a niche Tauri desktop dev tool (HelpButton/.field-help appear nowhere else in src/ — grep confirms 5 call sites, all in StorageSettings.tsx). (4) It is not novel or a regression: the repo has no accessible-name assertions anywhere (tests/frontend/storage-settings.integration.test.tsx:491-528 assert raw HTML source text only), and "Run an accessibility audit" is still an unstarted P2 backlog item at docs/PROJECT_IMPROVEMENT_REVIEW.md:411 — this is one instance of an admittedly unaudited class, worth a polish pass, not a medium-severity finding at the point of "typing credentials".
correction: Accurate but narrower statement: each R2 input's accessible name appends the help button's aria-label after the field name (e.g. "S3 API URL How to find the Cloudflare R2 S3 API URL", src/components/project-sync/StorageSettings.tsx:331/361/378/395/412). The visible label still leads the name, so no WCAG success criterion fails; this is screen-reader verbosity on a one-time setup panel. Note the same folding would occur as "S3 API URL ?" even with the aria-label removed, so the fix is structural (id/htmlFor with the button as a sibling of the label), not "delete the aria-label".

title: Live log stream has no role="log" and its rows carry no structure
reason:
Both halves fail against the actual code and the project's recorded intent.

(1) SILENCE IS DELIBERATE AND DOCUMENTED. The panel's container is wrapped by ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:180-186 in role="region" aria-label="Logs" tabIndex={-1}, opened by a toggle with aria-controls="activity-log-drawer"/aria-expanded — the W3C disclosure pattern, pinned by an existing gate at tests/frontend/activity-log.integration.test.tsx:147-149. docs/PLAN_NOTICE_SYSTEM.md:18 states the governing house rule (c): "Content already present when the view renders is not a status message — it must not be a live region. Standing information is role='region' with a name, or no role." Opening the drawer loads retained history first (loadActivityLogs), so rows are present at render. That doc records a 13-agent audit that swept 82 live-region attributes across 22 component files; the log panel emerged from it as a named region, not an oversight. The codebase repeatedly declines live roles with reasons in comments (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2579, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1392, ProjectSync.tsx:3517 records that role="alert" on a screen made a reader announce the whole page as one interruption).

(2) THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD REGRESS THE EXPERIENCE. Appends are rAF-batched with MAX_LOG_LINES = 2_000 (ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:15,160-176). A push burst emits dozens-to-hundreds of lines; role="log" queues every addition in document order, which is the textbook live-region flood — the screen reader would be talking continuously through the entire sync the finding wants narrated. Silence is the better outcome here, not a defect.

(3) THE MISSING CHANNEL ISN'T MISSING. Sync progress and outcome are announced by dedicated polite regions elsewhere: SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx:72 (role="status"), PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:864,875, ProjectActivityPage.tsx:963-964 and :1789. The drawer is the verbose diagnostic transcript a user opens to inspect, not the status channel.

(4) THE ROW-STRUCTURE CLAIM MISREADS THE FILE. LogPanel.tsx:112-133 gives each row a sync-visually-hidden word carrying the level ("Success"/"Warning"/"Error"), added explicitly for WCAG 1.4.1 per the comment at :80-95, plus the type as visible text. Each .log-line is display:flex (App.css:764), i.e. a block box, so browse mode reads one row per line. "Four sibling spans... run together as one undelimited text stream" is not what the markup produces. Adding role="list"/"listitem" over up to 2000 diagnostic rows buys no navigation a block row doesn't already give and adds per-item verbosity; the table-with-column-headers alternative is heavier still and would fight the tail-following behaviour (nextFollowTail, LogPanel.tsx:66-70).

Residue: the four columns have no explicit field labels, so a row reads as "12:04:31 Success PUSH <message>". That is the same undelimited-columns reading a sighted user gets, self-evident in context, and at most a cosmetic refinement — not a medium a11y defect.
correction: Only a narrow, low-value residue survives: log rows carry no explicit per-field labelling for the timestamp/type columns (level is already spoken via a visually hidden word). The role="log"/aria-live half should be dropped entirely — it contradicts docs/PLAN_NOTICE_SYSTEM.md rule (c), duplicates announcement channels that already exist (SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx:72 and friends), and would flood the screen reader during the very sync it aims to narrate.

title: Review panel keeps role="tabpanel" and a dangling aria-labelledby when the tab strip does not render
reason:
The markup is as described, but there is no user-visible consequence, and the half of it that is deliberate is deliberate and pinned by a test.

1. The strip-hiding is an intentional, tested design decision. `SyncReviewTabs.tsx:31-32` carries the comment "A single tab is not a choice; the strip only renders when there are tabs to switch between," and `tests/frontend/project-files.integration.test.tsx:126-133` pins it: `assert.equal(git, "", "a single-step review renders no tab strip at all")`. Any fix must preserve that, so the finding reduces to "the residual role/labelledby on the container is untidy."

2. The claimed screen-reader harm does not occur. The div at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:719-724 (and RestorePlanView.tsx:557-562) has no `tabIndex` and nothing focuses it, so it is never a Tab stop. `role="tabpanel"` has no required-context role in ARIA — a tabpanel with no tablist is valid ARIA and produces no error announcement; there is nothing to "escape to" because nothing traps or gates the reader. A dangling `aria-labelledby` resolves to empty under accname and simply leaves the container unnamed; naming a tabpanel is a SHOULD, not a MUST, and 4.1.2 requires a name only for interactive components, so this is not a WCAG 2.1 AA failure. The unnamed container also sits inside `<section aria-labelledby="sync-push-resource-title">` ("Push review") / `"sync-pull-review-title"` ("Pull review"), so the region a reader actually navigates by is already named and all content is reachable in document order.

3. The `aria-controls` half is a non-issue in practice. "Render only the active panel" is the standard React tab pattern, and no shipping AT implements move-to-controlled-element (JAWS removed its aria-controls key, NVDA and VoiceOver never had one), so the dangling reference on the inactive tab changes nothing for any real user.

4. It was already reviewed and accepted. The 2026-08-30 UI audit (docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md) source-reviewed these exact screens — it cites RestorePlanView.tsx#L573, inside this very region — and lists "Review tabs implement the expected tablist, roving focus, Arrow, Home, and End keyboard behavior" under "What works well" (#8). That same audit was sensitive to precisely this class of defect: H01 is literally "the Logs trigger also lacks aria-controls." It flagged the ones with consequences and left this one alone.

The finding is real as markup hygiene and would be a fine drive-by cleanup, but it is a lint-class nit with no realistic user or maintainer impact, not a defect.
correction: Accurate as a markup observation: when `showProjectFiles` is false, `syncReviewSteps` yields one step, `SyncReviewTabs` returns null, and the content container still carries `role="tabpanel"` plus an `aria-labelledby` pointing at an absent `#sync-review-history-tab`. The consequence, however, is only that a non-focusable container advertises a generic role with no accessible name, inside an already-named `<section>` — no keyboard impact, no content loss, no error announcement, no WCAG AA failure. The stated impacts ("no tablist to escape to", "'move to controlled element' fails") overstate it: nothing traps the reader, and no shipping assistive technology implements aria-controls navigation.

The framing needs two corrections: this is not a WCAG 2.1 AA failure (4.1.2 is satisfied, and 2.5.3 Label in Name is satisfied because the visible label "Logs" is contained in the accessible name), and it is not isolated — SectionHeading at lines 244-257 uses the identical construct, setting aria-label only when collapsed && flagged, so a collapsed unflagged section computes to "Projects 4" the same way.

This is a clarity nit, not a WCAG 2.1 AA conformance failure: 4.1.2 and 2.5.3 are both satisfied. The count saturates at 99 and the badge is suppressed while the drawer is open.
