title: App actions menu drops focus to <body> on Escape and has no menu keyboard contract
reason:
The markup is quoted correctly, but the impact does not survive contact with the actual widget.

1) The menu holds exactly ONE item. `role="menu"` here is announced as "menu, 1 item"; the missing ArrowUp/Down/Home/End is not a broken promise because `moveMenuFocus` over a one-element list is a self-focus no-op — ArrowDown computes `(0+1)%1 = 0`, ArrowUp `(0-1+1)%1 = 0`, Home and End both `0`. Wiring it in would produce zero observable behavior change. Half the finding is therefore vacuous.

2) The Escape scenario mis-states where focus is. The trigger's handler is only `onClick={() => setAppMenuOpen((c) => !c)}` (ProjectSync.tsx:2772) — unlike StorageCatalogPage.tsx:585, it does NOT call `focusMenuEdge` on open. So on the ordinary path (pointer click, or keyboard-activating the ⋯), focus is still on the `.storage-link-more` trigger when Escape fires, and `hidden` is applied to a container that does not contain the focused element. Nothing blurs. Reaching the described blur-to-body requires the user to additionally Tab off the trigger onto the single item and then choose Escape over Enter.

3) Platform narrows it further. This is a Tauri/WKWebView app on macOS, where Tab does not reach `<button>` elements at all unless the user has turned on Full Keyboard Access. The already-narrow path needs a non-default OS setting on top of it.

4) The proposed fix is a regression as written. `tabIndex={-1}` on the menuitem without also adding a focus-on-open call would make "Reload app data" unreachable by keyboard entirely, since Tab is the only route into it today. StorageCatalogPage pairs roving tabindex with `focusMenuEdge(node, "first")` on the ref; this menu has no such call, so copying only the tabindex half breaks it.

5) The command is not gated behind this widget. The identical "Reload app data" action lives in the path bar's Mallard overflow group (ProjectSync.tsx:2726-2745), which does carry the full contract (`moveMenuFocus` at SyncPathBar.tsx:277, opener restore at 409-411). The titlebar ⋯ only renders on the `showsPathBar === false` branch (ProjectSync.tsx:3715-3728), i.e. the screens where the path bar is absent.

6) Worst case, on that narrow path, is one wasted Tab cycle. No trap, no lost state, no unreachable control, and `refresh()` is idempotent so nothing is at risk.

What remains is that the titlebar ⋯ is the one popup in the app that does not import the shared `menuKeyboard.ts` helper — a consistency nit, below the bar for a reported defect, not the "menu keyboard contract broken / focus dropped to body" defect described.
correction: Accurate statement: the titlebar app-actions menu (ProjectSync.tsx:2778) is the only `role="menu"` popup in the app that does not use the shared `sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts` helper, and it does not restore focus to its ⋯ trigger on Escape. Because the menu contains a single item and opening it never moves focus into the menu, the arrow-key gap is unobservable and the focus drop only occurs if the user Tabs from the trigger onto the item and then presses Escape instead of Enter — which on macOS/WKWebView additionally requires Full Keyboard Access to be enabled. Cost is one extra Tab cycle. Any fix must add focus-on-open (`focusMenuEdge`) before setting `tabIndex={-1}`, or the sole item becomes keyboard-unreachable.

title: aria-label on role-less generic containers is discarded, so several field and fact groups have no name
reason: Citations are exact and the code behaves as described. <repo>/src/components/project-sync/session-detail/SessionDetailHeader.tsx:57 is verbatim `<div className="session-detail-chips" aria-label="Session facts">` and :91 is verbatim `<div className="session-detail-header-actions" aria-label="Session actions">`. I read the whole 119-line file: neither div carries a `role`, no props are spread onto them, and nothing wraps them in a role-bearing element (parents are `.session-detail-strip` div and `<header>`). A repo-wide grep for `setAttribute(...role...)` / `.role =` finds no runtime role injection, and App.css:6880 / 6920 only set flex layout (no `display: contents` or other DOM-shape trick). So these are plain `div`s → HTML-AAM maps them to role `generic`, whose ARIA 1.2 name-from is "prohibited"; the aria-label is an authoring error (axe-core `aria-prohibited-attr`) and is not exposed as an accessible name by current engines. The three secondary sites are equally accurate, at the exact lines given: ProjectActivityPage.tsx:696 `<div id={id} className="sync-history-thread-meta" aria-label="Session details">` (the optional `id` is not passed at the only in-repo call site, line 1327, and is not referenced by any aria-labelledby/describedby — so no description-path rescue), ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:400 and ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:221 (`aria-label={`${...relativePath} details`}`). The one path slip is StorageSettings.tsx:330, which lives at src/components/project-sync/StorageSettings.tsx — line number and text (`aria-label="Cloudflare R2 connection details"`) match exactly. No test asserts any of these names (only the two mockup files repeat the pattern), so the fix carries no test coupling. I could not run a live browser probe (file:// and data: navigation were both refused), so the engine-level behavior rests on the spec mapping rather than an executed trace, but the source-level fact — role-less container carrying a name it cannot own — is fully reproduced.
correction: The impact is overstated in one respect: nothing in these clusters becomes unnamed. Each action button carries its own `aria-label={action.label}` (SessionDetailHeader.tsx:103), and every fact chip has visible text content, as do the metric spans (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:701-706) and the R2 fields (each wrapped in a `<label>`). What is lost is only the group-level name — the author's grouping intent — not the individual readouts. Accurate statement: "The aria-label on these role-less containers is dropped because `div` maps to role `generic`, where naming is prohibited; the grouping the author intended (`Session facts`, `Session actions`, `Session details`, `Cloudflare R2 connection details`, per-file `<path> details`) never reaches the accessibility tree, while the chips, buttons and fields inside remain individually named." Severity stays low.

title: App actions menu drops focus to <body> on Escape and has no menu keyboard contract
reason: Citation checks out. ProjectSync.tsx:2777-2783 matches the quoted markup verbatim (role="menu", aria-label="App actions", hidden={!appMenuOpen}), and the Escape handler at 1317-1322 really does only stopPropagation + setAppMenuOpen(false) with no focus restore, while the sibling implementation at SyncPathBar.tsx:409-411 does restore (openerRefs.current.get(openMenu) then opener?.focus()). I resolved the CSS: App.css:3804 sets .storage-link-actions-menu[hidden]{display:none} and the two later rule blocks touching that selector (9149 border/background, 10190 animation:none) set no display, so `hidden` genuinely removes the focused menuitem from the focus tree. No onKeyDown exists on the trigger or menu container (the file's only onKeyDown is at 3707 for sidebar resize) and the menuitem carries no tabIndex. Two overstatements, though: the menu holds exactly ONE menuitem, so the missing arrow/Home/End handling is functionally inert, and nothing auto-focuses the menu on open, so the focus drop needs the narrow sequence focus-trigger, activate, Tab into the item, Escape — Escape pressed while focus is still on the trigger already behaves correctly. Also, the proposed fix is partly wrong: adding tabIndex={-1} without wiring focusMenuEdge on open would make the sole menuitem unreachable by keyboard.
correction: The app actions menu (ProjectSync.tsx:2777) declares role="menu" but its Escape handler (1317-1322) closes without returning focus to the .storage-link-more trigger, so a keyboard user who Tabs from the trigger into the single "Reload app data" menuitem and then presses Escape is blurred to <body> (App.css:3804 applies display:none via [hidden]); Escape pressed while focus is still on the trigger is unaffected. SyncPathBar.tsx:409-411 already restores focus correctly. Fix: capture the trigger and call opener.focus() before/after setAppMenuOpen(false). The missing ArrowUp/Down/Home/End handling is a semantic-contract gap only — the menu has exactly one item, so there is nothing to navigate between. Do NOT apply tabIndex={-1} to the menuitem as proposed unless focusMenuEdge is also wired to the open transition; nothing focuses the menu on open today, so a roving tabindex alone would make the only item keyboard-unreachable.

title: Logs nav button's accessible name absorbs the unread badge as a bare number
reason: The mechanic is real (Icon is aria-hidden by default at src/components/Icons.tsx:83, so the name computes to "Logs 7") but there is no user-visible consequence, and it matches an established, commented convention in this very file. 1. No conformance failure and no parity gap. The button keeps an accessible name containing its visible label, so 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value and 2.5.3 Label in Name both pass; it also carries aria-controls="activity-log-drawer" and aria-expanded, so it announces as "Logs 7, button, collapsed". Critically, the count is unlabeled ON SCREEN TOO — a sighted user sees a bare pill reading "7" next to "Logs" and infers "unread" from the badge's shape and position. The screen-reader user gets the same information from the same context. Nothing is available to one group and withheld from the other, which is what an a11y defect requires. The claim that it "reads as an index or a shortcut" is speculative: no other nav item carries a number, and badge-after-label is one of the most conventional patterns in desktop software. 2. It is the codebase's deliberate rule, documented in a comment 500 lines above. SectionHeading (ProjectSidebar.tsx:216-260) renders the identical shape — {collapsed && {count}} inside the toggle button, producing "Projects 7" — and adds an aria-label ONLY when the flag triangle is also showing. The comment states the rule: the triangle "is also named on the button, not only drawn, the same WCAG 1.4.1 rule the rows themselves follow." That is, non-text signals (a glyph conveying meaning by shape/color) get named; a number is already text and is left to speak for itself. The Logs badge follows that convention exactly. Fixing only the Logs button would make it inconsistent with the three section headings; fixing all four is a convention change, not a defect fix. 3. The state is transient and self-clearing. unreadLogs is capped at 99 (ProjectSync.tsx:603), reset to 0 whenever the drawer opens (ProjectSync.tsx:661, 3676), and the badge renders only while !activityOpen. The moment a user acts on the button the count is gone. 4. Nobody has ever hit it. Every test render passes unreadLogs={0} (tests/frontend/project-activity.integration.test.tsx, src/sidebar-collapse-mockup.tsx:131) — grep finds no nonzero value anywhere in the repo. No audit doc (docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md, docs/APP_AUDIT_2026-08-07.md) mentions badge or unread naming. The proposed fix is a reasonable polish improvement, but this is a "could be cleaner" item against a deliberate in-repo convention, not a defect with a realistic user consequence.

title: Session-detail fact chips announce bare values with the identifying glyph hidden
reason:
Refuted on impact, on the technical premise, and on intent.

1) The premise overstates the loss. Both chips carry a `title` (src/components/project-sync/session-detail/SessionDetailHeader.tsx:59 `title={`Branch ${detail.branch}`}`, :65 `title={detail.recorded_sha}` — the FULL sha, more than the visible 7 chars). Chromium does not drop a span that has a title: it exposes the node with a name/description computed from title (accname 1.2 step 2I), and the visible `<code>` text is read regardless. So the value is announced and the qualifier is present in the tree and on hover; "announced as a naked 'main' with nothing saying which is a branch" is not what ships.

2) It is a deliberate, documented choice, not an oversight. Lines 55-56 carry the intent verbatim: "Facts state themselves: a branch after the branch glyph and a 7-char sha need no caption." The codebase knows the exact remedy proposed and applies it where a caption was judged owed — `sync-visually-hidden` at src/components/project-sync/session-detail/SessionDetailEvent.tsx:228, src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2477, src/components/LogPanel.tsx:120, and for this very header's h1 at line 49. Not using it on the fact chips is a decision made with the tool in hand.

3) The chip shape is a pinned contract. tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:268 asserts `class="session-detail-chip" title="Branch main"` and :279 the clock chip's title — the chosen disclosure mechanism is under test. The project's own a11y contract (docs/PLAN_PROVIDER_NEUTRAL_SESSION_DETAIL.md section 4.6) requires accessible names for *icon-only actions*; those are satisfied (launch buttons at :95-104 carry `aria-label={action.label}`). Non-interactive text chips are outside that contract.

4) No realistic consequence. This is a local single-user Tauri desktop app; the two chips are non-interactive and restate context the page already establishes (a git-backed session detail). A VoiceOver user hears "main", "a1b2c3d", a time, a duration, a token count in fixed order — the ambiguity between a word and a 7-char hex string costs nothing actionable. The 2026-08-30 UI audit (docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md, 23 findings landed) covered this surface and did not raise it.

5) Generic, not novel. The identical icon+value idiom is house-wide (e.g. the activity branch pill at src/components/project-sync/ProjectActivityPage.tsx:205, checkpoint rows), and the sibling container `<div aria-label="Session facts">` at line 57 carries exactly the same generic-node caveat the finding builds its case on — which the finding did not notice. Flagging one instance of an intentional, systemic pattern is a style preference dressed as a defect.

Below the reporting bar: at most a polish nicety, already mitigated by title, already decided against in code and in test.

title: Session-detail fact chips announce bare values with the identifying glyph hidden
reason: Independently reproduced in source. Citation is exact: SessionDetailHeader.tsx:59 is the branch FactChip and lines 59-67 match the quoted evidence verbatim. Every link in the claimed chain holds: (1) FactChip at lines 21-23 renders literally `{children}` with no role and no aria-label, so it is a role=generic node, for which naming is prohibited and `title` cannot become the accessible name; (2) Icons.tsx:83 hardcodes aria-hidden="true" on the svg — `{...props}` does spread after it at line 90 so an override is possible, but neither call site (lines 60 and 66) passes one, so both glyphs are removed from the tree; (3) no mitigation exists anywhere — none of the three `.session-detail-chip` CSS blocks (App.css 6888, 9254, 10918) has a ::before/content caption, and the CSS comment states the intent outright ("the chips carry no captions; the full value stays in the tooltip"); (4) the container's aria-label="Session facts" at line 57 sits on a bare div, also role=generic, so it is dropped too and adds no context. The omission is deliberate and pinned: tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:268 asserts doesNotMatch(/>Started<|>Ended<|>Branch<|>Commit<|.../). The sync-visually-hidden idiom is already used for this exact purpose at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:228, so the remedy is available and simply unapplied here. Severity low is right: values remain readable, only the type label is missing, and sighted users get the glyph.
correction: The finding is real but understates the commit chip and overstates the branch chip. The branch chip's title is `Branch ${detail.branch}`, which does contain the word "Branch"; since this is a Tauri/WKWebView app, WebKit exposes title as AXHelp, so VoiceOver can surface it in verbose settings — "nothing saying which is a branch" is too strong for that chip. The commit chip is strictly worse than claimed: its title is the bare 40-char sha with no label at all, so the proposed fix of building an aria-label "from the same string already passed as title" would produce aria-label="a1b2c3d4..." and fix nothing there. Accurate statement: both chips delegate their type to an aria-hidden glyph and are announced as bare values; the branch chip has a partial fallback via its title's "Branch " prefix, while the commit chip has no textual indication of its type in any attribute. The fix must add a literal caption to each (e.g. Branch / "Commit "), not reuse title. Note that the pinned assertion at tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:268 forbids `>Branch<` and `>Commit<`, so it will need updating (a trailing space inside the hidden span happens to slip past the regex).

title: Path-bar switcher's filter box cannot be reached by keyboard — Tab closes the menu instead of entering it
reason: The mechanics are accurate but the impact is not. The finding's core claim — "a keyboard-only user with 12 projects must arrow past all of them one row at a time and can never filter" — is false. SyncPathBar.tsx:281-303 implements a 500ms typeahead buffer on the menu ("A repeated first letter cycles matches; a longer prefix narrows from the focused row, so typing 'te' stays on 'Team bucket'"), alongside moveMenuFocus's Arrow/Home/End (menuKeyboard.ts:22-34). The function the filter box serves — reach a named target without scanning — is already fully keyboard-operable, so there is no WCAG 2.1.1 functionality failure. Tab-closes-the-menu is also an explicit, documented decision, not an oversight: line 256-257 says "Tab is not menu navigation: the menu steps aside and the bar's own tab order continues wherever the browser takes it," which is the standard ARIA menu behavior, and menuKeyboard.ts's header comment establishes upholding the role="menu" contract as codebase doctrine. The feature's own design record (memory switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md) describes the shipped behavior as "ArrowDown/Up step into the list, Enter activates the first .target, typeahead skips the input" — the input was intentionally left out of the keyboard flow as a pointer affordance. The proposed fix is also net-negative: a textbox is not a permitted child of role="menu", so AT in menu-navigation mode prunes it whatever its tabIndex, meaning a Tab cycle helps no screen-reader user while breaking the menu contract the shared helper exists to enforce; the real remedy would be re-architecting to a combobox, a design change rather than a bug fix. Nothing is lost at runtime: no crash, no data risk, no unreachable capability, and the typed-state handling at lines 264-274 already covers the click path.
correction: Accurate residual, at low severity: the ≥6-target switcher filter box is pointer-only — no Tab or arrow path focuses it — so keyboard users fall back to the menu's typeahead and arrow navigation instead of the filter. A polish/pattern item (the input sits inside role="menu", where the correct long-term shape is a combobox), not a keyboard-operability defect.

title: Path-bar switcher's filter box cannot be reached by keyboard — Tab closes the menu instead of entering it
reason: All citations verified verbatim against the working tree: SyncPathBar.tsx:328-337 renders the searchable <input> (tag on line 329), :258 closes the menu on any Tab from inside it, :516 (plus the twin handlers on the non-split crumb and the overflow button) closes it on Tab from the opener, SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR=6 at :129, and menuKeyboard.ts:11 restricts option selection to the menuitem family. Control flow reproduces: the menu is hidden={!open} with .sync-path-menu[hidden]{display:none} (App.css:3080), so the input is in the tab order only while open; Enter/Space opening leaves focus on the toggle and the next Tab calls setOpenMenu(null) (React 19 createRoot flushes discrete-event updates synchronously before the browser's Tab default action, so the input is display:none before focus moves — and if it flushed later, focus would land in an element immediately hidden); ArrowDown/ArrowUp opening and the openMenuRequest effect both go through the local focusMenuOption, which focuses menuOptions(root)[0]/[n-1] and the roleless input can never match; Tab and Shift+Tab both report key==="Tab" so :258 catches both; moveMenuFocus wraps ArrowUp from index 0 to the last option, never to the input. No caller focuses .sync-path-menu-search, there is no autoFocus or focus effect, and the only document listeners are outside-mousedown and Escape. The :focus-visible rule at App.css:3202 shows focus there was intended. The control is genuinely mouse-only.
correction: The input is unreachable by keyboard as described, but the impact statement is wrong: lines 283-303 implement prefix type-ahead over option labels (repeat first letter cycles, longer prefix narrows from the focused row), so a keyboard user is not forced to arrow one row at a time and can still jump to any target. The unreachable filter box is therefore a redundant path, not lost functionality — closer to a focus-order/dead-control defect (WCAG 2.4.3) than a hard 2.1.1 failure, hence medium. Two notes on the proposed fix: tabIndex={0} is a no-op since <input> is natively tabbable (the real fix is focusing the input on open when searchable and dropping the blanket Tab-close for searchable menus), and a text input as a child of role="menu" is invalid ARIA that screen readers may not expose in menu mode at all, so the structure likely needs the combobox pattern rather than only a Tab special-case.

title: Role-by-position turns a lone "Add storage…" group into an unlabelled icon pill
reason: The code shape is as described (SyncPathBar.tsx:166-172, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1708-1734), but the consequence is cosmetic, not dead UI. (1) The control is fully live: it renders, sits in the roving menu order, is keyboard-activatable, fires onSelect, and carries both aria-label="Add storage…" (line 232) and a visible hover tooltip via title=verbTitle(item) (line 234) — so "unlabelled" and "dead-ui" both overstate it. (2) A glyph-only pill in that footer is the shipped design grammar, not an anomaly: .sync-path-menu-verb is `min-width:32px; padding:0` by construction (App.css:3236-3251), and the project crumb menu (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2389-2430) already renders Reveal / Agent profile / Rename / Reset as bare glyphs there. A lone "+" beside the lifted current-storage row is the same add affordance the user meets in every other crumb menu. (3) The position rule is documented intent landed 2026-09-01: SyncPathBar.tsx:119-128 states verbatim that "the first unlabelled group is the object's verbs … and the unlabelled groups after them are the ways to get more," and the switcher-menu memory records B · Switcher shipping deliberately "without touching any caller," reading groups by position. With no Switch-to list, first and trailing unlabelled group are the same group and the documented tie-break picks verbs — the component obeys its contract. (4) Realistic worst case: the same item is a text pill with 2+ storages and a glyph pill with 1, with no loss of function or accessible name. No test asserts either rendering, so no gate is violated.
correction: Narrowed accurate claim: on the storage settings page with exactly one storage configured, "Add storage…" renders as a glyph-only verb pill instead of the labelled text pill it becomes once a second storage exists, because it slides into the position-derived verbs slot. Purely a presentation inconsistency — the button works and keeps its accessible name and tooltip.

title: Prompt cards lose their turn duration entirely for tool-only turns after the SHOW default flip
reason: Independently reproduced. All citations are verbatim and correctly numbered: sessionDetailModel.ts:94 is `toolCalls: false,` (git diff confirms it was `sessionCountSupported(counts.tool_calls)` before this change); SessionDetailTimeline.tsx:58 is `const spans = sessionTurnSpans(events);`; sessionDetailModel.ts:316 guards `span.ended <= span.started`. The filtering is server-side — SessionDetailPage.tsx:229 passes `included_event_kinds: includedSessionEventKinds(activeFilters)` — so unchecked kinds never reach `events`, and no fallback, override, or backend-supplied turn extent exists (`turn_tool_summary` carries only a tool_calls count). A prompt whose turn continues solely into tool_call/intermediate_step therefore yields started === ended and `sessionTurnDurationLabel` returns null, while PromptCard still renders the clock and calls chips. Empirically simulated against ~/.mallard/session_timeline_cache.json (36 entries, 232 prompt turns, honoring per-provider `checkpoints: unsupported`): 7 turns lose their duration chip under the new defaults — claude 1030s/112 calls, codex 730s/55, codex 513s/45, claude 467s/29, claude 167s/11, claude 140s/10, codex 109s/9. The codex 730s turn's index holds prompt + 7 intermediate_step + 55 tool_call and no response event. All 7 sit at positions 0-30 of the default-filtered stream, i.e. on the first 50-event page, so they are visible on open. `intermediateSteps` was already false pre-diff, so the regression is attributable solely to the toolCalls flip. The stale comment at SessionDetailEvent.tsx:283 is present as claimed.
correction: Two numeric/wording corrections: (1) measuring the current cache I count 7 affected turns out of 232 prompt turns, not 8 of 229 (the cache file was rewritten at 14:00, so the sample likely shifted between reads); the two headline cases cited — a 730s codex turn and a 467s claude turn — both reproduce exactly. (2) The card does not print a zero duration; the duration chip is omitted entirely, so the head reads `clock · N calls`. The defect is an omitted fact plus an inconsistency between SHOW states, not a rendered "0s".

title: Role-by-position turns a lone "Add storage…" group into an unlabelled icon pill
reason: Verified against the real files and reproduced by rendering. SyncPathBar.tsx:166-171 matches the quoted code verbatim (verbs is line 168), and renderPill(item, false) at ~217-241 gates the label span on `tail`, so a verb prints its icon only. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1707-1730 builds the storage-editor crumb menu as [...(storages.some(c => c.id !== editedStorageConfig.id) ? [Switch to] : []), {items:[add-storage]}] — the only switcher menu in the app with no unconditional verbs group (the comment at 1697-1699 says its verbs live in the page overflow); every other switcher (ProjectLinksWorkspace 2274, 2387; StorageCatalogPage 1224, 1286) starts with an always-populated verbs group and is unaffected. Edit mode requires storages.find(id) to hit (1044-1048), so with exactly one configured storage the some() guard is false and populated[0] is the unlabelled Add group. I bundled SyncPathBar with esbuild and rendered it with renderToStaticMarkup: withSwitch=false yields class "sync-path-menu-verb", no "sync-path-menu-tail", and no visible "Add storage" text node — emitted markup is <button type="button" role="menuitem" class="sync-path-menu-verb" aria-label="Add storage…" tabindex="-1" title="Add storage…"><svg data-icon="plus" …/></button>; withSwitch=true yields a "sync-path-menu-tail" with the visible label. App.css:3236-3252 confirms .sync-path-menu-verb is a bare 32x32 pill with padding 0 and no generated content, and `caption` (line 174) is empty because add-storage has no `detail`, so the menu is the header row plus a lone + glyph. No guard, fallback or later CSS rule restores the text.
correction: Two imprecisions worth fixing. (1) The category "dead-ui" is wrong: the control is live, focusable, keyboard-activatable, and carries both aria-label="Add storage…" and title="Add storage…", so screen-reader and hover users get the name — what is lost is the visible label only. (2) "the trailing group is misread as the first group" mis-describes the mechanism: there is only one group and it genuinely is the first, so SyncPathBar behaves exactly as its own header comment (lines 118-126) documents ("the first unlabelled group is the object's verbs"). The real mismatch is at the call site: ProjectLinksWorkspace's storage-editor crumb is the one switcher that intentionally supplies no verbs group, so when "Switch to" is also absent its Add group falls into the verbs slot. Accurate statement: "With one storage configured, the storage-editor crumb menu supplies no verbs group, so SyncPathBar's documented position rule classifies the trailing Add group as verbs and 'Add storage…' renders as an unlabelled + pill (name preserved in aria-label/title only)." Either half of the proposed fix is valid; marking the group explicitly at the call site is the more faithful one, since the position rule itself is the documented contract.

title: Prompt cards lose their turn duration entirely for tool-only turns after the SHOW default flip
reason: Deliberate, test-pinned design decision with no false output. (1) INTENT: the same diff rewrites tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:185-192 from "tool calls are on by default" to "the conversation is what opens by default", asserting filters.toolCalls === false and filters.intermediateSteps === false. title: No error boundary anywhere: one render-time RangeError blanks the whole Tauri window with no way back
reason:
Refuted on novelty, scope, and trigger realism.

(1) ALREADY KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY DEFERRED. docs/PROJECT_IMPROVEMENT_REVIEW.md:241 is this finding verbatim — item 19 of 100 in the repo's own July 2026 review: "**19. Add a React error boundary.** `P1 · S · medium` / Zero `ErrorBoundary`/`componentDidCatch` in `src/`. One render throw in a 2,900-line component blanks the entire desktop app with no recovery path and no log entry. Wrap the workspace, report to the activity log, offer 'reload workspace'." Identical observation, identical evidence, identical severity, and even the proposed fix matches. This is a triaged, accepted backlog item, not a review discovery.

(2) NOTHING CITED IS IN THE DIFF. `git diff --stat -- src/main.tsx src/App.tsx src/clock.ts` is empty, and `git diff -U0 -- src/components/project-sync/ProjectActivityPage.tsx | grep toISOString` returns nothing. The anchor (main.tsx:9) and all seven `toISOString` sites are untouched pre-existing code. This is a whole-app architecture proposal, not a defect in the change under review.

(3) THE CLAIMED CHAIN DOES NOT CONNECT. The blamed helper `toEpochMilliseconds` (src/clock.ts:27) is used by NONE of the ProjectActivityPage call sites; those compute `new Date(x * 1_000)` directly on `u64`-seconds DTO fields (src/types.ts:1043-1044, 1114, 1354, 1367). Provider timestamp normalization happens in Rust at crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/providers/timeparse.rs:5 (`parse_timestamp_value`), which already divides values above 1e10 by 1000. The frontend helper the finding indicts is not on the path it describes.

(4) NO REALISTIC TRIGGER. Both providers write RFC3339 *strings*, not numbers: an empirical scan of 946 real transcripts under ~/.claude/projects found ZERO numeric `timestamp` fields — every one is of the form '2026-08-25T07:12:45.991Z'. Codex likewise parses via `DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339` (codex_paginated_projection.rs:931-941), which rejects out-of-range input outright. `parse_rfc3339` (timeparse.rs:25) validates month 1-12, day 1-31, hour <=23, minute <=59, second <=60 and rejects negatives. Reaching an out-of-range Date therefore requires a hand-authored transcript with an absurd year (e.g. "999999999-01-01T00:00:00Z") — adversarial/corrupted input, not realistic data. The "nanosecond-precision timestamp from a malformed transcript" scenario is invented, and the numeric branch it relies on is already downscaled by 1000 in Rust.

(5) IMPACT OVERSTATED. It is a desktop app: quit (memory notes ⌘Q works and even bypasses onCloseRequested) and relaunch is the ordinary recovery, and Settings > Local data > Reset Mallard exists. "Permanently white window with no way back" is not accurate.

The bare fact — no error boundary exists — is true, and I do not dispute it. But it is a documented, accepted hardening item on untouched code with no demonstrated realistic trigger, which is a robustness preference rather than a live defect surfaced by this change.
correction: Accurate restatement: "src/ has no React error boundary, so an uncaught render throw unmounts the workspace until the app is relaunched. This is already tracked as item 19 (`P1 · S · medium`) in docs/PROJECT_IMPROVEMENT_REVIEW.md. The specific date-overflow trigger claimed is not reachable from provider data — Claude and Codex both emit RFC3339 string timestamps (0 numeric timestamps across 946 real transcripts), and Rust's parse_timestamp_value already downscales values above 1e10 before the value reaches the frontend."

title: Push review's capture-budget banner counts conversations the review filters out of every list
reason: Independently reproduced. PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:564-569 contains the quoted comment and capturePendingCount verbatim (banner at 570-577). Tracing the real flow: service.rs:6501-6507 hold_over_budget_candidates stamps blocked_conversation_decision(CaptureBudget); conversation_reconciliation.rs:246-253 blocked() sets action=Blocked, selectable=false. In the UI, sessionSyncPresentation (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:497-502) maps local_only/local_ahead with a blocked push_decision to status "unavailable". title: No error boundary anywhere: one render-time RangeError blanks the whole Tauri window with no way back
reason: Independently reproduced. Citation is exact: src/main.tsx:9 matches verbatim, and `grep -rn "componentDidCatch|ErrorBoundary|getDerivedStateFromError" src/ tests/` returns empty — no error boundary exists anywhere. src/App.tsx:30 renders `<ProjectSync/>` bare, so the proposed fix location is right. React 19 with `createRoot` and no `onUncaughtError` option means an uncaught render throw unmounts the whole root, and in a Tauri webview there is no reload affordance. All 8 `toISOString()` sites exist at the exact cited line numbers. Verified in node that `toISOString()` and `Intl.DateTimeFormat.format` both throw RangeError on an out-of-range Date. Reachability confirmed: `ended_at` flows from `parse_timestamp_value` (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/providers/timeparse.rs, reached at claude/history.rs:149 and codex/history.rs:510) which, despite its "bounded" doc comment, applies only an ms->s divide with no upper bound; project_activity.rs:989 adds `.max(started_at)` but no ceiling. Simulating the pipeline, a transcript field `"timestamp": 1700000000000000000` (nanoseconds, i.e. time.UnixNano()) yields ended_at = 1.7e15, and `new Date(1.7e15 * 1000).toISOString()` at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:671 throws RangeError, as does formatFullDateTime via Intl. However the finding's stated mechanism is inverted and must be corrected (see correction): it blames the one helper that is actually safe, and several listed helpers do not throw at all. Severity stays medium: the failure mode is catastrophic and unrecoverable (entire window blanks, no way back), but the trigger requires a malformed transcript with a nanosecond-or-larger timestamp, which normal Claude/Codex transcripts (RFC3339 strings or second/ms epochs) do not produce.
correction: The defect (no error boundary; a reachable render-time RangeError blanks the Tauri window) is real, but the mechanism is misattributed. Corrected: the hazard is the bare `* 1_000` at the seven inline call sites, not `toEpochMilliseconds`. Rust's `parse_timestamp_value` already normalizes any value > 1e10 by dividing by 1000, so a nanosecond timestamp (1.7e18) reaches the frontend as 1.7e15 seconds — not 1.7e18 ms as the finding claims. Multiplying that by 1000 at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:404/671/1445/1923/1966, SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx:161 and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:719 gives 1.7e18 ms, outside Date's +/-8.64e15 range, so `toISOString()` throws RangeError; `formatFullDateTime` throws identically via `Intl.DateTimeFormat.format` (clock.ts:55, not :56). Conversely, `toEpochMilliseconds` (clock.ts:26-27) — the helper the finding blames — is the safest path in the set: `sessionDetailModel.ts:245` receives 1.7e15 and returns it unscaled as 1.7e15 ms, which is inside Date's range and renders "+055840-11-08" without throwing (it would throw only for a raw JSON value above ~8.64e18, near u64 max). Also, `formatSessionDetailClock` and `formatDateTime` use `toLocaleString`/`toLocaleTimeString`, which return the string "Invalid Date" and do NOT throw, so they are not part of the cascade. Minor citation slips: LogPanel is at src/components/LogPanel.tsx, not src/components/project-sync/LogPanel.tsx. The fix should therefore harden the seven inline `new Date(x * 1_000).toISOString()` sites (guard on `Number.isFinite(date.getTime())`), add the ErrorBoundary in App.tsx as proposed, and ideally add an upper bound in parse_timestamp_value rather than relying on frontend guards alone.
