title: Push review's capture-budget banner counts conversations the review filters out of every list
reason:
No user-visible defect, and the behavior it objects to is a deliberate rule of this screen.

1) The banner's actual copy never claims the deferred rows are listed. Title: "N conversations wait for the next round"; message: "This review's 512 MB capture budget filled before their turn. Push the selected conversations first, then open Push review again." That is accurate and gives the exact remedy. The only false text is the internal code comment at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:563-565 ("stay visible and unselectable"), which no user ever reads. The finding's claimed impacts ("cannot tell which sessions were deferred… no way to verify") are consequences the shipped copy does not create.

2) Hiding non-selectable rows is intentional and load-bearing, not an oversight. sync-review/pullReviewStatus.ts:9-19 states it: "Push review contains only work that can publish from this computer", and isPushReviewDecision requires selectable && (publish|create_cloud). That one gate filters the session list (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1545), the older-entries list (:1596-1600) and visibleConversations (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:437) alike.

3) The exact pattern the finding calls a bug is already shipped and committed. pushReviewPullHolds (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:160-167) matches push_decision.action require_pull / require_pull_metadata — decisions that fail isPushReviewDecision and whose statuses fail isPushReviewStatus — so those rows are absent from every Push-review list too, yet HEAD ships the "N conversations held for Pull" banner for them (present at line 538 of git show HEAD:…PushResourceWorkspace.tsx, unchanged by this diff). The review's grammar is: the list holds only pushable work; the banner zone accounts for what is held back and names the action that clears it. The new capture-budget banner was written to that same recipe, one banner below the precedent.

4) Verification is available on realistic paths. Outside selection mode the Activity page lists every session unfiltered (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1538 `if (!selectionMode) return allSessions;`), so the deferred sessions are still visible with their local-outstanding status; and the banner disappearing when Push review is reopened after the push is precisely the confirmation the message instructs. Per the design record (memory push-review-capture-budget, and the comment at src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:6720-6727), the state only arises when candidate capture exceeds the 512 MiB MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES — a cold start after a storage wipe + metadata reset with hundreds of unsynced sessions — and it clears itself over successive rounds.

5) The finding's first proposed fix would make things worse: rendering inert capture_budget rows breaks the invariant that every row listed in Push review is selectable work, and would drag in the section counts and tri-state head semantics that assume it.

Residual: a stale code comment, invisible to users, with no behavioral consequence. There is also no test covering the banner either way, so nothing regresses.
correction: The accurate, much narrower statement: the code comment at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:563-565 ("Candidates the review could not afford to capture stay visible and unselectable") describes behavior the review does not have — capture_budget rows are filtered out by isPushReviewDecision like every other blocked decision. The banner text itself is correct and needs no change, and the absence of the rows matches the existing "held for Pull" banner precedent.

title: Switcher menu has no max-height or scroll, so its verb footer falls off the clipped window on long switch lists
reason: Reproduced in a browser against the real stylesheet. Citation is exact: SyncPathBar.tsx:349 is the sync-path-menu-foot block verbatim, and .sync-path-menu (App.css:3061) computes to max-height:none / overflow:visible with no scroll region anywhere in the chain (.sync-path-menu-group has no CSS rule at all; html/body/#root, .app and .sync-app are all overflow:hidden). git diff HEAD confirms the regression: the verbs were previously the first group right under the header and are now a footer after the whole switch list. Probe with real App.css and real shell nesting (.app > .sync-app > .sync-workspace > .sync-pathbar), fonts awaited, hit-tested with elementFromPoint().closest(): menu top 64px; at 800x560 the verb strip stops being clickable at 10 targets (verb bottom 580.2 vs 560), at the default 1100x720 at 15 targets (750.2 vs 720); document.documentElement.scrollHeight === clientHeight, so no page scroll exists. otherProjects (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2362) is unbounded user data. One detail the finder missed makes it worse, not better: the verbs stay in menuOptions, so arrow-key focus reaches them and scroll-into-view scrolls the overflow:hidden .sync-app shell (measured appScrollTop 236, .sync-pathbar top -228), sliding the whole window chrome off the top with no pointer route back. Severity downgraded to medium because the trigger needs 11 total projects at the configured minimum window size, or 16 at the default 1100x720.
correction: The switch list holds *other* projects, so the trigger is 11 total projects at the 800x560 minimum window (9 targets is the last that fits) and 16 total at the default 1100x720 (14 targets is the last that fits) — not "10+ projects". Of the stranded verbs, only "Rename project…" and "Agent profile…" exist nowhere else; "Reset local sync state" is also reachable from PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:590/839 and RestorePlanView.tsx:489, and "Reveal in Finder" also appears on the storage crumb. The same footer-below-an-unbounded-list shape applies to the storage crumb switcher at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2348. The proposed CSS fix is correct as written.

title: Pull is permanently disabled and mislabelled "Loading storage changes…" when the in-review comparison fails
reason: The finding's central claims do not hold against the actual code. (1) "The only explanation offered is the tooltip" is false: ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1751-1759 pushes a `comparison-failed` warning into the NoticeZone rendered unconditionally at line 1786 inside the embedded review (line 2093, not gated by selectionMode), reading "Comparison with <storage> failed — <error> Every row below falls back to an unknown status."; every row also gets `Not compared. <error>` from unresolvedSyncPresentation (line 630-635). The user gets a truthful, prominent, visible explanation. (2) The activity-load half of the trigger is already handled in place: `loadError && activity === null` renders a whole-page error state inside the review with a "Try again" button (lines 1834-1842) wired to onRetryLoad -> loadWorkspace (line 2348), which re-runs both `load` and `loadComparison`, restoring reviewListReady in one click. (3) "Permanently disabled" is wrong: the review header carries a close control (RestorePlanView.tsx:547, `close={{ ariaLabel: "Close pull review for …", onClose: onBack }}`); closing and pressing Pull again re-runs planRestore and remounts the page. Recovery is two clicks, prompted by the visible failure notice. (4) The gate is an intentional fail-closed safety decision, documented in the code at RestorePlanView.tsx:363-366: "until it reports ready, the primary must not apply a selection the user has not seen." Without the comparison, every row's status is unknown; the proposed fix ("stop gating the primary on reviewListReady once the load has settled in failure") would re-enable a data-mutating Pull over an unverifiable list, reintroducing exactly the hazard the gate exists to prevent. (5) The path is narrow: beginProjectRestore (ProjectSync.tsx:2459-2534) only opens the review after planRestore succeeds — a full storage read — and a planning failure never opens the review and surfaces its own action_failed notice, so the scenario requires the storage to be reachable at plan time and then fail on the comparison invoke a second or two later during the review mount. What genuinely survives is a stale tooltip string and a missing in-place retry for the comparison-only failure — a copy/polish gap on a transient-race path where the user is already correctly informed and can recover.
correction: Narrowed and de-escalated: on the specific race where the activity load succeeds but the immediately-following thread comparison fails inside an open Pull review, the disabled primary's tooltip is stale ("Loading storage changes…" after the load settled in failure) and there is no in-place retry for the comparison — unlike the adjacent activity-load failure, which does render a "Try again" button. The disabled state itself is a deliberate fail-closed gate and is correct; the user is told what failed by a visible NoticeZone warning and by per-row "Not compared." badges, and recovers by closing the review (header close control) and pressing Pull again. The fix worth making is tooltip copy plus optionally a retry action on the existing comparison-failed notice — not removing the reviewListReady gate.

title: A failed project-file scan leaves the Push review showing an endless "Scanning project files" skeleton
reason: Independently reproduced by reading the source. The quoted code is verbatim at src/components/project-sync/ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:562-566 (line number exact). scanPendingProjectFiles (src/components/project-sync/ProjectSync.tsx:1963) sets projectContentScanned: true only inside the success path (line 2010; grep confirms it is the sole write); its catch sets only pushError and its finally clears projectContentLoading. So after a failed first scan the props at the call site (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:790-822) are scanned=false, loading=false, rows=[] — and eligibility falls back to {state: "eligible"} for a non-git project, which is precisely the case where showProjectFiles is true (ProjectSync.tsx:1918) and scanned starts false (line 1917). The branch therefore renders LoadingScaffold, which prints "Scanning project files…" behind a 150ms gate with .status-loader (App.css:136-145, animation: spin 0.9s linear infinite) — permanently, since the autoScanRequested ref (line 313-320) blocks any relaunch. The Rescan button (line 553-557) is enabled and reads "Rescan", not "Scanning…", beside it. The parent's error Notice (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:827-845) renders in addition to the body, not instead of it. No guard, fallback, override, or call-site condition avoids this; no test covers it (the frontend suite uses renderToStaticMarkup, where LoadingScaffold's 150ms gate returns null, so no gate could catch it).
correction: The defect is real, but the impact is milder than "a user will wait for a scan that is not running": a red blocking Notice carrying the failure text renders in the same short view and an enabled Rescan retry sits in the toolbar directly above the skeleton. The bug is a stale, contradictory progress indicator that survives until unmount or a successful rescan — confusing, not a dead end. It is also reachable only for non-git projects (git repos either get scanned=true from a locked inventory or never render the Files step).

title: A failed project-file scan leaves the Push review showing an endless "Scanning project files" skeleton
reason: The impact claim does not survive contact with the file. (1) The failure IS surfaced adjacent, not distantly: PushResourceWorkspace renders the pushError Notice as a sibling OUTSIDE the scroll box (`.sync-inline-action-scroll`, max-height min(54vh,590px)), pinned to the bottom of the same tab panel. On this exact path the body is empty, so the scroll box collapses to ~the toolbar plus the skeleton and the red box lands immediately beneath it — it cannot be scrolled out of view. Notice.tsx:73 maps timing="blocking" to role="alert", so it is announced assertively; LoadingScaffold is role="region" and announces nothing, so there is no competing AT signal. The premise "a user who does not notice the error banner will wait" requires ignoring a red alert box a few inches below the skeleton in a small dialog panel. (2) It is not endless: the toolbar's Rescan sits directly above the skeleton and is enabled after the failure (disabled={disabled || loading || !eligible}, loading is false), and the auto-scan guard `autoScanRequested` is a useRef that resets on unmount — the page is conditionally rendered on activeStep === "project_files", so the footer's own step navigator (history <-> project_files) remounts it and re-fires the scan automatically. Both plausible reactions to a stuck skeleton actually start a real scan. (3) The trigger is narrow: the skeleton needs scanned===false AND rows.length===0, so only a failed FIRST (auto) scan on a push context that returned no project_files entries qualifies; a failed rescan keeps scanned true and leaves the existing rows on screen. (4) It is a deliberate contract: the comment at ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:308-311 shows the author reasoned about this failure path and chose parent notice + Rescan as the retry, with the ref guard explicitly there to stop a failing walk from looping. (5) No consequence beyond presentation: projectContentInventory stays null so nothing wrong travels on Push, no data is lost, no state is unrecoverable, and closing/reopening the review re-runs the scan. What is actually defective is one clause of a code comment plus a placeholder that reads as progress while idle — cosmetic, not high.
correction: Accurate statement: when the auto-scan on mount fails and the push context carried no project files, the Project files tab keeps rendering the "Scanning project files…" LoadingScaffold as an idle placeholder even though no scan is running. The failure is not hidden — a role="alert" danger Notice is pinned in view directly below it — and recovery is one click on the adjacent enabled Rescan button, or automatic on any step round-trip (the page unmounts, resetting the autoScanRequested ref, and the auto-scan re-fires). The defect is a contradictory placeholder plus a stale clause in the comment at ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:308-311, not a stuck or unrecoverable state. Low severity, cosmetic.

title: `project_files_error` is never read, so a failed project-file inventory silently removes the Files step from the Push review
reason: Independently reproduced in source. ProjectSync.tsx:1875-1878 matches the quote verbatim and the flag at line 1918 is `showProjectFiles: !isGitRepository || lockedProjectContentInventory !== null`. Repo-wide grep for `project_files_error`/`projectFilesError` finds it only in src/types.ts:786 (declaration), service.rs (7351/7464/7556/7566/7581), commands.rs:1483 and one Rust test — no frontend reader. service.rs:7546-7559 confirms `wants_project_files` is true exactly for GitManaged and that a build failure leaves `project_files = None` while setting the error; failure is reachable via `project_content_versions(&snapshot.manifest)?` (service.rs:2607-2610) and the other `?` sites in build_project_files_inventory. In PushResourceWorkspace.tsx a false flag removes the step from `syncReviewSteps` (408), from `projectReviewTabs` (714) and hides the footer step button (877 `{showProjectFiles && (`), with nothing rendered in its place — identical to a git project whose stored inventory is legitimately empty. The sibling `threadComparisonError` does raise a danger banner (582-593), and `git diff HEAD` shows commands.rs gained logging for BOTH errors in this same working tree while only the comparison error was wired into the UI. No recovery path: the `showProjectFiles: true` at line 2011 belongs to the scan handler whose button lives inside the hidden step, and service.rs:7541-7543 says git-managed projects never use that Scan button. Not high, though: the error path is narrow, nothing is written incorrectly (a null inventory simply contributes no project-file actions), the reason still reaches the user-visible activity log via ActivityLogScope, and reopening the review retries.
correction: Two claims in the finding are imprecise. (1) "no UI consumes it" — the backend warning added at commands.rs:1483 is emitted through ActivityLogScope, which does surface in the app's activity log; what is missing is any surfacing inside the Push review itself. (2) For a Git-managed project the inventory is built from remote/base manifest entries with no local walk (service.rs:7541-7543, 2596-2610), so the hidden step is the surface for reviewing/removing files already stored in the bundle, not a set of local working-tree files the user believes are being published. Also, the `remote` Err sub-case (service.rs:7568-7573) sets `thread_comparison_error` as well, which does raise the danger banner — the fully silent case is `build_project_files_inventory` failing while the remote snapshot opened successfully. Accurate statement: when `build_project_files_inventory` fails for a Git-managed project, `prepare_push_review` returns `project_files: null` with `project_files_error` set; ProjectSync.tsx never reads that field, so `showProjectFiles` is false and the Project files tab, step navigator entry and footer step button are all absent, indistinguishable from a genuinely empty stored inventory, with no in-review banner and no retry affordance.

title: `project_files_error` is never read, so a failed project-file inventory silently removes the Files step from the Push review
reason: The claimed impact does not hold. `project_files_error` can only fire for Git-managed projects (service.rs:7460 gates `wants_project_files` on `eligibility.state == GitManaged`), and for those projects the Project files step is entirely read-only: `rowIsSelectable` (ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:186) returns false for any non-eligible binding, the page renders a "Project files are locked." danger notice, and no checkbox is emitted (pinned by tests/frontend/project-files.integration.test.tsx:865). So the hidden step publishes nothing, removes nothing, and alters no push decision. The finding's core claim — "the user pushes believing there is nothing to publish outside conversations, when in fact the check never completed" — is wrong: `build_project_files_inventory` is called with `discovery: None` for Git-managed bindings (explicit comment: "Git-managed inventories never walk local content"), so no local file is ever a push candidate on this path. Nothing can be silently left behind. Second, the dominant failure mode is already surfaced: the `Err(error)` arm at service.rs:7563-7568 assigns the identical message to both `thread_comparison_error` and `project_files_error`, so an unreachable/offline/credential-failed storage already raises the `comparison-failed` danger banner wired at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:582. The genuinely silent residue requires a Git-managed project plus a reachable remote plus a corrupt manifest (duplicate project-content resource id, or a logical path failing `project_content_relative_path`) — a bundle-integrity defect Mallard authors itself. Third, the state is indistinguishable from the normal case by design: `lockedProjectContentInventory` is equally null for a successful empty inventory, which is what nearly every Git-managed project returns, so there is no baseline a user could notice deviating from. Fourth, this is a deliberate choice, not a forgotten sibling: the comment added in the same working tree at commands.rs:1474 says the reason "must reach the log, not only the context the frontend may or may not render" — an argument for the log as the channel, not for a banner — and `push.project_files_failed` is emitted at warning level into the user-facing ActivityLogDrawer, which has a level filter. The asymmetry with `thread_comparison_error` is coherent: that one leaves every conversation row unselectable at 0/0, a review that cannot do its job, whereas this one hides a locked, uneditable listing.
correction: Accurate reduced form: in the rare case where a Git-managed project's remote manifest fails to parse while the storage is otherwise reachable, the Push review omits the read-only "Project files" listing of already-stored remote entries, with the reason visible only in the activity log (`push.project_files_failed`, warning level). No selectable content, no publishable content, and no push outcome is affected — the Git-managed step is locked and checkbox-free by design. This is an observability nit, not a data-integrity or silent-omission bug.

title: Pull is permanently disabled and mislabelled "Loading storage changes…" when the in-review comparison fails
reason: Reproduced by reading the source; every citation is accurate. RestorePlanView.tsx:375-381 is verbatim, including the line number. ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2252 (`reviewListReady = activity !== null && !loading && comparison !== null && !comparisonLoading`) and the loadComparison catch at 2214-2217 (`setComparison(null); setComparisonError(...)`, with `comparisonLoading` cleared in the finally) are verbatim. So when the comparison invoke rejects while a Pull review is open, `comparison` stays null with nothing in flight, `reviewListReady` reports false forever, and `primaryDisabledReason` sticks at "Loading storage changes…" — which is false, the load already settled in failure. Both Pull controls are gated on it: the footer button at RestorePlanView.tsx:692 (`disabled={busy || primaryDisabledReason !== null}`) and the path-bar Pull at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2619 via ProjectSync.tsx:3475-3476 (`continueDisabled: !pullReviewPrimary || pullReviewPrimary.disabledReason !== null`). I looked for the escape hatches a finder could miss and they are genuinely absent: refreshEpoch={0} is hardcoded (RestorePlanView.tsx:581) and comparisonOverride is not passed, so the mount effect's deps (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2250) never change; there are no event listeners or intervals in ProjectActivityPage that re-run the comparison; the comparison-failed notice at 1751-1759 has no `action` (unlike the refresh-failed notice at 1713-1724, which does carry a Try again button); and the path-bar refresh is unavailable because ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:3302 gates the standalone activity page on `!inlineStorageReview` while ProjectActivityPage's unmount cleanup nulls the header model, making `viewRefresh` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2569) falsy. The state is reachable: src-tauri/src/project_sync/commands.rs:425 returns Result<_, String> and the frontend's own comment ("A whole-comparison failure belongs in the shared notice zone") shows the authors expect it.
correction: Two claims are imprecise and should be narrowed. (1) The trap is comparison-only failure, not "the thread comparison (or the activity page load)": a failed activity load sets `loadError`, which renders a "Try again" box (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1841) and a retry notice action (1719) whose `onRetryLoad` calls `loadWorkspace` — and that re-runs `loadComparison` too, so the load-failure path recovers on its own. (2) "No on-screen hint" overstates it: a warning notice IS rendered above the list ("Comparison with <storage> failed — <error> Every row below falls back to an unknown status."); what is missing is a retry on that notice and any connection between it and the disabled button, whose tooltip actively contradicts it. Also, one unsignposted escape short of abandoning the review exists when the plan carries project-file content (showProjectFiles, RestorePlanView.tsx:301): switching to the "Project files" step and back unmounts and remounts ProjectActivityPage, re-running loadWorkspace and hence the comparison. Conversation-only plans have no step navigator and no such escape. Severity is medium rather than high: the block lasts only for that review mount, closing and reopening the review recovers, no data is lost, and it needs a transient comparison failure — but the primary action of the review is dead-ended behind an untruthful "still loading" message with no in-review retry.

title: Capture-budget conversations are filtered out of the Push review that the new banner points at
reason: Independently reproduced in source. All citations are verbatim and the line numbers are right: PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:564-569 holds the comment plus capturePendingCount; ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1545 is the compound filter; pullReviewStatus.ts:17-18 gates on decision.selectable; conversation_reconciliation.rs:246-252 sets selectable:false for every blocked decision. The exclusion is in fact stronger than claimed — ProjectActivityPage.tsx:496-500 maps a blocked push decision on local_only/local_ahead to status "unavailable", so isPushReviewStatus already fails before isPushReviewDecision runs, and the identical predicate repeats in olderEntries (1592-1602), so the rows are absent from the older-window fold as well. Reachability is real: service.rs:6728-6756 runs fit_capture_budget then hold_over_budget_candidates (6501-6507), which overwrites push_decision with the CaptureBudget blocker on entries already present in review.entries and leaves entry.state untouched; types.ts:1253 carries the blocker to the frontend. The banner zone (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:729-739) renders above the tab panel unconditionally, and selectionReviewEmpty (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1682-1687) is satisfiable when sessions and olderEntries are both empty, so the "Nothing to push" empty state can co-render with the warning banner. I found no guard, fallback, or alternate render path that puts capture-budget rows back on screen.
correction: Two qualifications the finding overstates. First, the same banner-for-rows-held-out-of-the-list pattern is already the house convention: pushReviewPullHolds (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:160-167) counts require_pull / require_pull_metadata entries whose statuses (cloud-outstanding, divergent, synced) are equally excluded by isPushReviewStatus, and the project-file banner is the same shape — so the empty-state/banner contradiction is pre-existing and shared, not introduced by the capture-budget change. Second, the user is not left without a reason: the banner names the count, the 512 MB cause, and the remedy ("Push the selected conversations first, then open Push review again"). The confirmed defect is therefore narrower than stated: the comment at line 564 asserts visibility the code never provides (the syncHoldDetail sentence added at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1119 for "capture_budget" is currently unreachable for push-review rows), and the all-over-budget case renders a contradictory "Nothing to push" beneath the banner.

title: Switcher footer reduces menu verbs to unlabelled icons, dropping the visible disabled reason a comment explicitly requires
reason: Reproduced in source. renderPill is at SyncPathBar.tsx:223 exactly as quoted. Only renderItem (line 190) renders disabledReason as a visible second line, and in switcher mode renderItem is called solely for labelled "Switch to" groups; the first unlabelled group (verbs) and all trailing unlabelled groups (tails) go through renderPill, where disabledReason exists only in the title attribute. git diff HEAD confirms the regression: the deleted renderer drew every item as a full row with detail = (inert && item.disabledReason) ? item.disabledReason : item.detail. CSS at App.css:3231-3282 confirms .sync-path-menu-verb is a 32px icon puck with no text and no content rule, and no later rule or media query overrides it. Call sites check out: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2283 (unlink, danger, icon link-off) is a verb, so it renders as a wordless red glyph; ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2317 (link-storage) is a tail, so it keeps its visible label but loses the visible reason "Everything you've added is already linked", contradicting its own source comment, and no menuBanner covers that case (storageMenuBanner is set only for workspaceControlsLocked). The finder also missed a worse instance: StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1236-1245 puts disabledReason "This row is not linked to it yet" on the unlink VERB, so both label and reason are invisible there. The interface doc at SyncPathBar.tsx:44 ("rendered as its second line") is now false for pills, and no test covers any of it.
correction: Correct as stated except for one detail: `detail` is not lost for verbs — the `caption` built at SyncPathBar.tsx:180-183 prints "label · detail" for every verb carrying a `detail` into the full-width `.sync-path-menu-cap` row (this is what the App.css:3223 comment describes for "Agent profile…"). `detail` is lost only for tail pills. `disabledReason` is title-only for both verbs and tails. Also, "Link storage…" is a tail pill and therefore keeps its visible label; only its reason line is lost. The strongest instance is StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1239, where `disabledReason: "This row is not linked to it yet"` sits on the `unlink` verb, so the row is reduced to a greyed red icon with neither label nor reason on screen.

title: Switcher footer reduces menu verbs to unlabelled icons, dropping the visible disabled reason a comment explicitly requires
reason: The finding's two concrete examples are both wrong, and the underlying shape is an intentional, user-picked design. (1) ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2285 "Unlink from <project>…" has NO disabledReason — its only disabled cause is workspaceControlsLocked, which the crumb's visible menuBanner explains in prose at the top of the menu (comment at 2261: one banner "instead of a tooltip per greyed row"); it also isn't a bare destructive click, since ProjectSync.tsx:2830 gates it behind a confirm() naming storage and project and deletes nothing. (2) "Link storage…" (2318) is in the TRAILING unlabelled group, so renderPill(tail=true) draws a text pill with its label visible — it loses the reason line, not its words, and the enabled "Add storage…" pill sits beside it. Only two disabledReason strings in the app reach a pill at all (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2321 and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1239); both keep role="menuitem", aria-disabled, roving tabindex, and the reason as title, which AT exposes as the accessible description, so the focusability/keyboard contract (which is written on the .sync-path-menu-item rows, and those still print reasons as a second line at SyncPathBar.tsx:190) is intact. The icon-pill verb footer is the design the user explicitly chose on 2026-09-01 (memory record switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md: direction "B · Switcher" picked from the menu-mockup.html specimen, verbs as 32px icon pills in a footer strip, then extended to the storage crumb and ⋯ on request), documented again in App.css:3225 and SyncPathBar.tsx:120-129; every verb across all five switcher menus carries an icon, so no pill renders wordless-and-glyphless, and no test asserts the removed text.
correction: The accurate, much smaller residual: two disabled reasons — "Everything you've added is already linked" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2321, on a labelled text pill) and "This row is not linked to it yet" (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1239, on an icon verb) — now surface only via the title tooltip and the accessible description instead of a visible second line. The unlink example carries no disabledReason and is unaffected.

title: The new switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard and is an invalid child of `role="menu"`
reason: The mechanics are right but the impact is not. The switcher already ships the keyboard affordance the WAI-ARIA menu pattern prescribes: type-ahead at SyncPathBar.tsx:281-303 (500 ms buffer, repeated-first-letter cycling, label matched from .sync-path-menu-copy > span or aria-label) lets a keyboard user jump straight to a distant target, so the claimed consequence — "must arrow through the whole unbounded list" — does not occur. The search pill is a deliberate pointer convenience on top of that: the design memory for this very change (switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md, B · Switcher, 2026-09-01) records the shipped contract as "filters on label+detail, ArrowDown/Up step into the list, Enter activates the first .target, typeahead skips the input", and the typing branch at lines 264-274 exists precisely so a user who clicked into the field can step out of it; App.css:3202 gives the input a :focus-visible style for that click-focus path. The ARIA half is likewise not novel: role="menu" here already held non-menuitem children before this change (.sync-path-menu-banner and the .sync-path-menu-current header row are both pre-change per git diff), and the file carries an explicit comment at lines 306-309 reasoning about that exact constraint — a considered house pattern, not an oversight. Because the filter can only be driven by pointer entry, a screen-reader user in menu navigation mode never reaches the "No match." paragraph and is served by type-ahead instead. The only real residual is a narrow capability difference — the field matches a substring of label+path while type-ahead matches a label prefix — which is a minor polish item, not a keyboard-inoperable feature.
correction: Accurate residual: the search field can only be focused with the pointer, so keyboard users fall back to the existing menu type-ahead, which matches a label prefix rather than a substring of label+path. Switching remains fully keyboard-operable; what is unavailable by keyboard is path-substring filtering.

title: A failed autosave wedges project setup: Finish goes dead with no reason and no retry
reason: The citation is accurate and the mechanism reproduces from source. ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:584-589 does exclude saveState === "error" from canFinalize; the autosave effect (299-335) clears dirtyRef at line 305 before awaiting at 308 and its catch (324-328) never restores it, and since the failure path calls no setDraft the effect's deps [draft, draftId] don't change either — so no automatic retry occurs and Finish stays disabled. grep confirms setSaveState appears only at 306/310/326/340, so there is no retry control anywhere. However two claims in the finding are false. (1) "no reason": lines 995-997 render a blocking danger Notice containing the actual error text from the same catch, directly above the footer — the user is not left with just the two words "Not saved". (2) "permanently": edit() at 337-342 sets dirtyRef.current = true and saveState = "saving" and calls setDraft, which re-runs the effect and retries; auditing every disabled= prop (634, 686, 708, 768, 777, 804, 837, 912, 951, 973) shows they all gate on `working` (busy || finalizing, both false here), so every field remains interactive — only "Add storage" (867) is blocked by the error state. Severity is further reduced by the backend reality: update_setup_draft_with_repository (src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:13926) fails chiefly on a missing/non-directory project root, a malformed path, or a stale revision, and for all of those the user's corrective action is itself an edit, which re-arms the save. Only a transient IPC/disk failure would genuinely need a Retry button. Nothing is destroyed — the persisted draft is intact — so the destructive-safety category does not fit.
correction: A failed autosave leaves saveState === "error" with no automatic retry (the catch at ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:324-328 does not restore dirtyRef, and the effect's deps do not change), which disables Finish until the user happens to edit some other field — every field stays enabled and any edit re-arms the save. The failure reason IS shown, in a blocking danger Notice above the footer; what is missing is an explicit retry affordance and any hint that editing something is the way out.

title: Capture-budget conversations are filtered out of the Push review that the new banner points at
reason: Verified in the real files. Filtering unselectable rows out of the Push list is this codebase's deliberate, documented policy, not an oversight: `RequirePull`/`RequirePullMetadata` also return None from `planned_action()` (conversation_reconciliation.rs:114-121) and are therefore equally invisible, yet the app already ships the `pull-holds` banner (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:507-549) counting exactly those invisible rows with an "Open Pull review" route, and docs/DESIGN_PUSH_PULL_FLOW.md:237 states the rule ("unselectable in push review; the jump to pull..."). The capture-budget banner follows that same established grammar: count + reason + the exact next step. The remedy is round-based (held candidates are re-admitted newest-first on the next review), so row identity carries no user decision, and the sessions remain fully visible on the ordinary non-selection Activity page. The claimed contradictory empty state is unreachable in the shipped configuration: `selectionReviewEmpty` needs `sessions.length === 0`, but `fit_capture_budget_with` seeds `spent` from `base_selection`, which contains only conversations of providers WITHOUT a tail cursor (service.rs:6631-6642), and both shipped adapters return `supports_tail_cursor() == true` (claude/mod.rs:260, codex/mod.rs:121). So `base_selection` is empty, `spent` starts at 0, and the newest candidate is always admitted unless one single JSONL transcript exceeds 512 MiB — not realistic data. At least one selectable row therefore always survives whenever the banner fires. What remains is a stale code comment at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:564-566 that no longer describes the code — a documentation nit, not a state-coverage gap or user-visible defect.
correction: The only accurate residue: the comment at src/components/project-sync/PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:564-566 ("Candidates the review could not afford to capture stay visible and unselectable") contradicts the shipped list policy, under which every blocked/unselectable decision — capture_budget included, exactly like the existing require_pull holds — is routed out of the Push review list and represented by a counted banner instead. Fix the comment, not the filter.

title: Path-bar switcher menus have no max-height and are hard-clipped by the app's `overflow: hidden` root
reason:
Citation is exact. `<repo>/src/App.css:3061` opens `.sync-path-menu { position:absolute; top:calc(100% + 6px); left:0; z-index:30; min-width:260px; max-width:380px; padding:8px; … }` verbatim, and `App.css:7` has `html, body, #root { height:100%; width:100%; overflow:hidden }`. App.css is the only stylesheet in src/, and a full grep of it shows no `max-height` or `overflow` on `.sync-path-menu`, `.sync-path-menu-group`, or any later override (`8225`, `9083-9114` only set fonts). No JS sizing either: `SyncPathBar.tsx` never measures or clamps the menu (no inline style, no portal); the menu is a plain child of `li.sync-path-item` (`App.css:2565`, `position: relative`).

Clipping chain confirmed: `.sync-pathbar` (App.css:2534) uses `container: sync-pathbar / inline-size` (layout, not paint containment — its own comment says so, so it does not clip), `.sync-workspace` is explicitly `overflow: visible` (App.css:8607), and the clipper is `.sync-app { height:100%; overflow:hidden }` (App.css:804-811) inside the `overflow:hidden` root.

Reproduced, not merely reasoned: I served a specimen that links the real App.css and reproduces the exact switcher DOM the component emits (header row with path detail, `.sync-path-menu-search`, 20 one-line `.sync-path-menu-item.target` rows — project targets are one line because `detail = reason ?? (target && item.detailIsPath ? undefined : item.detail)` suppresses the path — and `.sync-path-menu-foot`). Measured: rows are exactly 34px, menu top 64px, computed `max-height: none`, `overflow-y: visible`. At 1000x720 the menu is 868px tall, bottom 932, the whole footer strip sits at 856-930 (below the 720 fold), 4 rows are below the fold, `.sync-app` reports scrollHeight 932 vs clientHeight 720 with `overflow-y: hidden` (clipped, not user-scrollable), and the document root is not scrollable. At the 560px `minHeight` from src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (width 1100, height 720, minHeight 560), 9 rows plus the whole footer are clipped. Solving for the threshold from the measured 188px of chrome: ~13-14 targets at 720px, ~9-10 at 560px — the finding's arithmetic holds. `.sync-history-branch-menu` in the same bar (App.css:4932/4972) already does exactly the proposed fix (`max-height: min(360px, calc(100vh - 130px))` + an inner `overflow-y:auto` list), so the fix matches house pattern.

Two corrections rather than refutations. (1) Keyboard focus is not stranded on invisible rows: focusing the last row scrolls the `overflow:hidden` `.sync-app` programmatically (measured scrollTop 372) — the rows do become visible, but the entire app chrome is dragged off-screen (pathbar top -364) with no user-visible way to scroll back. (2) Severity is medium, not high: it needs ~14+ (or ~10 at min height) sibling projects — the dev's own ~/.mallard/sync_config.json has 6 projects / 5 storages, below even the SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR of 6 targets; typing in the always-visible search field filters the list and brings the footer back into view; and both clipped tails have alternate entry points (ProjectSidebar.tsx:788 "Add project", ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2908/3023 "Link storage").
correction: `.sync-path-menu` (src/App.css:3061) sets no `max-height` and no `overflow`, and its only scroll-capable ancestor is `.sync-app` (src/App.css:804-811, `height:100%; overflow:hidden`) inside the `overflow:hidden` root, so a switcher taller than the viewport is hard-clipped with no scrollbar. Measured on the real stylesheet with the real switcher DOM: 34px target rows plus ~188px of chrome (header row, search field, footer strip) means the `.sync-path-menu-foot` — carrying the verbs plus "Add project…"/"Link storage…" — falls entirely below the fold at roughly 14 switch targets in the 720px default window and roughly 10 at the 560px `minHeight`; at 20 targets in a 720px window the menu is 868px tall and the footer sits at 856-930. Mouse users cannot reach the clipped rows or the footer at all. Keyboard users do reach them, but only because focus scrolls the `overflow:hidden` `.sync-app` container (measured scrollTop 372), which drags the path bar and the whole app chrome off-screen with no way to scroll back. Severity medium: it needs an unusually large project list, the always-visible search field filters the menu back into range, and both "Add project…" and "Link storage…" have alternate entry points in the sidebar and the workspace body.

title: The new switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard and is an invalid child of `role="menu"`
reason: Verified in source. src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:328-337 renders the search input as claimed (the ` is 345 not 355) and focusMenuEdge is not used by this file at all — it is imported only by StorageCatalogPage.tsx:585 — but that does not change the mechanism. title: Path-bar switcher menus have no max-height and are hard-clipped by the app's `overflow: hidden` root
reason: The CSS defect is real and reproducible as described — .sync-path-menu (App.css:3061) has no max-height or overflow, the switcher is a fixed 380px column, it is position:absolute in the path bar (not portalled; TopLayer is only used for the debug popover), and the root is overflow:hidden (App.css:7). So I cannot refute the mechanism. But "high" is inflated on three counts. (1) The trigger is a power-user tail state, not a realistic default: projects are registered one at a time through a folder picker -> setup draft -> storage link -> profile flow (ProjectSync.tsx:1503), and ~15 registered projects are needed to overflow the shipped 1100x720 window; the 560px figure additionally requires dragging the window to its exact minimum height. The storage half of the finding is effectively unreachable — otherStorages is the storages linked to this one project (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1443, 2270), realistically 1-3, never ~15. (2) Nothing becomes unreachable. The sidebar is always mounted, lists every project (ProjectSidebar.tsx:856-913) and carries permanent "+ Add project" and "+ Add storage" buttons in its section headings (ProjectSidebar.tsx:783-791, 1014-1022) that stay visible even when a section is collapsed; agent-profile and reset-sync-state also sit on the project index rows (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2954, 3171, 3330). The crumb menu duplicates the primary navigation; only "Rename project…" is unique to the clipped footer. (3) The menu already carries the design's own answer to scale: the search field appears at >=6 targets (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR, SyncPathBar.tsx:129/174) and renders above the list, so it is on screen in every overflowing state — one keystroke filters the list and pulls the footer back. The claimed keyboard consequence is also wrong: overflow:hidden still creates a programmatically scrollable box, so focus() from moveMenuFocus scrolls off-screen rows into view (ugly, since the whole shell shifts, but not a dead end). What I could not refute is intent: the codebase's own sibling — .sync-history-branch-menu, the same path-bar-anchored absolute dropdown with a variable list (App.css:4939-4948, max-height: min(360px, calc(100vh - 130px)) plus .sync-history-branch-options with max-height + overflow-y:auto) — is capped and scrolled, so this is an omission against an established in-repo pattern rather than a deliberate decision, and the proposed fix matches that precedent. Verdict: a real but minor polish defect in a rarely-reached state where every clipped function but one has an always-visible alternative.
correction: At roughly 15+ registered projects on the default 1100x720 window (or ~10 with the window dragged to the 560px minimum), the project crumb's switcher menu runs past the bottom of the viewport and the root's overflow:hidden clips the tail rows and the whole .sync-path-menu-foot strip with no scrollbar. The state is self-healing — the search field that appears at >=6 targets sits above the list, and typing anything shrinks the menu back into view — and every clipped command except "Rename project…" has an always-visible duplicate in the sidebar or on the project index, so this is a polish gap, not a lockout. It should still be fixed to match .sync-history-branch-menu (App.css:4939-4948), which caps its height and scrolls only its option list.

title: A failed autosave wedges project setup: Finish goes dead with no reason and no retry
reason:
The headline ("goes dead with no reason and no retry") is contradicted by the code the finding itself cites, and the guard it flags is a deliberate fail-closed mechanism.

1. A reason IS shown. The autosave catch at ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:323-327 calls `setError(errorMessage(reason))`, and line 984-993 renders that backend message in a blocking danger `Notice` directly above the footer — the source comment there says explicitly "What fills it is an autosave or a Finish that failed... it stops the flow". The messages name the fix ("project root '/x' is not a directory", "setup draft 'd-1' does not exist"). The footer's "Not saved" is a status pill, not the only feedback.

2. It is not wedged. `saveState === "error"` disables exactly ONE control — "Add storage" (line 867). Every content control (display name line 766, Change… folder 777, provider toggles 804, profile selects 673/686/708, Storage select 837, repository choices 912/951/973, acknowledge checkbox) is gated only on `working` (busy||finalizing). Any of them calls `edit()` (line 337-341), which sets `dirtyRef.current = true`, flips `saveState` off "error", and produces a new draft object, re-running the effect and retrying the save. Every mutate spreads into a fresh object, so identity always changes. And the most likely failure — a project root deleted/renamed mid-setup — is fixed by exactly such an edit (Change…).

3. Two more labelled exits. Discard is an always-enabled footer button (line 1007, only disabled while finalizing). Close is a header button whose aria-label is literally "Close setup; the draft is kept" (line 736); ProjectSync.tsx:3853-3855 mounts the workspace conditionally with `key={setupDraftId}`, so close+reopen remounts, reloads the draft from disk and resets saveState to "idle" — the documented "survive navigation and application restart" behavior in docs/PLAN_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_WORKFLOW.md:99-104.

4. The blocked Finish is intentional, not an oversight. persistence.rs:1250-1268 gives setup drafts optimistic concurrency: every save bumps `revision` and a stale revision is rejected. `finalize()` (line 500-517) pins `expectedRevision = draft.revision` and finalize_project_setup reloads and revalidates the draft from disk (docs "Safe Finalization", steps 1 and the note "preserving the revision protections"). Finishing while the on-disk draft is behind the UI would register a project from a stale record. `saveState !== "error"` in canFinalize is that protection, so the "destructive-safety" category is inverted — the flagged line is the safety.

5. Trigger rate is very low. `updateSetupDraft` is a local Tauri IPC writing one JSON file under ~/.mallard behind a file lock. It fails only if the project root vanishes/unmounts mid-setup, the draft file is deleted, the disk is full/read-only, or a revision conflict occurs — and a conflict is unreachable with one mounted editor, since `savingRef` serializes saves and each success adopts `saved.revision`.

What survives is a small polish nit, not a medium destructive-safety defect: the catch does not restore `dirtyRef.current`, so a failed pass does not re-queue itself and recovery needs a user action (any edit, close+reopen, or Discard) rather than happening automatically.
correction: Narrowed: the autosave catch (ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:323-327) does not restore `dirtyRef.current = true`, so a failed save is not automatically re-attempted and the edits since the last success stay unpersisted until the user touches a field again. Recovery is user-driven but readily available and signposted — the backend error text renders in a blocking danger Notice above the footer, every content control stays enabled and any edit retries the save, and Discard/Close (which remounts and reloads the draft) are labelled footer/header buttons. Finish being disabled while the draft is unsaved is intentional: finalize pins the draft revision and the store rejects stale revisions.

title: Catalog and setup-draft list failures are swallowed, so the sidebar shows "Add your first…" for content that exists
reason: Verified against the real file. All three cited catch blocks exist at the exact cited lines (refreshSetupDrafts catch 1390, refreshStorageSetupDrafts catch 1410, refreshCatalogScopes catch 1542, comment text verbatim), and loadShell's destructure at 1030 is `const [projectsResult, , , , repositoryKindsResult] = await projectReads;`, eliding the three middle allSettled slots. Because the helpers swallow instead of rethrowing, they are always `fulfilled` and contribute nothing to `failures` (947) or `setBackendError` (1069), and they never call setError; every other call site is `void refreshCatalogScopes()/refreshStorageSetupDrafts()`, so no other surface reports the failure. storageCatalogApi.listScopes is a bare invoke("list_catalog_scopes") (src/components/storage-catalog/api.ts:51) and can genuinely reject. catalogScopes initializes to [] (346) and is reset to [] on host-identity change (871), and ProjectSidebar.tsx:949-957 renders "Add your first resource" purely on catalogScopes.length === 0 with NO loading guard (contrast the Projects section at 853, which does gate on `loading`), so a failed catalog listing is rendered as a factual first-run empty state with no notice anywhere. No guard, fallback, retry, or later override rescues this. The one part that does not hold is the Storages half: that empty state (1030) is `storages.length === 0 && storageDrafts.length === 0`, and `storages` is `config.storages` (ProjectSync.tsx:3649), whose load failure IS reported via `failures.push("Configuration: ...")` (996) — so a failed draft listing cannot hide configured storage rows, only drafts. Severity lowered because the trigger is a per-command backend failure that does not take down the sibling reads on the same IPC transport, nothing is lost or overwritten, and the display self-heals on the next successful refresh; the concrete harm is a misleading affirmative empty state for Catalog and silently vanished resumable drafts.
correction: refreshSetupDrafts (catch at 1390), refreshStorageSetupDrafts (1410) and refreshCatalogScopes (1542) all swallow their rejection, so loadShell's Promise.allSettled (1018-1024) always sees them fulfilled and they contribute nothing to `failures`/`backendError` — no notice appears on any screen. The confirmed user-visible consequence is: (a) a failed `list_catalog_scopes` on a cold start (or after a host-identity change, which clears catalogScopes at 871) leaves catalogScopes empty, and ProjectSidebar.tsx:949-957 renders the first-run "Add your first resource" with no loading guard, presenting a failed read as "you have no resources"; (b) an interrupted project or storage setup draft silently disappears from the sidebar. The claim that the Storages section shows "Add your first storage" despite the user having rows is wrong: that empty state (ProjectSidebar.tsx:1030) also requires `storages.length === 0`, and `storages` is `config.storages`, whose load failure IS folded into `failures` at line 996 — so configured storages are never hidden by this bug; only draft rows are.

title: Catalog and setup-draft list failures are swallowed, so the sidebar shows "Add your first…" for content that exists
reason:
The code shape is as quoted (ProjectSync.tsx:1390, 1410, 1542 swallow; loadShell:1018-1022 allSettled), but the claimed user-visible consequence does not survive contact with the rest of the system.

1. The realistic failure mode is already covered by a hard screen. All three listings and every other shell read go through the same `~/.mallard` root and the same process-wide `persistence_guard` (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/persistence.rs:2577). Any environment-level failure (missing/unreadable root, poisoned lock, permissions) fails `getHostIdentityStatus`, which `loadShell` awaits FIRST (ProjectSync.tsx:953-969) and on whose failure it returns `unavailableResult()`; the app then renders the full-screen "Host identity unavailable" recovery page with a Retry (ProjectSync.tsx:3515-3539). The sidebar is never painted in that state. There is no plausible cause that takes down only these three commands while getConfig, listProjects, listAgentProviders, listProviderProfiles and listBindings all succeed.

2. The per-file corruption case is deliberately fail-soft in the backend and never rejects. `list_setup_drafts` (persistence.rs:1203) and `list_documents` (1609) turn a malformed or oversize draft into a warning and still return the readable drafts ("A malformed draft file becomes a warning instead of hiding the readable drafts behind one error"); `list_storage_setup_drafts` (1312) does the same with fixed, secret-safe sentences. A missing directory returns an empty list, which is genuinely empty. So the corrupt-state scenario produces partial lists, not a swallowed rejection.

3. The concrete impact claims are contradicted by the code. The Storages empty state is gated on `storages.length === 0 && storageDrafts.length === 0` (ProjectSidebar.tsx:1030), and `storages` is `config.storages` (ProjectSync.tsx:3649) — from `getConfig`, which DOES push into `failures`. A user "who has rows" never sees "Add your first storage" from a draft-listing failure. And acting on a false prompt cannot create duplicates: `create_setup_draft_with_repository` (service.rs:13838-13847) finds the existing draft for the same canonical root and returns `resumed: true`, which the UI announces as "Resumed setup draft for …" (ProjectSync.tsx:1518); `create_catalog_scope_with_repositories` (storage_catalog/service.rs:748-755) refuses a duplicate (profile, kind) with "this Catalog row already exists", which surfaces through `error`. The "invites the user to create a duplicate" harm does not exist.

4. It is an intentional, commented design decision with a cost to reversing. All three comments say the same thing ("Drafts are a convenience surface; the projects list stays usable", "The menu is a convenience surface; the rest of the shell stays usable"), landed across three commits (8a11bbf, 96e1e41, f956ad8). The helpers have 17 call sites, six of them fire-and-forget `void refreshX()` — a Tauri event listener (1422) and child callbacks (3760, 3768, 3841). Making them reject would turn those into unhandled rejections and would raise a red "Project-sync backend unavailable" notice after actions that already succeeded (add/remove scope, save draft), which is a worse state-coverage bug than the one alleged.

The only residual sliver is `list_catalog_scopes`, which rejects wholesale when a scope references a missing profile (storage_catalog/service.rs:325). There is no delete-profile command, so that requires hand-edited or partially-restored `~/.mallard` state — and in that state the DTO genuinely cannot be built, so rows could not be shown regardless. The global "Reload app data" / Retry already recovers it. Polish at most, not a medium defect.
correction: Narrowed to what actually holds: if `list_catalog_scopes` rejects — reachable only via hand-edited local state where a Catalog scope references a missing catalog profile — the Catalog pane silently renders the first-run "Add your first resource" prompt with no notice, recoverable only through the global Retry. The project- and storage-draft listings are fail-soft in the backend and their empty states are additionally gated on config-derived data, so they carry no equivalent exposure.

title: A failed tool-detail fetch hides the preview payload the row already has, and offers no retry
reason: Independently reproduced. The citation is exact: SessionDetailToolCall.tsx:188 holds the danger Notice and :191 holds the `!detailState?.error` guard that gates ToolPayload; lines 140-141 match verbatim. The previews are real, not hypothetical — claude/history.rs:1524 and codex/history.rs:2464 populate argument_preview/result_preview on every timeline-page tool event under a 1 MiB budget (app_settings.rs:165), and session_detail.rs:656-715 validates them on the page, so they are in memory when the row expands. The `!encoded.contains("argument_preview")` assertion at session_detail.rs:2562 covers the metadata index, not the timeline page, so it does not refute this. The error state necessarily carries `detail: null` (SessionDetailPage.tsx:270 early-returns when a detail already exists), so `argumentsValue` resolves to `tool.argument_preview` and is then thrown away by the guard. I rendered the real component with `{loading:false, error:"…", detail:null}` and populated previews: output was the Notice alone — argument preview absent, result preview absent, Paths section absent, no button of any kind. The same props with `error:null` rendered all three. Retry: re-expanding does re-fire the request (both `loading` and `detail` are falsy after a failure), so collapse-and-reopen works but is undiscoverable, exactly as claimed. No test in tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx exercises error-with-previews.
correction: Two refinements. (1) The loss is wider than stated: the `affected_paths` that came with the timeline page are discarded too, so the Paths section vanishes along with Arguments and Result — the row degrades to a bare red box with no content whatsoever. (2) One error code has a partial page-level out: `snapshot_changed` also raises a Refresh banner in SessionDetailPage.tsx:410-419, though it reloads the whole session rather than the row and the previews stay hidden until then; the other reachable codes (ProviderError from `read_event_detail`, InvalidRequest, NotFound, OwnershipChanged) have no affordance at all. Implementation note on the proposed fix: the component receives only `onExpandedChange`, so a Retry action needs a new callback prop threaded from SessionDetailPage's `requestToolDetail` — and that function must also be relaxed, since it is memoized on `toolDetails` but currently only early-returns on `loading`/`detail`, which a retry does not trip. Also worth deleting the inline comment at lines 183-187, whose premise ("it leaves the pane with no payload at all") is true only because of the guard it justifies.

title: The non-Git Files page replaces the whole view with an error box that carries no retry
reason: The claimed impact ("no retry", "generic refresh icon", "user concludes the folder cannot be scanned") does not survive contact with the code. (1) The retry is always present and is view-scoped: ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:461-467 registers the header model from the container, which renders in the error state too, and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2564-2568 renders it in the path bar with title/aria-label "Rescan project files" — not a generic label. It is enabled after a failed scan (disabled only while refreshing), sits in the 52px bar directly above the notice in the same column, and clicking it bumps scanEpoch, which the effect at lines 444-459 handles by calling setError(null) and re-running the scan. correction: A duplicate in-box retry would match StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1949-1956, but the files view already exposes a labeled, view-scoped "Rescan project files" control in the path bar during the error state, and clicking it clears the error and re-scans. title: Add Catalog resource: a failed capability load leaves an empty provider dropdown with no retry
reason: Independently reproduced in source. AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:78 is verbatim `} catch (reason) {` with `setError(errorMessage(reason))` on 79; the mount effect (67-85) has `[]` deps, no loading flag, and no re-invocation path anywhere — ProjectSync.tsx:3741 mounts it under `addingCatalogScope ?` with no key and no capability props. On rejection `setCapabilities` never runs, so `supportedProviders` (line 101, `capabilities.filter(...)`) is `[]` and the select at 269-272 offers only the placeholder; Kind radios are `disabled={working}` (false here) so they stay live, and `canAdd` requires `provider !== null` so Add is permanently disabled with no title. The Notice at 345-355 (finding said 345-354, off by one on the closing paren) passes no `action`, though Notice/NoticeShell do support one (src/components/notice/Notice.tsx:86,105), so the proposed fix is buildable. No retry exists in tests/frontend/storage-catalog.integration.test.tsx either.
correction: Two precision fixes, neither refuting. (1) The title's trigger is unreachable: `list_catalog_capabilities` is infallible in Rust — `Ok(StorageCatalogService::capabilities())` over the pure static `capability_matrix()` (src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/resource_commands.rs:28, adapters.rs:254). The reachable trigger is `listProfiles`, which does real disk work (`StorageCatalogService::from_user_home()?`, `validate_new_profile_home`, `load_profiles`, `mutate_profiles`) and can Err. Because both reads share one `Promise.all`, a profiles failure discards the capabilities that already resolved — that coupling is the actual mechanism, and splitting the two reads is part of the fix. (2) Impact is understated in one place and overstated in another: `chooseKind` calls `setError(null)` (line 114), so the user's first action in the flow erases the red box, leaving an empty provider dropdown with no explanation at all; conversely, close-and-reopen only recovers a transient failure, so it is "the only retry," not "the only recovery."

title: No React error boundary: an uncaught render error blanks the window with no way back
reason:
Not novel, and the reachability argument is factually wrong.

NOT NOVEL — already tracked by the maintainer. <repo>/docs/PROJECT_IMPROVEMENT_REVIEW.md:241 is verbatim this finding: "**19. Add a React error boundary.** `P1 · S · medium` — Zero `ErrorBoundary`/`componentDidCatch` in `src/`. One render throw ... blanks the entire desktop app with no recovery path ... Wrap the workspace, report to the activity log, offer 'reload workspace'." The absence is a known, triaged backlog item, not a discovery.

THE CLAIMED TRIGGER IS UNREACHABLE. The finding rests on "a nanosecond-precision timestamp from a provider log yields an Invalid Date and toISOString() throws RangeError." Every provider timestamp is normalized in Rust before it reaches the frontend: `parse_timestamp_value` (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/providers/timeparse.rs:5) divides any numeric above 10_000_000_000 by 1000 and parses RFC3339 strings to epoch seconds; non-integer JSON (a float) returns None, which renders as "Time unavailable"/undefined. A realistic ns stamp (1.75e18) becomes 1.75e15, which `toEpochMilliseconds` treats as ms — and `new Date(1.75e15).toISOString()` is VALID (verified in node: "+057425-04-17T15:06:40.000Z"). ECMAScript's limit is 8.64e15 ms, so a throw needs a raw provider value above 8.64e18 — within 2x of u64 overflow, i.e. corrupt garbage, not "nanosecond precision". The same arithmetic refutes the ProjectActivityPage.tsx:404/671/1445/1923/1966 sites, which multiply already-normalized seconds by 1000. All of these feed a machine-readable `dateTime=` attribute, not visible text.

THE RECOVERY CLAIM IS WRONG. `titleBarStyle: "Overlay"` (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json) hides the title text (`hiddenTitle`) but keeps the native macOS traffic lights drawn over the content — the config even positions them (`trafficLightPosition: {x:26,y:35}`). Close/minimize stay clickable, and the macOS menu bar (Mallard > Quit, Window > Close) is untouched. "Must force-quit" is false; this is a desktop app whose state lives on disk, so relaunching costs seconds.

What remains is real but generic defensive hardening with no demonstrated reachable trigger, already on the maintainer's own P1 list.
correction: The app has no React error boundary (already tracked as docs/PROJECT_IMPROVEMENT_REVIEW.md item 19, "P1 · S · medium"), so any uncaught render throw would unmount the tree. No reachable trigger was demonstrated: provider timestamps are normalized to epoch seconds by parse_timestamp_value (timeparse.rs:5) before reaching sessionDetailDateTime, and even a nanosecond-scale value produces a valid Date rather than a RangeError. The window also retains its native macOS traffic lights under titleBarStyle "Overlay", so the user can close and relaunch rather than force-quit.

title: No React error boundary: an uncaught render error blanks the window with no way back
reason: Citation is accurate (src/main.tsx:9 verbatim, no error boundary anywhere in src/, React ^19.1.0, tauri.conf.json lines 16/21, App.css:7-11), but both load-bearing claims fail. (1) The reachable trigger does not exist. So a nanosecond log timestamp (~1.7566e18) arrives at the frontend as 1.7566e15; toEpochMilliseconds passes it unscaled and new Date(1.7566e15) is a VALID Date, since the ECMAScript time-value limit is 8.64e15 ms, so toISOString() returns an expanded-year string ("+057648-...") rather than throwing RangeError. Triggering a throw would require a raw provider number above ~8.64e18 (near u64::MAX); anything beyond u64 fails as_u64/as_i64/as_str and yields None, which the existing `value == null` guard at sessionDetailModel.ts:243-244 already handles. The same arithmetic clears the five ProjectActivityPage.tsx sites (404, 671, 1445, 1923, 1966), which multiply seconds by 1000. (2) "Must force-quit / no way back" is wrong. titleBarStyle "Overlay" on macOS is a full-size-content-view with a transparent titlebar; the native traffic lights remain visible and functional, and the config proves it by setting trafficLightPosition {x:26,y:35} (lines 17-20). `decorations` is not disabled.
