correction: The app has no React error boundary, so any uncaught render error would unmount the tree and leave a blank window requiring a relaunch (window controls and Cmd+Q remain functional — not a force-quit). No reachable render-time throw was demonstrated: provider timestamps are normalized to seconds in Rust by parse_timestamp_value, so the cited toISOString() calls cannot produce a RangeError from real provider data. This is defensive hardening, not a defect with a failure scenario.

title: A failed tool-detail fetch hides the preview payload the row already has, and offers no retry
reason:
The code is as quoted (SessionDetailToolCall.tsx:188-199), but the impact claims do not survive contact with the surrounding system.

1. The "no retry" claim is factually wrong. In SessionDetailPage.tsx:268-271, `requestToolDetail` early-returns on `if (existing?.loading || existing?.detail) return;` — an errored entry is deliberately NOT excluded. Collapsing and reopening the native `<details>` re-fires the fetch through `handleToolExpandedChange`. Retry is bound to the same disclosure control the user just clicked.

2. The dominant (effectively only) reachable failure already has a first-class recovery elsewhere. Enumerating `get_project_session_event_detail` (session_detail.rs:1775-1835): `invalid_request` "The timeline event does not exist." and "Only tool-call events have expanded detail." are unreachable from a UI that offers expansion only on tool rows it rendered from that same snapshot; `not_found` means no registered provider; the `provider_error` cases need the transcript to be unreadable at a known span. What a real user hits is `snapshot_changed` (line 1790) — the transcript grew while the pane was open. The catch handler sets `setSnapshotChanged(true)`, and SessionDetailPage.tsx:410-421 then renders a page-level blocking notice, "This session changed. / Refresh before continuing so pages are not mixed across snapshots," with a working **Refresh** button, and re-times the whole NoticeZone to blocking so it announces. The proposed per-row Retry would fail identically on every press until that Refresh happens — a strictly worse affordance than what ships.

3. The proposed fix contradicts a stated invariant of this codebase. Under `snapshot_changed`, `tool.argument_preview`/`result_preview` are from the superseded snapshot. Rendering them beside a banner that says do not mix pages across snapshots is precisely the mixed-snapshot state the pane is built to refuse.

4. Design intent is explicit and documented. The suppression carries a deliberate comment at the site, and it is consistent with the sibling `!detailState?.loading` guard, which suppresses `ToolPayload` for the same reason — the pane renders one authoritative payload, never a preview-then-detail swap. docs/PLAN_PROVIDER_NEUTRAL_SESSION_DETAIL.md §7.3 requires only that "per-event expansion errors have local visible states" and that a malformed tool result "must not blank the rest of the timeline"; both hold.

5. Nothing is taken off the screen. The body renders only under `{expanded && ...}` (line 176), so the preview was never visible before the click. This is reduced richness in a rare degraded mode, not a content regression.

Severity is inflated: a rare error path, with retry available, with a better recovery already surfaced at page level, and the suppression being the coherent choice for the failure that actually occurs.
correction: A much weaker, non-blocking version survives and is worth at most a polish note. The in-code comment's premise — "it leaves the pane with no payload at all" — is imprecise: the timeline page does ship tool previews (built by the same `tool_payloads` reader that feeds the detail, claude/history.rs:1512-1537), so a fallback payload does exist in memory. And because `timeline_tool_preview_bytes()` and `timeline_tool_detail_bytes()` both read the single `TIMELINE_PREVIEW_LIMIT_BYTES` knob (app_settings.rs:159-172, default 1 MiB), for any tool call whose arguments+result fit the budget the expanded detail is byte-identical to the preview already held; for an oversized pair the preview is strictly richer (1 MiB per field vs. `timeline_tool_detail_budgets`' split half-budget). So rendering the preview under a non-snapshot error would be nearly free. But it must not be done under `snapshot_changed`, which is the failure users actually reach, and no Retry button should be added there — the page-level Refresh is the correct and existing recovery. Note also that the doc's original 4 KiB preview / 64 KiB detail split (§ response limits table) has since collapsed onto one knob, which is why the expand round-trip now adds little; that convergence, not the error branch, is the more interesting observation.

title: Add Catalog resource: a failed capability load leaves an empty provider dropdown with no retry
reason:
Not novel, barely reachable, and the "no recovery" claim is false.

(1) ALREADY DOCUMENTED AND TRIAGED. docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md, finding "M08 — Entry-state recovery is inconsistent", cites the identical anchors (AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx#L67 = the mount effect, #L345 = the error Notice) and states both halves of this finding almost word for word: "Setup draft load failure and Add Catalog load failure render an error without a local Retry... Add Catalog also lacks a clear initial loading state." Its prescribed repair is the same one proposed here ("Standardize one entry-state component with a title, error detail, Retry, and safe exit. Add explicit loading to Add Catalog."). This is a known, deliberately-deferred, cross-cutting backlog item — the audit's own framing is "inconsistent", not broken.

(2) THE TRIGGER IS NEARLY UNREACHABLE. Half the Promise.all cannot fail: src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/resource_commands.rs:28 is `pub async fn list_catalog_capabilities() -> Result<...> { Ok(StorageCatalogService::capabilities()) }` — pure, no I/O, no `?`, derived from the compile-time `capability_matrix()` in adapters.rs:253. The only fallible half is `list_catalog_resource_profiles`, which needs `dirs::home_dir()` plus a catalog config read via `StorageCatalogService::from_user_home()`. But the shell already reads that same store on every load — `storageCatalogApi.listScopes()` at ProjectSync.tsx:1022/1536 — to draw the Catalog sidebar the user must click through to reach Add. A user hitting this state is already in a broken-home/broken-config app, not in a Catalog-specific failure.

(3) RECOVERY EXISTS, IS VISIBLE, AND IS ENABLED. Cancel (lines 360-367) and the header X (210-218) are both `disabled={submitting}`; `submitting` is false in this failure state, so both are live. Both call `onClose` → `openCatalogIndex`, and re-entering Add remounts the component and re-runs the effect. Closing a two-field form via a labelled Cancel button and re-entering is the ordinary affordance for a workspace page, not a hidden workaround. The finding concedes the recovery exists and only objects that it "is not stated" — a copy preference.

(4) THE STATE IS NOT SILENT. The failure renders a `severity="danger" timing="blocking"` Notice (role="alert") carrying the real error text; the `attentionBadge` fires on the Agent profile band (line 256) whenever kind is chosen and provider is not; the hint at line 338 renders. Add being disabled is correct — a scope cannot be created without a provider.

(5) THE TREATMENT IS DOCUMENTED INTENT. The comment at lines 345-351 addresses this exact case: "The mount listing writes here too, and a Catalog page that could not load its providers is worth the same rung." (landed in e9a0d0d). The author considered the mount-failure state and deliberately routed it to the page-level blocking Notice.

(6) THE "NO SKELETON / POPS IN" HALF IS A HOUSE CONVENTION, NOT A DEFECT. It is a same-tick local-IPC race, invisible in practice. LoadingScaffold is used for row/detail list pages (Activity, session detail, Settings, Files, StorageCatalogPage); the setup-workspace family that this file is explicitly tested to mirror — ProjectSetupWorkspace ("It wears the project-setup language", storage-catalog.integration.test.tsx) — has no mount skeleton either.
correction: The only defensible residue: on a mount-listing failure the page offers no in-place Retry, so the user must use Cancel/X and re-enter. That is a known cosmetic polish item already recorded as M08 in docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md, whose accepted repair is a shared entry-state component across all such pages — not a change local to this file.

title: Two concurrent session row actions clobber each other's busy state
reason: Confirmed against the real file. runSessionAction at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2335 matches the quoted evidence verbatim, and the two supporting citations are exact: line 1655 passes busy={actionBusyResourceId === session.resource_id}, and line 1304 (plus 1276 for the primary openAction button) gates only on disabled={!action.enabled || busy}. Busy state is two scalars declared at 2158-2159, so it can name exactly one row at a time. Row B's buttons stay enabled while row A is in flight; clicking B overwrites both scalars, which re-enables A's buttons and stops A's spinner while A's request is still running (A can be launched again), and the first promise to settle runs the shared finally, nulling the state so the still-running row shows no spinner and accepts more clicks. There is no entry guard, no per-call ownership check in finally, and no ref; the dispatch site at 2348 is an unguarded passthrough. The race window is substantial rather than theoretical: execute_project_session_action (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/project_activity.rs:1396) loads bindings and runs a full adapter.discover() provider-home filesystem scan before launching the external app. The setActionError(null) clobber at the top of the second call is also real. Severity stays low: it requires a deliberate second click inside the in-flight window, and the worst outcome is a duplicate external app launch plus a stale/absent spinner, not data loss.
correction: Precise statement: busy state is a single (resourceId, actionId) pair, so only the row currently marked busy has its launch buttons disabled (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1276 and :1304 via the busy prop set at :1655). Starting an action on a second row overwrites that pair, re-enabling the first row's buttons and clearing its spinner while its request is still in flight; the shared finally block then clears the pair when whichever request settles first completes, leaving the still-running row unguarded. The proposed fix (a Set keyed by `${resource_id}:${action_id}`, cleared only for this call's own entry) is correct; note that clearing must also be scoped in the error path, and setActionError(null) should not blank an error reported by a still-in-flight sibling call.

title: The session-detail loading skeleton draws a two-column layout the loaded page never has
reason: Independently reproduced from source. src/components/LoadingScaffold.tsx:88 matches the quoted evidence verbatim, including the line number: DetailBones' third block is `<div className="loading-scaffold-panes">` mapping `[0, 1]` to two `.loading-scaffold-pane` boxes. src/App.css:287 is `.loading-scaffold-panes { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 10px; }` and it is the ONLY definition of that class in the repo — App.css is the sole stylesheet, a repo-wide grep returns one rule plus one use site, and nothing in the RetroTheme section (~10900), the `@container session-detail-layout` queries (7853, 7871), or any media query redeclares it. So the two-column grid is unconditional at every width; `.loading-scaffold-bones { display: contents }` (App.css:201) makes the panes div a full-width child of the scaffold's flex column, so the two panes land at roughly half width each. The `detail` shape has exactly one consumer, SessionDetailPage.tsx:85 inside SessionDetailEntryState({state:"loading"}), returned at line 400 whenever detail is null with no error — a live path on every cold session open past the 150ms gate. The loaded page genuinely has no two-column content region: `.session-detail-layout` is `display:grid; gap:14px` (6935) holding a wrapping flex toolbar plus `.session-detail-timeline`; `.session-detail-event-list` is `display:grid; gap:0` (7081); the only multi-column rules in the entire 6830-7900 session-detail range are `24px` (7120) and the rail `24px minmax(0,1fr)` (7144) plus a `max-content` chip reflow (7874). I checked the strongest candidate counterexample, the tool payload pane, and it refutes itself: its comment says "Stacked, not tabbed" and `.session-detail-tool-payload` (7663) is a single-column `display:grid; gap:9px`. No guard, fallback, override, later rule, or call-site condition exists. Severity low is right: it is a transient, purely cosmetic column-count change during cold loads.
correction: Two refinements that do not change the verdict. (1) The panes block is not the only unmatched shape: `.loading-scaffold-band` (54 wrapped tiles, App.css:269) also has no counterpart in the loaded markup — the punchcard there is per-row 24px `.session-detail-event-node` tiles stacked vertically inside the rail, never a wrapped horizontal band. (2) The proposed fix should not use plain full-width card bones: loaded event bodies sit in `.session-detail-event { grid-template-columns: 24px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 0 14px }` (App.css:7144), so a faithful bone stack needs that same 24px node column and 14px gutter, with the card bones inset to the right column, otherwise the replacement still changes geometry on arrival by ~38px of horizontal offset.

title: The main empty pane offers no primary action and names only Codex
reason:
Verified against the real file. `<repo>/src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2229-2247` is the deselected backdrop (`!workspaceProject && !editingStorage && !newProjectSetup`), not an onboarding page, and the finding's core claim collapses on three counts.

(2) The StorageIndexPage/CatalogIndexPage comparison is inapt. Those are index destinations rooted at a path crumb; each already carries its own `Add …` action in the `SyncPathBar` (`StorageIndexPage.tsx:46-58`, `CatalogIndexPage.tsx:29-41`) and their `.profile-links-empty` block is a second copy of it, because their sidebar rails do not show an equivalent empty CTA in that state. (3) "Completed project" is not undefined jargon — the product distinguishes setup drafts from completed projects everywhere in this rail: the sidebar lists `StorageSetupDraft`/project drafts with "Continue setup for X" and "Discard the setup draft for X" (`ProjectSidebar.tsx:830-851`), and selecting a draft sets `newProjectSetup`, which nulls `workspaceProject` (`ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1397`) and swaps in `ProjectSetupWorkspace`. title: Two concurrent session row actions clobber each other's busy state
reason:
Code confirmed as quoted (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2335-2347, busy prop at :1655, disable at :1304), but there is no real consequence.

1) What the action actually does. `SessionActionKind` is exactly two values — `open_in_app` | `open_in_terminal` (src/types.ts:1014). The backend chain execute_project_session_action -> adapter.execute_action lands in crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/providers/{claude,codex}/actions.rs, which shell out to `/usr/bin/open` and `/usr/bin/osascript`. These are fire-and-forget launches of an external app/Terminal: non-mutating, idempotent in effect (macOS `open` on a running app just focuses it), and instantly visible to the user when they succeed. There is no write, no sync, no capture, nothing that a double-fire corrupts.

2) No stuck or wrong terminal state. Every path clears busy unconditionally in `finally`, so for any interleaving the settled state is "not busy" — which is correct. The finding names no sequence that leaves a spinner stuck on an idle row, because none exists. The entire residue is a transient missing spinner on a still-launching row for the ~0.5-2s the discovery scan takes.

3) The double-launch requires a deliberate third click. Row A's buttons re-enable only after the user has already clicked row B; to actually launch A twice the user must then click A a third time, during a sub-two-second window, for an operation whose success is self-evident (a window appears). The realistic reading of overlapping clicks on two rows is "open two sessions," and that already works correctly today — both launches complete.

4) The `setActionError(null)` claim inverts a documented intent. Clearing the last complaint when starting a fresh attempt is a codebase-wide idiom here, used at :2168 on load and at :2245 with an explicit comment ("Leaving the error and loading flags set carried the previous project's failure banner onto the next one"). A new launch wiping a prior launch's banner is the wanted behavior, not a defect.

5) Concurrency is modeled where it matters, deliberately. The same component carries `requestRef`/`comparisonRequestRef` sequence guards with commented rationale for the data loads (:2160-2161, :2248) and pointedly does not carry one for the launch actions. That is a maintainer who knows the stale-response pattern and scoped it to the calls with consequences — a design decision, not an oversight.

This is a polish observation ("could be cleaner"), not a bug a user or maintainer would ever hit with consequence. The proposed `if (actionBusyResourceId) return;` guard would be a regression: it would silently swallow a legitimate click on a second row.
correction: If retained at all, the accurate statement is far narrower: while two launch actions overlap, the spinner on the earlier row stops early, so its button briefly reads as idle while its `open`/`osascript` launch is still resolving. No stuck state, no data effect, and re-firing the launch is idempotent. Cosmetic only.

title: The session-detail loading skeleton draws a two-column layout the loaded page never has
reason: The source observation is accurate but has no user-visible consequence, and it is the codebase's deliberate design. (a) The entire `detail` shape is an impressionistic sketch, not a mirror: its second block, the 54-tile `.loading-scaffold-band` shimmer, has no landed counterpart either — there is no punchcard band anywhere in the loaded session detail (only the scaffold's own CSS rule mentions one). But it is a long-standing intentional abstraction (shipped in d78e3c5 against an already single-column detail page and kept through the specimen review), it is hidden entirely on warm opens by the 150ms gate, and it produces no scroll, focus, interaction, or accessibility consequence. More importantly the finding understates the defect: the exact fix it proposes already exists in the same file and is shadowed. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2836-2848 renders a `projects.length === 0` empty state with a folder icon, "Add a project to choose which resources and storage belong to it.", and an onAddProject button — but it lives in the main return at 2724, which the 2229 early return preempts for every no-project case (reachable only if editingStorage were truthy while storageDraft/editedStorageConfig were not, per the 1561 guard). So the fix is to delete or narrow the 2229 early return (or move the Add-project empty state into it) rather than to author a new button; onAddProject is already destructured at 622 and in scope there. The stale "git-info-heading" id and "sync-git-info-page" class on this branch mark it as a leftover of an older single-provider Git-info page.

title: The retheme's hard cast shadow is invisible in the dark theme (1.00–1.04:1) while the light theme carries it at 4.03–5.83:1
reason:
Deliberate, pre-existing, and already carried by a louder cue.

(1) NOT INTRODUCED HERE. `git diff HEAD -- src/App.css` shows the dark `--shadow-card: 2px 2px 0 rgba(26, 16, 8, 0.32)` as an unchanged context line; only the offsets on `--shadow-overlay`/`--shadow-popover` moved 4px to 3px. The value entered at commit 9d6964e. The finding's framing ("the dark block was left on the old translucent wash") assumes the wash was ever meant to be visible on dark ground.

(2) IT IS THE APPROVED SPECIMEN'S OWN TOKEN PAIR. codex-retheme-mockup.html:66, inside `:root, :root[data-theme="dark"]`, defines `--shadow-ink: oklch(8% .005 70)` — deliberately DARKER than that block's darkest surface `--desk: oklch(10% .008 70)`. Line 95, inside `:root[data-theme="light"]`, defines `--shadow-ink: oklch(38% .035 70)`, which is ~#6f6057, precisely what shipped. The user picked style A from this specimen and steered ~10 fixes live over HMR during the cutover. The light/dark asymmetry is the specimen's, reproduced faithfully — not a half-finished conversion.

(3) THE BOX GRAMMAR'S CARRIER IN DARK IS THE INK EDGE. App.css:7947 `--box-border: 2px solid var(--accent)`, with dark `--accent: #efe7d4` (App.css:8044) — a near-white 2px edge at ~15:1 on near-black, on every tile/card/button/popover. Its own comment: "the chunky 2px line is the box grammar itself, not a divider." So "in dark mode every lifted box is flat" is false; every box is outlined in bright ink. The shadow is a light-theme accent on top of that.

(4) THE TWO NAMED CUES SURVIVE. `.sync-primary-nav button.active` (App.css:8734) also sets `border-color: var(--accent)` on its 2px border AND `background: var(--surface-row-active)` — the active destination is unmistakable with or without a shadow. `.btn:active` has TWO other press signals: the base rule at App.css:325 sets `background: var(--button-bg-active)` (#362f28 against a #181512 button — plainly visible in dark) and the retheme rule adds `transform: translate(1px, 1px)`. The press is not "a bare 1px jump with nothing behind it".

(5) THE PROPOSED FIX IS BACKWARDS. Reproducing #6f6057's 4.0-5.8:1 separation against near-black grounds requires an ink LIGHTER than the paper — a highlight, not a shadow — painting a warm-grey L-rim on every button, card, tile, path pill and sidebar pane in dark mode. That is a visual redesign, and this codebase has already rejected the analogous "add shading in dark" move: the retheme memory records pill fold buttons with shadow shown live, reverted by the user, with "Don't re-propose shaded fold buttons."

(6) NO ACCESSIBILITY OR FUNCTIONAL STAKE. WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast is met by the 2px accent edge; the shadow encodes no information and gates no interaction. Nothing is unreadable, unclickable, or ambiguous. The measured 1.00-1.04:1 numbers are correct arithmetic describing a dark ink on a darker ground — the physics of the medium, not a token defect.
correction: A defensible neutral statement: "In the dark theme the cast shadow is a no-op (1.00-1.04:1 on its grounds); depth there is carried entirely by the 2px `--accent` ink edge, while the light theme spends a solid #6f6057 because a translucent tint smudged on cream." That is an accurate description of an intentional, specimen-sanctioned asymmetry — not a token-integrity bug, and not something a user or maintainer experiences as breakage.

title: The retheme's hard cast shadow is invisible in the dark theme (1.00–1.04:1) while the light theme carries it at 4.03–5.83:1
reason: Citation is accurate and my numbers reproduce the finder's (dark --shadow-card composites to 1.00-1.08:1 on every dark ground; light #6f6057 hits 4.03:1 on --retro-frame-gutter). But the finding fails as a defect claim on four independently checked points. (1) Not this diff: git diff shows App.css:8074 as a CONTEXT line — dark's --shadow-card is untouched; the only dark shadow edits shrank --shadow-overlay/--shadow-popover from 4px to 3px offsets. (2) The history is mis-stated: the blocks never shared a construction. Light's pre-diff value was rgba(82,58,43,0.07) — a 7% wash of a MID-brown — while dark's is rgba(26,16,8,0.32), 4.5x the alpha of a near-black. Dark is not "the old wash" light abandoned; the light edit fixed the light-specific smudge its own comment names. (3) No working dark solid was lost: `git show HEAD:src/App.css | grep retro-bevel-shadow` returns only the two definitions and ZERO consumers — it was a dead token, and its dark value #0a0807 measures 1.05:1 on --bg-0 anyway. Dark's cast shadow has never been visible at any commit. (4) The proposed fix is arithmetically impossible. --retro-frame-gutter in dark is #040303 (Y=0.00098); pure black against it is 1.0195:1 — WORSE than the current token, which composites lighter (rgb 11,7,5) and reaches 1.027:1. Matching light's 4:1 would require Y≈0.154, a mid-grey ~#6d6d6d offset band — a glow, not a shadow, and a direct contradiction of the palette rule at App.css:7979 ("the shadow ink is warm brown-black, never blue"). Finally the impact is overstated: dark --accent is #efe7d4 and --box-border is `2px solid var(--accent)` (App.css:7947), so every retheme box wears a near-white 2px ink edge that I measure at 15.05:1 on --surface-card — that edge, not the shadow, is the box grammar in dark. .sync-primary-nav button.active (8734-8738) additionally flips border-color to --accent and background to --surface-row-active, and .btn:active (8505-8508) retains transform: translate(1px,1px). Verified there is no [data-theme]-scoped shadow override (only 8676-8678, a logo filter) and App.css is the only CSS file.
correction: Accurate residual statement: dark --shadow-card (App.css:8074) composites to 1.00-1.08:1 against every dark ground, so the offset band contributes no perceptible separation (ΔL* ≈ 0.20 on --bg-0, ≈ 1.2 on --retro-frame-gutter), whereas light's #6f6057 carries 4.03-5.83:1. This is a pre-existing property of a subtractive shadow on a 1.6%-luminance ground, unchanged by this diff, and it is not correctable by "a solid dark ink" — no ink darker than #040303 exists. If the intent is that dark boxes should read as lifted, that is a design question answered by the 2px --accent edge already on every box (15:1), not a token-parity bug; any real fix would have to abandon "shadow" in dark for a light-side bevel/highlight, which contradicts the palette comment at App.css:7979.

title: Keyboard focus on a session-detail tool row draws nothing: a 2px --accent outline is inset exactly onto the row's 2px --accent border
reason: Independently reproduced. The citation is exact: src/App.css:7583-7586 declares `.session-detail-tool-call > summary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: -2px; }` and src/App.css:7565 gives that same summary `border: var(--box-border)` with `border-radius: 8px`. Resolving the var chains myself: `--box-border: 2px solid var(--accent)` on bare :root (App.css:7947), and `--focus-ring: var(--accent)` in BOTH palette blocks (App.css:8070 dark, App.css:8182 light) — so ring colour is identical to border colour in both themes (#efe7d4 dark / #2a211d light). Cascade offers no rescue: the app-wide default at App.css:38-41 (`summary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px }`) is specificity (0,1,1) and earlier in source, losing to the row rule's (0,2,1); the only later rules on this element are App.css:10969 (`box-shadow: none`) and App.css:10980 (`:active { transform: none }`); no rule re-colours the summary border, and `:focus-visible` changes no background (`:hover` and `[open]` do, but keyboard focus triggers neither). App.css is the only stylesheet in src/, imported once at src/App.tsx:10. Markup confirmed at src/components/project-sync/session-detail/SessionDetailToolCall.tsx:144-157 — `<details className="session-detail-tool-call …"><summary>`, a natively focusable direct-child summary, so the selector matches the real tab stop. I rendered the shipped geometry in a browser rather than trusting the spec: with a red outline at -2px the entire 2px border band turns red with no cream visible, proving the outline is painted exactly over the border; with the real accent colour the focused row is indistinguishable from the unfocused one; red at -4px shows border plus a separate inner ring. The regression claim also checks out — `git show HEAD:src/App.css` lines 7331-7358 show the summary previously had `margin: 0 -8px; padding: 4px 8px; border-radius: 3px` and no border, so the same -2px ring was the only ink there and was visible. Keyboard users get zero focus indication on the session transcript's tool rows (WCAG 2.4.7 failure).
correction: Accurate as stated; one refinement to the fix. Because the app-wide default at src/App.css:38-41 already renders a visible `outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px` for every `summary:focus-visible`, simply deleting the override at src/App.css:7583-7586 restores a visible ring (provided no ancestor clips the 2px outward offset). `outline-offset: -4px` is the other verified-visible option. Also worth noting the app-wide rule means this is a local override introducing the defect, not a missing style.

title: Warning glyphs painted in raw --yellow measure 2.19–2.49:1 in the light theme against 8.0–11.1:1 in dark
reason: The numbers check out but the impact premise does not. (1) This is an explicit, documented, tested design decision, not an oversight: both palette blocks state the two-rung doctrine in prose (App.css:8054 "error sentences and status copy must clear 4.5:1 where a 3:1 glyph can ride the brighter raw signal"; the light comment at 8166 mirrors it), and tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx is a purpose-built contrast gate that names the 3:1 non-text floor twice, gates every `-text` rung at 4.5 against its own composited tint, and deliberately leaves the raw hues ungated. That gate already records this exact case being caught and fixed where it mattered: "Amber `pending` once measured 2.22 here" — the status badge that carried meaning alone was moved to --thread-status-local #895503. (2) All five cited sites pair the mark with text that states the same fact, which is WCAG 1.4.11's own carve-out for graphics not required to understand content: SyncPathBar.tsx:311 is Icon name="refresh" + {banner} (not a warning glyph at all); ConversationPathRepairNotice.tsx:89 sits inside a button labelled "Repair"; SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx:71 sits beside {outcome.title}; ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1799 sits beside No agent profile is connected. with a "Choose Agent profile" button. (3) The sidebar case the finding calls sharpest is the most explicitly handled: ProjectSidebar.tsx:874 carries the comment "The triangle is decorative, so the button's accessible name must include the project issue" and the aria-label appends "Project issue: No agent profile is assigned". `.needs-profile` paints nothing, so the triangle is the row's only mark — but the row is not actionable for this condition; it navigates to ProjectActivityPage, which restates it in bold high-contrast text with a CTA, and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1423 repeats it. No user reaches a state where the dim triangle is the last word; missing it costs an early hint, not the information. (4) The proposed fix would collapse the mark/prose rung distinction the whole retro theme is built on, and darkening light --yellow to clear 3:1 on near-white cream pushes it toward brown — which is exactly what --warning-text #885e06 already is.
correction: The real residual is narrower than claimed and is a documentation inconsistency, not an accessibility defect: the light palette's comment at src/App.css:8166 signs off a 2.4:1 amber as "fine for glyphs" while the dark block at 8054 and the css-hygiene gate both put the glyph bar at 3:1. Reconciling that comment (or nudging light --yellow a step darker so the raw hue matches its own stated 3:1 bar) is worthwhile polish. The one soft user-facing item is that the ProjectSidebar.tsx:891 triangle is dimmer than ideal for low-vision sighted users, whom the aria-label does not serve — but since `.needs-profile` is a redundant wayfinding hint whose condition is restated in high-contrast text with a CTA on the page it links to, this is not a WCAG 1.4.11 violation and no information is lost.

title: The settings switch's off-state thumb is nearly invisible in the light theme (2.50:1) but clear in dark (7.06:1)
reason:
The finding's load-bearing premise is factually wrong. It claims "its off state is conveyed only by the thumb ... the track itself is --switch-off in both states." src/App.css:4327-4330 says otherwise:

  .sync-settings-switch:checked { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--accent); }

The whole 36x20 track flips fill AND border on check. Measured off-track vs on-track: LIGHT #ad9e92 -> #2a211d = 6.06:1; DARK #575048 -> #efe7d4 = 6.44:1. That is the state signal, and it is at near-perfect theme parity — a 6% difference, not the claimed 2.8x asymmetry. In light mode an off toggle is a tan pill and an on toggle is a near-black pill; those cannot be confused. State is in fact triple-encoded (track fill, thumb position via translateX(16px), thumb color), so the 2.50:1 vs 7.06:1 pair the finding measured is an internal decorative boundary, not the state cue.

It is also an intentional, documented decision. src/App.css:7937-7941 states the codebase's own doctrine: "The boundary of anything the user operates — inputs, selects, drawn checkboxes — must clear 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11). Only --border-strong does". The switch honors exactly that with `border: 1px solid var(--control-border)` (line 4307). docs/PLAN_GLOBAL_SETTINGS_PAGE.md:129-134 records the construction on purpose, calling out that checked = --accent track + --accent-contrast thumb is what keeps the thumb "visible in both palettes" (15.17:1 light, 15.65:1 dark).

Two of the finding's own supporting numbers are wrong in ways that invert its parity thesis. The rim is --control-border (resolving through --border-strong), and it measures 4.55:1 in light (#7a7065 on #fcf7f0), not the claimed 6.48:1 — and the finding never measured the dark rim, which is only 2.66:1 (#66574f on #171412). So on "finding the control," light is the better theme and the only genuine parity gap runs opposite to the claim.

Non-visual state is correct: SettingsPage.tsx:83-94 renders a real <input type="checkbox" role="switch"> with `checked` and `aria-label`, and App.css:38-43 gives every input a 2px accent focus-visible ring. Realistic path is weak too: all three preferences default on, so a user seeing an off switch just watched a near-black pill become tan under the stepped 90ms transition.

Residual (cosmetic only): the light off thumb is 1.03:1 against the paper, so it reads as a hole punched through the tan pill rather than a distinct dot. That is a coherent idiom on this single sepia-axis palette, and "nearly invisible" overstates 2.50:1 for a solid 12x12 square. The one fair point is that docs/PLAN_GLOBAL_SETTINGS_PAGE.md:222-224 asserted the switch token pairs were "already used at >=3:1", which is not true of the light off pair — so a small tightening is defensible polish, but no state is unreadable and no user or maintainer hits a real consequence.
correction: Not a state-legibility or theme-parity defect. State is carried by the track fill flipping to --accent on :checked (App.css:4327-4330), at 6.06:1 light vs 6.44:1 dark — parity. The accurate, much narrower statement: the light theme's off thumb (#fffaf4) sits at 2.50:1 on its --switch-off track and 1.03:1 against the card, so it reads as a paper-colored notch rather than a distinct dot; the dark equivalent is 7.06:1. Purely cosmetic, since the tan-vs-near-black pill flip carries the state and --control-border (4.55:1 light, 2.66:1 dark) carries the WCAG 1.4.11 boundary per the documented rule at App.css:7937-7941.

title: Warning glyphs painted in raw --yellow measure 2.19–2.49:1 in the light theme against 8.0–11.1:1 in dark
reason: Reproduced independently in the source. src/App.css:2285-2289 is `.sync-sidebar-profile-warning { ...; color: var(--yellow); }` with `color` on line 2288 exactly as quoted; the four companion sites at 3297, 3864, 5089 and 6031 are also real. src/App.css is the only stylesheet in src/, `--yellow` is defined exactly twice (`:root, :root[data-theme="dark"]` #f4b94f at 8050; `:root[data-theme="light"]` #d99609 at 8163), each of the five selectors appears exactly once, and nothing in the RetroTheme layer (8598+) overrides these color declarations — so there is no cascade escape. Recomputing the ratios from the hex values: #d99609 has relative luminance 0.36583, giving 2.41:1 on --bg-1 #fdf9f4, 2.49:1 on --bg-4, 2.37:1 on --surface-card #fcf7f0, and 2.19:1 on --warning-soft rgba(192,124,12,0.1) composited over --surface-popover; dark #f4b94f measures 10.39:1 on dark --surface-card. The proposed fix's number checks out too: --warning-text #885e06 is 5.40:1 on --surface-card. The sole-signal claim is confirmed and is in fact stronger than the finding states: ProjectSidebar.tsx:891-897 renders the triangle aria-hidden, the row's only other channel is the `needs-profile` class (line 866), and `grep -n "needs-profile" src/App.css` returns nothing — that class has no styling anywhere and exists only as a test hook (tests/frontend/project-activity.integration.test.tsx:2515); the row's `title` (lines 878-882) carries git/alias/root but not the profile issue, so only the aria-label conveys it. The "No profile" text in that test is a fixture `local_alias`, not a rendered label. The codebase's own gate corroborates rather than refutes: tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx:112-118 holds badge hues to 4.5:1 (not 3:1) because "the badge rim is a 1px hairline… Amber `pending` once measured 2.22" — and the alert-triangle is a 1-unit outline on a 24 grid at size={12}, i.e. a 1-device-pixel hairline, at 2.41:1.
correction: Three tightenings. (1) The explanatory comment is at src/App.css:8167, not 8166 (8166 is `--purple`); its full text continues "Each variant holds ≥4.5:1 on every paper surface down to --surface-row-active (#f0e3d5)", which the finding truncated. (2) The sidebar ground is --bg-1 #fdf9f4 (2.41:1), painted by `.sidebar-project-pane` at App.css:8764-8767 — not --bg-4; --bg-4's 2.49:1 is the app-wide best case, not the sidebar's. The dark range is 10.0-11.1:1 on the grounds actually named; 8.85:1 is the floor on --surface-row-active. (3) WCAG 1.4.11 binds cleanly only to the sidebar glyph: the other four sites (path-menu banner, history profile state, path-repair button, outcome notice head) each pair the glyph with adjacent text carrying the same meaning, so those triangles are redundant rather than "required to understand the content". They still share the raw ink and would be fixed by the same repoint, but the standards violation is the sidebar one.

title: The settings switch's off-state thumb is nearly invisible in the light theme (2.50:1) but clear in dark (7.06:1)
reason: Independently reproduced in source. src/App.css:8143-8144 carries `--switch-off: #ad9e92; --switch-thumb: #fffaf4;` inside `:root[data-theme="light"]` (block opens 8094), and 8037-8038 carries `--switch-off: #575048; --switch-thumb: #f6f2df;` inside `:root, :root[data-theme="dark"]` (opens 7982) — both verbatim at the cited lines. `.sync-settings-switch::before` at 4314-4325 paints the thumb with `background: var(--switch-thumb)` and nothing else (no border, shadow, or outline), over a track at 4309 filled with `var(--switch-off)`. Markup confirmed at src/components/project-sync/SettingsPage.tsx:85-94 (`<input type="checkbox" role="switch" className="sync-settings-switch">`), instantiated three times (434, 441, 670). No override was missed: `--switch-off` and `--switch-thumb` each have exactly two definitions and one consumer; src/App.css is the only stylesheet under src/; the file contains no `forced-colors`, `prefers-contrast`, or `prefers-color-scheme` block; and the light palette is reachable via preferences.ts:65-72, which resolves "system" through matchMedia and stamps documentElement.dataset.theme. Contrast recomputed from scratch: light #fffaf4 on #ad9e92 = 2.503:1, dark #f6f2df on #575048 = 7.061:1, light track vs --surface-card #fcf7f0 = 2.438:1, dark track vs --surface-card #171412 = 2.311:1, rim #66574f vs card = 6.478:1 — every figure in the finding matches. Nothing gates it: tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx measures text ink on surfaces only. The authored comment at App.css:4295-4299 corroborates the omission ("Checked rides --accent with the thumb in --accent-contrast so both palettes keep the thumb visible") — the checked thumb measures 15.17:1 light / 15.65:1 dark; only the off state was left unchecked. Three imprecisions, none fatal: (1) the rim is `var(--control-border)` at 4307, which resolves through `--control-border: var(--border-strong)` at 7942 — the value and 6.48:1 are right but the token name is wrong, and dark's rim is only 3.78:1 against its card, an asymmetry running the other way; (2) the off state is NOT conveyed by the thumb alone — `:checked` at 4327-4330 also swaps the track from `--switch-off` to `--accent`, in light #ad9e92 to #2a211d, a 6.06:1 change, so on/off stays legible at a glance from the track fill; (3) the proposed #8d7d70 measures 3.82:1, not ~3.6:1.
correction: The off-state thumb of `.sync-settings-switch` measures 2.50:1 against its track in the light palette versus 7.06:1 in dark — a same-construction theme asymmetry that puts the light off-state position indicator below the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor. The on/off distinction itself is NOT lost, because `:checked` (App.css:4327-4330) also swaps the track from `--switch-off` (#ad9e92) to `--accent` (#2a211d), a 6.06:1 change; what falls below floor is the thumb as a discernible sub-component, not the state signal. The rim token is `var(--control-border)` (App.css:4307), aliased to `--border-strong` at 7942 (light #66574f = 6.48:1 on card; dark #7a7065 = only 3.78:1). The proposed #8d7d70 measures 3.82:1, not ~3.6:1.

title: Keyboard focus on a session-detail tool row draws nothing: a 2px --accent outline is inset exactly onto the row's 2px --accent border
reason:
The finding reads one rule in isolation and misses the cascade. Two rules later in the same sheet also match this element, and one of them wins.

App.css:8526-8533 (verified by reading the file):
  .sync-app button:focus-visible,
  .sync-app input:focus-visible,
  .sync-app select:focus-visible,
  .sync-app textarea:focus-visible,
  .sync-app summary:focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring);
    outline-offset: 2px;
  }

Specificity of `.sync-app summary:focus-visible` is (0,2,1) — identical to `.session-detail-tool-call > summary:focus-visible` (0,2,1) at App.css:7583. Equal specificity, so source order decides, and 8526 comes after 7583. The `.sync-app` rule therefore overrides BOTH declarations, including `outline-offset`, making the effective offset +2px, not -2px.

The row is always inside `.sync-app`: SessionDetailToolCall (src/components/project-sync/session-detail/SessionDetailToolCall.tsx:145) renders under SessionDetailPage, mounted at src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:3352, which ProjectSync renders at src/components/project-sync/ProjectSync.tsx:3797 — inside the `className={`sync-app…`}` root opened at ProjectSync.tsx:3627. No portal is involved (no createPortal in either file).

Verified empirically rather than by reading: I served the real src/App.css with the real DOM shape (div.sync-app > details.session-detail-tool-call > summary), tabbed to the summary with an actual keypress so :focus-visible genuinely matched, and read the computed style:
  fv: true, outline: "2px solid rgb(239, 231, 212)", outline-offset: "2px"
A rule-enumeration pass over the loaded sheet listed all three matching :focus-visible rules in source order, with `.sync-app summary:focus-visible {outline-offset: 2px}` last. The screenshot shows the focused row wearing an unmistakable double line — the 2px accent border plus a separate 2px accent ring outside it with a dark gap between them.

So the claimed "draws nothing" state never renders. The report's browser experiment reproduced the geometry of the single rule it quoted, not the geometry the app actually computes.

Note the same override swallows every other `outline-offset: -2px` in the file (.sidebar-section-divider:focus-visible, .sidebar-section-toggle:focus-visible, .sync-storage-index-row:focus-visible, .session-detail-payload-action:focus-visible — all specificity (0,2,0), losing outright to (0,2,1)). Those declarations are dead, which is a tidiness observation, not a WCAG 2.4.7 defect.
correction: The `outline-offset: -2px` at src/App.css:7585 is dead code: `.sync-app summary:focus-visible` (src/App.css:8526-8533) has equal specificity and comes later, so the rendered focus ring is `outline: 2px solid var(--accent)` at `outline-offset: 2px` — a visible ring outside the row's border. Removing the overridden `-2px` line (and the other four dead `-2px` offsets) would be a cleanup, with no change in rendering.

title: Two focusable readouts replace the global focus ring with a translucent shadow that never reaches 3:1
reason: The claimed impact — "a keyboard user cannot see where focus is" — is false against the actual file. Both selectors bind :focus-visible to reveal an opaque tooltip, not just the tint: App.css:5273-5277 and 5444-5448 flip the ::after to opacity:1/visibility:visible, and those tooltips are fully opaque boxes (indicator: background var(--surface-popover), border-color var(--accent), box-shadow var(--shadow-popover) at App.css:10297-10303; metric: same surface plus --border-strong at App.css:5395-5405). Focusing either element pops a bordered, shadowed popover carrying the readout's meaning in text, directly adjacent. I scanned every production instance (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:596-605/670-707, ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:177/225/234/256, ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:352-437, SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx:130-143, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:178/193/715): zero carry tabIndex={0} without data-tooltip, so the tooltip cue is universal, and all carry aria-label as well. The tabIndex exists precisely to make these hover-only readouts keyboard-reachable — the tooltip IS the focus affordance, and the translucent shadow is supplementary. title: The Settings theme segmented control clips its buttons' focus ring — overflow:hidden with a +2px outline offset
reason: Independently reproduced. Measured DOM geometry in Chrome: segment padding 0px, overflow hidden, buttons height 28px inside a 30px segment, so the button border box coincides with the segment padding box vertically and a +2px outline falls entirely outside the overflow clip. Headless render with the shipped CSS confirms: overflow:visible draws a full ring, the shipped overflow:hidden collapses it to vertical bars at the divider positions. SettingsPage.tsx:391-404 is the Theme radiogroup with three plain buttons and no roving tabindex, so all three are tab stops and keyboard focus does match :focus-visible.
correction: Two refinements, one of which makes the defect worse than described. (1) `--button-radius` resolves to 999px (pill, from the codex retheme), not a small radius, so for the FIRST or LAST button the outline is clipped down to a single bar at the one interior divider — nothing on the outer edge, top, or bottom. Focusing "System" and focusing "Light" both brighten the same System|Light divider, so the residual cue is ambiguous between two adjacent buttons, not merely faint. (2) The bars are not literally identical to the dividers: 2px --accent versus 1px --button-border, so a sighted user may notice something brightened but cannot tell which button owns it. title: The Settings theme segmented control clips its buttons' focus ring — overflow:hidden with a +2px outline offset
reason:
The CSS mechanism is real — I verified it in the live DOM, not from the quote. At src/App.css:4338 `.sync-settings-segment` has `overflow:hidden`, `padding:0`, `border:1px`, `border-radius: var(--button-radius)` = **999px**, and rendering it against the real stylesheet gives segment rect 176x30 at y=43 with buttons 28px tall at y=44 — the button border box is exactly the segment padding box, so the +2px-offset ring from src/App.css:8526 does fall outside the clip on the top and bottom edges. But three things sink the finding as stated.

(1) NOT NOVEL — the repo's own audit already owns this exact control, twice. `docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md` L03 (**Low** priority) anchors at `src/App.css#L4150`, which at the audited commit f2cdac4 is literally the `.sync-settings-segment { overflow: hidden; ... }` block I re-read, and prescribes "one segmented-control primitive ... and one focus, disabled, hover, and selected contract". M02 (Medium) anchors at `src/components/project-sync/SettingsPage.tsx#L391` — the same Theme radiogroup — for the keyboard model. So this control's focus and keyboard contract are documented, triaged open items, and the maintainers rated the focus half **Low**. Fixing M02 as prescribed (roving `tabIndex`) also makes Tab land once, on the *checked* radio, which wears the `.active` fill — shrinking this further.

(2) THE CLIP IS DELIBERATE, not stray. `--button-radius: 999px` (src/App.css:8015) makes this a pill. The child buttons carry no radius of their own, so their square `:hover`/`.active` fills would spill past the pill's rounded ends without the clip. `overflow:hidden` is the mechanism of the shipped Codex-retheme pill, and the codebase demonstrably knows the inset-ring idiom where clipping matters (`outline-offset: -1px/-2px` at `.sidebar-section-action`, `.sync-sidebar-resizer`, `.sidebar-section-divider`, `.sidebar-section-toggle`, `.sync-storage-index-row`, `.sync-pull-item-main`). This one just wasn't given one.

(3) IMPACT OVERSTATED. The claim "the user cannot tell which of System / Light / Dark is focused" and "slivers that look exactly like the existing dividers" doesn't survive the geometry. The ring's vertical edges survive the clip wherever they fall inside the control, and they are 2px of `--focus-ring` (#2a211d in light) sitting 2px *away from* the 1px `--button-border` (#9d8b7f) divider — darker, doubled width, and not coincident with it. That yields three distinguishable states (right bar only = System, bars both sides = Light, left bar only = Dark). Focus is degraded, not absent: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible is not outright failed; this is a Focus Appearance quality gap. Audience is keyboard-only users on one 3-button theme picker whose current value is always legible from the `.active` fill.

The one-line inset fix is still worth taking, but as documented Low polish (already L03), not a High keyboard-access break.
correction: The Settings theme segmented control clips the top and bottom of its buttons' focus ring: `.sync-settings-segment` (src/App.css:4338) sets `overflow:hidden` with zero padding, so the button border box coincides with the segment padding box and the global +2px `outline-offset` (src/App.css:8526) is cut. The ring's left/right edges survive as 2px `--focus-ring` bars where they fall inside the control, so the focused button is still distinguishable — the indicator is weakened, not removed. The clip itself is load-bearing (`--button-radius: 999px` pill; children have no radius), so the fix is `.sync-settings-segment > button:focus-visible { outline-offset: -2px }`, not removing the clip or adding padding. Already tracked as L03 (Low) and M02 (Medium) in docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md against this exact control.

title: The new switcher menu's search field cannot be reached with the keyboard
reason:
The code is as described, but the claimed consequence does not exist and the design is deliberate.

1) No functionality is lost by keyboard. The menu implements a full ARIA-pattern typeahead (SyncPathBar.tsx:280-297): printable characters accumulate for 500ms and focus the next option whose label starts with the buffer, cycling on a repeated first letter. It reads labels from `.sync-path-menu-copy > span` — exactly the switch-target rows the search field filters — and on a switcher the targets are rendered first, so `options[0]` (where ArrowDown lands) is already the first target. A keyboard user with seven projects presses "h" and lands on "HorrorGame"; Arrow/Home/End reach every row. Filtering is an accelerator to the same functionality, and the keyboard has its own accelerator for it. WCAG 2.1.1 asks that functionality be operable by keyboard, not that every pointer accelerator have a focusable twin — there is no failure here.

2) It is an explicit design decision, documented twice. The file comments say "Tab is not menu navigation: the menu steps aside and the bar's own tab order continues" (L255-257) and "The search field keeps its own Home/End and its characters; the arrows step from it into the list, and Enter takes the first match" (L262-264). The implementation memory for the shipped switcher (switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md, 2026-09-01) records the contract verbatim: "ArrowDown/Up step into the list, Enter activates the first `.target`, typeahead skips the input." The previous UI audit (docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md:75) lists this menu's "deliberate keyboard navigation, typeahead" as a strength, not a gap.

3) The claim that L264-274 is "unreachable code" is factually wrong, and it is the finding's main support. That branch fires whenever focus is in the input — i.e. the ordinary flow the field exists for: click the field, type, press Enter or ArrowDown. Click-then-type is the dominant use of a filter field, so the handler is live on the primary path, not dead.

4) The proposed fix contradicts the codebase's own stated ARIA doctrine and would regress others. The same file argues (L303-306) that `role="menu"` "admits only the menuitem family" — which is why the banner is not a live region. Auto-focusing a `<input type="search">` on open would put initial focus on a non-menuitem inside `role="menu"`, and would silently kill typeahead for every keyboard user (characters would be swallowed by the input) while changing what mouse users see on open.

The only residual asymmetry is that typeahead is prefix-only on the label while the field substring-matches label+detail — a marginal convenience gap for similarly-prefixed project names, not a keyboard-access defect. That is a low-severity enhancement at most, not a medium keyboard-focus bug.
correction: If anything is worth logging, it is narrow and optional: keyboard users get prefix-only matching on the label, whereas the pointer-only search field substring-matches label plus path detail. Every switch target remains reachable and selectable by keyboard via Arrow/Home/End and typeahead.

title: The SHOW filter's drawn checkbox is below the 3:1 non-text floor in both themes, and the retheme made its low-contrast state the default
reason:

THE DEFAULT IS THE WRITTEN SPEC, NOT A RETHEME SIDE EFFECT. <repo>/docs/PLAN_PROVIDER_NEUTRAL_SESSION_DETAIL.md, section 4.4 "Inspector behavior — Default state", lists verbatim: "Intermediate steps: off", "Tool calls: off", "every supported tool category: selected but disabled while Tool calls is off". NOT NOVEL, NOT LOCAL. --border-mid is the documented middle rung of a three-rung ladder (PLAN_PROVIDER_NEUTRAL_SESSION_DETAIL.md:300) used at 56 sites in App.css; the repo deliberately gates text at 4.5 and ships no 3:1 non-text gate. title: The pill radius the retheme added to the session-detail filter toggle never applies
reason: Independently reproduced in source. src/App.css:6973 opens `.session-detail-filter-toggle {` and line 6980 is verbatim `border-radius: var(--r-pill);`; src/App.css:10975-10978 is `.session-detail-filter-toggle, .session-detail-filter-box { border-radius: 0; }` (comment at 10973-10974). No other rule that can match the class declares border-radius (the class appears only at 6973, 6987 :hover, 6992 :focus-visible, 7005 .is-on, 7011, 7023, 10975, and none of the middle ones set a radius). App.css is the only stylesheet (sole import at src/App.tsx:10) and the element is a bare button with that class (SessionDetailToolbar.tsx:47), so nothing else intervenes. `--r-pill: 999px` is defined at line 8073 under `:root, :root[data-theme="dark"]`, so the var resolves and the declaration is well-formed — just outranked. git show HEAD:src/App.css confirms the base rule had no border-radius at HEAD (line 6774) while the override already existed unchanged (10683-10686), so line 6980 is newly added and dead.

At HEAD the base rule had no border-radius and the same `border-radius: 0` override was already present, so the SHOW chips rendered square before this diff and render square after — nothing changed on screen. Also, the override at 10973-10977 carries an explicit rationale comment ("square box, square corners"), so of the two proposed fixes only deleting line 6980 is consistent with the stated design intent; removing `.session-detail-filter-toggle` from the override would silently reverse a deliberate decision. title: Scrollbar thumbs sit below the 3:1 floor in both themes, and unevenly between them
reason:
The code and the numbers are as claimed (src/App.css:8416-8426; --accent #2a211d on --bg-0 #fefbf6 light, #efe7d4 on #12100d dark; the 35% oklab-with-transparent mix does composite to #b4afaa / #5f5b53). What fails is the impact and novelty case.

1) It is a deliberate, user-reviewed decision, twice over. The rule carries its own intent comment: "The thumb is a pill of the theme's own ink, faded into the paper with color-mix — no fixed grey, so it lands correctly on every tile fill in both themes." The project memory note `scrollbar-corner-inset` records that the user "reviewed four retheme options and chose to keep the current scrollbar, so this is known and accepted, not an oversight," and the current form is part of the codex-retheme cutover the user steered live over ~10 fixes. The same record documents that the alternatives are closed: `scroller:hover::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb` provably does not repaint in WebKit (no hover-reveal), and setting `scrollbar-color` disables `::-webkit-scrollbar` styling entirely. The quiet end of a narrow design space was chosen on purpose, and the surrounding grammar is consistently quiet chrome (ghosts/segments/notices "quiet by design"; the user rejected shaded pill fold buttons on the rail and said "revert").

2) The codebase already has a contrast gate and deliberately scoped it to exclude this. tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx holds notice ink, the seven verdict-bearing status badges, and --text-3 to 4.5:1 — above WCAG — with comments that explicitly reason about "the 3:1 WCAG 2.2 sets for non-text" and explain why each element is or is not held to it. Meaning-bearing pixels are gated; decorative chrome is not. That is a considered boundary, not a gap.

3) The finding concedes it is a strict improvement (light went ~1.4:1 → 2.11:1) and identifies no regression. Flagging a change that moves a number toward a floor as a defect is a polish preference.

4) The user-visible consequence is close to nil on realistic paths. This is a macOS Tauri desktop app; scrolling happens by trackpad/wheel, and a 6px non-overlay thumb with `scrollbar-gutter: stable` is positional garnish, not the operative control — no task requires locating or dragging it, and scroll position is redundantly conveyed by the content moving. Every mainstream comparison point sits at or below this: Chrome's own default thumb (#c1c1c1 on #f1f1f1) is ~1.3:1 and macOS overlay thumbs are translucent grey. Nothing here is worse than what it replaced or than the platform default.

5) The asymmetry sub-claim is a metric artifact, not a defect. oklab mixing is perceptually uniform by construction and WCAG's ratio is not, so equal ink density across inverted paper necessarily yields different ratios. The token was written to hold ink density constant — which it does — and the proposed 50%/40% split would trade that stated invariant for a heavier bar (50% light lands near #948e8c, a dark rail beside a 2px-ink-box grammar) to satisfy a floor the app's own gate does not apply to chrome.

Nothing here is unhandled, novel, or reachable as a user problem; it is a taste call the maintainer has already made and declined to change.

title: Path-bar switcher search field cannot be reached or held by the keyboard
reason: Verified in source. The search input (SyncPathBar.tsx:328-337) has no role, no autoFocus, and no ref-focus; every menu row is tabIndex={-1} (201, 233), so it is the only tabbable node in an open menu; and focusMenuOption (422-430), moveMenuFocus and the typeahead all address only menuOptions() ([role="menuitem"|menuitemcheckbox|menuitemradio], menuKeyboard.ts:11), which excludes it. Four separate Tab handlers close the menu — the container (258) and all three openers (516, 551, 618) — and .sync-path-menu[hidden]{display:none} (App.css:3080) pulls the input out of the focus order on the same synchronous React 19 discrete-event commit, before the browser's default Tab action. There is therefore no pure-keyboard path to the field, which is a genuine WCAG 2.1.1 failure for a visible interactive control, and it has zero test coverage (no hits for sync-path-menu-search or searchable under tests/). Reviewer B does not actually rebut the mechanism, and its strongest evidence overreaches: the shipped design record says "ArrowDown/Up step into the list, Enter activates the first .target, typeahead skips the input", which describes behaviour once focus is IN the input and so presumes it is reachable — it documents an intent the code does not deliver rather than blessing unreachability; the Tab comment at 256-257 predates the input's existence. But Reviewer A is right that three sub-claims are false: the Enter-takes-first-match branch (267-272) is live via the ordinary mouse-click-then-type path, the field IS held once focused (line 273 early-returns for every key but Enter/ArrowDown/ArrowUp, so characters, Home/End and Backspace all reach it), and the Shift+Tab sequence is backwards (keydown closes before focus moves, so the input is never focused-then-dropped) — and that Tab behaviour is identical in the three non-searchable menus, so it is not search-specific. Severity is medium, not high: no function is blocked, since arrows/Home/End and the label typeahead reach every switch target and the unfiltered list always renders; only the substring filter (which also matches detail/path, unlike the prefix typeahead) is unavailable. Worth a maintainer's time because the minimal fix is small — focus the input first when searchable, as ArrowDown/Enter already step out of it correctly — though the finding's Tab-trapping half is the wrong half and would push further from the menu pattern, given a bare input is already an invalid child of role="menu".
correction: The search field is unreachable by keyboard, but it is not "unholdable" and nothing is blocked. Corrected statement: when a switcher renders 6+ switch targets, the .sync-path-menu-search input is the only tabbable node in the open menu, yet nothing focuses it programmatically (focusMenuOption and moveMenuFocus address only [role="menuitem*"]) and all four Tab handlers — the menu container (SyncPathBar.tsx:258) and the three openers (516, 551, 618) — close the menu, hiding it via .sync-path-menu[hidden]{display:none} on the same synchronous commit. So a keyboard-only user can never focus the field and loses its substring filter over label+detail, falling back to Arrow/Home/End roving and the 500ms label-prefix typeahead, which still reach every target. Once focused with a mouse the field behaves correctly (line 273 passes all other keys through), and the Enter-takes-first-match branch at 267-272 is live, not dead code. The Shift+Tab claim is wrong: the handler closes before focus moves, so the input is never momentarily focused, and that Tab-closes contract is shared by the three non-searchable menus and is not introduced by this field. Minimal fix: focus the input on open when searchable, rather than trapping Tab; separately, a bare <input> is an invalid child of role="menu" and should be moved outside the menu container or the pattern changed.

title: Pull review names every conversation "Conversation" instead of its session title, which the model already carries
reason: The quoted code and line numbers are correct (RestorePlanView.tsx:234 `{item.title}`, aria-labels at 210/222), but the claimed user-visible impact does not occur on the live path. Line 234 sits inside `function ItemList` (line 137), and the default export routes conversation rows to `ItemList` only as a fallback: at lines 577-612 the history step renders `conversationItems.length > 0 && project ? : conversationItems.length > 0 ? `, and the comment at line 365 names it ("The ItemList fallback is synchronous", guarded by `activityHistoryInUse = conversationItems.length > 0 && Boolean(project)`). "Exclude" : "Include"} ${session.title || "Untitled session"}`}` (lines 1164, 1206, 1246), and storage-only rows (the ones a Pull introduces) use `entry.display_name.trim() && entry.display_name !== entry.thread_id ? entry.display_name : "Untitled thread"` with `identityLabel` on the checkbox (lines 1375-1393). The finding also misreads the model: pullReviewModel.ts:16-21 documents `title` as a deliberate shared kind label read by `itemKindLabel` and the review's grouping, with `threadTitle` as the separate name field; `itemKindLabel` (line 374) classifies by review rows/actions/resource-id, so nothing about grouping depends on the rendered string. title: The pill radius the retheme added to the session-detail filter toggle never applies
reason:
I attempted to refute this on the three usual grounds and all three fail.

VERIFIED BY COMPUTED STYLE (not by reading). I served src/App.css to a real browser and rendered the actual markup SessionDetailToolbar.tsx emits. Result: `.session-detail-filter-toggle` computes `border-radius: 0px` while `--r-pill` resolves to `999px`. Enumerating the matched CSSOM rules returned exactly two, both radius-bearing, the `0px` one last: `.session-detail-filter-toggle {var(--r-pill)}` and `.session-detail-filter-toggle, .session-detail-filter-box {0px}`. The retro block is at brace depth 0 (no @media wrapper), so plain source order decides. The declaration added at src/App.css:6980 is dead. This is the exact failure class this repo's own memory note "verify-css-by-computed-style" records: the CSS gates assert App.css source text, so nothing catches it.

NOT a deliberate choice of this change. The square rule and its "pressed state, not a painted control" comment pre-exist at HEAD (git show HEAD:src/App.css, line 10683), landed 2026-08-29 in 9d6964e. The diff added only the pill. The retheme's own record — memory/codex-retheme-cutover.md, the same-day sweep entry — lists under the pills group: "pills → settings switch, flags/state/repo/branch/tool-status/bundle-recommended chips, SHOW filter toggles (on = accent edge)". So the author explicitly moved these toggles into the pill family. The sibling declaration from the same hunk (`.is-on { border-color: var(--accent) }`) does land — I measured rgb(239,231,212) = `--accent` #efe7d4 — so the "accent edge" half of that intent shipped and the "pill" half silently did not. The stale rule encoding the older doctrine was never revisited. Refuting on "intentional" grounds would be wrong: two rules now encode contradictory intent and the newer, documented one is the one lost.

REAL, ON THE DEFAULT PATH. SessionDetailPage.tsx:463 renders the toolbar directly beneath the header's fact-chip strip. On that one screen I measured `.session-detail-chip` = 999px and `.btn` = 999px against the SHOW toggles at 0px — pills above, square chips immediately below, no scrolling or unusual window size needed. The reviewed specimen session-detail-mockup.html:35 restates `.session-detail-filter-toggle { border-radius: var(--r-pill) }` in its own <style> after the App.css <link>, so the specimen wins the cascade and shows pills — the shipped app diverges from the picture the shape was signed off against.

Nothing handles it elsewhere: no wrapper, parent guard, or later rule reinstates the radius (only two matching rules exist), and no test pins it — grep over tests/ finds only session-detail.integration.test.tsx:243-244 asserting markup, not radius. Severity "low" is already correct and not inflated: purely cosmetic, one toolbar, no functional, data, or accessibility impact (the WCAG 2.5.8 min-height on the same rule does land — 26px measured).
correction:
Two corrections to the finding's framing, neither of which changes the verdict. (1) The evidence block labels the RetroTheme rule as part of this diff; it is not — `.session-detail-filter-toggle, .session-detail-filter-box { border-radius: 0 }` exists at HEAD (src/App.css:10683 at 789eea5, from commit 9d6964e). Only `border-radius: var(--r-pill)` at src/App.css:6980 is new, so this is a new declaration landing dead against pre-existing CSS, not two rules added in conflict. (2) "every other chip and control on the page went to --r-pill in this diff" is overstated as measured — `.session-detail-chip` and `.btn` compute 999px, but `.sync-flag-chip` and `.sync-state-chip` computed 0px in isolation; the accurate claim is that the toggles are square directly beneath the pill fact-chip strip they sit under.

The proposed fix should not stay an either/or. The retheme record ("pills → ... SHOW filter toggles (on = accent edge)") settles the direction: drop `.session-detail-filter-toggle` from the rule at src/App.css:10975-10977, leaving only `.session-detail-filter-box` square — the 9px box is the checkbox mark and is meant to stay square. Deleting the pill at 6980 instead would silently reverse a documented decision from this change.

title: The app paints the dark palette before the theme attribute is stamped, so light-theme users get a dark flash on every launch
reason: Every citation checks out verbatim at the stated lines. src/App.css:7982-7985 is `:root, :root[data-theme="dark"] { --color-scheme: dark; --bg-0: #12100d; }`, and `--bg-0` is defined in only two places file-wide: that bare-`:root` dark value and `#fefbf6` at 8096 inside `:root[data-theme="light"]` (8094). There is no `@media (prefers-color-scheme: …)` anywhere in the CSS (App.css is the project's only stylesheet), so no CSS-level light fallback exists before JS runs. body at App.css:13-17 paints `var(--bg-0)` and `color-scheme: var(--color-scheme)`, with the 180ms background-color transition at 19-22. index.html has no theme attribute, no inline style, no inline script; src/preferences.ts:72-73 (called from main.tsx:7) is the only non-mockup code that stamps `data-theme`. The committed production build makes the ordering directly observable: dist/index.html head carries a deferred 629 KB `<script type="module">` followed by a render-blocking `<link rel=stylesheet>`, and the minified CSS keeps the same cascade (`:root,:root[data-theme=dark]{`, `:root[data-theme=light]{`, zero prefers-color-scheme). tauri.conf.json sets no window backgroundColor and no hidden-until-ready window, so nothing masks the first frame. No guard, override, or later rule rescues the light case.
correction: Two scope corrections, neither of which rescues the defect. (1) It is a production-build defect only: under `tauri dev`, Vite injects App.css through the module graph, so the stylesheet lands and `applyThemeChoice` stamps the attribute inside the same synchronous module evaluation, leaving no paint opportunity between them — which is why it goes unnoticed in daily work. (2) The proposed inline-`<script>` fix would be blocked by the app's own CSP (`script-src 'self'`, no `unsafe-inline`, in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json) unless a hash or nonce is added; the `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` guard on bare `:root` works as-is, but it only covers System/light-OS users — a user whose stored choice is `light` under a dark OS would still get the dark first frame.

title: The new switcher menu's search field cannot be reached with the keyboard
reason: Independently reproduced in a real browser. Citation is verbatim-accurate: SyncPathBar.tsx:328 is `{searchable && (` with the search input at 329-336; L258 is the Tab -> onClose(false) branch; L427 is `if (position === "first") options[0]?.focus();`; menuKeyboard.ts:11 restricts MENU_OPTION_SELECTOR to the menuitem family. I bundled the actual component with esbuild against the real App.css and drove it in Chrome with 7 switch targets (searchable = switcher && targetCount >= SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR(6), L174/L129). Rendered DOM: the input has NO tabindex (so tabIndex 0, tabbable) while all 9 menuitems carry tabindex="-1", making the search field the only natural tab stop inside the menu, positioned immediately after the crumb button in DOM order. A REAL Tab keypress with the menu open moved focus from the crumb button past the search field to the button after the whole bar, and menu.hidden flipped to true. Every other route is closed: moveMenuFocus/focusMenuEdge iterate menuOptions(), which matches only the three menuitem roles, so the roleless input is never in the list, and ArrowUp from the first menuitem wraps to the LAST menuitem (menuKeyboard.ts:28) rather than stepping up to the field; typeahead (L283-303) and openMenuRequest -> focusMenuOption -> options[0] (L439) both target options; Escape returns focus to the opener; there is no autoFocus, no ref, and the file's only .focus() calls target options[] or the opener button. The React-flush-vs-default-action race is irrelevant because both orderings fail: if React flushes first the input is skipped, and if the browser moves focus first it lands on an element immediately display:none'd by .sync-path-menu[hidden] (App.css:3080) and focus is dumped to body. The trigger is real: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2426-2438 builds the "Switch to" group from otherProjects, so 7 projects (6 others) reaches the floor. This is new uncommitted code (164 insertions in the working tree).
correction: The finding is correct in substance but overstates one detail: the L267-274 "while typing" handler is NOT unreachable code — it is reachable by mouse click into the field (Enter clicks the first .target, arrows step into the list). It is unreachable only for keyboard-only users. Additionally, keyboard users are not left with no navigation at all: the typeahead at L283-303 still jumps by label prefix. What they specifically lose is the field's substring matching across both label and detail/path (`matches`, L176-178), which is strictly broader than the prefix-only, label-only typeahead. Accurate statement: the search input rendered at SyncPathBar.tsx:328-336 is focusable but unreachable by keyboard, because it carries no menuitem role (so moveMenuFocus/focusMenuEdge skip it) and every Tab route closes the menu first (L258 in-menu; L516, L551, L618 on the three openers) — a WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A) failure.
