title: Pull review names every conversation "Conversation" instead of its session title, which the model already carries
reason: The finding assumes `ItemList` is what draws conversation rows in the Pull review. It is not, on any realistic path. `RestorePlanView.tsx:582-600` routes conversations to `ProjectActivityPage` with `selectionMode="pull"` whenever `project` is present; `ItemList` is only the `: conversationItems.length > 0 ?` fallback for a missing project summary, and the code comment above it says so explicitly ("The Activity review renders the storage rows... The ItemList fallback is synchronous"). `project` is `projects.find(p => p.local_project_id === restoreBinding.local_project_id)` (ProjectSync.tsx:3480), and `projects` is derived from `registrations` (ProjectSync.tsx:731) — the same registry the binding's `local_project_id` comes from — so the fallback is effectively unreachable when a Pull review opens. On the live path, each session is a `sync-history-thread-card` printing `session.title || "Untitled session"` (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1164, 1246) and storage-only rows print their own `fullTitle` (1377, 1423), with checkbox labels `Include ${session.title || "Untitled session"}` (1200, 1206) and `Include ${identityLabel}` (1393). So the claimed impact — ten identical "Conversation" rows, no name while choosing versus real names in the after-receipt — does not occur; the choosing surface already shows the real names, and the asymmetry the finding rests on is false. Separately, the "Conversation" string is a deliberate, documented kind label, not a missing name: `PullReviewItem.title` carries the doc comment "Conversations share the one label 'Conversation' ... it is not a place to put a session's name" (pullReviewModel.ts:15-18), `threadTitle` was added alongside it precisely so the outcome receipt has a name, and the current fallback rendering is pinned by an existing test (`assert.match(html, /Select Conversation/)`, tests/frontend/pull-review.integration.test.tsx:280, with the companion test at :403 asserting the receipt title is never the bare kind label). The remaining truth is cosmetic and confined to a defensive branch: if the fallback ever rendered, its rows would read by kind. That is low, not high.
correction: The bold "Conversation" text is confined to `ItemList`, which draws conversations only in the missing-project-summary fallback (RestorePlanView.tsx:596); the live Pull review draws every session through ProjectActivityPage with its real title and titled checkbox labels. Rendering `item.threadTitle || item.title` in the fallback would be a small polish to an effectively unreachable branch, not a fix for a user-visible defect — and it would need to leave `itemKindLabel`-based grouping and the pinned test at pull-review.integration.test.tsx:280 intact.

title: The Clear storage data confirmation names "Library", a product concept that no longer exists in the UI
reason: The string exists as quoted at ProjectSync.tsx:3242 and is reachable (storage ⋯ menu → "Clear storage data…" → ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1773 → clearStorageData), but the claimed impact does not survive inspection. (1) No user-visible consequence: the decision-carrying clause is "Permanently clear all Mallard data from “X”?", which is complete and correct, and the third sentence enumerates what is NOT deleted — Catalog is absent from that carve-out list. There is no reading of the dialog under which less is deleted than the user expects, so the word choice cannot produce a wrong click; a reader confused by an unfamiliar noun in a danger dialog cancels, which is the fail-safe direction. (2) The claimed harm is misattributed to the proposed fix: "has no way to know that means their skills, plugins and pets" is not remedied by "Catalog resource", which also names none of those kinds. The fix and the stated harm are unrelated; the severity was reasoned from the dialog's destructiveness rather than the delta the edit produces. (3) The premise that "Library" is a product concept that no longer exists is wrong. It is the live domain/storage vocabulary across layers: the object layout `.mallard/v1/library/`, the DTO field `library_objects_deleted` returned by this very command and consumed 22 lines below at ProjectSync.tsx:3264 (src/types.ts:264), `LibraryResourceEngine` in Rust, and the design/audit docs (docs/APP_AUDIT_2026-08-07.md, docs/BACKEND_CORE_SIMPLIFICATION_AUDIT_2026-08-19.md), plus live code comments in Icons.tsx, App.css, LoadingScaffold.tsx and storage-catalog/types.ts in the current dirty tree. "Catalog" is the UI label; this is a cross-layer naming seam, and the string is original to d2957b8 (2026-08-12), predating the Catalog UI vocabulary. The observation is accurate as a copy-consistency nit and the one-word edit is harmless, but it is polish, not a high-severity defect.
correction: Accurate statement: the Clear-storage confirmation at ProjectSync.tsx:3242 uses the domain-layer term "Library resource" where the UI everywhere else says "Catalog" — a cosmetic cross-layer terminology seam in one sentence of itemization. It carries no risk of a mistaken confirmation, because the dialog's opening clause already says "Permanently clear all Mallard data" and the following sentence lists what is spared (Catalog is not among the spared). Worth a one-word edit for consistency; not a destructive-confirmation defect, and it would not by itself tell users their skills/plugins/pets are included — only enumerating the kinds would do that.

title: Path-bar switcher renders its action verbs as bare icons, including the destructive ones
reason: Citation is accurate. src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:241-242 contains the quoted lines verbatim inside renderPill, and the `tail &&` guard does suppress the label. renderPill(item, false) is called at line 353 for the `verbs` array, which line 168 derives from the first unlabelled group of a switcher menu. Call sites confirm the consequences: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2391-2425 yields four icon-only verbs (folder/terminal/edit/trash, the trash being "Reset local sync state…" with danger:true); StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1290-1315 yields refresh/edit/trash ("Remove this Catalog row…"); StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1226-1241 yields settings/link-off. App.css:3236-3251 confirms the pill is a 32px square with padding:0, so no text is expected. The caption logic at 179-182 does filter on item.detail, and only the agent item has one. However, the finder missed four mitigations that all cut against the claimed severity: (1) line 232 sets aria-label={item.label} on every verb pill, so the accessible name is the full label and screen-reader users are unaffected; (2) line 234 sets a title tooltip, and all three destructive verbs carry explanatory item.title sentences that disclose the consequence on hover; (3) App.css:3273 tints .sync-path-menu-verb.danger with var(--danger-text), so destructive glyphs are visually marked; (4) all three destructive actions are gated behind a titled native confirm() dialog naming the action and its full consequences (ProjectSync.tsx:2678 and :1581, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1160), so a mis-clicked glyph cannot lose anything. The folder-glyph collision is also weaker than stated: switch targets use git-folder for git repos and folder only for non-git ones, and those rows render their text labels via renderItem, so only the footer glyph is bare.
correction: The switcher footer renders each verb as an icon-only 32px pill (SyncPathBar.tsx:241-242, called with tail=false at :353), so the project crumb shows four unlabelled glyphs and the Catalog/storage crumbs three and two. This is a legibility and discoverability problem for sighted pointer users who do not hover — one open menu uses the plain `folder` glyph for both "Reveal in Finder" (footer) and "a non-git project" (switch target), and the sole caption line reads as if it labels the whole strip. It is not an accessibility or data-loss defect: each pill carries aria-label={item.label}, a title tooltip explaining the action, a danger tint on destructive verbs, and every destructive verb is behind a titled confirm() dialog stating exactly what is forgotten (ProjectSync.tsx:2678, ProjectSync.tsx:1581, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1160). Note also that verbTitle prefers item.title over item.label, so the danger verbs' tooltips state the consequence but never repeat the verb name — worth fixing alongside any labelling change.

title: Path-bar switcher renders its action verbs as bare icons, including the destructive ones
reason: Deliberate, user-selected design — not a defect. The specimen at menu-mockup.html put four directions side by side on real App.css; A (line 154-157) and D (line 229-232) render the verbs as labelled list rows, which is exactly this finding's proposed fix, and B (line 188) renders them as icon-only pills with title attributes including the red trash. The user picked B and then asked for the same treatment on the storage crumb and the ⋯ overflow (memory: switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md, "IMPLEMENTED uncommitted 2026-09-01"). The component's own header comment at SyncPathBar.tsx:119-128 states the contract: "the verbs as the row-end icon cluster in a footer strip". The finding proposes reverting a rejected alternative. The quoted evidence is also incomplete: it stops one line short of aria-label={tail ? undefined : item.label} (line 232) and title={... verbTitle(item)} (line 234), so every verb pill carries its full label as its accessible name and an explanatory tooltip on hover — the reset verb's tooltip is "Forget local sync bases, conversation mappings, recovery records, and saved plans; files and cloud data are kept" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2421). The typeahead handler at line 291-295 falls back to aria-label specifically so keyboard search still reaches icon-only verbs — code written for this rendering, not overlooking it. The claimed impact does not survive either: all three "destructive" verbs are intercepted by a confirm modal that names the object and enumerates the consequences — Reset local sync state at ProjectSync.tsx:2678, Unlink storage at 2842, Remove Catalog row at 1581 ("Only the menu row is removed. No provider or storage content is touched") — and none deletes files or cloud data by their own copy. Danger verbs are additionally colored red via .sync-path-menu-verb.danger (App.css:3273), so the one destructive pill is visually distinct from the neutrals. The folder-glyph collision is real at the glyph level but the two zones are not confusable in the rendered menu: switch targets are 34px full-width rows with the project name in display face, verbs are 32px pills in a bordered, differently-shaded footer strip below a border-top (App.css:3212-3252) — and the project crumb's own icon is git-folder for git repos, which is most projects in a git-sync app. The caption line is a full-width micro line above the pills (flex-basis: 100%, App.css:3225-3230) with a CSS comment stating the intent. What remains is the ordinary learnability cost of any icon toolbar, knowingly accepted, with hover tooltips, screen-reader labels, red danger styling and confirmation dialogs all covering it.

title: The app paints the dark palette before the theme attribute is stamped, so light-theme users get a dark flash on every launch
reason: The cascade fact is correct (bare :root is the dark palette, no prefers-color-scheme guard, no inline head script), but the claimed impact does not survive measurement. I served the actual production dist build (630 KB index js + 182 KB index css, both in <head>) with an inline probe: CSS responseEnd 11.4 ms, JS responseEnd 11.8 ms, data-theme="light" stamped at 21.9 ms, DOMContentLoaded 22.0 ms, load 22.8 ms. The deferred module script is itself blocked on the pending stylesheet (HTML spec "the end", step 4 spins until no stylesheet blocks scripts), so the exposure is only the ~10 ms between the stylesheet being parsed and the stamp landing 0.1 ms before DOMContentLoaded — under one 16.7 ms frame at 60 Hz. The finding's "the first painted frame uses the bare :root block for every user whose choice is light" is therefore a race, not a certainty; the "cannot deliver" verdict on preferences.ts:74 is wrong, since the stamp demonstrably lands before React mounts and the loaded page renders cream. What is at stake in that window is an EMPTY window (body is one bare <div id="root">, no content yet) during macOS window creation, and the 180 ms body transition only runs if a style change event already resolved body's style — the same condition as the flash, so the fade is not an additional, independent cost. No functional consequence, no wrong state, nothing a user can act on; it is at most a sub-frame cosmetic race on launch for light-theme users. The structure is also a documented deliberate choice: tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx:23 states "the dark palette rides the bare :root that also carries the shared tokens", and the pre-mount stamp in main.tsx is the codebase's chosen mitigation, already in place.
correction: Accurate statement: the pre-mount theme stamp leaves a ~10 ms window (measured on the shipped dist bundle: stylesheet ready at 11.4 ms, attribute stamped at 21.9 ms) in which a rendering opportunity could present one frame of the dark bare-:root background on an otherwise empty window. It is a launch-timing race that widens on a cold first run where the 630 KB module graph takes longer to compile than the 182 KB stylesheet takes to parse — not a guaranteed dark-to-cream fade on every light-theme launch. If the maintainer wants it closed for free, adding a @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) redefinition on bare :root is the cheaper of the two proposed fixes and needs no change to index.html.

title: "Add storage…" degrades to an unlabelled + icon when the user has exactly one storage
reason: The classification mechanism is real, but the claimed user-visible harm is not. renderPill (SyncPathBar.tsx:223-245) gives the verb pill aria-label={item.label} and title=verbTitle(item) = "Add storage…", so the control has both an accessible name and a hover tooltip — it is not "unlabelled" or "unexplained", and the click still fires onAddStorage(). An icon-only plus labelled only by title/aria-label and meaning "Add storage" is this codebase's own shipped idiom, appearing verbatim at ProjectSidebar.tsx:1013-1023 and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2917-2929, so the rendering matches the app's established vocabulary rather than contradicting it. Classification by group position is a deliberate, documented contract (the doc block at SyncPathBar.tsx:119-128, and the switcher was landed specifically to read existing PathBarMenuGroup[] by position without touching any caller); the storage-editor crumb at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1698-1731 is the single caller that intentionally supplies no verbs group because its verbs live in the page overflow. correction: In the single-storage state the add-storage item is classified as a verb and drawn as an icon pill (plus glyph, aria-label and tooltip "Add storage…") instead of the text pill it becomes once a second storage exists — a cosmetic inconsistency in one menu, not a loss of label, affordance, or function.

title: Push and Pull failures print raw Rust error strings containing Debug-formatted enum variants and action UUIDs
reason: The file citations are correct (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:844 is `{error}` in a danger Notice; RestorePlanView.tsx:484 is `message: error,`), and `error` does reach the screen as near-raw backend text via storageFailureMessage → storageAccessErrorMessage → errorMessage → userFacingRepoTerms. But the finding's load-bearing example is refuted by the actual control flow. service.rs:9360's "conversation Push action '{}' is stale at {:?}" is generated inside the `revalidate` closure whose Err is collected into `stale_conversations` (9365-9371), carried through ReviewedPublishOutcome (9412, 9457), and consumed at 9913 as a per-resource OperationResourceResult{state:"failed", message}. The push then returns `success: true` with a purpose-written human sentence ("Published revision N; 1 reviewed conversation changed during review, kept its stored state, and needs a fresh Push review", 9925-9944). Nothing is thrown, so setPushError (ProjectSync.tsx:2156) is never reached and the danger banner never shows that string. A pinned Rust test (service.rs ~25085-25112) asserts precisely this: pushed.success is true, pushed.message contains "changed during review", and "is stale at" appears only in results[].message. The Pull mirror at service.rs:10423 is the same shape — the `?` is inside the `prepare_one` closure and prepare_pull_conversation_actions collects it into `failures` (10453-10459) → failed_conversation_receipt → per-action ApplyReceipt.error, surfaced by syncOutcome.ts:205 as an outcome row, not by RestorePlanView's `error` banner. So neither cited banner can print a Debug-formatted enum variant, and the "danger banner reads e.g. 'conversation Push action 0198f3a4-… is stale at SemanticDigest'" reproduction does not occur. The two sibling messages (8402, 8835) do propagate via `?` and would carry an action UUID, but they are ok_or_else guards on impossible internal states (missing descriptor, missing publishable tail), not the routine failure mode the "high" severity rests on.
correction: What actually holds is narrower: operation-level backend failures reach the Push/Pull danger banners with only repo-terminology substitution applied (no cause-and-next-step mapping), and a few of those strings — reachable only through internal-invariant guards such as service.rs:8402 and 8835 — would embed an action UUID. The routine stale-during-review case the finding names is already handled with purpose-written user copy on a successful push, and its raw "is stale at {:?}" text is confined to per-resource result messages rendered by SyncOutcome, not by PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:844 or RestorePlanView.tsx:484. isIrrecoverableSyncError's "stale at semanticdigest" match on the banner `error` therefore also never fires from that path.

title: Push and Pull failures print raw Rust error strings containing Debug-formatted enum variants and action UUIDs
reason: The finding's headline evidence is unreachable at the cited line. service.rs:9360 does not propagate — its result is collected into `stale_conversations` (9365-9370) and the push returns `success: true` with already-humanized prose ("; 1 reviewed conversation changed during review, kept its stored state, and needs a fresh Push review", 9925-9934); the Debug string lives only in a per-resource `OperationResourceResult.message`, which `buildPushOutcome` (syncOutcome.ts:80-135) never renders. A Rust test (service.rs:25092-25112) pins that contract. So PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:844 cannot print "is stale at SemanticDigest". RestorePlanView.tsx:480 is likewise guarded by `error && !hasResult` (hasResult defined at line 345), so a pin-stale Pull error — which always arrives with a restore result — routes to the outcome card, never the raw banner; the only errors that do reach that banner are the no-result transport/planning failures, which already pass through storageFailureMessage → storageAccessErrorMessage (src/storageError.ts:21-29), the exact shape-matching translator the fix proposes. The proposed "Details disclosure" also already exists: buildPullOutcome emits `technical: [{ label: "Error", value: error }]`. isIrrecoverableSyncError is not passthrough neglect but the deliberate seam that swaps Retry for a labelled "Reset local sync state" action, pinned by tests/frontend/pull-review.integration.test.tsx:475-500 using this precise message. The residue is a narrow, rare integrity path (ProjectSync.tsx:2936 assigns result.error unfiltered) that surfaces in an outcome-card row reason alongside a human title, stat row and named recovery button — a copy nit on a should-never-happen path, not a high-severity user-facing defect.
correction: Narrowed and de-escalated: the Push path never surfaces the Debug-formatted string (backend already returns human copy and the frontend drops the raw per-resource message). On the Pull path a raw backend string can appear as an outcome-card row `reason` and in the collapsed `technical` list (ProjectSync.tsx:2936 → syncOutcome.ts buildPullOutcome), never in the RestorePlanView danger banner, which is guarded by `!hasResult` and already fed through storageAccessErrorMessage. That residual raw text sits beside a human outcome title and a labelled "Reset local sync state" action, and covers internal invariant violations where paraphrase would misinform.

title: One sentence in the repo-connection dialog uses "repository" and "repo" for two different objects
reason: Independently reproduced. src/components/project-sync/BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:99 is verbatim `? "Connect to this repository's repo"` inside the `sibling` ternary of the dialog's <h1>. The branch is genuinely reachable: ProjectSync.tsx:3824 sets `reason: "sibling"` in onConnectSibling, the value flows through `reason={pendingBundleConnection.reason}` at ProjectSync.tsx:3902, and BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:47 computes `const sibling = reason === "sibling"`. All four inconsistent spellings verified verbatim: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1737 "Repositories", ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:411 "Repository ID", ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:887 "Repository", ProjectBindingEditor.tsx:295 "Repo". src/terminology.ts exists mapping Bundle→Repo and is applied at exactly two sites, both backend-text paths (storageError.ts:13, LogPanel.tsx:125), never to authored UI copy. Only unverified sub-claim is the "prior audit filed this as M07" provenance — grep for "M07" across docs/*.md returns nothing — but that is peripheral to the defect. Severity medium rather than low is justified because the <h1> is the dialog's accessible name (aria-labelledby="sync-bundle-connection-title"), so it is also the screen-reader announcement, and the dialog governs an identity-adoption choice whose own warning at line 65 says connecting will "adopt its repository identity" — ambiguity here has a wrong-choice consequence, not merely a cosmetic one.

Connecting will adopt its repository identity.") and in the sibling body copy at line 106. Also worth noting that the line-99 heading is the dialog's accessible name via aria-labelledby, so the fix affects screen-reader output as well as visible copy. title: The same pull action is called "session" on the chip and "task" in that chip's own tooltip
reason: Verified against the real file, not the quoted evidence. src/components/project-sync/ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1063, 1069, 1071 contain the quoted lines verbatim at exactly those line numbers ("Publish new task", "Update this task", "Create local task"), and lines 1256-1258 are the chip: {selectionMode === "pull" && pullOperationChip(syncEntry) && ({pullOperationChip(syncEntry)})} — the title sits on line 1257 as claimed. I traced the control flow looking for an escape hatch: for a pull row with compared_against_storage=true and pull_decision.action="materialize_cloud", syncHoldDetail("pull", entry) returns null (materialize_cloud is neither "blocked" nor either of the two push-only require_pull branches, and pullOperationChip already excludes state==="unavailable"), so the `holdDetail ??` fallback does NOT shadow reviewStateLabel. I then reproduced it for real by building a probe off tests/frontend/project-activity.integration.test.tsx and rendering ProjectChatHistoryContent with selectionMode="pull", a materialize_cloud/compared_against_storage entry, and the row selected. Rendered HTML: Update session and the neighbouring status indicator carries aria-label="Update this task". One DOM element, visible text "Update session", its own native tooltip "Update this task". The defect is real but three details need correcting, and two of them change the fix.

1. The "Update session" / "Update this task" collision only occurs when the row is SELECTED. Unselected, syncReviewStateLabel returns "Keep local" while the chip still reads "Update session" — a second mismatch on the same element that the proposed fix does not address.

2. "task" is not confined to those three lines. src/components/project-sync/pullReviewModel.ts:54-83 uses "task" twelve more times ("More than one local task could match this stored task", "Creates a local task from the reviewed storage history", "Brings the reviewed storage history into this task", etc.), and that module feeds the ItemList fallback rendered by the SAME Pull review step (RestorePlanView.tsx:584 and its sibling ItemList branch). Fixing only ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1063/1069/1071 leaves the vocabulary split intact in the sibling path.

3. The "Sessions" tab claim is conditional: reviewSteps.ts historyStepLabel returns "Sessions" only when the project is eligible for project-file sync; a git-backed project's tab reads "Git & sessions". The tab says "session" either way, so the point stands, but not as stated.

title: The same pull action is called "session" on the chip and "task" in that chip's own tooltip

The single real collision (hovering a selected materialize_cloud pull chip with no holdDetail yields title "Update this task" under chip text "Update session") is a synonym restatement of the same verb and referent: no wrong action, no data risk, no misunderstanding of the operation.
correction: Narrow, accurate version: hovering the pull operation chip on a selected materialize_cloud row (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1257, when syncHoldDetail returns null) shows a native tooltip "Update this task" beneath chip text reading "Update session". title: One sentence in the repo-connection dialog uses "repository" and "repo" for two different objects
reason: Intentional, documented, and test-pinned wording — not a defect. (1) The exact copy is specified in the accepted plan: docs/PLAN_REPO_BUNDLE_CONVERGENCE.md:123 (D3) writes "This storage already has this repository in another repo (‘HorrorGame’, …) — Connect.", and D2 (lines 97-110) uses the same split repeatedly. The convention is deliberate: "repository" = the Git checkout carrying the fingerprint, "repo" = the Mallard sync object in the storage. (2) tests/frontend/repo-bundle-convergence.integration.test.tsx:85 pins the precise headline under review — assert.match(html, /Connect to this repository('|')s repo/) — with line 86 pinning the body sentence and lines 48-62 pinning the parallel SiblingRepoNotice phrasing. The wording is a fixture of the suite, so it was authored and reviewed, not drifted into. (3) The terminology.ts argument is a misreading: its docstring at src/terminology.ts:8 says it translates "the internal protocol term", and its map is only Bundle→Repo. It scrubs the leaked word "bundle" out of machine-generated strings, which is why it is applied at storageError.ts:13 and LogPanel.tsx:125 and nowhere else; authored copy never says "bundle", so applying it there would be a no-op. It was never built to arbitrate "repository" vs "repo". (4) No realistic user consequence: the sibling heading renders only in the rare unconverged split state (D3 gates the scan on an absent or registration-empty own head), and it is never the only cue — the eyebrow "Repo identity", the disambiguating paragraph immediately below (line 106), the context row "Current local repo b751caac…" (line 120), a radiogroup of concretely named candidate repos with revision/resource/timestamp facts, and a notice that says "different Git fingerprint" all sit in the same viewport. The decision asked for is "which of these listed repos", which the list resolves outright; no user can be led to a wrong action by the word stem. (5) The proposed fix is net-negative: "sync repo" appears nowhere in the product or docs, so it introduces a third term, breaks two pinned assertions, and churns four unrelated files for zero behavioral change.
correction: The only defensible residue is far narrower than filed: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:411 labels a bundle_id (the Mallard-side object) as "Repository ID", which crosses the documented convention where "repository" means the Git checkout. That is a single cosmetic label, low severity, and unrelated to BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:99, whose two-word construction is the intended vocabulary.

title: A Settings control labelled "Thread size limit" describes itself using two other nouns
reason: Citation is exact, not near-enough: <repo>/src/components/project-sync/SettingsPage.tsx:455 is `label="Thread size limit"`, :464 is `aria-label="Thread size limit"`, and :476-477 read verbatim "The biggest session transcript Mallard will read. Threads over the / cap are skipped by compare, Push, and Pull." The terminology mismatch reproduces in source. A repo-wide grep for user-visible "thread" text (excluding identifiers, CSS class names, and mockup files) returns only these three lines plus SettingsPage.tsx:531 "Worker threads that scan and compare local sessions" — which uses "threads" in the unrelated OS-worker sense, so it does not give the user a bridge to "session"; if anything it adds a second meaning. Every list/tab/step does call them sessions: ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1618 and :2021 ("Sessions"), reviewSteps.ts:18 ("Sessions" / "Git & sessions"), ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1518 and :2511 ("Sessions"). The "compare" sub-claim also holds: grepping for a Compare/Recompare control returns nothing; the affordances are "Refresh" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1811, :2561, :2572, :2761), so "compare" is a lowercase common verb standing beside the title-cased control names Push and Pull. No guard, override, or later string overrides any of this — it is static JSX text. I could not find grounds to refute.
correction: Two parts of the finding overstate the case and should be trimmed. (1) "A user setting this cannot tell whether it caps their Codex sessions or something else" is wrong: the description's own first sentence says "The biggest session transcript Mallard will read", which names the object explicitly. The real defect is that the label and the second sentence drift to a noun the UI uses nowhere else, not that the control is unintelligible. (2) The label is not a lone offender on its own page — SettingsPage.tsx:421-422 already says "captured conversations" for the same object, so this is one instance of a page-wide noun drift across session / thread / conversation, and a fix that renames only this row leaves the drift in place. Fix-side note the finding misses: tests/frontend/settings-page.integration.test.tsx:81 pins `aria-label="Thread size limit"` in its regex, so the proposed rename breaks that assertion unless the test is updated in the same change.

title: A Settings control labelled "Thread size limit" describes itself using two other nouns
reason:
The finding's load-bearing premise is factually wrong. It claims "Thread" is an internal wire noun that "appears nowhere the user can connect it to a session." It appears all over the shipped user-facing copy: src/components/project-sync/ProjectActivityPage.tsx:578-581 builds the Activity attention summary out of "thread changed on both sides / threads waiting to sync / threads Mallard could not match / threads that can't be synced"; ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2648 and :2691 label the two primary sync buttons "Pull N newer threads from <storage>" / "Push N newer threads to <storage>", and :2586 says "N threads need attention"; ProjectActivityPage.tsx:492 "This thread can't be synced safely right now.", :835 "Mallard thread ID copied.", :1377 "Untitled thread", :1418 "<provider> thread"; PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:542 "Selected threads still push." The design commentary in src/App.css:2884 states the copy doctrine in exactly this vocabulary ("3 threads are newer here than in storage", said once) and :2926 reasons about "an unsyncable thread". So the Settings label is consistent with the app's established user-facing noun, not a leak of a wire name, and the claim that "every list, tab and card in the app calls it a session" is false — the app deliberately runs a two-noun vocabulary (session = the card/detail object; thread = the sync unit being counted and moved).

The claimed user-visible consequence also does not survive contact with the row. The user "cannot tell whether it caps their Codex sessions or something else" — but the row's own first sentence at SettingsPage.tsx:476 is "The biggest session transcript Mallard will read." That sentence names the thing being capped, in the finding's own preferred noun, directly under the label and above the MB dropdown. There is no realistic path on which a user reads the label, reads that sentence, and is left unable to identify what is capped.

The "compare" sub-claim inverts the codebase's actual convention. Push and Pull are title-cased because they are literal button labels (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2660, :2703 render them via sync-path-sync-label); "compare" is lowercase precisely because it is a plain verb and not a control — the same convention used at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:641 ("Link a storage to compare and sync it.") and ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:77 / ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:139 ("State unknown. Rescan to compare."). The proposed rewrite ("skipped when comparing, pushing and pulling") would lowercase the two real control names and destroy that control-vs-verb signal, making the copy worse by this codebase's own rules. Note also that "Refresh" is not the compare affordance's only face — it is the path-bar verb (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1811, :2110) — while comparison is the background operation the sentence is actually describing ("Comparing threads with <storage>", ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1637).

Finally, the label is pinned by an existing gate: tests/frontend/settings-page.integration.test.tsx:81 asserts aria-label="Thread size limit", and the Performance group's shape is a documented, deliberately-landed design (four tuning knobs, Settings > Performance). What remains is a taste preference about which of two established nouns a single Settings row should use — no user-visible defect, no misconfiguration risk, nothing a maintainer hits.
correction: If anything survives, it is only this: the app maintains two user-facing nouns for the same object ("session" on cards/detail, "thread" in sync counts and buttons), and this Settings row happens to show both in three lines. That is an app-wide vocabulary question, not a defect in SettingsPage.tsx:455 — changing this one row would not resolve it and would diverge the row from the "threads" wording used by the Push/Pull buttons and the Activity summary it describes.

title: The new capture-budget message says "conversations" in Push review and "sessions" in the activity list for the same blocker

Push the selected sessions first…" arm verbatim; git diff confirms both are new in the working tree and both key off the same `push_decision.blocker === "capture_budget"`. title: The switcher search field lowercases a proper noun, producing "Switch catalog row…" and "Filter catalog row list"
reason: Reproduced in source. SyncPathBar.tsx:332-333 matches the quoted evidence verbatim (`placeholder={`Switch ${label.toLowerCase()}…`}` / `aria-label={`Filter ${label.toLowerCase()} list`}`), and the line number is correct. `label` is `crumb.menuLabel ?? crumb.label` (line 586); StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1279 sets `menuLabel: "Catalog row"` on the "scope" crumb, which carries a `menuHeader` (line 1280) so `switcher = true`, and its one labelled group "Switch to" (line 1320) lists the other Catalog scopes. CATALOG_KINDS has 4 kinds (model.ts:26-36), so two profiles give 8 rows / 7 targets, clearing SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR = 6 — the field renders as "Switch catalog row…" / "Filter catalog row list". The capitalisation convention is real and consistent: "Add Catalog resource…", "Remove this Catalog row…", and mid-sentence at StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1932 (subject="notes about this Catalog row"); the only lowercase "catalog rows" in the tree is a code comment (LoadingScaffold.tsx:40). However two sub-claims fail and the severity is inflated: (1) the `crumb.label` fallback is unreachable — every crumb supplying `menuHeader` (the gate for `switcher`, hence for `searchable`) also supplies `menuLabel` ("Storage", "Project", "Catalog row", "Switch view"), and "Team bucket" exists only in a comment at line 289, not as a production label, so "Switch team bucket…" cannot render; (2) the "Switch view" crumb (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2520) has exactly one target and can never reach the floor. The overflow menu passes no header and is never searchable. So the blast radius is one placeholder plus one aria-label on the Catalog page only, gated behind 7+ rows — "Switch storage…" and "Switch project…" read correctly. Also, "Filter catalog row list" is clunky rather than strictly ungrammatical; the solid defect is the lowercased product noun.
correction: On the Catalog scope crumb only (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1279, menuLabel "Catalog row"), once a user has 7 or more Catalog rows the switcher search field renders `placeholder="Switch catalog row…"` and `aria-label="Filter catalog row list"`, lowercasing the product noun "Catalog" that every other surface capitalises — including mid-sentence at StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1932. The other switcher crumbs are unaffected: "Storage" and "Project" lowercase cleanly, and "Switch view" has a single target so it can never cross SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR. The finding's secondary scenario — the `crumb.menuLabel ?? crumb.label` fallback at line 586 yielding "Switch team bucket…" — cannot occur, because `searchable` requires `menuHeader` and every crumb that sets `menuHeader` also sets `menuLabel`. The fix still stands: pass an author-supplied plural switch-noun and use it verbatim instead of `.toLowerCase()`-ing a label.

title: Switcher target rows drop the path that distinguishes same-named projects and storages
reason: This is a deliberate, user-chosen design decision, not a defect, and the described consequence is already covered several ways. 1) Intent is documented in three places. The code comment directly above the line says it outright: "A switch target keeps its path in the tooltip and stays one line high." (SyncPathBar.tsx:187-190). The stylesheet repeats it: "the switch targets are one line high in the display face" (App.css:3154-3157). And the project memory record `switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md` shows the user was shown four directions in a static specimen (`menu-mockup.html`) on 2026-09-01 and explicitly picked B · Switcher, whose written description is "other projects one line high with the path in the tooltip"; the implementation note repeats "path detail moved to `title`". The reviewer is re-litigating a choice the user made from alternatives that included printing the path (A · Sheet, C · Tiles both print mono paths). 2) It matches the app's own, older convention on the primary switching surface. `ProjectSidebar.tsx:889-891` renders each project as `{label}` with the path only in `title` — the always-visible project list has never printed the path. The path bar switcher now agrees with it rather than diverging. 3) The path is not gone from the interaction. It stays in `title` (exposed to screen readers as the accessible description, so AT users do hear it), and it stays in the switcher's filter predicate — `matches()` tests `${item.label} ${item.detail}` — so the search pill, which appears at ≥6 targets (exactly the many-projects case where collisions get likely), disambiguates by path from the keyboard. The current object's own path is always printed in the lifted `.sync-path-menu-current` header, so after a switch the header immediately shows which one you landed on. 4) The action is a non-destructive navigation. Picking the wrong "api" changes the workspace view; the header path tells you instantly and the menu switches back. Nothing is written, deleted or pushed. The app also ships "Rename project…" producing a `local_alias` (projectLabel = alias || display_name) as the first-class fix for two folders with the same basename. 5) The evidence is also imprecise: it is not true that "every switch target ... sets detailIsPath: true". Storage targets pass `detailIsPath: storageSubtitleIsPath(candidate)` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:215-217), which is true only for `kind === "local"`; S3/R2 storages have a phrase subtitle ("Bucket · X") and still print their second line unchanged. So the storage half of the claimed impact only applies to two local storages both named e.g. "backup" — a narrower case than stated. What is left is a real but small residue: a sighted keyboard-only user, with fewer than 6 targets, who has registered two projects with identical labels, has no on-screen disambiguator. That is a narrow a11y polish item on a reversible navigation, not a medium copy defect — and note the finding is filed under a copy/terminology lens while no wording is actually wrong.
correction: Narrowed and corrected: for switch targets whose detail is a filesystem path (all project targets; local-kind storage targets only — S3 storages keep their printed "Bucket · X" subtitle), the path moves from a printed second line to the row's `title`, by deliberate design (option B of four specimen directions, chosen by the user 2026-09-01). Residual: with fewer than 6 targets no search pill appears, so a sighted keyboard-only user facing two identically-labelled projects has no on-screen disambiguator — screen readers still get the path via the accessible description, and renaming to a local alias is the app's intended remedy.

title: The switcher search field lowercases a proper noun, producing "Switch catalog row…" and "Filter catalog row list"
reason: Cosmetic-only, largely unreachable, and it argues against a deliberate house idiom. (a) The `crumb.label` fallback cited as the worst case (line 586, "Switch team bucket…") can never reach the search input: the input renders only when `switcher && targetCount >= 6`, `switcher` requires `menuHeader`, and every menuHeader-bearing crumb in the app sets `menuLabel` (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1213/1279, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1732/2356/2449/2520). Same for the "Switch view" crumb — it has exactly one switch target, five below SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR. (b) Lowercasing an author-supplied label into sentence prose is a 45-site convention in src/components/ (`Copy ${value.label.toLowerCase()}`, `Select at least one ${kind.label.toLowerCase()} to push`, `Add a storage to compare these ${kind.plural.toLowerCase()}…`), so the proposed rule "do not .toLowerCase() an author-supplied label" contradicts the codebase's settled design. (c) The reach arithmetic in the finding is wrong: pets are Codex-only (AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:244), so one Claude + one Codex profile gives at most 6 rows = 5 targets, below the floor; the field needs 7+ Catalog rows, i.e. three or more provider homes. (d) "Filter catalog row list" is a normal noun-adjunct compound ("the file list"), clunky but not ungrammatical, and screen readers do not announce case, so there is no a11y or comprehension effect. The only real residue is one letter's case in a transient placeholder behind a rare configuration, and the proposed fix widens the public PathBarCrumb type across four call sites to correct it.
correction: Narrowed and downgraded: the sole live instance is the Catalog scope crumb's `menuLabel: "Catalog row"` (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1279) being sentence-cased into "Switch catalog row…" once a user has 7+ Catalog rows — a one-letter inconsistency with the app's own capitalized "Catalog row" copy. There is no defect in SyncPathBar.tsx: the fallback path and the "Switch view" crumb cannot produce a search placeholder at all. If addressed, it is a caller-side wording choice, not a type-surface change — and note `menuLabel` also supplies the crumb chevron's title and aria-label (SyncPathBar.tsx:509-510).

title: Switcher group headings are deleted and their label put on an element that cannot carry a name
reason: The dropped heading is a deliberate, documented design decision, not lost copy. The memory record switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md shows four directions were mocked; direction A ("Sheet") was the one with the visible micro "SWITCH TO" label, and the user picked direction B ("Switcher"), implemented 2026-09-01 with 269/269 + tsc green. B's premise is that switching is the menu's job: the current object is a lifted, ticked, aria-current header row and everything under it is by position the set of alternatives. SyncPathBar.tsx's own header comment states this contract explicitly ("groups play roles by position", "position says 'this is the one you're on'"). Impact is also near zero on realistic data: every switcher in the codebase has exactly one labelled group (label: "Switch to" at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1709/2298/2428/2527 and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1246/1321, one per menuHeader), so a heading has nothing to disambiguate; and at >=6 targets the switcher renders a search field whose placeholder is literally "Switch project…"/"Switch storage…" (line 331), so the "switch" wording is on screen exactly when the list is long enough to need it. The screen-reader half is also not a regression: the old .sync-path-menu-label was a static text div inside role="menu", not an owned menuitem, so AT skipped it in menu mode too; nothing that was announced stopped being announced. The menu is named (role="menu" aria-label="Storage"/"Project"/"Catalog row"), the opener has aria-haspopup + aria-label, and the current row has aria-current plus a check icon. The proposed fix would reverse the direction the user chose after comparing specimens.
correction: Not a copy defect. The only residue worth noting is hygiene: aria-label on a role=generic div (line 343) is inert per ARIA and would be flagged by axe's aria-prohibited-attr rule. It announces nothing and misleads no one — the correct minimal fix is to delete the attribute, or add role="group" if the wrapper is ever meant to be named. Restoring the visible heading would undo the shipped B-Switcher direction.

title: The session timeline readout says "N of M events", which now reads as truncation because tool calls default to hidden
reason: Citation is verbatim-correct (SessionDetailToolbar.tsx:31-34) and the numeric mechanism is real — sessionEventCoverage (sessionDetailModel.ts:149-160) takes no filter argument while loadedCount is events.length (SessionDetailPage.tsx:466). But the claimed defect does not hold. (a) The finding's key evidence is inverted: the comment says the denominator is "the whole record" and the numerator is what is "on screen" — accurate under any filter set — and the behavior is pinned as intended by a test literally named "the toolbar states one count, with the denominator the page never had", asserting /5 of 10\+ events/ against a total of 10 (session-detail.integration.test.tsx:229-242). (b) The filter-caused gap predates the change: in git diff, `intermediateSteps: false` is a context line, not an added one, so the readout already under-counted by a default the user never set. (c) Paging is a co-equal cause the finding omits — TIMELINE_PAGE_SIZE=50 (SessionDetailPage.tsx:33) caps events.length independently of filters, so under the OLD defaults the same 260-event session painted "50 of 260 events", a wider gap than the "38 of 260" called newly alarming. (d) The proposed fix is not implementable: it would misattribute the paging shortfall to filters, and coverage.total is null when any supported count is unknown and only `approximate` when any is a lower_bound, so a printed exact hiddenCount would fabricate precision the model deliberately refuses (sessionDetailModel.ts:144-148, 155-157). (e) The cause is already adjacent on screen: .session-detail-toolbar is one flex row (App.css:6946) with the readout at margin-left:auto (App.css:7032) beside the unpressed "Tool calls 222" toggle, and the empty state reads "No events match these filters. Turn another kind back on in the row above." (SessionDetailTimeline.tsx:92-97). What remains is an unverified assertion about reader interpretation of a numerically accurate string, not a code defect.
correction: Both numbers are correct by their own definitions and the divergence is by design ("on screen" vs "whole record"), documented in the comment and pinned by test. The uncommitted `toolCalls: false` default does widen the gap and removes the Load-more affordance on short conversation-only sessions, leaving filters as the only unexplained cause of the shortfall — a marginal copy-polish opportunity at most, not a data-loss claim, and not something the proposed hiddenCount arithmetic can state honestly given lower_bound/null counts.

title: The session timeline readout says "N of M events", which now reads as truncation because tool calls default to hidden
reason:
Refuted on three grounds: pre-existing, intentional, and misdiagnosed.

(a) Not introduced by the change. In the actual diff of sessionDetailModel.ts, `intermediateSteps: false` is a CONTEXT line, not an added one — steps were already off at HEAD, and `intermediate_steps` (a lower_bound count) already fed the denominator. The numerator and denominator already disagreed before this commit.

(b) The numerator is paging-bound, not filter-bound. SessionDetailPage.tsx:33 sets TIMELINE_PAGE_SIZE = 50 and SessionDetailTimeline.tsx:156-165 renders a "Load 50 more" button whenever nextCursor exists. On the finding's own 260-event example the readout said "50 of 260+ events" BEFORE the change, with every filter on. "N of M" is fundamentally a load-progress readout, and the control that resolves it sits directly beneath the list. The default change alters the resting number, not the semantics.

(c) The cause is rendered in the same strip. SessionDetailToolbar renders the toggle row and the readout side by side: "Tool calls 160" appears with aria-pressed="false" immediately left of "38 of 260+ events". Nothing is unreachable, unlabeled, or lost — one click restores it. The "+" from coverage.approximate further frames the denominator as an estimate of the whole record rather than a load target. No error styling, no warning notice, and when the filtered set is fully loaded no Load-more button appears to suggest a stall.

(d) Deliberate design, pinned by tests. tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:230 is named "the toolbar states one count, with the denominator the page never had", and a sibling assertion pins that "the count that contradicted the filter panel" was removed. A whole-record denominator was explicitly chosen over a filter-agreeing one.

(e) The proposed fix is worse. `total - loadedCount` conflates filtered-out events with not-yet-paged ones, so "222 hidden by Show filters" would be factually false on any session over 50 events. An accurate hidden-by-filter figure needs the off-toggle counts, which are lower bounds — precision sessionEventCoverage deliberately declines to claim (that is what `approximate` and "Unavailable" exist for).

At most this is a copy-nuance preference on long-standing behavior, with no user-visible loss and disambiguating controls adjacent.
correction: If restated accurately: "The toolbar readout has always used a whole-record denominator against a filtered-and-paged numerator (page size 50), so it reads N-of-M-with-a-gap in nearly every session regardless of filter defaults; turning tool calls off by default widens the typical gap but changes nothing structural." That is a pre-existing, test-pinned design choice, not a defect introduced by the uncommitted change.

title: Switcher target rows drop the path that distinguishes same-named projects and storages
reason: The citation is exact: src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:191 matches verbatim at that line number, and the git diff confirms the suppression is new (HEAD's line 224 had no `target` clause). The mechanism reproduces: renderItem(item, true) is called only from the labelled-group `lists.map` block, `.target` has no CSS rule in App.css to restore anything, and no test pins the behavior. So switch targets with a path detail genuinely lose their second line. BUT the finding's headline example is refuted by a backend invariant the finder missed: project labels ARE uniqueness-constrained. src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:13043 `deduplicated_local_alias` builds its taken-set from `local_alias ?? display_name` — precisely what `projectLabel` (src/components/project-sync/model.ts:32) renders — and appends " (2)", " (3)", …. It runs on both registration paths (service.rs:14539 and 16945) and is pinned by tests at service.rs:19855/19859. Two projects both showing "api" cannot arise from registration; only a deliberate rename can collide, since rename_local_project_with_repository (service.rs:13648) skips the dedup. The defect therefore does not hold for the cited ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2432 case in normal use. It does hold for storages — crates/mallard-domain/src/lib.rs:810 validates storage name as display text only, with no uniqueness check, and storageSubtitleIsPath is true for kind === "local" — and for the catalog scope switcher (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1326-1328), where catalogScopeLabel is "<plural> · <profile display_name>" over folder-stem-derived profile names with no dedup, leaving configured_home as the sole differentiator. Two further mitigations were missed: `title` IS set on these rows, and since the button's accessible name comes from its contents, title maps to the accessible description, so screen-reader users are read the path; and at >= 6 targets the search field's `matches` predicate tests `${item.label} ${item.detail}`, so a path fragment still filters. The gap is confined to sighted keyboard-only and touch users, the collision requires duplicate user-typed storage names or same-named parent folders, and the worst outcome is switching to the wrong scope — immediately visible and recoverable by switching again. Real, but narrower and less severe than stated.
correction: Switcher target rows drop the path line for storages and catalog scopes, whose names are not uniqueness-constrained. SyncPathBar.tsx:191 suppresses the `detail` second line for any switch target with `detailIsPath`, so identically-named targets render as visually identical icon+name rows. This does NOT affect the project switcher as claimed: `deduplicated_local_alias` (src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:13043, called at 14539 and 16945, tests at 19855/19859) guarantees `local_alias ?? display_name` — exactly what `projectLabel` renders — is unique per machine, appending " (2)", " (3)", …; only a manual rename, which skips the dedup, can collide. It does affect local storages (no uniqueness check on storage name; crates/mallard-domain/src/lib.rs:810) and catalog scopes (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1326-1328, where `catalogScopeLabel` is "<plural> · <profile display_name>" over folder-stem-derived, non-deduped profile names, leaving `configured_home` the only differentiator). Mitigations the finding omits: `title` is set on these rows and, because the accessible name comes from the button's contents, is exposed as the accessible description, so screen-reader users do get the path; and at >= 6 targets the search field matches against `detail`, so a path fragment filters the list. The residual gap is sighted keyboard-only and touch users, and the consequence — switching to the wrong storage or scope — is visible and reversible.

title: A group of sessions is headed "Uncommitted", which in a Git view reads as uncommitted changes
reason:
The heading text is real (src/components/project-sync/ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1895), but the finding is a style preference against a documented, deliberate, and user-reviewed naming decision, with no realistic user consequence. 1. Deliberate and documented. Three separate design documents name this section and explicitly anticipate the exact confusion the finding raises, then reject it: docs/git-chat-mapping-design/README.md:27 ("The `Uncommitted Changes` label means no overlapping commit and no qualifying follow-up commit on the recorded branch. It does not describe current `git status`."), docs/git-chat-mapping-design/gaps-and-validation.md:7 ("temporal classification, not a claim about current working-tree modifications"), and .superdesign/design-system.md:26 (same sentence, in the component list). The term is also load-bearing in the mapping spec's own vocabulary (README.md:36-38, technical-design.md:76/86/103: a session "lives in exactly one place on the rail — one commit or `Uncommitted`"). This is a decision made with the ambiguity in view, not an oversight. 2. User-reviewed specimen. Both design specimens the user reviewed and picked from carry this exact head — activity-mockup.html:274/280/281 (the A/B/C flavours, with "Uncommitted" as the group head in every one, and the description at line 287 naming "Uncommitted's head") and codex-retheme-mockup.html:1190. Per the repo's own workflow (memory: "Review UI changes as static HTML"), the heading passed a human design review in its current form. 3. Pinned test. tests/frontend/project-activity.integration.test.tsx:1543 asserts the exact markup `

…Uncommitted

`, and the neighbouring assertions show the group's copy was tuned deliberately (count badge removed, reason text deliberately withheld: "The unmapped reason is bookkeeping, not something the reader needs on screen"). The proposed change breaks a test that was written on purpose. 4. No realistic misreading. The section renders only session cards (`uncommittedReferences` are session resources; line 1898 maps them through `renderSession`), sitting directly above a commit rail whose group heads are commit subjects. Nothing on this page renders files or diffs anywhere, in any mode, so a user cannot "expect file diffs" and then be let down — the group's contents are visibly conversations, and "Uncommitted" reads as the counterpart of the commit heads beneath it. It is also literally accurate: these sessions are not captured by any commit. 5. Already handled for the case that matters. The fold control's accessible name spells out the meaning in full ("Collapse N sessions not linked to a commit", line 1891), so the non-visual path already carries the long phrase; the visible head stays short by design. 6. The consistency argument inverts. "Only in " must be a phrase because it interpolates a storage name; "Uncommitted" stands where a commit subject stands on the rail, and a sentence-shaped head ("Not linked to a commit") would read as prose in a column of commit subjects. The two headings follow one rule — name the group's relation to the rail — not two.

title: The project overview counts are hard-plural for two nouns and hard-singular for the third
reason:
The line exists verbatim at src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2756 and I could not refute it on impact, handling, or intent.

Reachability is the app's primary index screen, not an edge path. The heading block renders whenever `!newProjectSetup && !workspaceProject` (line 2749), i.e. the Project links landing page, and it is NOT suppressed by the zero-projects empty state — that empty state is a sibling rendered below it (line 2842), so a fresh install shows the counts strip above "Add a project…". Not handled elsewhere: no wrapper, no parent guard, no test touches it (`.profile-links-counts` appears only in App.css and this one JSX site; no test asserts the string).

Not deliberate. The codebase's house style is to pluralize counts everywhere else, including in this same file (lines 1787, 1790, 2586, 2648, 2691, 2943-2944), plus a `plural()` helper at src/components/project-sync/syncOutcome.ts:59, `countPhrase()` at src/components/project-sync/ProjectActivityPage.tsx:546, and pluralized sidebar count chips. "storage" is not treated as a mass noun in this app either — it is a countable entity the UI elsewhere calls "Storages" (ProjectSidebar.tsx:212, StorageIndexPage.tsx:45, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1686 "All storages"). The App.css comment above the rule ("Counts glued into an English phrase") shows the author reads this as prose, not as category labels. `git log -S` traces the line to a single early bulk commit (faa24dc) and it has never been revisited; nothing in docs/, the mockup specimens, or memory records a decision to leave it.

What it is NOT: no functional, data, or accessibility consequence — it is one small ungrammatical microcopy line. Low is the right severity, and the finding already claims low, so nothing is inflated.
correction: Two details in the write-up are imprecise. (1) The fresh-install string is "0 projects · 0 storage · 0 links", of which only "0 storage" is wrong — "0 projects" and "0 links" are correct at zero, so it is not wrong "in both directions at once" on that path. The accurate statement: two nouns are hard-plural (wrong only at count 1) and one is hard-singular (wrong at every count except 1); the worst realistic case is the common one-project/one-link setup, which reads "1 projects · 1 storage · 1 links". (2) The proposed fix cannot lift ProjectActivityPage.tsx:546's `countPhrase` verbatim — it returns `null` at 0, while this strip must print zeros. Use the inline `${n} noun${n === 1 ? "" : "s"}` branch the rest of the file already uses, or lift a zero-tolerant variant.

title: A group of sessions is headed "Uncommitted", which in a Git view reads as uncommitted changes
reason: The quoted line is verbatim correct (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1895) and the icon really is a pencil, but the finding's supporting argument does not hold and the claimed impact is not reachable. (a) The consistency premise is false: the "Only in <storage>" heading is at line 1876, inside <section className="sync-history-storage-only"> opened at 1868, which renders BEFORE and OUTSIDE the <div className="sync-history-timeline"> opened at 1885 — the code comment at 1861-1867 states this deliberately ("Above the timeline, not on it..."). They are not two headings in one timeline written to different rules; they are two different containers naming different things (a place vs. a rail slot). (b) The disambiguating wording is not confined to a comment: SectionFold (lines 1456-1477) sets label on both aria-label AND title, so the fold beside the heading renders a hover tooltip and accessible name reading "Collapse N sessions not linked to a commit". (c) The claimed impact ("expects file diffs") is not reachable: inside the timeline every other group head is a commit subject + sha, and the rows under this heading are session cards (title, message/tool/token counts, duration, provider marks) with no diff affordance — the group reads as the no-commit slot on the commit rail. (d) The string is a deliberate documented product term, not drift: docs/git-chat-mapping-design/README.md:27 defines it and explicitly disclaims the git-status reading, and tests/frontend/project-activity.integration.test.tsx:1543 pins the exact heading markup. What remains is a subjective preference for a longer heading, not a defect.
correction: A precise version of the residual observation would be: within the git timeline the group head is the single word "Uncommitted" while its explanatory wording ("N sessions not linked to a commit") lives only on the adjacent fold's title/aria-label, so the phrasing is available on hover rather than in the visible heading. It is not a mismatch with the storage-only heading, which is rendered outside the timeline.

title: The Logs drawer titles itself lowercase "log" and cannot distinguish an empty log from a filtered one
reason: Both claims fail against the real code. (1) The title never renders lowercase: src/App.css:544 sets `.log-panel-title { text-transform: uppercase; }`, plus letter-spacing:1px (App.css:10695) and --weight-heavy display face (App.css:8292); App.css is the only stylesheet and nothing overrides text-transform. The user sees a tracked uppercase nameplate "LOG", a deliberate chrome micro-label in the same documented family as .sync-eyebrow, .sync-draft-badge and the adjacent "Type"/"Level" keys and lowercase "clear" button. The lowercase source string is an artifact of that CSS convention, not a copy defect. The drawer already carries the plural as its accessible name — ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:187 `aria-label="Logs"`, test-gated at tests/frontend/activity-log.integration.test.tsx:148 — so screen-reader users get "Logs" and sighted users get a nameplate, neither of which strands anyone. Singular-vs-plural on a tracked uppercase masthead is a style preference with no user-visible consequence. (2) The empty-state scenario is unreachable on the path described. src-tauri/src/lib.rs:65-72 emits and persists a System/info "Mallard started" entry during Tauri setup on every single launch, before any command runs; the defaults are all seven types (ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:70), level "all" (line 71) and empty search, which that entry matches. Retention has a 1-day floor and cleanup preserves the active day's file (crates/mallard-infrastructure/src/activity_log.rs:1017, 1050), so no purge can empty the current day. A user who has never synced, with untouched filters, therefore always sees at least one row — never "No entries match these filters." The only real ways to hit that string are: the user deselected types (ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:119-125 short-circuits to an empty list — the copy is then literally true), the user narrowed level/search (copy true), or a store read failed, in which case the danger Notice "Could not load retained logs: {error}" renders directly above it and explains the emptiness. No realistic user wastes time clearing filters that are not the cause.
correction: The visible title is "LOG" (uppercase via CSS text-transform), not lowercase "log"; the accessible region name is already "Logs". The empty-state message is not reachable with default filters because every launch persists a matching System "Mallard started" entry that survives retention cleanup.

title: Repo chooser always says "resources" and shows the full 32-character repo id as a row subtitle
reason:
The finding bundles three claims; the two that carry its weight are wrong, and the third is a cosmetic nit. (1) "Shows the full 32-character repo id" — no user-visible consequence, and it is the codebase's deliberate convention. `/src/App.css:1714-1722` styles the exact span holding `{match.bundle_id}` (`.sync-bundle-choice-copy span`, shared with `.sync-bundle-match-copy span`, which covers ProjectSetupWorkspace:956) with `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`, and the flex parent at line 1703 carries `min-width: 0` — the textbook flexbox truncation recipe, applied on purpose. The id can never overflow or break the row; it ellipses on its own. In practice it does not even reach that: the dialog is `width: min(680px, …)` (App.css:1729), the copy column is `flex: 1` beside a 17px radio and a `flex-shrink: 0` meta stack, and 32 mono chars at `--type-3xs` occupy roughly 190px of ~450px available. Nothing is clipped, nothing is confusing. (2) The claimed inconsistency with `currentBundleId.slice(0, 12)` is a false equivalence, and the house norm points the other way. The context row at BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:120 inlines the id inside a running sentence ("Current local repo abc123…"), where CSS ellipsis cannot apply to a fragment and the id is a hint, not a selector. In the chooser rows the id is a standalone monospace identifier whose job is to disambiguate — which is the entire reason the chooser exists, since `display_name` can repeat across repos. The app's own dedicated-id-field convention is the full value: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:447 renders `
Repository ID
{bundle.bundle_id}
` untruncated. Applying the proposed `slice(0, 12)` would make these rows the outlier and would shorten the only unique key the user has for telling two same-named repos apart. (3) "rev" — a compact label in a narrow right-aligned meta column at `--type-2xs`/`--type-3xs` (App.css:1724-1727). The cited "Revision" at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:455 is a two-part chip in a much wider layout, not the same slot. "rev" is universally legible, and the value itself is described in-code as "server-owned bookkeeping" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:659). Pure preference. Only the plural survives, and it is trivial. "1 resources" is reachable (a repo holding one session), and the codebase does branch plurals elsewhere (SettingsPage, ProjectActivityPage, ProjectFilesReviewPage), so it is a real deviation — but the number sits directly beside the noun, nothing is misread, no action is misdirected, and the app's convention for this specific datum is a label/value pair with no plural at all (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:421-422: `
Resources
{bundle.resource_count}
`). No test asserts the string; the fixtures in tests/frontend/repo-bundle-convergence.integration.test.tsx use counts of 2 and 0, both grammatical. This dialog also already went through a dedicated copy/terminology audit: docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md cites BundleConnectionDialog.tsx#L123 (this very choice list) and #L96 (its copy) and raised only repo/repository naming — not id length, not the plural, not "rev". A prior pass over these exact lines judged none of this worth listing.
correction: Only one atom of the finding holds: BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:145 renders `{match.resource_count ?? 0} resources` without branching the noun, so a repo containing exactly one resource reads "1 resources" — a cosmetic deviation from the plural-branching used elsewhere in the app. The id and "rev" halves of the finding do not hold: the id already truncates via CSS ellipsis (App.css:1714-1722, with `min-width: 0` at 1703) and in a 680px dialog does not overflow at all, and rendering a full bundle id in a dedicated id slot is the established convention (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:447). Applying the proposed `slice(0, 12)` would remove disambiguating characters from the one control whose purpose is telling same-named repos apart.

title: One project-file row calls the same entry a Folder, a Directory, and a folder
reason: Read src/components/project-sync/ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx directly. Line 426 matches the quoted evidence verbatim, including the line number: `entryTypeLabel={isDirectory ? "Directory" : row.entryType === "blocked" ? "Blocked entry" : "Regular file"}`. Line 407 is `{isDirectory ? "Folder" : fileKindLabel(row.relativePath)}` and line 403 puts "Folder" in the tooltip too. Lines 75-76 in `pullOperationLabel` are "Delete folder"/"Create folder" as quoted. ProjectFileDetailsMenu.tsx:51 renders the prop with no transformation — `{ key: "type", label: "Type", value: entryTypeLabel }` — so the string reaches the user unaltered; there is no fallback, override, or call-site condition that rewrites it. pullReviewModel.ts:376-377 does say "Project folder"/"Project file" as claimed. Both the metric chip (always rendered) and the details menu button sit on the same card for the same row, so a directory row genuinely presents "Folder" in the chip and "Directory" one click away in Type. Defect confirmed; it is cosmetic copy drift inside a popover, so low severity is right.
correction: The row carries two competing words, not three: "Folder"/"folder" are the same word in different sentence positions, so the actual clash is "Directory" (details-menu Type field) vs "Folder" (metric chip and operation chips). Two secondary details in the finding need adjusting: (1) the "Create folder"/"Delete folder" chip from `pullOperationLabel` only renders on Pull rows — line 370 gates it behind `mode === "pull"`; on a Push directory row the chip position instead reads "Required folder" (line 371), so a folder-word is present in both modes but not the one quoted. (2) "Regular file" is not free-floating stat(1) jargon — it is the other arm of the same ternary as "Blocked entry", and blocked entries are exactly symlinks and non-regular file types (service.rs:1548, 3712), so "Regular" is carrying that contrast. The identical pair appears at ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:246. Flattening it to "File" therefore drops a real distinction and must be done in both files together, or the Type field ends up saying "File" for something the row elsewhere calls blocked.

title: The Logs drawer titles itself lowercase "log" and cannot distinguish an empty log from a filtered one
reason: Both citations exist verbatim at the stated lines (LogPanel.tsx:240 and :358), but the headline half of the finding is wrong. The title is NOT lowercase as rendered: App.css:544-547 sets `.log-panel-title { color: var(--text-1); text-transform: uppercase; }`. App.css is the project's only stylesheet, and the three other `.log-panel-title` rules (8227 font-family/weight, 8292 font-weight, 10695 font-size + letter-spacing:1px) set no text-transform, so nothing overrides it. The panel renders "LOG" — display face, heavy weight, 1px tracking — a deliberate all-caps chrome eyebrow, the same treatment as sibling labels like `.log-type`. The finder read JSX source text as if it were rendered copy (the repo's own "verify CSS by computed style" lesson). The accessibility half of the impact claim also fails: the drawer wrapper in ActivityLogDrawer.tsx carries role="region" aria-label="Logs", so the accessible name already matches the sidebar item (ProjectSidebar.tsx:749) and the Settings heading (SettingsPage.tsx:569). The only surviving delta is singular "LOG" vs plural "Logs" in a stylized label — much weaker than "lowercase singular". The SECOND half of the finding does reproduce: LogPanel.tsx:355-359 branches only on `loading` and `lines.length === 0`, never on filter state, and ActivityLogDrawer.tsx initialises logTypeFilters to all ACTIVITY_LOG_TYPES, logLevelFilter to "all" and search to "", so a fresh install whose retained log is genuinely empty is told "No entries match these filters." with no filter narrowed. Since one of the two bundled defects is independently reproduced in source, refuted=false with the finding narrowed to the empty-state copy.
correction: Drop the title claim entirely — App.css:546 applies `text-transform: uppercase` to `.log-panel-title`, so the panel renders "LOG", not lowercase "log", and the drawer's accessible name is already "Logs" via aria-label on the region in ActivityLogDrawer.tsx. Corrected finding: LogPanel.tsx:358 renders "No entries match these filters." whenever `lines.length === 0` and loading has finished, without consulting filter state; ActivityLogDrawer.tsx defaults to all types, level "all" and empty search, so an empty retained log (fresh install, no sync yet) blames filters the user never touched. Fix: branch the empty copy on whether any filter is narrowed — "No activity logged yet." when typeFilters covers all ACTIVITY_LOG_TYPES, levelFilter === "all" and search is empty; keep the filter wording otherwise.

title: One project-file row calls the same entry a Folder, a Directory, and a folder
reason: No real user-visible consequence, and the premise is factually wrong in two places. (1) The three strings are not one register: ProjectFileDetailsMenu is documented in its own header as "the project-file counterpart to a session's debug-info menu" — a click-to-open, portalled inspector of copyable technical values (absolute Path, Type, Mode, Modified), where Mode is printed by formatMode (ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:154-156) as an octal POSIX mode ("0644"). "Regular file"/"Directory" is the stat(1) vocabulary that pairs with an octal mode; the proposed "File"/"Folder" would leave "Mode: 0755" under Finder words. (2) The finding mislabels the metric chip: line 403/407 renders `Kind · {isDirectory ? "Folder" : fileKindLabel(...)}`, and fileKindLabel (model.ts:115-120) returns a FORMAT name — "TypeScript", "Markdown", "PNG", or the bare uppercased extension — never "File". So no collision exists on file rows at all; on directory rows it reduces to "Folder" vs "Directory", exact synonyms. (3) entryTypeLabel carries information the chip cannot: it is the only place "Blocked entry" is named, and "Regular file" is load-bearing here because capture rejects symlinks and non-regular files (provider_capture.rs:1276, 1548, 1912, 1942) — the proposed fix erases that distinction. (4) pullReviewModel.ts:376-382 is a different taxonomy (itemKindLabel names resource kinds across the whole Pull review: Conversation / Project folder / Project file / File / Definition); the "Project" prefix disambiguates from conversations, and line 383 already spends the bare word "File" on a different kind, so the proposed rename would collide. (5) Nothing branches on the string, no test asserts it, and ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:246 already uses identical labels, so the two surfaces sharing the component are consistent with each other.

title: The storage crumb reads "(unnamed)" but announces "Unnamed storage"
reason: The quoted lines exist verbatim at /src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2343-2349, but all three placeholders are UNREACHABLE dead fallbacks on that element, and the cross-app "split vocabulary" claim misreads a convention the code already follows. 1) An unnamed storage cannot reach this crumb. `workspaceStorage` is drawn from `workspaceLinkedStorages` (line 1446) — a COMMITTED, linked storage, never a draft. Three independent gates guarantee a committed storage has a non-empty name: (a) `newStorage()` in StorageSettings.tsx:117 seeds every new storage with `"Local storage N"` / `"R2 storage N"`, so the field is never blank to begin with; (b) `storageConfigReady()` at StorageSettings.tsx:105 returns false on `!storage.name?.trim()`, and it disables every save/finish button at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2098, 2185, 2194; (c) the Rust backend rejects it outright — `validate_name` at crates/mallard-application/src/storage_setup.rs:1292-1299 errors `storage_name_invalid` on `name.is_empty()`, and it is called on both storage-creating paths (lines 443 and 699, i.e. the R2 upsert the UI calls via `upsertR2Storage`). So no user, with any realistic data, ever sees "(unnamed)", "Storage", or "Unnamed storage" on this crumb. The only surface where a blank name is genuinely reachable is a half-finished setup DRAFT (StorageIndexPage.tsx:117, ProjectSidebar.tsx:1085) — and every draft site uses the same single string, "(unnamed)". 2) The app is already standardised one-form-per-object-type, which is exactly what the "fix" proposes. Storages: "(unnamed)" at 10 sites (StorageIndexPage 74/117, ProjectSidebar 1054/1085, ProjectLinksWorkspace 1570/1662/1714/2301/3255, ProjectSetupWorkspace 858, ProjectSync 1659, StorageCatalogPage 1207/1251). Sessions: "Untitled session" at 5 sites (ProjectActivityPage 1164/1206, syncOutcome.ts:64, SessionDetailHeader 40, SessionDetailPage 183). Repos: "Unnamed repository" (ProjectLinksWorkspace:442). Different NOUNS for different object types is the intended vocabulary, not an inconsistency. 3) The per-surface variation is defensible, not a defect. A visible crumb in a width-constrained path bar, a tooltip, and a spoken aria-label are three different registers; no single user perceives more than one of them for a given element. Reading "(unnamed). Storage menu" aloud is worse than "Unnamed storage.
