Storage menu" — screen readers announce parentheses inconsistently — so spelling the aria form out is the better a11y choice, and "Storage · /path" reads correctly as a tooltip where a parenthesised token would not. 4) The string is pinned by existing gates. tests/frontend/project-sync-cutover.integration.test.tsx:517 asserts the exact source text `label: workspaceStorage.name || "(unnamed)",` and tests/frontend/storage-settings.integration.test.tsx:826 asserts a rendered `(unnamed)`. Changing the wording breaks two green tests to alter text no user can reach.
correction: The accurate, much narrower statement: the blank-name fallbacks at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2343-2349 (and 2646/2648, which add a fourth variant, "storage") are dead defensive code — a linked storage always has a name, enforced by `newStorage()`, `storageConfigReady()`, and Rust `validate_name`. If anyone touches them it is a tidiness nit, not a copy defect.

title: Switcher type-ahead cannot reach the footer's text pills because their label lookup resolves to an empty string
reason: Verified in the real file. Lines 291-295 match the quoted evidence verbatim (cited line 292 is the querySelector line). renderPill (SyncPathBar.tsx:223-245) is the only tail renderer: it emits role="menuitem" (so menuOptions in menuKeyboard.ts collects it), explicitly sets aria-label={tail ? undefined : item.label}, and renders the visible text as a bare {item.label} with no .sync-path-menu-copy ancestor. The label map therefore resolves querySelector -> null -> undefined, getAttribute("aria-label") -> null -> undefined, and falls through to "", and "".startsWith(buffer) is false for every non-empty buffer, so tails can never be selected by type-ahead. Verb pills are unaffected because they carry aria-label. Confirmed against real call sites: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2273-2340 builds a switcher (menuHeader present) whose trailing unlabelled group is "Link storage…" and "Add storage…", collected into `tails` at line 171 and rendered via renderPill(item, true); StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1263-1270 does the same with "Add storage…". No guard rescues it: the label map never consults `title`, moveMenuFocus returns false for single printable keys so the type-ahead does run, and the only early return is when focus is inside the search input — while focus lands on options[0] (a menu option) when a menu opens via focusMenuOption. No CSS or other component supplies the missing wrapper.
correction: Precise statement: tail pills in a switcher's footer render their label in a bare <span> with aria-label explicitly undefined (SyncPathBar.tsx:232, 242), so the type-ahead label lookup at lines 291-295 computes "" for them and they are permanently unreachable by typing. Scope of the impact is narrower than "cannot reach": tails remain reachable by ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End and by mouse, and their `title` tooltip is correct — only the type-ahead ring skips them. Also note the type-ahead only runs when focus is on a menu option (where it lands on open); when a switcher is searchable (>= 6 targets) and focus is in the search field, keystrokes go to the field and never reach this code. Category is keyboard/accessibility behavior rather than copy.

title: Switcher type-ahead cannot reach the footer's text pills because their label lookup resolves to an empty string
reason: The DOM mechanism is real (tail pills compute a "" typeahead label), but the user-visible consequence claimed does not exist. (1) Not unreachable: the foot strip renders last (SyncPathBar.tsx:349-357), so tail pills are the FINAL role="menuitem" nodes in the menu. moveMenuFocus (menuKeyboard.ts) maps End to the last option and wraps ArrowUp-from-first to the last option, and the crumb opener's ArrowUp handler (line 523) opens the menu directly onto the last option. "Add storage…" is therefore the cheapest keyboard target in the entire menu — one keystroke — not an unreachable one. (2) Deliberate design: the file's own doc comment (lines 119-127) and the project memory note switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md state that labelled groups are the switch list and trailing unlabelled groups are "the ways to get more", demoted out of the list into a footer strip so "the list itself is only the things you can switch to". Typeahead is the list-navigation aid; the tails are by construction not list entries. (3) The proposed fix fights the codebase's accessible-name discipline: the aria-label fallback at line 293 was added in this same uncommitted change specifically because verbs are ICON-ONLY and need a name; tails carry visible text, so aria-label={tail ? undefined : item.label} is the correct choice — adding one would be a redundant accessible name duplicating the visible label (WCAG 2.5.3 drift risk). (4) Realistic data weakens it further: in the only real caller (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2318) one of the two tails, "Link storage…", is routinely disabled with a reason, so typeahead focus on it would be inert regardless. (5) Category mismatch: filed under a copy/terminology lens, but no string, label, or term a user reads is wrong — this is a keyboard-affordance nit, not a copy defect. Nothing is lost: the pills are clickable, arrow-reachable, End-reachable, and visible in a ~300px popover footer.
correction: If kept at all, the accurate statement is narrower: "Switcher footer text pills are excluded from the type-ahead prefix ring because their label lookup finds neither a .sync-path-menu-copy > span nor an aria-label. They remain fully reachable by click, ArrowUp/ArrowDown wrap, and End (they are the last options in the menu), so the effect is that one keyboard shortcut among several does not target them." The 'never lands on Add storage… no matter how many times it is pressed' framing implies inaccessibility, which is false. If a change is wanted, the correct one is a final textContent fallback in the label map — not an aria-label on a button that already has visible text.

title: The storage crumb reads "(unnamed)" but announces "Unnamed storage"
reason: Citation is exact and the code behaves as described. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2343 is `label: workspaceStorage.name || "(unnamed)"`, :2346 is `title: ${workspaceStorage.name || "Storage"} · …`, :2347 is `ariaLabel: ${workspaceStorage.name || "Unnamed storage"}. Storage menu`. SyncPathBar.tsx:535-576 renders all three on the same crumb element (title, aria-label, and the visible label span), so an unnamed storage really does show "(unnamed)", tooltip "Storage · <subtitle>", and accessible name "Unnamed storage. Storage menu". A fourth form, lowercase "storage", appears in the same file's Push/Pull titles (2646, 2648-2649, 2689-2692). The adjacent storage-setup crumb (1570, 1696-1702) reuses one `storageName` constant across label/title/ariaLabel, so 2343 is the outlier rather than a deliberate pattern. Two caveats reduce, but do not remove, the finding. (1) Reachability: storageConfigReady (StorageSettings.tsx:104-105) rejects a blank name and gates the editor's Save (2098/2185/2194), and rename requires a non-empty draft (1569), so the normal UI cannot mint an empty-named storage; the branch is defensive. It is not dead by contract though — the domain explicitly allows it (crates/mallard-domain/src/lib.rs:810 passes allow_empty = true) and the backend carries its own id fallback (src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:1009/1032/1099), so a hand-edited or legacy config surfaces it. (2) The app-wide half of the evidence does not hold: "Unnamed repository" (line 442) names a bundle and "Untitled session"/"Untitled thread" name sessions, different object types; storages already read "(unnamed)" consistently everywhere else (StorageIndexPage.tsx:74/117, ProjectSidebar.tsx:1054/1085, ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:858, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1207/1251, ProjectSync.tsx:1659). So the real defect is local to this one crumb, not a split vocabulary across the app. Severity stays low: cosmetic, and only observable for a storage state the editor's save gate blocks.
correction: Within one crumb in ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx (2343-2347, plus the "storage" fallback at 2646-2692) an unnamed storage is given four different placeholder names — "(unnamed)" visibly, "Storage" in the tooltip, "Unnamed storage" to a screen reader, "storage" in the Push/Pull titles — while the sibling storage-setup crumb at 1570/1696-1702 already reuses a single `storageName` constant across all three slots. The app-wide inconsistency claim is wrong: placeholder vocabulary is already consistent per object type ("(unnamed)" for storages everywhere else, "Unnamed repository" for bundles, "Untitled session" for sessions). Fix is to hoist one `storageName` constant at 2343 the way 1570 does. Note the branch only renders for an empty storage name, which storageConfigReady blocks on save, so it is defensive-only in the shipped UI.

title: Catalog kinds expose the internal format version as the user-facing name, with no way to tell the two apart
reason:
Refuted on three independent grounds: the version is not internal, the split is an explicitly documented decision, and there is no user-visible consequence on the realistic path.

1) "v1/v2" is the PROVIDER's vocabulary, not Mallard's internal format version. `src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/codex_pet.rs:20-22` shows the discriminator is Codex's own `spriteVersionNumber` field inside the user's `pet.json` ("absent for v1 and exactly `2` for v2"), written by Codex into `<CODEX_HOME>/pets/<name>/pet.json`. Naming the kinds "Pet v1"/"Pet v2" mirrors the exact token the user's own files and the source app carry. Inventing app-only names would be the terminology defect, not the fix.

2) The split — and specifically the decision that the two are told apart by label alone — is deliberate and documented at three layers, not an oversight. `src/components/storage-catalog/model.ts:21-24` (the comment the finding itself cites): "Pet v1 and v2 are distinct rows because the portable format is the discriminator; there is no conversion — so they share one glyph and are told apart by their label." Mirrored in `src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/domain.rs:252-254` and in `docs/CLOUDFLARE_R2_MANAGED_CLOUD_ARCHITECTURE_V2.md:519-539` §5.4: "V1 and V2 are different resource kinds and can coexist as independent Catalog items… V1 does not convert between pet formats." A finding that contradicts an explicit, cross-layer, doc-backed product decision is a preference.

3) No realistic consequence. Choosing a kind in Add is free, reversible (row removal exists), non-destructive, and by design both rows may coexist. The moment a row exists, the app answers "which one are my pets" unmistakably: pet rows are the one kind that renders artwork — `StorageCatalogPage.tsx:506-543` draws a `catalog-pet-preview` idle-frame tile per pet with the pet's display name and its description as tooltip — and an empty row states it in words at `StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1966`: "No pet v1 on this Mac, and none stored yet." One click resolves the ambiguity with the user's own sprites on screen. `service.rs:3186-3196` even pins the behavior in a test (a v1 pet never renders in the v2 scope).

4) The evidence is imprecise about the subtitle. `AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:243` is a PROVIDER-availability line ("Codex only" vs "Codex and Claude"), a different axis; Skill and Plugin likewise share "Codex and Claude", so a shared subtitle across a pair is the norm in that list, not a pet-specific defect. And the proposed fix is not truthfully writable as stated: both formats live in the same `<CODEX_HOME>/pets` root (`inventory.rs:293`; `service.rs:3187` "shares the pets directory but not the row"), so "where each is stored" is identical, and the only real difference is atlas grid geometry (8x9 vs 8x11 cells, `domain.rs:270-284`) — putting that in a radio subtitle would expose MORE internal format detail, inverting the finding's own complaint.

At most this is a cosmetic copy nit (a one-line hint could name Codex's sprite version), not a defect.

title: Catalog kinds expose the internal format version as the user-facing name, with no way to tell the two apart
reason: Reproduced directly in source. model.ts lines 34-35 (finding says 33 — off by one) define `{ kind: "codex_pet_v1", label: "Pet v1", plural: "Pets v1", icon: "paw" }` and the v2 twin. AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:229 maps CATALOG_KINDS with NO filter, so both pet options always appear; line 243 renders `option.label` and line 244 renders `option.kind.startsWith("codex_pet") ? "Codex only" : "Codex and Claude"` — both pet rows therefore get the byte-identical subtitle "Codex only". I read the entire 383-line file: the only other copy is the profile hint "Each Catalog resource tracks one kind from one agent profile." Nothing on the screen explains what a v1 vs v2 pet is. StorageCatalogPage.tsx:941 is exactly `${count} ${noun} ${phrase}` with noun = kind.plural.toLowerCase(), so "2 pets v1 changed on both sides" is accurate. catalogScopeLabel (model.ts:43-49) does feed sidebar and path-bar names. Two stated details are wrong: (1) the Add radio list renders no icon at all — the shared paw glyph appears on other surfaces (ProjectSidebar.tsx:973, CatalogIndexPage.tsx:56, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1329), not on the screen the finding centers on; (2) the discriminator is not purely internal — codex_pet.rs:194-196 reads `sprite_version_number` from the user's own pet.json (absent = V1, 2 = V2), though V1 pets carry no marker so the user still cannot tell without opening the file. The proposed fix is also partly unbuildable as written: both formats live in the SAME `<CODEX_HOME>/pets` directory (inventory.rs:293; service.rs:3187 comment "The sibling v2 scope shares the pets directory but not the row"), so a subtitle about "where each is stored" would state a falsehood. The real difference is the sprite atlas (domain.rs:271-284): 1536x1872 / 8x9 cells for v1 vs 1536x2288 / 8x11 for v2. Severity stays low: worst case a user creates the wrong row, sees it empty, and removes it — no data or correctness impact.
correction: Catalog kinds label two pet formats by version number alone. src/components/storage-catalog/model.ts:34-35 defines `codex_pet_v1` / `codex_pet_v2` as "Pet v1" / "Pet v2" ("Pets v1" / "Pets v2"). AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:229 renders CATALOG_KINDS unfiltered, and line 244 gives every codex_pet kind the same subtitle "Codex only", so the Add Catalog resource radio list shows two options differing only by a version digit, with no other copy anywhere in the flow explaining the difference. (The radio options render no glyph; the shared paw appears on sidebar/index/path-bar rows instead.) The labels also flow into catalogScopeLabel row names and the count sentence at StorageCatalogPage.tsx:941. The version comes from the pet's own pet.json `sprite_version_number` (codex_pet.rs:194-196; absent = v1), but v1 pets declare nothing, so a user cannot tell which they have from the UI. Fix by giving each option a distinguishing subtitle in AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx — note that both formats install into the same `<CODEX_HOME>/pets` directory, so the distinguisher must be the sprite sheet (v2 declares sprite_version_number 2 and carries the taller 11-row atlas; v1 declares none), not a storage location.

title: Older-activity fold nests two (and with the inert sub-fold, three) identical ink frames inside each other
reason: Independently reproduced from source. src/App.css:6535 is verbatim `.sync-history-older-group > .sync-history-thread-list { padding: 10px 12px; }`, and `.sync-history-older-group` (actually L6511, not L6509) carries `border: var(--box-border); border-radius: var(--retro-panel-radius); box-shadow: var(--shadow-card); overflow: hidden`. `.sync-history-thread-list.flat` at L9804 now declares the same `--box-border` (2px solid var(--accent), L7947) and `--retro-panel-radius` (14px, L8084) plus `background: var(--surface-row)` and `box-shadow: var(--shadow-card)`. The group's direct child at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2061 is `sync-history-thread-list flat`, so both frames draw. No override exists: `grep "\.flat"` over App.css yields only 8 selectors, the only ancestor-scoped resets are `.sync-history-uncommitted` (L9395) and `.sync-history-storage-only` (L10011), and the older section (tsx:2050) is a SIBLING of those two sections (1868-1882, 1887-1900), not nested — verified by matching section open/close pairs. App.css is the only stylesheet under src/, so no second sheet can reset it. Specificity is a (0,2,0) tie between L6535 and L9804 and L6535 declares only padding, so nothing suppresses the frame; the group has no padding, so the inner list's border box is flush with the group's inner edge (4px of identical accent ink, 14px inner radius colliding with a 12px effective outer inner-corner, inner shadow fully clipped by the group's overflow:hidden). tsx:2076 nests a third `.flat` list inside `.sync-history-older-inert` (whose own border was deleted in this change; L6539/6547 style only its summary), giving three nested frames when that fold is open. The oversight reading is confirmed by `git diff -U8 HEAD`: `.flat` was `gap: 5px` with no frame at HEAD, and the author added `box-shadow: none;` to BOTH sibling resets in this same uncommitted change while adding nothing for the older group.
correction: Two precision fixes. (1) The group rule is at src/App.css:6511, not 6509. (2) Reachability is narrower than claimed: the render gate at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2049 is `!selectionReviewEmpty && selectionMode && !activity.older && olderEntries.length > 0`, so it also requires the activity feed to be fully paged (`activity.older === null`), not merely that a Push/Pull selection review has out-of-window sessions. Also worth noting for the fix: the two sibling resets are not new code the author wrote alongside this change — they pre-existed at HEAD, and what this change added to each was the single `box-shadow: none;` line, which is the reset the older group is missing.

title: The Files-page search input is overridden by the same generic input skin, so its retheme edit never lands
reason: The cascade is real and verified: .sync-project-files-search input (App.css:6373, specificity 0,1,1) loses border-color/border-radius/background/box-shadow to .sync-app input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]) (L8568, 0,3,1, later in source); only the 2px width and 14px padding survive. The secondary claims check out too (.sync-path-rename input L3339 and .catalog-fork-drawer input L6751 both lose their intentional --focus-ring border). And the codex-retheme-cutover record explicitly says the Files search input was made "pill+ink+shadow with a focus ring", so the written intent and the rendered result genuinely disagree. However the impact framing is inflated on three counts. (1) It is NOT a retheme regression: git show HEAD:src/App.css contains the identical generic skin at the same position, so at HEAD the rule's 1px/--control-border/7px/--bg-1 lost exactly the same four declarations. The block has been inert for many commits; no user has ever seen this field wear its own rule. (2) The claim that it is "the one control on that screen that does not wear the new box grammar" is false — the same retheme record states "Left deliberately quiet: inputs/selects (4px), segments' 1px chrome, notices, review rows, ghosts, checkbox families, tabs' underline style", and the Files page carries quiet checkboxes, ghosts, review rows and notices by design. The field reads as an ordinary app input matching every other text input in .sync-app; the only real oddity is 2px where sibling inputs are 1px. (3) Zero functional or accessibility consequence: the focus ring at L6386 is (0,2,1) and sets `outline`, which the generic skin never declares, so focus behaviour is intact. The trap itself is already known and documented in the project record (the log-toolbar note names the exact (0,3,1) specificity and the fix shape). Net: a genuine cosmetic polish gap on one field, on a pre-existing cascade — low, not medium.
correction: Cosmetic only, and pre-existing rather than introduced by the retheme. The generic skin at L8568 is byte-identical at HEAD, so the L6373 block was already fully overridden before the retheme (its old 1px/--control-border/7px/--bg-1 lost the same four declarations); the retheme merely rewrote a rule that had been inert for many commits. The rendered field is a normal .sync-app input (4px radius, --button-border, --bg-4, inset shadow) — consistent with every other text input in the app, which the cutover record says were "left deliberately quiet"; the only visual oddity is a 2px border where sibling inputs are 1px. The "one control on that screen not wearing the new box grammar" claim is wrong: checkboxes, ghosts, review rows and notices on that page are deliberately quiet too. Focus behaviour is unaffected (the L6386 focus-visible rule sets `outline`, which the generic skin never declares). The real defect is narrower: the retheme's own third-pass note records the Files search input as pill+ink+shadow, and the code does not deliver that.

title: The new switcher search field is silently overridden by the generic `.sync-app input` skin — every declaration but the border width is dead
reason: I tried to refute this and could not. Verified against the real file: no @layer anywhere in App.css, so plain specificity+order applies; .sync-path-menu-search (0,1,0) at L3186 genuinely loses to .sync-app input:not([type="checkbox"]):not([type="radio"]) (0,3,1) at L8568. SyncPathBar.tsx:331 renders a real <input type="search"> with no portal, and ProjectSync.tsx:3627 wraps the tree in .sync-app, so the generic rule does apply. No restatement exists anywhere (only 3 .sync-path-menu-search occurrences, all in the 3186 block; the later 9083-9118 block is typography). The "intentional design" defence fails in the opposite direction: menu-mockup.html:60, the specimen for direction B that memory records as shipped, styles the search as border:var(--box-border);border-radius:999px;background:var(--bg-1);box-shadow:var(--shadow-card) — the exact dead declarations — and dodged the trap only because line 179 uses a <div class="search"> under its own .menu.b .search selector instead of an <input>. So the approved design is a pill and the shipped render is not. But severity is inflated: the impact is purely cosmetic, the fallback is the app's own standard field skin (legible, contrast-correct, focus ring and placeholder colour unaffected since both competing rules declare identical values), and the control only renders when one switcher holds >=6 targets (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR=6, SyncPathBar.tsx:129,174). Against this codebase's high bar (silent capture failures, unclearable dead-end flows, contrast gate breaks), a one-control skin mismatch behind a count threshold is low.
correction: The cascade override is real but narrower than claimed. "Every declaration but the border width is dead" is wrong: of the 11 declarations in .sync-path-menu-search, 8 survive intact (width, height, margin, padding, font, font-size, plus the border shorthand's width AND style — the generic rule only sets border-color). Four are overridden, and one of those (color: var(--text-0)) is overridden with an identical value. The sibling rules are also inert differences: :focus-visible loses to .sync-app input:focus-visible (L8527) and ::placeholder loses to .sync-app input::placeholder (L8581), but both pairs declare identical values, so focus ring and placeholder colour are unaffected. Only three deltas are visible — border-radius 999px to 4px, border-color --accent to --button-border (#efe7d4 to #6f6459 dark, #2a211d to #9d8b7f light; the largest delta), and cast 2px 2px 0 shadow to a faint inset. Background is imperceptible (--bg-1 #0d0b09 vs --bg-4 #14120f dark; #fdf9f4 vs #fffdf9 light), so it should not be cited as an impact. Restated: in a switcher menu with >=6 targets, the search field renders in the app's generic field skin instead of the menu's pill grammar, sitting directly above a correctly ink-edged, shadow-cast .sync-path-menu-current row. Cosmetic design-fidelity gap against the approved specimen, one-line fix, no functional or accessibility consequence.

title: The new switcher search field is silently overridden by the generic `.sync-app input` skin — every declaration but the border width is dead
reason: CONFIRMED, with two corrections. Citation is exact: src/App.css:3186 `.sync-path-menu-search` contains the quoted eleven declarations verbatim, and it is new in the working tree (`git show HEAD:src/App.css | grep -c sync-path-menu-search` = 0). The competing rule is real at src/App.css:8568, `.sync-app input:not([type="checkbox"]):not([type="radio"])`, setting border-color/border-radius/background/color/box-shadow. Specificity math checks out: (0,1,0) vs (0,3,1) (`.sync-app` + two `:not([attr])` + `input`), and it is ~5400 lines later. No `@layer`/`@import`/`@scope` anywhere in App.css, so plain cascade applies. grep confirms only three `.sync-path-menu-search` rules exist (3186/3199/3202) and no later restatement; the block at 9083-9120 touches only type, not the search. The menu is NOT portalled (no createPortal in SyncPathBar.tsx) and every SyncPathBar call site renders under the `.sync-app` root at ProjectSync.tsx:3627, so the ancestor match holds. I built a probe page under the project root, served it through the already-running vite on :1420, and measured getComputedStyle on the real stylesheet. Search field: border-radius 4px, background rgb(20,18,15) = `--bg-4` (#14120f; `--bg-1` is #0d0b09), box-shadow `rgba(0,0,0,0.24) 1px 1px 0 inset`, border-color rgb(111,100,89) = `--button-border` (#6f6459; `--accent` is #efe7d4). Sibling `.sync-path-menu-verb`/`-tail` in the same probe: 999px, `2px 2px 0` cast shadow, rgb(239,231,212) ink edge. Every number in the finding's evidence matches mine. Reachable in practice: SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR = 6 (SyncPathBar.tsx:129), so any switcher with 6+ targets renders it.
correction: Two fixes to the finding. (1) The title overstates the damage: only four declarations die — border-color, border-radius, background, box-shadow. width, height (measured 32px), margin, padding (12px), font-size (12px = --type-sm), border-width (2px) and border-style (solid) all survive, and `color: var(--text-0)` is set identically by both rules so it is redundant, not dead. The `:focus-visible` rule at 3202 is also harmless — `.sync-app input:focus-visible` (0,2,1) at L8527 outranks it but declares the identical outline, so there is no a11y impact; this is purely cosmetic. (2) The PROPOSED FIX DOES NOT WORK. `.sync-app .sync-path-menu-search` is (0,2,0), which still loses to (0,3,1) regardless of source order — I appended exactly that rule after the whole stylesheet and re-measured: radius still 4px, bg still rgb(20,18,15), shadow still the inset. It is not analogous to the L10716 log-drawer restatement, which reaches (0,3,1) via three classes plus `input` and therefore only needed later source order. A selector at or above (0,3,1) is required; `.sync-app .sync-path-menu input.sync-path-menu-search` is (0,3,1) and, placed later, measured 999px / rgb(13,11,9) / `rgba(26,16,8,0.32) 2px 2px 0` / rgb(239,231,212) — the intended skin.

title: Files review: the flat row list draws a second full frame flush inside the file tile, doubling the ink edge and clipping its own shadow
reason:
Reproduced against the real stylesheet, not just read. ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:571-575 nests `sync-history-thread-list flat` as a direct child of the unpadded, overflow-hidden `sync-project-file-tile` (App.css:6442). Measured computed style in a browser with src/App.css loaded: tile border box x 56->844, list border box x 58->842, so gapLeft/gapRight/gapBottom are each exactly 2px — the tile's own border width, i.e. zero space between the two frames. Both compute `2px solid rgb(239,231,212)`, both `border-radius: 14px`, both carry --shadow-card. The screenshot shows an obvious second rounded frame with a hooked inner corner under the header strip and a doubled ink rule down the left and across the bottom. Unconditional on a primary flow (Push and Pull Files review, every folder tile, any window size).

Not intentional and not handled elsewhere: the same uncommitted retheme that gave `.sync-history-thread-list.flat` its box (App.css:9804; it was `gap: 5px` alone at HEAD) also went through the two other contexts where a .flat list sits inside an already-framed parent and added `box-shadow: none;` to their pre-existing un-frame resets — `.sync-history-uncommitted .sync-history-thread-list.flat` (L9395) and `.sync-history-storage-only .sync-history-thread-list.flat` (L10011) — and added the deliberate carve-out `.sync-history-thread-card.catalog-card:not(.sync-project-file-tile .sync-history-thread-card)` at L9847. The author was demonstrably thinking about both the un-frame pattern and the file tile in this change; they reset the card and missed the list. No mockup specimen shows a nested frame (files-review-mockup.tsx uses its own .mk-folder-card class) and no test asserts this chrome.

Severity corrected to medium rather than high: the consequence is entirely cosmetic — no data loss, no blocked interaction, no unreachable control — and the fix is one additive rule.
correction: The defect stands, but the second half of the proposed fix is wrong and would cause a regression. `.sync-project-file-tile > .sync-history-thread-list { gap: 0; }` at App.css:6484 is NOT dead and must NOT be deleted: ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:372 and :397 render `sync-history-thread-list` WITHOUT the `flat` class, and I confirmed by computed style that those lists get `row-gap: 0px` from L6484 alone (the base rule at App.css:5182 is `gap: 6px`). Deleting it opens a 6px gap between rows in every Files activity tile, whose cards have already had their borders stripped by L6485. Only the additive reset should land: `.sync-project-file-tile > .sync-history-thread-list.flat { border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; box-shadow: none; }`, matching the two sibling resets at L9395 and L10011.

title: The Files-page search input is overridden by the same generic input skin, so its retheme edit never lands
reason: Independently reproduced. (1) Citation is exact: <repo>/src/App.css:6373 `.sync-project-files-search input` contains verbatim `border: var(--box-border); border-radius: var(--r-pill); box-shadow: var(--shadow-card); background: var(--bg-1)`. (2) `git diff HEAD` confirms the retheme rewrote it from `padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid var(--control-border); border-radius: 7px` to the pill-plus-cast-shadow grammar. (3) The overriding rule is real: L8568 `.sync-app input:not([type="checkbox"]):not([type="radio"])` sets border-color/border-radius/background/box-shadow; it is (0,3,1) vs the target's (0,1,1) and later in source. grep confirms no later rule touches `.sync-project-files-search input` (only 6386 focus-visible and 6387 the sibling span), and App.css is the only stylesheet. (4) Both call sites — ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:533 and ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:335 — render a bare `<input type="search">` inside `.sync-project-files-search`, under the `.sync-app` root at ProjectSync.tsx:3627, so the generic skin matches. (5) Computed style measured in the running dev app (localhost:1420) with the working-tree App.css injected: the field resolves to `border-radius: 4px`, `background: rgb(20,18,15)` (--bg-4, not --bg-1 = rgb(13,11,9)), `box-shadow: rgba(0,0,0,0.24) 1px 1px 0 inset`, `border-color: rgb(111,100,89)` (--button-border, not --accent #efe7d4) — only the 2px width survives, because the generic rule sets `border-color` and not the `border` shorthand. Light theme is the same story (radius 4px, rgb(157,139,127) border, inset shadow). A `.btn` in the same row measures `999px` / `rgba(26,16,8,0.32) 2px 2px 0` / border rgb(239,231,212), so the visual mismatch the finding describes is real. Side claims also confirmed: `.sync-path-rename input` (L3339) and `.catalog-fork-drawer input` (L6751) both ask for `1px solid var(--focus-ring)` and measure rgb(111,100,89) instead.
correction: Two corrections. (a) The PROPOSED FIX DOES NOT WORK. `.sync-app .sync-project-files-search input` is (0,2,1), still below the generic skin's (0,3,1), so source order never comes into play. Verified empirically: injecting that exact rule after App.css left the computed style unchanged (4px / rgb(20,18,15) / inset shadow / rgb(111,100,89)). A three-class selector does land — `.sync-app .sync-project-files-page .sync-project-files-search input { border: var(--box-border); border-radius: var(--r-pill); background: var(--bg-1); box-shadow: var(--shadow-card); }` measured 999px, rgb(13,11,9), `rgba(26,16,8,0.32) 2px 2px 0`, border rgb(239,231,212). This matches the existing precedent at L10716, `.sync-app .log-drawer .log-search-control input`, which is deliberately three classes. The same arithmetic sinks the parenthetical hint for `.sync-path-menu-search`: that class is on the input element itself (L3186), so `.sync-app .sync-path-menu-search` would be (0,2,0) and lose too — it needs `.sync-app input.sync-path-menu-search` (0,3,1) or heavier. (b) This is not a regression the retheme introduced. `git diff HEAD` shows the L8568 generic skin is unchanged from HEAD, so the field already wore the generic skin before the retheme (the old `1px solid var(--control-border)` / 7px was equally defeated). The retheme did not break the cascade; it added a new declaration into a pre-existing trap, and the newly pill-shaped `.btn` beside it is what makes the stale skin visible.

title: Files review: the flat row list draws a second full frame flush inside the file tile, doubling the ink edge and clipping its own shadow
reason: Independently reproduced against the real stylesheet. App.css:6484-6489 matches the quoted code verbatim; .sync-project-file-tile (L6442) and .sync-history-thread-list.flat (L9804) both set border: var(--box-border) (2px solid var(--accent)), border-radius: var(--retro-panel-radius) (14px), background: var(--surface-row) and box-shadow: var(--shadow-card) (2px 2px 0). ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:571-576 does nest `sync-history-thread-list flat` as a direct child of the tile, inside section.sync-project-files-page, reached from PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:790 and RestorePlanView.tsx:630. I checked all 22 .sync-history-thread-list rules for an override: the two sibling resets at L9395 and L10011 are descendant selectors whose ancestor classes (.sync-history-uncommitted / .sync-history-storage-only) appear only on ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1868,1887, never above the review page, so neither reaches. Browser measurement with App.css loaded (1605 rules, light theme): tile x=40 right=868 bottom=180 with overflow:hidden; list x=42 right=866 bottom=178 — the list border box sits exactly on the tile padding box, so the two 2px ink lines abut as a 4px rule on left, right and bottom; tile inner arc 12px vs list arc 14px, so the corners cross; the list's 2px 2px 0 shadow would paint at 866-868/178-180, outside the tile padding box, and is clipped. Screenshot corroborates the doubled edge.
correction: The defect is real, but the fix as proposed is half wrong: the `gap: 0` at L6484 is NOT dead and must be kept. ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:373 and :396 render `sync-history-thread-list` WITHOUT `flat` inside the same tile, so L9804 never matches there and L6484 is the only rule collapsing the 6px base gap from L5182. Verified by deleting that rule live via CSSOM against the activity markup: computed gap went 0px to 6px and the row-to-row delta went 0 to 6px, splitting the joined-hairline rows in every folder tile on the Files activity face. Correct fix: ADD the `.sync-project-file-tile > .sync-history-thread-list.flat { border: 0; border-radius: 0; background: transparent; box-shadow: none; }` reset beside the existing card reset, and LEAVE L6484 in place.

title: Hovering the active primary-nav destination erases its selected state: the ink edge and the fill both drop out
reason: Independently reproduced. The quoted code is verbatim and the line numbers are exact: <repo>/src/App.css:8728 is `.sync-primary-nav button:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--border); background: var(--bg-hover); }` and L8734 is `.sync-primary-nav button.active { border-color: var(--accent); background: var(--surface-row-active); box-shadow: var(--shadow-card); }`. Both are top-level (I computed brace depth at every line: depth 0, no nesting, no media/`[data-theme]` wrapper), App.css is the only stylesheet (`src/App.tsx:10` imports it and nothing else), and grep shows no `.sync-primary-nav` rule after L8743 and no later selector that could re-assert the active box. Specificity: hover is (0,3,1) — `.sync-primary-nav` + `:hover` + `:disabled` inside `:not()` + `button`; active is (0,2,1). Hover wins regardless of source order. Reproduced by computed style: I copied App.css with `:hover` textually swapped for the equal-weight class `.FAKEHOVER`, rendered the real ProjectSidebar markup (`src/components/project-sync/ProjectSidebar.tsx:708-753`) and read getComputedStyle. Dark (`:root` default): `.active` = border rgb(239,231,212) / bg rgb(39,35,30); `.active` + hover = border rgb(46,41,37) / bg rgba(255,238,217,0.067) — byte-identical to a plain hovered row except the surviving shadow. Light (`[data-theme="light"]`) collapses the same way: border rgb(42,33,29) → rgb(216,206,196), bg rgb(240,227,213) → rgba(82,58,43,0.043). Contrast of the swapped-in edge against the rail (`.sync-sidebar-head` = rgb(13,11,9) dark / rgb(253,249,244) light) is 1.37:1 dark and ~1.13:1 light, down from 15.9:1 — so "all but invisible" is fair. The buttons carry `disabled={busy}` only, so `:not(:disabled)` matches in the ordinary idle state; there is no guard. The retheme-caused claim also checks out: at HEAD the identical defeat existed but swapped `--border-mid` (#443d36) for `--border` (#2e2925) with `box-shadow: none` — a barely visible delta — whereas the retheme raised the active edge to `--accent`, turning a latent cascade bug into a loud one. `.sidebar-profile-item` at L8815/L8820 is indeed equal-specificity (0,2,0)/(0,2,0) with active last, so it behaves correctly — the contrast is real. Proposed fix is sound: `.sync-primary-nav button.active:hover:not(:disabled)` is (0,4,1) and wins.
correction: Two refinements. (1) "Only the 2px cast shadow survives" understates what is left: the earlier rule at src/App.css:917 (`.sync-primary-nav button.active { color: var(--text-0); font-weight: var(--weight-bold); }`) is not defeated — hover at L916 only sets `color` — so the hovered active row keeps bold label text in addition to the shadow. What is erased is the whole box grammar (ink edge + fill), not every trace of selection. (2) The cascade defeat is not new in the retheme — HEAD's L8517/L8522 pair has the same (0,3,1) vs (0,2,1) inversion; the retheme changed the active border from `--border-mid` to `--accent` and added `--shadow-card`, which is what turned an unnoticeable swap into a visible one. Severity is better read as medium: the defect is transient (hover only), affects no function or data, and the row retains bold text plus its shadow.

title: Older-activity fold nests two (and with the inert sub-fold, three) identical ink frames inside each other
reason: Reproduced in a standalone specimen against the real src/App.css, measured in headless Chrome. The group's border box is x 24.0→876.0 (2px solid rgb(239,231,212), radius 14px, overflow:hidden) and its direct child .sync-history-thread-list.flat is x 26.0→874.0 with the identical 2px border, radius 14px and 2px 2px 0 shadow — exactly flush, because the padding:10px 12px at App.css:6535 is the list's INNER padding and does not inset the list. Visible result: a continuous 4px ink band that parts at the four corners (two 14px radii offset 2px), a tripled rule under [open] > summary (its 1px border-bottom plus the list's 2px top border), and the inner shadow clipped by overflow:hidden. Screenshot-confirmed. It is novel to this diff, not pre-existing: at HEAD .sync-history-thread-list.flat was only `gap: 5px` with no frame, and the retheme both made .flat the box (App.css:9804) and upgraded .sync-history-older-group to var(--box-border)+radius+shadow while deleting the old older-group/older-inert radius block. It is not intentional: the same diff ADDS `box-shadow: none` to .sync-history-storage-only .sync-history-thread-list.flat, showing the author was actively resetting this exact class while porting the two sibling groups and missed this one. No docs, mockup, or commit evidence of intent, and no wrapper/global rule handles it. Not refutable — but the severity is inflated and two claims are imprecise (see correction).
correction: Two corrections. (1) .sync-history-older-inert draws no frame of its own (computed border 0px, style none) — the third box is the nested .sync-history-thread-list.flat at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2076, and it is inset 12px (x 40.0→860.0), not stacked flush, and only appears after the user opens that sub-fold. So it is two flush frames plus one inset third, not "three identical ink frames inside each other". (2) The fold is not reached "whenever a Push/Pull selection review has out-of-window sessions": ProjectActivityPage.tsx:2049 also requires activity.older === null, i.e. paging exhausted. The code comment calls it "The catcher, not the route." It is a covered path (project-activity.integration.test.tsx:3086, thread-variants.integration.test.tsx:278) but a secondary one. Consequence is cosmetic only — nothing unreadable, no content clipped (only the inner shadow), no functional breakage — so this is a medium, not a high.

title: Hovering the active primary-nav destination erases its selected state: the ink edge and the fill both drop out
reason:
The specificity math is right (`:hover:not(:disabled)` (0,3,1) beats `.active` (0,2,1) at src/App.css:8728 vs :8734, and the active nav button is never `disabled` except during `busy`, so the state is reachable). What is wrong is the impact story and, decisively, the novelty claim.

NOT NOVEL — the retheme did not cause this. `git show HEAD:src/App.css` lines 8517-8526 carry the identical pair of selectors with the identical specificity relationship: hover already set `border-color: var(--border); background: var(--bg-hover)` and active already set `background: var(--surface-row-active)`. The background half of the defeat — the larger visual half — is byte-identical to what has been shipping. The retheme changed only the *values* on the active rule and, in doing so, made the hovered-active row MORE distinguishable, not less: at HEAD `.active` declared `box-shadow: none`, so a hovered active row was separated from a hovered inactive row by nothing but `font-weight: semibold` (App.css:888). The working tree adds `box-shadow: var(--shadow-card)` and raises the weight to bold (:917). Both survive the hover defeat because hover touches neither property. The finding's own framing ("only the 2px cast shadow survives") describes a mark the retheme *added*.

NOT ERASURE — degraded, at most. While hovered the active row keeps a bold label against every other row's medium, keeps the 2px cast shadow (`--shadow-card` = `2px 2px 0 #6f6057` in light, clearly visible on the `--bg-1` rail), and gains the hover fill. No inactive row wears a shadow. The claim that it "reads as an unframed row" understates the survivors.

ALREADY HANDLED — the current destination is stated redundantly and permanently by the workspace path bar, whose own contract is explicit that "the last crumb is where you are" (src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:13). The nav mark is not the only, or even the primary, answer to "where am I".

REALISTIC PATH IS TRANSIENT — the state exists only under the pointer, on exactly one row, anchored by the cursor itself, and reverts the instant the mouse moves. The worst case (pointer resting where the user just clicked) resolves on the next mouse movement, with the destination named in the path bar throughout. Nothing is blocked, misread, or persistent.

The specimen (codex-retheme-mockup.html:309-310) does show `.nav-item.on` keeping its border and shadow through hover at equal specificity, so tightening the rule is a defensible polish edit — but it is a cosmetic cleanup of long-shipped behavior, not a regression this change introduced, and nowhere near "high".
correction: Pre-existing (present at HEAD, unchanged by the retheme): `.sync-primary-nav button:hover:not(:disabled)` outranks `.sync-primary-nav button.active`, so hovering the current destination swaps its border and fill to the hover treatment. Its bold label and 2px cast shadow persist, and the path bar names the destination regardless, so the row stays identifiable; the retheme's added shadow made this state more distinguishable than it was at HEAD, not less. Cosmetic polish nit worth aligning with `.sidebar-profile-item` and the specimen, low severity.

title: Hovering the open Push/Pull button strips its primary fill, so the "this review is open" signal disappears under the cursor
reason: Not novel and not a real consequence. (1) NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS DIFF: at HEAD the hover rule read `border-color: var(--border-strong); color: var(--accent); background: var(--button-bg-hover)` and `.sync-path-sync.active` read `border-color: var(--button-primary-border); background: var(--button-primary-bg); color: var(--button-primary-text)`. The hover rule already overrode ALL THREE active declarations, so a hovered-active button already rendered exactly like a hovered ordinary button before the retheme. The diff only deleted `border-color` from both rules (border is now the shared `var(--box-border)` in every state), so the hovered-active rendering is unchanged relative to HEAD. The finding's stated cause — "the active state now hangs entirely on a background the hover rule overwrites" — is factually wrong; at HEAD it hung on background AND border, and hover overwrote both. (2) NO REAL USER CONSEQUENCE: the "review is open" signal is not this 30px pill. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2735 puts `sync-sync-review-page` on <main> when `inlineStorageReview` is set — the whole page becomes the review workspace (header, tabs, item list, footer step navigator). The button additionally swaps its title/aria-label and drops its count chip (showPullCount/showPushCount at 2550-2551 go false when a review opens), so the button itself is visibly different even while hovered. The fill returns on the smallest pointer movement, and the pointer must move because selecting review items is the next action; keyboard and touch users never see it at all. (3) CONSISTENT WITH HOUSE PATTERN/INTENT: App.css:5049-5050 deliberately groups `.sync-history-icon-action:hover:not(:disabled)` with `.sync-history-icon-action.active` so hover and active render identically; `.sync-project-tabs > button:hover, > button.active` likewise share a color and carry the active state on ::after. The retheme's own recorded doctrine is "hover/expanded no longer swap border colour — ink stays, fill moves", which is precisely what this diff did. The proposed `:not(.active)` guard is a defensible polish item, but it fixes a pre-existing cosmetic quirk, not a defect this change introduced.
correction: The cascade math is right (hover at 0,3,0 beats .active at 0,2,0) but the framing is wrong: this override is pre-existing at HEAD, where the hover rule also overrode the active rule's border-color, so the hovered-active button already looked like an ordinary hovered button before the retheme. This diff changes nothing about that rendering. Accurate statement: "Pre-existing: hovering an open Push/Pull button has always masked its primary fill; the retheme did not introduce or worsen it, and the review workspace occupying the whole page remains the actual open-state signal."

title: Duplicate `border-radius` in the settings switch thumb: the retheme's pill is defeated one line later by the old 2px square
reason: No user-visible consequence and no regression: the added `50%` is the dead line, so the switch renders exactly as it did at HEAD (2px thumb). Nothing about layout, fit, contrast, hit target, or interaction changes — the thumb clears the track in both states either way; the delta is corner fill on a 12px block. The surviving 2px is consistent with the app's entire drawn-control family (all rounded squares, zero circles in 10,989 lines) and with the retheme's explicitly mixed Box+Round vocabulary, so "the two halves disagree about the corner language" presumes a single-radius system this codebase does not have. Scope is three toggles on the Settings page; the css-hygiene gate and the full suite are green with it. The residue is one dead declaration — hygiene, not token integrity — and notably the harmless fix (drop the inert 50%) changes nothing on screen, while the proposed fix (drop the 2px) would change shipped appearance on an assumption about author intent that the diff does not support.
correction: The duplication is real but the impact claim is inverted. git diff against HEAD shows `border-radius: 50%` is the line the retheme ADDED (App.css:4321) above the pre-existing `2px`; the track went 4px -> var(--r-pill) in the same edit. So the rendered switch is byte-identical to what shipped at HEAD — no regression, nothing a user can newly hit. The 2px square-ish thumb also matches every other drawn control in the app (checkboxes at App.css:1266, 1786, 6318 are 13-14px squares at 4px radius; 4632 is 2px), and the block's own comment says it shares construction with those checkboxes; no drawn control anywhere in the file is circular. The retheme is documented as a mixed "Box + Round" vocabulary (2px ink boxes, pill shaded buttons), so a pill track with a boxy thumb is within the grammar rather than a contradiction of it. What actually remains is one inert declaration — CSS hygiene on 3 toggles of one page — and the safe cleanup is the OPPOSITE of the proposed fix: delete the dead `border-radius: 50%` (zero visual change), not the `2px`, which would alter shipped appearance on a guess about intent.

title: Hovering the open Push/Pull button strips its primary fill, so the "this review is open" signal disappears under the cursor
reason: Independently reproduced. src/App.css:2868 is verbatim `.sync-path-sync:hover:not(:disabled) { color: var(--accent); background: var(--button-bg-hover); }` and :3000 is `.sync-path-sync.active { background: var(--button-primary-bg); color: var(--button-primary-text); }`. Specificity is (0,3,0) vs (0,2,0) — :not() takes its argument's weight — so hover wins regardless of the active rule coming later. I grepped every other .sync-path-sync rule (8241, 9078, 9137, 9190 are font-only; 3010 is padding in a container query) and found no .sync-path-sync.active:hover anywhere, and .btn-primary:hover at :8521 does not apply because .sync-path-sync is not a .btn. Rendering App.css standalone in a browser with a real pointer hover: unhovered .active = rgb(173,128,90) bg / rgb(22,18,16) ink; with element.matches(':hover')===true = rgb(39,34,29) bg / rgb(239,231,212) ink, byte-identical to a plain hovered button. The finder's measured values are exact and the call sites (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2613/:2665, plus StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1419/:1437) are correct. Two corrections: (1) the attribution to the retheme is wrong — before this diff the hover rule also carried border-color: var(--border-strong), which outspecified the active rule's border-color: var(--button-primary-border), so hover already erased both the border and the background at HEAD; the defect is pre-existing and untouched in severity by the retheme; (2) when inlineStorageReview.continueDisabled is set the button is disabled, :hover:not(:disabled) stops matching, and the primary fill survives at opacity 0.45 — the loss only happens on the enabled path.
correction: The hover rule at src/App.css:2868 (0,3,0) outspecifies `.sync-path-sync.active` at :3000 (0,2,0), so hovering an open Push/Pull button replaces the caramel primary fill with the ordinary hover fill (dark: rgb(173,128,90)/rgb(22,18,16) becomes rgb(39,34,29)/rgb(239,231,212)) whenever the button is enabled. This is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by the retheme: the pre-diff hover rule also set `border-color: var(--border-strong)`, which overrode the active rule's `border-color: var(--button-primary-border)` by the same specificity margin, so the active state was already fully erased under the cursor at HEAD. The same defect affects StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1419/:1437, and it does not occur while the button is disabled (`inlineStorageReview.continueDisabled`), where the fill persists at opacity 0.45. The proposed fix is correct as written.

title: Duplicate `border-radius` in the settings switch thumb: the retheme's pill is defeated one line later by the old 2px square
reason:
Independently reproduced; the citation is exact and the auxiliary claims all check out.

1. Citation verified verbatim. <repo>/src/App.css L4314 opens `.sync-settings-switch::before {`; L4321 is `  border-radius: 50%;` and L4322 is `  border-radius: 2px;`, both inside that one block, in that order. Line numbers are exactly right.

2. Cascade traced. Same block, same origin, same specificity, both values valid — the later declaration wins, so the thumb resolves to 2px. I checked for any escape hatch: the only other rules touching this pseudo-element are L472-473 (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` setting only transition/animation) and L4332 `.sync-settings-switch:checked::before` (only transform + background). No `!important`, no later override, no second stylesheet — `src/App.css` is the only stylesheet in `src/` and `.sync-settings-switch` is used in exactly one place (src/components/project-sync/SettingsPage.tsx:89).

3. var() chain resolved. `--r-pill: 999px` is defined at L8073 under the combined selector `:root, :root[data-theme="dark"]` (L7982-7983) and is not redefined in the light block (L8094), so the track is 999px in every theme.

4. Computed-style confirmation (not source reading). I served the real App.css over a local static server and read getComputedStyle on a real `.sync-settings-switch`: {trackRadius: "999px", trackW: "36px", trackH: "20px", thumbRadius: "2px", thumbAll: "2px", thumbW: "12px", thumbH: "12px", checkedThumbRadius: "2px"}. Stadium track, near-square 12px thumb — exactly as claimed.

5. Provenance confirms it is an unfinished edit, not an intentional mix. `git show HEAD:src/App.css` has the track at `border-radius: 4px` and the thumb at `border-radius: 2px` only. The uncommitted retheme diff changes the track `4px -> var(--r-pill)` and ADDS `border-radius: 50%` to the thumb while leaving the pre-existing `2px` line directly beneath it. The new line is the one being defeated.

6. "Only duplicated property in the file" verified. A brace-depth scan over all 10989 lines finds exactly one duplicated declaration in any block: (4322, 'border-radius', previously 4321). Line count 10989 also matches.

No test pins the 2px value (tests/frontend/settings-page.integration.test.tsx:53 only matches role/class attributes), so deleting L4322 breaks nothing.

Proposed fix is correct: delete `  border-radius: 2px;` at src/App.css:4322.

title: `--button-primary-border` is declared in both themes but no longer referenced anywhere
reason: Independently reproduced. src/App.css:8011 reads `--button-primary-border: #ad805a;` verbatim inside the dark `:root, :root[data-theme="dark"]` block, and L8120 reads `--button-primary-border: #8a6347;` in the light block — both line numbers exact. A repo-wide grep for the literal string (excluding node_modules/.git/target) returns ONLY those two declaration lines: there is no `var(--button-primary-border)` anywhere in src/, tests/, or the mockup HTML. `git show HEAD:src/App.css` confirms the three consumers existed before this change at HEAD L328 (.btn-primary border-color), L2936 (.sync-path-sync.active), and L8307 (RetroTheme .btn.btn-primary); in the working tree all three rules (L334, L3000, L8516) now set only background/color/font-weight. I traced the cascade for an override and found none — the edge comes from the base `.btn { border: var(--box-border); }` at L308-319, and the RetroTheme layer at L8486+ adds only radius/background/shadow/type, never re-specifying border-color for the primary variant. I also independently ran the declaration-vs-var() census the finding cites: 7 tokens are unused in the working tree (--accent-glow, --amber, --bg-3, --button-primary-border, --editor-active-line, --surface-overlay, --surface-subtle-hover), and set-differencing against HEAD's unused set shows --button-primary-border is the only newly-orphaned one, exactly as claimed. The "single source of truth" framing is also real: L7949 reads `/* Theme-invariant tokens. This file is the palette's single source of truth. */`, and both palette blocks carry multi-line design-rationale comments about the primary-button fill, so a maintainer tuning that palette is aimed at a value that paints nothing. No guard, fallback, later rule, or specificity path rescues the token. Severity low is correct: dead token and maintainer trap, no user-visible rendering defect. The proposed fix (delete both declarations) is correct and complete.

title: Tool-call action labels dropped to 9px uppercase and fail 4.5:1 on the expanded row in the light theme
reason:
The measurements are arithmetically correct (I reproduced 3.94:1 and 4.18:1 on #f0e3d5), but the finding fails on both novelty and impact.

1) NOT A RETHEME REGRESSION — every input to that ratio is byte-identical at HEAD. `git show HEAD:src/App.css` vs the working tree: `--session-detail-link` and `--session-detail-amber` (src/App.css:6850-6851), `--yellow: #d99609`, `--blue: #2f88b4`, `--text-0: #1e1817`, `--surface-row-active: #f0e3d5`, and the `.session-detail-tool-call[open] > summary { background: var(--surface-row-active) }` rule are all unchanged. The diff touched only `flex`, `font-family`, `font-size`, `letter-spacing`, `text-transform`. At HEAD the same labels measured the same 3.94/4.18:1 at `--type-sm` (12px semibold), which is nowhere near the WCAG large-text exemption (18.66px bold / 24px) — so the expanded row failed AA identically before the retheme. The finding is framed as "the retheme took it to 9px and it now fails"; the colour shortfall is pre-existing and untouched by the change under review.

2) THE CLAIMED IMPACT IS FALSE — "a user cannot reliably tell READ from EDIT rows once a call is expanded" does not follow. `descriptor.label` is the literal word (src/components/project-sync/session-detail/sessionDetailModel.ts:523-541: `read → "Read"`, `edit → "Edit"`, `exec → "Bash"`), printed in the span at SessionDetailToolCall.tsx:158-160. Category colour is redundant reinforcement of a word that is already different letters, so WCAG 1.4.1 is satisfied; 3.94:1 is dim, not illegible, and is above the 3:1 non-text floor.

3) SCOPE IS ONE TRANSIENT SELF-INFLICTED STATE — only `[open] > summary` is affected, i.e. the single row the user just clicked and whose payload they are now reading. The closed rows they scan measure 4.74/5.03:1 and pass, hover passes, and dark theme passes at 8.8-12.6:1 as the finding concedes.

4) BOUNDED BY AN EXISTING, DOCUMENTED DECISION — the codebase's contrast gate (tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx:72-140) explicitly enumerates which inks are held to 4.5 on which surfaces (notice rungs on their composite fills, the seven thread-status badges on `--surface-row-hover`, `--text-3` on thirteen opaque surfaces including `--surface-row-active`). The session-detail category tints are deliberately outside that set, and their declaration carries a comment naming the exact target they were tuned for ("Mixing the body colour in clears the bar... The rails and borders keep the pure hue, where 3:1 is the bar", App.css:6842-6849). This is a bounded tuning choice with a stated scope, not an unnoticed defect.

The residual merit — 9px uppercase mono with 1px tracking is small type for a sub-4.5:1 tint — is a legibility-comfort nit worth a one-line token override, not a medium correctness/accessibility defect introduced by this diff.
correction: On the light theme's expanded tool row (`.session-detail-tool-call[open] > summary`, background `--surface-row-active` #f0e3d5), the `cat-read` (rgb 44,119,156) and `cat-file_edit` (rgb 142,100,15) labels measure 3.94:1 and 4.18:1, below the 4.5:1 AA floor. This is pre-existing, not caused by the retheme: all colour tokens and the open-row background are unchanged from HEAD, where the same labels failed identically at 12px. No information is lost, because the label prints the word ("READ"/"EDIT"/"BASH") and colour only reinforces it; the affected surface is the single row the user has expanded, while closed rows (4.74/5.03:1) and the whole dark theme pass. Cosmetic legibility nit, worth a light-theme override of the two mixes if touched, not a regression in this diff.

title: Departure Mono is still shipped in public/fonts but no production code references it any more
reason: Independently reproduced. Citation is exact: src/App.css:7880 is `@font-face {` with `font-family: "Baloo 2";` on 7881, and the quoted six-line block matches verbatim (src 7882, font-style 7883, font-weight 400 800 on 7884, font-display: block on 7885). `--font-pixel` is genuinely absent from src/ — a tree-wide grep including untracked files finds it only in the untracked specimen codex-retheme-mockup.html and a stale line in docs/PLAN_GLOBAL_SETTINGS_PAGE.md. `git grep -i departure` finds no production consumer: only THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, docs/PLAN_PROVIDER_NEUTRAL_SESSION_DETAIL.md, and the unrelated English word "departures" in a comment at src/components/Icons.tsx:402. index.html links only the favicon, no font preload. The "ships in the bundle" claim is provable rather than inferred: vite.config.ts sets no publicDir so Vite's default copies public/ verbatim, and a real prior build output is still on disk — dist/fonts/ (01:08 today) contains exactly DepartureMono-Regular.woff2 (22496 bytes) and DepartureMono-OFL.txt and nothing else. No guard, fallback, later rule, or call-site condition was missed; there is no override that keeps Departure Mono alive. Only the framing needs tightening (see correction).
correction: Two refinements. (1) The licensing manifest at issue is THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, not the OFL text file: it still carries a "## Departure Mono" section pointing at public/fonts/DepartureMono-OFL.txt, and it contains NO Baloo 2 entry at all, so the font the app actually bundles is undocumented — the larger half of the manifest problem. (2) The proposed fix's "keep Baloo2-OFL.txt, which is now the live attribution" is not sufficient: `git ls-files public/fonts` returns only DepartureMono-OFL.txt and DepartureMono-Regular.woff2. Baloo2-Variable.woff2 (33056 bytes) and Baloo2-OFL.txt are untracked, so as the tree stands a fresh clone or CI build ships the dead 22KB font and not the live one, silently falling back to "Arial Rounded MT Bold" / var(--font-sans) via --font-display. The fix must git add those two files, delete the two DepartureMono files, and edit THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md to replace the Departure Mono section with a Baloo 2 one.

title: Session titles and commit subjects were moved to a display face whose bundled subset has no Latin-Extended, Cyrillic or CJK coverage
reason:
This is a deliberate, documented, user-approved design decision, not a defect. Both cited rules carry comments in src/App.css naming them as the intentional exception: L5168 "Titles are the one carve-out from the 'user data reads in the clean face' rule: a commit subject or session title is this page's headline, and the headline voice is the display face", and L9631 "Session titles take the display face for the same headline reason the commit subject does". The typography contract at L7889 codifies the three-face system, and the retheme cutover record states it verbatim: "titles carve-out: commit subjects, session titles (.sync-history-thread-title > strong), catalog names take the display face DESPITE BEING USER DATA — the approved mock look." The user watched the cutover live over HMR and steered ~10 fixes; this survived unchanged, and a test gate (tests/frontend/project-sync-cutover.integration.test.tsx:236) pins the Baloo 2 @font-face.

There is no functional consequence. src/App.css:7909 defines --font-display: "Baloo 2", "Arial Rounded MT Bold", var(--font-sans), and the @font-face at L7879 declares NO unicode-range, so uncovered codepoints get ordinary per-character CSS fallback down to the system sans stack. Text always renders — never tofu, never dropped. The only effect is a typeface change for uncovered glyphs, which is how every webfont on the web behaves. Titles are single-line, nowrap, ellipsized, so there is no layout risk from the width delta either.

The finding is also factually wrong in three places. (1) Its exhaustiveness claim — "only these two user-data selectors are exposed" — is false: .session-detail-checkpoint-branch renders {checkpoint.branch}, a git branch name (SessionDetailEvent.tsx:406); .sync-path-menu-copy > span renders switcher targets, i.e. project/storage/path names (SyncPathBar.tsx:210, 319); .sync-provider-monogram derives from a provider display_name off an open registry (ProviderMark.tsx:20); .sync-storage-repo-chip > span and .sync-storage-editor-title carry user-named storages. The memory record names catalog names as a third intended carve-out. (2) Its coverage probe is wrong: reading the cmap of public/fonts/Baloo2-Variable.woff2 directly with fontTools gives 230 codepoints, and both "ā" and "ć" are NOT present, though the finding lists them as covered — the browser probe measured the fallback face, not Baloo 2. (3) Its proposed fix is half unachievable: Baloo 2 upstream ships Latin, Latin-Ext, Vietnamese and Devanagari and has no Cyrillic or CJK in any subset, so re-subsetting cannot deliver the coverage implied; only abandoning the approved face could.

Finally, the pattern is established precedent, not a retheme regression: var(--font-mono) is applied at 49 sites to paths, shas and ids using a system mono stack (SF Mono / Menlo / Consolas) that has no CJK either, so mixed-script per-character fallback over user data has been accepted app-wide long before this change.
correction: The accurate statement is narrower and is a design note, not a defect: the bundled Baloo2-Variable.woff2 covers 230 codepoints (Latin-1 plus chrome punctuation; ā, ć, ł, ę, ř, İ, Cyrillic and CJK are all absent), so headline nodes set in --font-display — which include session titles, commit subjects, catalog names, git branch names, switcher targets and provider monograms — render non-Latin-1 characters through the declared fallback chain ("Arial Rounded MT Bold", then the system sans). This is intended: the display face is a deliberate, user-approved carve-out for headline user data, the @font-face declares no unicode-range so fallback is graceful and per-character, and Baloo 2 has no Cyrillic or CJK upstream, so no subsetting change would alter the outcome for those scripts.

title: `--button-primary-border` is declared in both themes but no longer referenced anywhere
reason:
The mechanical claim is true — `--button-primary-border` is declared at src/App.css:8011 (dark) and :8120 (light) with zero var() references, having lost its three HEAD consumers (:326, :2936, :8307) to the retheme. But there is no consequence. An unreferenced CSS custom property resolves lazily and is never resolved; it paints nothing, affects no cascade, and costs two lines in an 8,000-line file. No user on any path, at any window size, with any data, can observe a difference.

The novelty claim is the weakest link. A full declaration-vs-var() census gives 7 orphans out of 123 declared tokens, and I verified the other six against HEAD: --accent-glow, --amber, --bg-3, --editor-active-line, --surface-overlay and --surface-subtle-hover each had 0 var() refs at HEAD already. The codebase's steady state is six orphaned palette tokens; this change makes it seven. The claimed hazard ("a maintainer will edit a value that paints nothing") is a pre-existing, tolerated house condition, not something the cutover introduced — which is precisely what the finding leans on to justify reporting it.

The specific hazard is further defused by the value: both declarations set the token to the identical hex as --button-primary-bg on the line immediately above (#ad805a dark, #8a6347 light). It was a redundant alias even at HEAD, where its only job was drawing a border matching its own fill. A maintainer retuning the primary button edits the adjacent -bg/-hover lines.

It is also downstream of a deliberate decision, not an oversight: --box-border: 2px solid var(--accent) at L7946 carries an explicit comment that boxes draw their edge in the theme's own ink, with 50 consumers. Buttons giving up a private border colour is the retheme's stated doctrine. Whether the superseded token is swept or kept as a palette record is taste.

No gate fails: tests/frontend/css-hygiene.integration.test.tsx holds exactly two assertions, both contrast checks (notice rungs, status badges). There is no unused-token gate.

Finally, a correction to the supporting rhetoric: the "palette's single source of truth" comment is at L7949, inside the base :root block (7904-7974), introducing the theme-invariant pair --button-disabled-opacity / --z-log. It does not sit above --button-primary-border, which lives in the separate :root[data-theme="dark"] block (7983-8092). The comment makes no claim about this token.

This is a tidiness preference — fine to sweep alongside the other six in a dedicated pass, but not a defect worth reporting against this change.
correction: Accurate statement: the retheme left `--button-primary-border` declared at src/App.css:8011 and :8120 with no remaining consumers, bringing src/App.css from six orphaned palette tokens to seven (--accent-glow, --amber, --bg-3, --editor-active-line, --surface-overlay and --surface-subtle-hover were already unreferenced at HEAD). Its value is identical to --button-primary-bg on the preceding line in both blocks, so it carries no independent palette information. If cleaned up at all, all seven should be swept together as a hygiene pass rather than this one singled out as a defect of the retheme.

title: The switcher menu has no max-height or scroll, and the retheme moved its verbs into a footer that a long list pushes off-screen
reason: Three load-bearing claims fail against the actual code. (1) NOT NOVEL: `git show HEAD:src/App.css` line 2997 contains the identical `.sync-path-menu` block with no max-height and no overflow — the unbounded menu predates the retheme entirely. At HEAD, SyncPathBar rendered all groups in document order, so the trailing group ("Add project…") was already pushed below the fold by a long "Switch to" list. The retheme's real delta is that four verbs joined an already-losable trailing zone, plus 3px of row height — not the creation of the overflow problem. (2) ALREADY HANDLED, by the same change: SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR = 6 (SyncPathBar.tsx:129) gates a search field HEAD did not have. The finding's own threshold is 9 targets at the minimum window — always >= 6, so every configuration that could fail always renders the search box; typing collapses the list and lifts the footer back into view. Keyboard arrows/typeahead/Home/End reach every row regardless, since an overflow:hidden root is still programmatically scrollable so focus reveals it. (3) UNREALISTIC DATA: ~/.mallard/sync_config.json on the author's own dogfooding machine holds projects: 6, storages: 5, links: 7 — the switcher lists 5 other projects, below even the search floor, giving a ~290px menu against ~625px of room at the shipped 1100x720 default. The finding measures 19 targets at the 560px hand-dragged floor: over 3x the real corpus at a size the user must deliberately shrink to. Break-even at the default window is ~14 other projects. (4) NO DEAD END: the sidebar project list is a real scroll container (App.css:3411, `.sidebar-split-pane > .sidebar-profile-list { overflow-y: scroll }`) and is the primary switching surface; "Add project…"/"Add storage…" are dedicated + buttons (ProjectSidebar.tsx:785, 1016); "Reset local sync state" also lives on PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:590 and RestorePlanView.tsx:489; "Agent profile…" has a CTA at ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1811. Only "Reveal in Finder" and "Rename project…" are menu-exclusive — the two lowest-stakes verbs, restored by resizing a normal resizable window.
correction: A defensible narrow version: `.sync-path-menu` has never had a `max-height`/`overflow` (unchanged from HEAD), so a switcher with roughly 14+ other projects at the default 1100x720 window (or 9+ at the 560px minimum) clips its trailing rows and its footer. This is a pre-existing robustness gap the retheme slightly widened by relocating four verbs into the trailing footer and growing rows from ~31px to a 34px min-height. It is mitigated in practice by the search field that is guaranteed present above the failure threshold (floor 6 < threshold 9), by keyboard navigation, by window resizing, and by the scrollable sidebar carrying alternate routes to every command except "Reveal in Finder" and "Rename project…". Adding `max-height: calc(100vh - 120px)` with a scrolling list region is a reasonable hardening, not a bug fix.

title: Tool-call action labels dropped to 9px uppercase and fail 4.5:1 on the expanded row in the light theme
reason: The defect reproduces in source. Citation is exact: src/App.css:7595 holds the quoted block verbatim. I traced the cascade — .session-detail-tool-call[open] > summary (L7579) sets background: var(--surface-row-active); nothing overrides it later (L10969/10980 touch only box-shadow/transform, L10924 only font-family), and the tying :hover rule (0,2,1) loses on source order. Light-theme var() chain resolves to --text-0 #1e1817 (L8146), --blue #2f88b4 (L8165), --yellow #d99609 (L8163), giving --session-detail-link = rgb(44,119,156) and --session-detail-amber = rgb(142,100,15) from the color-mix at L6850-6851. Recomputed against #f0e3d5: 3.93:1 and 4.20:1, both under the 4.5:1 AA floor (closed rows on --surface-row pass at 4.72/5.05; dark passes at 8.81/10.56). Light theme is reachable in production via src/preferences.ts:72, and the classes are really emitted (SessionDetailToolCall.tsx:158 plus the category map at sessionDetailModel.ts:530-540). However, the finding's causal framing is wrong and I could not confirm it as a retheme regression: font size does not affect contrast ratio, and both the old --type-sm (12px) and the new --type-3xs (9px) sit below WCAG's large-text exemption (24px, or 18.66px bold), so both required 4.5:1 equally. At HEAD the relevant tokens and the [open] background rule are byte-identical (App.css L6652-6653, L7352, --surface-row-active #f0e3d5), so the identical 3.93/4.20 failure predates the retheme. The first branch of the proposed fix (raising the font size) would not change the ratio by a single point.
correction: Pre-existing (not retheme-introduced) WCAG AA shortfall: in the light theme, `.session-detail-tool-name.cat-read` (rgb(44,119,156)) and `.cat-file_edit` (rgb(142,100,15)) render on an expanded row's `--surface-row-active` (#f0e3d5) at 3.93:1 and 4.20:1, below the 4.5:1 floor. The color tokens (src/App.css:6850-6851) and the expanded-row background rule (src/App.css:7579) are unchanged from HEAD, so the retheme's font-size/case/family change at src/App.css:7595 neither caused nor worsened the ratio — contrast is size-independent, and both 12px and 9px are below WCAG's large-text exemption. Only the second proposed remedy is valid: give `--session-detail-link` and `--session-detail-amber` light-theme overrides (raise the `--text-0` share in the color-mix) so they clear 4.5:1 on `--surface-row-active` as well as on the page background. Raising the font size back to `--type-xs`/`--type-sm` would not fix the contrast, though it is defensible on separate legibility grounds at 9px uppercase mono with 1px tracking.

title: Departure Mono is still shipped in public/fonts but no production code references it any more
reason: Refuted on three grounds. (a) INTENTIONAL: the retheme cutover record for this very change states the fonts were kept on purpose — "Departure Mono @font-face, --font-pixel, ... are DELETED from App.css (DepartureMono files stay in public/fonts — the mock's Pixel option still consumes them)". The CSS removal and the asset retention were one deliberate decision, and codex-retheme-mockup.html:27-29 still loads the woff2 through two src paths, so deleting it would break a specimen the user is actively steering on an uncommitted branch. (b) THE LICENSING CLAIM IS FACTUALLY INVERTED: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:48-53 says "Mallard bundles Departure Mono ... The complete license text is included at public/fonts/DepartureMono-OFL.txt" — a true statement about what ships, and shipping the OFL text alongside the font is exactly what OFL 1.1 requires. There is no manifest inaccuracy. Worse, the proposed fix's premise ("keep Baloo2-OFL.txt, which is now the live attribution") is wrong: Baloo2-OFL.txt is untracked and has no THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md entry whatsoever. (c) NO CONSEQUENCE: with no @font-face referencing it, nothing fetches or decodes the file at runtime — zero network, zero render, zero cold-load cost. It is 22 KB + 4 KB of static assets embedded in a Tauri binary against a 1.0 MB dist and a tens-of-MB .app. No user or maintainer reaches a degraded path. This is housekeeping that the author already considered and deferred on purpose; it sits below the reporting bar.
correction: If anything is worth noting here it is the opposite of the finding: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md still carries an accurate Departure Mono entry (the font and its OFL text both ship), while Baloo 2 — the face the app now actually renders via src/App.css:7880 — has no THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md entry at all, and public/fonts/Baloo2-OFL.txt plus Baloo2-Variable.woff2 are still untracked. The real (minor, and expected mid-cutover) gap is a missing Baloo 2 attribution, not a stale Departure Mono one. The Departure Mono asset deletion is correctly gated on the specimen and was deliberately deferred.

title: Escape discards the prepared Push review from anywhere, including inside the Logs drawer
reason: Verified in source. The window-level Escape effect at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:417-423 is live during an idle review (busy = busy || projectContentLoading, both false), and onClose at ProjectSync.tsx:3395-3402 discards pendingPush plus pushError, pushProjectContentRemovals and pushWarningAcknowledgements with no confirm and no undo. ActivityLogDrawer.tsx has zero keydown/Escape handling in all 221 lines, and its root takes programmatic focus on open (ProjectSync.tsx:3679), so a keyboard user is focused in a region where Escape acts destructively on a different, unfocused surface. Reachability is not incidental: the Logs trigger (ProjectSidebar.tsx:741-748) is the only nav button lacking disabled={busy} while Projects/Catalog/Storages/Settings all have it and the sidebar is passed busy={busy || !!inlineStorageReview} (ProjectSync.tsx:3667), so drawer-over-review is a supported state by design.
