The author acknowledged this precise hazard at LogPanel.tsx:305-307 but mitigated only the search field, with the type filter (LogPanel.tsx:180-192) the sole other stop; Level select, Manage logs, Close, Load older and the drawer region itself all fall through. Reviewer B is right that the window listener is an intentional contract (eight stopPropagation sites) and that rescoping it to the review subtree would break them, but that argues against half the proposed fix, not against the finding: the house pattern is "the layer under focus consumes Escape", and the drawer is the one focusable layer that does not. Severity lowered to low, not medium: nothing on disk or in remote storage is touched, pendingPush is re-preparable by one click on Push with defaults restored via setPushSelected(new Set(projectDefaults)) (ProjectSync.tsx:1920), the review visibly vanishes rather than being lost silently, a running push is already sealed by !busy plus the if (busy) return guard, and the drawer already contains a click-path to the same discard (onManage -> openSettings:1496 -> closeWorkspaceSettings:1430 -> setPendingPush(null)). Still worth a maintainer's time as a small, house-pattern-consistent fix.
correction: Escape pressed while focus is inside the Logs drawer — the one surface deliberately left openable over a prepared review — reaches the review's window listener and discards the prepared push and all selection deviations with no confirmation. Two claims in the finding are wrong: the loss is not silent (the review visibly disappears from the main region behind the drawer), and no user can expect Escape to close this drawer since it has no Escape-to-close behavior anywhere in the app. The correct fix is only the first half of the proposal — have ActivityLogDrawer consume Escape (stopPropagation, optionally closing the drawer) so the focused layer owns the key, matching the eight existing stopPropagation sites. Do NOT rescope the review's listener to the review subtree: that would break the window contract those eight sites are built against (LogPanel.tsx:184, SyncPathBar.tsx:407, ProjectActivityPage.tsx:184/880, ProjectSync.tsx:1320, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:235/399/957, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx).

title: Catalog Pull tells the user "nothing was changed" on failure paths that run after every selected resource has already been overwritten on disk
reason: Independently reproduced. (1) Citation is exact: StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1150 is verbatim `notify(`Pull failed — nothing was changed.`, "attention")` in runPull's catch, and :1069 is verbatim `Push failed — nothing was published.` in runPush's catch. (2) The error path is live: api.ts:131 invokes `apply_catalog_scope_pull`, resource_commands.rs:206 returns Result<Dto, String>, so a backend Err rejects the promise into that catch with no intermediate mapping. (3) The backend really does write before it can fail: in src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/service.rs, apply_pull_with_repositories runs its apply loop at line 2009, and execute_scope_pull_item (apply.rs:1063) converts every per-item error into a CatalogActionResult rather than propagating it — nothing in the loop uses `?`. Only afterwards, at line 2049, does `catalog.mutate_scope_links(...)?` run with a `?`, and it can fail from guard() (persistence.rs:113 — poisoned mutex, ensure_restricted_directory, open_lock_file, file.lock()), load_document/validate, either of the closure's two staleness returns, or write_json_atomic. All of those fire after the provider home has already been rewritten, including the requires_destructive_approval overwrites. A grep of apply.rs for rollback/undo/restore finds nothing — there is no compensating unwind. (4) Push has the same shape and one extra post-write `?` the finding did not list: engine.publish at service.rs:1730 has already advanced the storage revision before `.ok_or("the published manifest lost a selected resource")?` (1758) and mutate_scope_links (1767). The finding's approximate line numbers (~2005, 2049, 1729) are each within a line of the real ones. I found no guard, fallback, or call-site condition that prevents the false claim.
correction: The defect holds, with two precision qualifiers. Reachability is narrower than the finding implies: the pre-flight guards in apply_pull_with_repositories ("the scope link changed after review", "the storage changed after review", "the stored content changed after review", verify_pins, and the conflicting-claims re-check) all `return Err` BEFORE any write, so ordinary staleness is correctly reported as "nothing was changed". The surviving false-claim window requires either a genuine IO/lock failure inside mutate_scope_links or a truly concurrent link mutation between the apply loop and line 2049 — and on the Pull side it is additionally gated behind `if base_changed`. Second, the toast is not the only signal: `setFailures([storageFailureMessage(reason)])` does render the raw backend string (e.g. "the scope link changed while accepting Pull") beneath it, so the user gets a contradictory detail line — the headline is what asserts the unverifiable rollback. The proposed fix is still the right shape; the minimum change (rewording both strings to name the uncertainty) is correct, and Push additionally needs the post-publish `.ok_or("the published manifest lost a selected resource")?` at service.rs:1758 counted as a post-write failure path.

title: The switcher menu has no max-height or scroll, and the retheme moved its verbs into a footer that a long list pushes off-screen
reason:
CONFIRMED — every load-bearing claim checks out against the working tree, and I reproduced the overflow in a browser against the real App.css.

CITATION: `.sync-path-menu {` is exactly at src/App.css:3061 and the quoted block is verbatim through `box-shadow: var(--shadow-popover);` at 3072. No `max-height`, no `overflow`. I enumerated every `sync-path-menu` occurrence in App.css (2196, 3061-3312, 8225, 9083-9114) — that is the only stylesheet in src/ — and none of them sets `max-height` or `overflow`. There is no `.sync-path-menu-group` rule at all, no `[role=menu]` catch-all, and no JS positioning in SyncPathBar.tsx (no getBoundingClientRect, no maxHeight, no flip logic). src/App.css:7-11 is `html, body, #root { height:100%; width:100%; overflow:hidden }` as quoted.

MARKUP: SyncPathBar.tsx:338-359 — in the switcher branch the list groups render first and `.sync-path-menu-foot` (verbs + tails) is the last child, with no scroll wrapper anywhere. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2362 (finding said 2360) is `const otherProjects = projects.filter(...)`, unbounded. The bar is a sibling of `<main>` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2727-2735), so the menu is not inside the app's scroll region.

RETHEME DELTAS VERIFIED AGAINST HEAD: `git show HEAD:src/App.css` has no `.sync-path-menu.switcher`, no `.sync-path-menu-foot`, no search field, and `.sync-path-menu-item` at HEAD is `padding: 7px 8px; border: 0` with no min-height (measures ~31px); the working tree adds `min-height: 34px` plus 2px borders. At HEAD `populated.map` rendered the unlabeled verb group FIRST. Both the 31→34px and the verbs-first→footer-last claims are correct.

MEASURED (real App.css, 800x560, `.app { height:100vh; overflow:hidden }` confirmed at App.css:24-30): computed `max-height: none`, `overflow-y: visible`, row height exactly 34px. n=8 → menu bottom 506 (fits); n=9 → 540 (fits, 20px to spare); n=10 → 574, footer clipped; n=19 → menu height 834px, bottom 880 — 320px below the fold. `#root`.scrollHeight stays 560, so a wheel/trackpad has nothing to scroll and the rows past the fold are unclickable.

EXTRA, MISSED BY THE FINDER AND WORSE: `.app` is `overflow:hidden` with scrollHeight 880 vs clientHeight 560, i.e. programmatically scrollable. Arrow-key focus into the footer therefore calls scrollIntoView and displaces the ENTIRE app column upward by ~308px, and it stays displaced after the menu closes — the user cannot scroll it back, because overflow:hidden is not user-scrollable.
correction: The defect is real but two details are off, and one mitigation was missed. (1) The unbounded filter is at src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2362, not 2360. (2) The threshold is 10 targets, not 9: measured at 800x560 with the real stylesheet, 9 targets puts the menu bottom at 540 of 560 (still fully reachable) and 10 puts it at 574. With 19 targets the menu is 834px tall (the claimed 813 is close); the claimed menu top of y=95 did not reproduce — a bare pathbar puts it at y=46, and the threshold moves toward 9 only if the real crumb sits lower. At the default 1100x720 window it takes ~15 targets. (3) The finder missed an escape hatch: the search field appears at exactly the same point the problem does (SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR = 6, SyncPathBar.tsx:129), and typing a non-matching query collapses the list to a single "No match." line (SyncPathBar.tsx:345), which lifts the footer verbs back above the fold. That is unadvertised but real, so the footer is not permanently unreachable by pointer. The proposed fix is still the right one.

title: Catalog Pull tells the user "nothing was changed" on failure paths that run after every selected resource has already been overwritten on disk
reason:
The finding misattributes the realistic path and inflates a rare copy imprecision into "high / destructive-safety".

1) The path that actually reports partial application is NOT the catch block. `execute_scope_pull_item` (src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/apply.rs:1063) returns `CatalogActionResult`, not `Result` — and service.rs:2010 collects it with no `?`. So every ordinary "some resources written, some failed" outcome returns Ok, and StorageCatalogPage.tsx already renders honest copy for it: `Pulled {applied} of {N} … {K} failed` plus the per-item failure lines (lines ~1124-1140). The codebase already handles the case the finding is worried about.

2) Of the Err returns in `apply_pull_with_repositories`, all but one are pre-flight guards that fire before a single byte is written (plan expired, "the scope link changed after review", "the storage changed after review", `verify_pins`, "the stored content changed after review", cross-storage claim drift, `validate_scope_pull_selection`). On every one of those — i.e. essentially every failure a user will ever see — "nothing was changed" is literally true. The only post-write Err is the trailing `catalog.mutate_scope_links(...)?` bookkeeping write, and it is skipped entirely when `base_changed` is false.

3) That one window is barely reachable. Catalog state is serialized by a process-wide mutex plus a file lock (`CATALOG_STATE_LOCK`, persistence.rs:34; `self.guard()` at persistence.rs:312), and the UI gates every competing control behind `busy` (Unlink at StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1238), so no concurrent link-revision bump can interleave. That leaves an OS write failure on a small JSON doc that occurs only *after* all the far larger payload writes succeeded — an ordering under which disk-full/permission failures would have landed in the honest per-item path first.

4) Even on that window the consequence is bounded and self-healing, not silent damage: the writes are exactly the ones the user selected and, for destructive ones, acknowledged on the ack chips; the catch calls `await load()` so the refreshed row list shows real on-disk state; the base did not advance, so the rows still read as differing and a re-run converges; the raw cause ("…while accepting Pull") is surfaced verbatim via `setFailures`; and there is a journaled recovery pass for interrupted operations (`recover_catalog_operations`, apply.rs:1296).

5) The Push half is not a destructive-safety issue at all. Push writes to storage, never to the user's disk, and is additive by construction ("never a replace, so a push can never delete another replica's resources", service.rs ~1693). "nothing was published" is the documented contract for pre-CAS failure in docs/DESIGN2.md:811 ("Any upload or metadata write before the CAS fails → nothing was published"). A post-CAS bookkeeping failure only leaves a stale local base, which the next Push reconciles on the explicit no-op path.

This is a toast-wording accuracy nit on a near-unreachable last-step failure, with a refreshed list and re-runnable convergence behind it — not the "user has no reason to look for damage" scenario claimed.
correction: Narrowly: on the single post-write failure of the trailing `mutate_scope_links` bookkeeping (and only when `base_changed` is true), the toast "Pull failed — nothing was changed." overstates. Everything else in that catch block — every pre-flight guard — is accurately described by the copy, and genuine partial application is already reported honestly through the Ok branch's "Pulled N of M — K failed" path.

title: The path-bar Push button commits the review without the project-file deletion acknowledgement the footer Push requires
reason: Citations check out line-for-line (ProjectSync.tsx:3393 predicate, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2671-2676 path-bar primary calling onContinue -> publishPendingPush, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:190/491/612-613/897), but the claimed defect is not reachable in the source. The footer's deletion gate arms only when projectFileDeletionCount(projectFileImpact) > 0, and pushProjectFileCommitImpact (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:359-365) increments deleteFile/deleteDirectory ONLY for ids in projectContentRemovals. That prop is the shell's pushProjectContentRemovals (ProjectSync.tsx:383), and all six of its setter call sites (849, 1815, 2102, 2127, 3400, 3444/3451) assign `new Set()` — nothing ever adds an id, because PushResourceWorkspace renders ProjectFilesReviewPage (lines 789-822) without `onToggleRemoval`, and the removal control is gated on `mode === "push" && row.storagePresent && onToggleRemoval` (ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:384). ProjectSync.tsx:3404 is the only production render of PushResourceWorkspace. Therefore, in the shipped app the removals set is permanently empty, the deletion count is permanently 0, "Approve the selected project file deletions" is never produced, the footer and path-bar predicates never disagree, and publishPendingPush always sends `[]` removal ids (ProjectSync.tsx:2199) — no file is ever deleted from storage by either button. The finding concedes this masking, so what remains is a latent predicate-duplication risk contingent on a separate unshipped repair, not a live destructive-safety bug. The finding is also imprecise in stating "the deletion state ... is never lifted, so the shell structurally cannot see it": the removals set does live in the shell and is read by continueDisabled; only the deletionApproved checkbox (useState at :491) is unlifted.
correction: Narrowed and accurate statement: ProjectSync.tsx:3393 recomputes a subset of PushResourceWorkspace's gates, omitting the local `deletionApproved` acknowledgement (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:491, 612-613), so the path-bar Push and the footer Push would diverge IF a push review could ever carry project-file removals. Today it cannot — `pushProjectContentRemovals` has no populating setter and `onToggleRemoval` is never passed to ProjectFilesReviewPage — so the divergence is unreachable and no deletion can be committed by either button. It is a latent duplicated-gate hazard to fix alongside restoring the removal control, not a current bypass.

title: The path-bar Push button commits the review without the project-file deletion acknowledgement the footer Push requires
reason: No reachable path produces the claimed consequence. `pushProjectContentRemovals` is write-only-to-empty: every one of its eight sites in ProjectSync.tsx declares it or resets it to `new Set()`, and neither PushResourceWorkspace's Props (lines 37-68) nor ProjectFilesReviewPage exposes any removal-toggle callback — `removalIds` (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:802) is a read-only display prop. Because `pushProjectFileCommitImpact` (line 348) counts deletions ONLY for ids present in `removals`, `projectFileDeletionCount(projectFileImpact)` is permanently 0 on the Push side. That makes the `"Approve the selected project file deletions"` branch at line 612 dead code, and ProjectFileCommitImpact gates the checkbox behind `deletionCount > 0`, so the acknowledgement control never even mounts in a Push review. The path-bar gate and the footer gate therefore cannot diverge on any user-reachable state; the finding concedes this itself ("masked today only because the removal control itself is unreachable"). Its entire impact is conditional on a different, unfixed finding being repaired first, which makes it a latent duplication note rather than a live destructive-safety defect. Two further deflations: (a) the acknowledgement it would bypass is `deletionTarget="storage"` — copy reads "Approve removal of N files and M folders from storage", i.e. dropping entries from the cloud bundle recipe (`delete recipe.entries[resourceId]`, ProjectSync.tsx:2191) with local files untouched and prior bundle revisions intact; the local-deletion variant ("Files are backed up.") is Pull-only, and Pull DOES propagate its gate correctly; (b) the shell predicate is not uniformly weaker — it adds `|| projectContentLoading`, which the footer's reason chain does not carry. The Pull-side `onPrimaryChange` contrast is accurate as structure, so the proposed fix is worth doing as hygiene when the removal control is wired, but nothing destructive can happen on the shipped build.
correction: Restated accurately: the path-bar Push recomputes a subset of the footer's gate instead of mirroring it (as Pull does via RestorePlanView's `onPrimaryChange`, lines 393-398). The only gate the shell omits is the project-file deletion acknowledgement, which is currently unreachable — no code path ever adds an id to `pushProjectContentRemovals`, so the deletion count is always 0, the checkbox never renders, and the two predicates are equivalent in practice. This is a latent duplicated-gate hazard to fix in the same change that wires a removal control, not a live bypass; and the acknowledgement it would guard covers removal from cloud storage, not deletion of local files.

title: The irreversible "Clear storage data" confirmation uses the default info dialog, so Return confirms the wipe on a button labelled "Ok"
reason: Reproduced in source. ProjectSync.tsx:3241-3244 contains the quoted confirm verbatim, with the options object `{ title: "Clear storage data" }` on line 3243 exactly as cited. `confirm` is the real Tauri dialog (import at ProjectSync.tsx:8, `import { confirm, open } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog"`) — no local wrapper or shim. The plugin source confirms the behavior: `customButtons = opts?.okLabel || opts?.cancelLabel` is falsy here, so it sends `buttons: 'OkCancel'` with `kind: undefined`, and index.d.ts:234 documents kind as defaulting to `info`. I traced the call path for a missed guard and found none: onClearStorage (ProjectSync.tsx:3837) is wired to a `danger: true` overflow-menu row in ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1778 that calls clearStorageData directly — no typed-name gate, no second confirmation, only `disabled: busy`. The contrast case is real: SettingsPage.tsx:208-214 and :255-258 pass `{ kind: "warning", okLabel: ..., cancelLabel: "Cancel" }` for smaller consequences. The message also omits the object counts, which the backend only reports after the wipe. Two collateral claims are inaccurate but do not affect the core defect, so the finding stands with a correction rather than refuted.

title: Dead "Remove storage" trash button in the storage editor header
reason:
The code facts check out — `onRemove?: () => void` (StorageSettings.tsx:162) is optional, the button is gated behind `{onRemove && (...)}` (line 273), and the sole production mount at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1935 never passes it (no prop spread anywhere; the only other mount is a test render at storage-settings.integration.test.tsx:212, also without it). But under an impact/novelty lens this has no consequence and is a deliberate design decision, so it should not stand as a destructive-safety finding.

(1) Zero user-visible surface, with inverted polarity for the lens. The control never renders, so no user can hit it — nothing destructive is reachable, which is the safe direction. A destructive-safety review flagging "a delete button that cannot be clicked" is reporting the absence of a hazard.

(2) It is intentional, and the intent is pinned by an existing test. storage-settings.integration.test.tsx:869-870 states the design outright: "The storage page: Storages / name ⌄ / Repositories, with the old header's gear, pencil, and ✕ folded into the bar's single overflow." The header's destructive control was deliberately retired into the path-bar overflow during that cutover; the same test asserts the two surviving routes (`onRemoveStorage(storage.id)` in the sidebar, `onRemoveStorage(editedStorageConfig.id)` in the overflow). The leftover prop is a vestige of a documented, test-locked redesign, not an oversight nobody decided about.

(3) Half the proposed fix is an actual destructive-safety regression. Wiring `onRemove={() => onRemoveStorage(editedStorageConfig.id)}` at the mount would mint an icon-only trash button with no confirm affordance that bypasses both existing guards: the overflow item is `disabled: busy || storageLinkCount > 0` with a `disabledReason` ("Linked to N projects — unlink first", lines 1785-1790) and its label carries the "…" that signals a confirm step ("Remove storage…"); the sidebar twin is `disabled={busy || usage > 0}` with the matching title. The dead header button is guarded only by `disabled` (busy), so enabling it would let a user destroy a storage still linked to projects from a bare icon. Recommending it as an equal alternative to deletion is wrong.

(4) The maintainer-confusion impact is speculative. `onRemove?: () => void` plus `{onRemove && ...}` is the standard React idiom for an opt-in control; a maintainer reads it as "the host may seat a remove action here", not as "the editor offers Remove". The orphaned App.css:2069 rule is ~70 bytes of unmatched selector with no runtime, layout, or accessibility effect (and note line 2073 already gives `margin-left: auto` to the segmented control that actually occupies that slot).

What remains is genuine dead code — three lines of TSX plus one CSS rule — worth deleting on the codebase's own "no deadcode, clean cutovers" convention. That is a tidiness item for a dead-code sweep, not a destructive-safety finding, and it has no user or maintainer consequence on any realistic path.
correction: Re-file under dead-code/hygiene, not destructive-safety, and drop the second fix option: the `onRemove` prop (StorageSettings.tsx:152/162), the header button (lines 273-275), and the orphaned `.sync-storage-card > header .danger` rule (App.css:2069) are unreachable residue from the documented cutover that folded the header's gear/pencil/✕ into the path-bar overflow (pinned at storage-settings.integration.test.tsx:869-870). Do NOT wire `onRemove` at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1935 — that would add an unconfirmed icon-only delete that bypasses the `storageLinkCount > 0` guard and `disabledReason` carried by the overflow's "Remove storage…" item and by the sidebar's `disabled={busy || usage > 0}` twin, making destructive safety strictly worse.

title: The new path-bar switcher menus render destructive commands as unlabelled icon pills
reason:

The memory record <local-review-memory>/switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md documents that the user was shown four directions in the specimen menu-mockup.html and explicitly picked "B · Switcher", whose description names the exact row objected to: "the four verbs as 32px icon pills (Reveal/Terminal/Rename/red Reset) in a surface-footer strip". (2) The pills are not unlabelled. renderPill sets aria-label={item.label} (SyncPathBar.tsx:230) in addition to title={verbTitle(item)}. "The only text is a hover tooltip" is false.

(3) Every one of the three cited destructive verbs is gated by an explicit confirmation dialog that names what happens and what does not: Reset local sync state -> ProjectSync.tsx:2678-2681 ("Project files, provider sessions, project setup, recipes, storage configuration, and cloud data will not be deleted."); Unlink -> ProjectSync.tsx:2843-2846 ("No project files or cloud objects will be deleted... you can link the storage again later."); Remove this Catalog row -> ProjectSync.tsx:1581-1584 ("Only the menu row is removed. No provider or storage content is touched."). The finding's own impact statement concedes the confirmation exists. None of the three is a "wipe" — the worst outcome after confirming a mis-click is a forgotten sync base, an unlinked pairing, or a hidden menu row, all re-establishable; no file, session, or cloud object is destroyed.

(4) It is already the app's established idiom rather than a new hazard: StorageSettings.tsx:274, unchanged at HEAD, is an icon-only red trash button carrying only title/aria-label "Remove storage". Geometry is also within spec — 32x32 targets with an 8px gap clears WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24x24), and danger is additionally coded red via .sync-path-menu-verb.danger plus a distinct trash glyph sitting last in the row. `git diff HEAD --stat` on ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx and StorageCatalogPage.tsx is empty, confirming the danger flags and descriptive titles were authored for this rendering.

What remains is a discoverability preference — a sighted mouse user must hover to read a verb's name — which is a design-taste note against a decision the user already made with a specimen in front of them, not a destructive-safety defect.

This was the design direction the user selected from a four-way specimen, and every danger verb remains behind a named confirmation dialog whose action destroys no files, sessions, or cloud data.

When `thread_comparison_error` is set, service.rs:7536/7563 leaves `conversation_push_plan_id` None and `conversation_action_ids` empty, so `publishPendingPush` (ProjectSync.tsx:2165) sends a project-files-only push with an empty action list — it cannot produce any of those messages. `pushError` otherwise only comes from that publish or a project-file scan failure (ProjectSync.tsx:2016/2156). So the two buttons cannot realistically be on screen together, and the "same command twice with two different danger readings" scenario never occurs.

2. Neither button is destructive on click. Both route to `resetProjectSyncMetadata` (ProjectSync.tsx:2671), which awaits a native `confirm` naming exactly what is forgotten ("reviewed sync bases, conversation mappings, recovery records, Pull results, and saved Push/Pull plans") and what is preserved, and returns without any call if not approved. A user who mis-reads the button weight loses nothing — the confirm dialog carries the whole safety contract. This is the codebase's stated "native dialogs" convention.

3. The banner already carries the danger reading: it is pushed with `severity: "danger"` into the banner zone with the title "Conversations couldn't be compared, so nothing can be selected". The button sits inside a red danger notice; the sibling at :837 is inside a `Notice severity="danger" timing="blocking"` for the same reason. The zones are also spatially distinct — the banner zone heads the review scroll, the error Notice sits below the entire resource list.

What actually remains is a cosmetic divergence from a house convention: the other three "Reset local sync state" buttons (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:837, RestorePlanView.tsx:487, and the ProjectLinksWorkspace menu at :3167) all use `btn btn-ghost danger` with a `trash` icon. That is a consistency nit worth a one-word class edit, not a destructive-safety defect, and the second half of the proposed fix (suppressing the banner action when the notice offers the same recovery) guards a state that cannot be reached.
correction: Not a destructive-safety issue. Accurately stated: the new comparison-failed banner action at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:590 omits the `danger` class and `trash` icon used by the other three "Reset local sync state" buttons (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:837, RestorePlanView.tsx:487, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:3167), a house-style inconsistency inside an already-danger-severity banner whose click is confirm-gated.

title: Switcher target lists have no accessible name: the group label is dropped visually and set with aria-label on a role-less div
reason:
The markup is quoted correctly (SyncPathBar.tsx:343), but the claimed impact does not hold, and the missing label is a deliberate, user-chosen design decision.

1) Intent is documented and picked by the user. PathBarMenu's own doc comment (SyncPathBar.tsx:119-128) states that in a switcher "groups play roles by position ... the list itself is only the things you can switch to" — the label is dropped on purpose. The specimen <repo>/menu-mockup.html shows four directions: A (line 159), C (206) and D (235) all render a `Switch to` label; B · Switcher — the one the user picked and that shipped uncommitted 2026-09-01 per the switcher-menu-directions memory — has no label at all, by construction. Restoring a visible label would revert the chosen direction.

2) There is nothing to disambiguate. Every switcher menu in the app has exactly one labelled group, always literally "Switch to": ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1709, 2298, 2428, 2527 and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1246, 1321. A screen-reader user never meets two competing target lists. The run of targets is already bracketed by the current-object row above it (`.sync-path-menu-current` with aria-current="true" plus a check icon, line 317) and the footer verb strip below it, and the menu itself carries an accessible name on the real role: `role="menu" aria-label={label}` (lines 252-253) resolving to "Storage" / "Project" / "Catalog row" / "Switch view". At >=6 targets a search field is added labelled "Filter storage list" with placeholder "Switch storage…" (lines 328-336). The word "switch" is therefore said in the menu's name, the opener's aria-label ("<name>. Storage menu"), and the search affordance.

3) The proposed fix would add a capability this codebase never had, not restore one. In the non-switcher branch the label at line 363 is a bare `<div className="sync-path-menu-label">` with no role, no heading, and no aria-labelledby on its container — it is not a group name in the accessibility tree either, and while an AT is in menu navigation mode inside role="menu" it reads menuitems, not loose text. So nothing regressed for AT relative to the branch it is being compared against.

4) No functional consequence. menuOptions/moveMenuFocus (src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts) select `[role="menuitem"]` descendants via querySelectorAll, so the generic wrapper affects neither roving focus, typeahead, Home/End, nor Enter-on-first-match. The identical role-less `.sync-path-menu-group` wrapper is used by the long-shipped non-switcher branch (line 361) and by StorageCatalogPage.tsx:594, and the finding does not claim those are broken. `role="separator"` in a menu is decorative and non-focusable; the switcher replaces it with a visually and structurally distinct footer strip.

What is left after all that is one dead attribute: `aria-label` on an element with the implicit generic role is ignored, so it is inert markup — lint noise, not a user-visible defect, and not something a user or maintainer "hits" on any path. This is also outside the destructive-safety lens that produced it.
correction: Accurate residual statement: the `aria-label={group.label}` at SyncPathBar.tsx:343 is inert (ARIA prohibits an author name on the generic role), so it is dead markup that should simply be deleted; the absent "Switch to" heading is the intended B · Switcher design (position conveys the role, exactly one target list ever exists, and the menu itself is named via role="menu" aria-label), not a lost announcement.

title: H02 (still open) — portalled details popovers still never receive focus, so their copy actions are unreachable by keyboard
reason: Factually wrong: the fix it proposes is already implemented, in the shared hook the finding never read. All three popovers call useDebugPopoverPlacement (ProjectFileDetailsMenu.tsx:44, ProjectActivityPage.tsx:817, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:215), and <repo>/src/components/sync-review/debugPopoverPlacement.ts ends with an effect that focuses the panel's first enabled button as soon as placement resolves: `panelRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>("button:not([disabled])")?.focus()`. The hook's own doc comment documents the intent — "Once placed, the first enabled action receives focus" — so this is deliberate, committed behavior (landed in f2cdac4, unmodified in the working tree), not an oversight. The finding's evidence block quotes only the trigger's onClick and the focusin handler and omits line 44, which is where the focus move comes from. Because focus lands on a button inside panelRef, the focusin dismissal's inside() check (which tests rootRef OR panelRef) sees an inside target and does not close; the keyboard user arrives directly on the first Copy button with no Tab needed, and Tab walks the remaining copy rows and Copy all. The premise that "the next Tab from the trigger lands on the following control in the row" never occurs, because focus is no longer on the trigger. Escape is also handled and restores focus to the trigger via closeMenu(true). The panel needs no tabIndex={-1} precisely because a real focusable child receives focus instead. The only residual is the absence of a focus trap — tabbing past the last panel button dismisses the popover rather than cycling — which is a defensible dismissal model for a transient copy popover (it matches the hook's scroll/resize dismissal doctrine of never leaving a fixed panel stranded) and leaves every action reachable. No user-visible consequence; nothing to fix.
correction: The behavior described as missing exists: useDebugPopoverPlacement focuses the panel's first enabled button on open for all three popovers, and Escape restores focus to the trigger. At most one could note that the popovers do not trap focus — tabbing past the last button dismisses them — which is a deliberate transient-popover choice, not a keyboard-reachability defect.

title: Two "Reset local sync state" buttons can co-render in one Push review with different visual weight
reason: Citation and line numbers are accurate (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:590 plain ghost, :837 ghost+danger+trash), and the CSS weight difference is real (.btn-ghost color: var(--text-1) at App.css:346-355 vs .notice .btn.danger { color: var(--danger-text) } at App.css:1382, specificity 0-3-0 > 0-1-0). But the claimed impact does not hold. Both buttons receive the identical prop from one call site, ProjectSync.tsx:3462 (onResetMetadata={() => void resetProjectSyncMetadata(pendingPush.projectId)}), and resetProjectSyncMetadata (ProjectSync.tsx:2671) gates every invocation on a native Tauri confirm() titled "Reset local sync state" that enumerates exactly what is forgotten (reviewed sync bases, conversation mappings, recovery records, Pull results, saved Push/Pull plans) and what is not, returning early unless approved. It is the only path to projectSyncApi.resetProjectSyncMetadata. So no click at either site can "forget every reviewed sync base, conversation mapping, recovery record and saved plan" without an explicit confirmation — the ghost styling is not the safety gate. The banner also renders inside a .notice.danger box (App.css:1384) whose red tint, border, and bold "Error ·" lead already carry the destructive context. correction: Cosmetic only: the same "Reset local sync state" recovery is offered with two different button treatments (plain ghost in the comparison-failed banner at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:590, ghost+danger+trash in the push-error notice at :837). Both route to the same confirm()-gated handler, so no data can be lost from either click; matching the classes would be a consistency polish, not a safety fix.

title: M10 (still open, now a safety bypass) — the path-bar Push commits the review, skipping the deletion acknowledgement the footer enforces
reason: Independently reproduced from source. (1) ProjectSync.tsx:3386-3395 matches the quoted evidence near-verbatim; continueDisabled = (selection empty AND removals empty) || pendingPushBlockingCount > 0 || projectContentLoading — no deletion-approval term. (2) The path-bar Push button (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2660-2679) is rendered concurrently with the review: syncPathActions is built at :2575 gated only on workspaceProject && workspaceStorage, handed to SyncPathBar at :2726, and inlineStorageReview.content renders below at :3228. storageActionLockedForReview("push","push") returns false (:583-588), so the button stays live during a push review, and its onClick short-circuits to inlineStorageReview?.onContinue?.() when workspacePushReviewOpen. (3) pushReviewBlockers (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:169-211) not only ignores deletionApproved, it explicitly skips removals at :189 (`if (projectContentRemovals.has(resourceId)) continue;`). (4) The repo's OWN test proves the gap: tests/frontend/project-files.integration.test.tsx:361-364 asserts pushReviewBlockingCount(...removals) === 0 for 1 file + 1 folder deletion, while :388-391 of the same test asserts the footer renders the unticked checkbox with title="Approve the selected project file deletions". So continueDisabled is false in exactly the state where pushDisabledReason (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:608-616) is non-null. (5) deletionApproved is useState local to PushResourceWorkspace (:491) with no outward callback; grep confirms onPrimaryChange exists only on RestorePlanView (:66,:286,:393-398) and its consumer ProjectSync.tsx:3510 — the Pull/Push asymmetry is real. (6) The click is genuinely destructive: publishPendingPush passes [...pushProjectContentRemovals] to publishProject (ProjectSync.tsx:2199), which calls projectSyncApi.pushBundle (:2074-2083) with no confirmation dialog anywhere in the path. No guard, fallback, or call-site condition rescues it.
