correction: The core defect is confirmed, but the second half of the proposed fix is already implemented and should be dropped: PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:487-492 already derives a `deletionSignature` from `projectContentRemovals` and runs `useEffect(() => setDeletionApproved(false), [deletionSignature])`, so an approval of 2 deletions cannot carry over to a later selection of 40. Only the `onPrimaryChange` lift is needed — hoist `pushDisabledReason` (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:608-616, including the `projectFileDeletionCount(projectFileImpact) > 0 && !deletionApproved` clause) out to ProjectSync and feed it into `inlineStorageReview.continueDisabled`/`continueTitle`, mirroring RestorePlanView.tsx:393-398. Minor citation drift, non-material: the onPrimaryChange consumer is ProjectSync.tsx:3510 (not 3475); SyncPathBar renders at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2726 (not 2727); the footer's disabled title binding is PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:897-898, with the reason string built at :608-616 (not :612 alone).

title: Switcher target lists have no accessible name: the group label is dropped visually and set with aria-label on a role-less div
reason: Citation is accurate: src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:343 contains the quoted line verbatim, and the switcher branch (guarded by `switcher = !!header`, line 166) renders `lists` with neither `.sync-path-menu-label` nor `role="separator"`, while the non-switcher branch at 360-366 still renders both. git diff confirms header-bearing menus previously did render the visible label and separators. No runtime role assignment (menuKeyboard.ts only selects [role=menuitem*]) and no CSS rule in App.css (3061-3320, 8225, 9083) restores a heading or adds a ::before, so the container keeps its implicit `generic` role, on which ARIA 1.2 prohibits an author-supplied name — the aria-label is inert. Defect reproduced. However the stated impact is imprecise on three points, so I am correcting rather than confirming verbatim.
correction: The switcher list group carries an inert `aria-label` on a role-less `div` (implicit `generic`, where ARIA prohibits naming), and the visible `.sync-path-menu-label` heading the non-switcher branch still renders at line 363 (not 366) is not rendered in switcher mode — so the group's name exists neither visually nor in the accessibility tree. Three corrections to the impact: (1) the visible label lives at line 363; (2) a structural boundary does still exist visually — `.sync-path-menu-current` is a bordered, shadowed card with margin-bottom (App.css 3163-3173) and `.sync-path-menu-foot` has `border-top: 1px solid var(--border-mid)` (App.css 3212-3222) — only the programmatic `role="separator"` is gone; (3) the screen-reader user does not "hear the current object" first: `.sync-path-menu-current` is likewise a role-less div inside `role="menu"` and is skipped by menuOptions()/moveMenuFocus, so that context arrives only via the menu's own aria-label and the crumb button's ariaLabel (e.g. "<storage>. Storage menu"). Every shipped switcher call site supplies exactly one labelled group, always "Switch to", so the loss is one heading over an unambiguous list, not a lost distinction between multiple groups. Fix as proposed: `role="group"` on the container plus a visually-hidden or visible `.sync-path-menu-label`.

title: M02 (still open) — five role="radio" groups still implement no radio keyboard behaviour
reason: Independently reproduced. SettingsPage.tsx:391 is verbatim the quoted radiogroup div, followed by the THEME_CHOICES map emitting role="radio" buttons with aria-checked and only onClick — line number exact, quote exact. All five cited groups exist: SettingsPage.tsx:391, StorageSettings.tsx:230, ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:905, BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:123, AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:228 (7 role="radio" elements total, matching the repo-wide count). grep for onKeyDown/onKeyUp/onKeyPress/Arrow/tabIndex/roving returns nothing in any of the five files; repo-wide the only Arrow handlers are SyncReviewTabs.tsx:55-58 (a tablist) and ProjectSync.tsx:720-721 (sidebar resize). None of the eleven document/window keydown listeners is radio-related (all Escape-closers, sidebar shortcut, activity-page handlers) and none lives in these files, so there is no delegated fallback the finder missed. There is no shared segmented-control component supplying behaviour — each site hand-rolls its own div. Every option is a native button with no tabIndex override, so each defaults to 0 and is its own tab stop, confirming the tab-order inflation claim (AddCatalogScope +3, ProjectSetup +1+N bundles). Severity medium is correct rather than high: Tab plus Enter/Space still activates each option via native button semantics, so this is a broken ARIA-pattern expectation and tab-order noise, not an unreachable control.
correction: ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx contains ONE radiogroup, at line 905, not two — line 937 is a role="radio" option inside that same group (the mapped remote-bundle button). The finding's "905/937" phrasing implies two groups in that file; the overall count of five groups is nonetheless correct. Also worth stating precisely: the options are not unreachable — native button semantics still give Tab focus and Enter/Space activation — so the defect is the missing roving tabIndex plus Arrow/Home/End handling required by the ARIA radiogroup pattern, and the resulting extra Tab stops, not a loss of keyboard operability.

title: M10 (still open, now a safety bypass) — the path-bar Push commits the review, skipping the deletion acknowledgement the footer enforces
reason: The bypass is unreachable — no user can select a project-file deletion in a Push review at all. Three independent structural facts: (1) ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:384 gates the "Remove from storage" trash button on `onToggleRemoval`, and PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:790-822 never passes it (the prop is absent from its Props interface at :37-69); (2) all 8 writers of `pushProjectContentRemovals` in ProjectSync.tsx (lines 383, 849, 1815, 2102, 2127, 3400, 3444, 3451) assign `new Set()` — the set is permanently empty in the app; (3) the Push files step lists only local-outstanding rows (`local_present && (local_only||local_ahead)`, PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:83-85, 452), while the trash button also requires `row.storagePresent`, so removal candidates are doubly filtered out. Since pushProjectFileCommitImpact derives deleteFile/deleteDirectory solely from `removals` (:361-365), projectFileDeletionCount is always 0 in Push: the approval checkbox never renders (ProjectFileCommitImpact.tsx:43) and the "Approve the selected project file deletions" branch of pushDisabledReason (:612-613) is dead. The footer Push is therefore never disabled for deletions, so the path-bar Push bypasses nothing — the two buttons agree in every reachable state. The cited test injects `projectContentRemovals` as a direct prop, which is the only place in the repo it is ever non-empty. Two further errors in the finding: the proposed reset already exists (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:487-492, `useEffect(() => setDeletionApproved(false), [deletionSignature])`), and the hypothetical "deletion" is a manifest exclusion in a new bundle revision (service.rs:9885), touching nothing local and leaving prior revisions intact — the actually-destructive local delete is the Pull side, which is gated and backed up. What remains is a latent contract asymmetry for whoever later wires onToggleRemoval through, not a live destructive-safety defect.
correction: Latent, not live: the path-bar Push reuses `inlineStorageReview.continueDisabled`, which omits the deletion-approval clause the footer applies — but `pushProjectContentRemovals` is永 empty in the shipped app (no `onToggleRemoval` is wired into PushResourceWorkspace, and every ProjectSync writer assigns an empty set), so the deletion checkbox never renders and no state exists in which the two buttons disagree. The finding would only become real if the "Remove from storage" affordance were wired into the Push review; at that point the gate should be lifted out to ProjectSync. The suggested `deletionApproved` reset is already implemented at PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:487-492.

title: M01 (still open) — the Logs resize separator is still mouse-only and 16px thick
reason: Independently reproduced. ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:191-198 matches the quoted JSX verbatim (line 191 = opening <div>, 192 = className="log-resizer"): role="separator" with only onMouseDown/onDoubleClick, no tabIndex, no aria-valuemin/valuemax/valuenow, no onKeyDown. Tracing the handler, ProjectSync.tsx:665-686 startLogResize guards on event.button !== 0 and drives the drag with document mousemove/mouseup listeners; logHeight (ProjectSync.tsx:398) is written only from that drag, the double-click reset at 3883, and a window-resize clamp at 589 — there is no keyboard path, and neither ActivityLogDrawer.tsx nor LogPanel.tsx registers a keydown other than Escape-to-close (LogPanel.tsx:180-195). The contrast case is real: ProjectSync.tsx:3694-3709 gives the sidebar separator aria-valuemin/max/now, tabIndex={0}, pointer events and onKeyDown={resizeSidebarWithKeyboard} (defined at 718). CSS resolves as stated: .log-resizer height 8px (App.css:493-501) is overridden by .sync-log-drawer .log-resizer height: calc(var(--retro-gutter) + 8px) (App.css:10601-10604); --retro-gutter is defined exactly once as 8px (App.css:8082) with no later redefinition, no other height rule for the selector, and no pointer-area extension (::before is display:none at 10606; the ::after pill sits inside the box) — 16px confirmed. Only the WCAG citation is off: 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is WCAG 2.2 AA (with a spacing exception), not 2.1; the load-bearing failure is 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A) plus a separator exposing no value.
correction: The Logs resize separator (src/components/project-sync/ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:191-198) is operable by mouse only — it has no tabIndex, no onKeyDown and no aria-valuemin/valuemax/valuenow, and ProjectSync.tsx:665-686 drives the resize purely from mousedown + document mousemove/mouseup, so keyboard and switch users cannot resize or reset the drawer at all (WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, Level A) and a screen reader announces a separator with no value. The sidebar separator at ProjectSync.tsx:3694-3709 already implements the full contract. Secondarily, the drag strip resolves to 16px tall (App.css:10603 calc(var(--retro-gutter) + 8px) with --retro-gutter: 8px at App.css:8082), below the 24px minimum of WCAG 2.2 (not 2.1) SC 2.5.8, which also allows a spacing exception.

title: M04 (still open) — the two custom focus rings are still translucent and fall below 3:1
reason:
The CSS quote is accurate and the contrast math roughly checks out (I recomputed 45% --accent over --surface-row in light: ~2.69:1; 35%: ~2.09:1). But the claimed impact — "a keyboard user tabbing through an activity row in light mode cannot see where focus is" — is false, and the proposed fix rests on a wrong premise.

1. The ring is not the focus affordance; the tooltip is. Both selectors reveal a tooltip on the SAME :focus-visible state. src/App.css:5273-5277 `.sync-thread-sync-indicator:hover::after, .sync-thread-sync-indicator:focus-visible::after { opacity: 1; visibility: visible; }` and src/App.css:5444-5448 the same for `.sync-history-thread-metric[data-tooltip]`. That tooltip is a solid panel: `background: var(--surface-popover)`, `box-shadow: var(--shadow-popover)`, `color: var(--text-0)`, `border: 1px solid var(--border-strong)` (raised to `--accent` for the indicator at src/App.css:10297-10303). Tabbing pops a bordered, shadowed popover of text next to the chip — an unmissable state change, orders of magnitude louder than any 2px ring.

2. It always fires. Every `tabIndex={0}` instance of both classes carries `data-tooltip` (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:599-603, 670, 701-706; ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:174-177, 223, 232, 254; StorageCatalogPage.tsx:175-179, 190-194). The only metrics without a tooltip (ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:239, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:700) are `aria-hidden="true"` layout spacers with no tabIndex — not tabbable.

3. It is deliberate and already gated. src/App.css:9587-9592 carries the comment that the badge must be lifted on `:hover` OR `:focus-visible` "so its tooltip clears the rows" — the codebase explicitly models focus as a tooltip-opening state. tests/frontend/project-activity.integration.test.tsx ("sync tooltip hover keeps the sibling icon rail geometry stable", ~line 1020-1041) gates every ancestor against `overflow: hidden|clip|auto|scroll` so the focus tooltip can escape, and gates it against animating. An existing test protects this focus presentation.

4. On the very page the finding names, the ring is not painted at all — and nothing broke. src/App.css:9940-9943 `.sync-history-commit > .sync-history-thread-list .sync-thread-sync-indicator { background: transparent; box-shadow: none; }` is specificity 0-3-0 and beats `.sync-thread-sync-indicator:focus-visible` at 0-2-0, so inside commit thread lists the focus box-shadow is suppressed entirely. Focus has been ring-less there in shipped code with no reported loss of location, because the tooltip carries it.

5. Nothing is actionable. These are `<span>` readouts, not controls. Tab lands, a tooltip opens, and there is no action to mis-target — no keystroke does anything destructive or even mutating from this focus.

6. The proposed fix is wrong on its face. "Drop the `outline: none` and let the global 2px `--accent` outline (App.css:38-44) apply" cannot work: that rule is `button:focus-visible, input:focus-visible, select:focus-visible, summary:focus-visible` (verified at src/App.css:38-44), and there is no `[tabindex]` or span selector anywhere in App.css. These elements are spans and never matched the global rule; removing `outline: none` would fall back to the UA default ring, not the accent ring. The finding's "still open / prior regression" framing also misreads history — this ring was never the global ring being overridden.

WCAG 1.4.11 / 2.4.7 are satisfied when a visible focus indicator meets the bar, not when every decorative layer does; the conformance-carrying indicator here is the popover.
correction: Accurate as a measurement, not as an impact: the two translucent rings do measure below 3:1 (~2.09:1 and ~2.69:1 in light), but they are supplementary decoration, not the focus indicator. The same :focus-visible state opens a solid bordered/shadowed tooltip (App.css:5273-5277 and 5444-5448) on every tabbable instance, which is the conformance-carrying and user-visible focus cue — and inside commit thread lists the ring is already suppressed outright by App.css:9940-9943. The real (cosmetic) nit is that the rings under-measure and that App.css:38-44 never covered these spans, so `outline: none` at 5215/5367 suppresses only the UA default; the suggested "let the global outline apply" repair would not produce an accent ring.

title: M03 (still open) — three menu-button patterns still open without moving focus, and the path-bar menu closes on Tab
reason: Citations check out verbatim: SyncPathBar.tsx:541 is the crumb onClick, 549-558 the keydown with the Tab-close and the Arrow-only focusMenuOption; ProjectSync.tsx:2764-2801/1318-1324 and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2032-2077/1278-1282 all match. The core defect is real and independently reproduced in source: PathBarMenu has no focus-on-open (no autoFocus anywhere, search input at 328-335 is not focused), and only the ArrowDown/ArrowUp branch calls focusMenuOption, so Enter/Space opens with focus parked on the trigger; the app-actions and agent-setup menus have no keydown handler at all, and because one is `hidden` and the other conditionally rendered, Escape pressed while focus is inside them drops focus to body. However, the finding's Tab half is wrong and its severity is overstated. Tab-closing is deliberate and correct: every PathBarMenu option is rendered tabIndex={-1} (lines 190 and 227), so Tab can never enter the menu; the menu container carries the same Tab-close at 255-260 with a comment stating Tab is not menu navigation; and neither handler preventDefaults, so the browser does continue past the trigger — the WAI-ARIA menu-button behavior. The proposed "let it move focus into the menu" would break that. Conversely the two other menus render items WITHOUT tabIndex={-1}, so keyboard users can Tab into them today; they are non-conformant, not unreachable, and in the ordinary flow Escape finds focus still on the trigger. No status file claims M03 was fixed (docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md:166), so this is a partially-addressed open item, not a regression — menuKeyboard.ts is consumed by SyncPathBar and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:585,591 but never by the other two.
correction: Three menu-button patterns omit ARIA-conformant focus movement. In SyncPathBar (src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:541-560, and the same shape on the split-crumb toggle at 514-527 and the overflow button at 616-628), Enter/Space opens the menu but leaves focus on the trigger; only ArrowDown/ArrowUp call focusMenuOption. The Tab branch is NOT a defect — options are tabIndex={-1} (lines 190, 227), no preventDefault is called, and the container repeats the same close at 255-260 with an explanatory comment, which is the correct menu-button contract. The app-actions menu (ProjectSync.tsx:2764-2801) and the agent-setup split menu (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2032-2077) have no keydown handler at all: no focus on open and no Arrow/Home/End; their items are tabbable, so they can be reached with Tab, but Escape while focus is inside (ProjectSync.tsx:1318-1324, ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1278-1282) hides/unmounts the focused item and drops focus to body. Fix: call focusMenuOption(crumb.id, "first") from the SyncPathBar click handlers (keep the Tab-close), and adopt menuKeyboard's moveMenuFocus/focusMenuEdge plus focus-return on the other two menus, as StorageCatalogPage.tsx:585,591 already does.

title: M01 (still open) — the Logs resize separator is still mouse-only and 16px thick
reason: Two of the finding's three legs are wrong and the third is a comfort-knob nit. (1) Target size: the finding's own cited reference, .sync-sidebar-resizer, is width: 12px with a 4px pill (App.css:8916, 8929) — NARROWER than the log resizer's 16px. The slim-pill-in-a-thin-gutter handle is the deliberate house geometry, documented in the CSS comment at App.css:10598 ("spans the main tile's 2px bottom edge, the gutter, and the drawer's 2px top edge, then reaches 4px into the drawer for grip"). WCAG 2.5.8 is a 2.2 criterion, and its spacing exception applies anyway: the strip sits alone in the gutter with no focusable target within 4px. (2) Screen reader: a role="separator" WITHOUT tabIndex is the valid static-separator form in ARIA; aria-valuemin/max/now are required only for the focusable window-splitter form, so "announces a separator with no value" is not a defect as authored. (3) Impact: .log-panel-body is overflow-y: auto (App.css:731-734), the drawer opens at 240px, and every control in it (type filters, level select, search, Load older, Manage logs, Clear, Close) is a real button/input — a keyboard user reaches 100% of log content and every log function without resizing. logHeight is useState(240) (ProjectSync.tsx:398), never persisted and auto-clamped to 140-520 on window resize, i.e. a transient comfort adjustment for an already-scrolling pane, not a gate on anything. Novelty also fails: nothing in docs/, tests/, or the audit memory files (frontend-reaudit-2026-08-25.md, ui-audit-fixes-landed.md) mentions the log resizer or its keyboard contract, and resizeSidebarWithKeyboard arrived in feature commit 826d890 rather than as audit remediation — so the "M01 still open / prior regression" framing has no record behind it.
correction: Accurate residue, narrowed: ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:191-198 wires the resize handle to mouse events only, so a keyboard user cannot adjust the Logs drawer height. All log content and controls remain fully keyboard-accessible at the default 240px (the panel body scrolls), the height is transient and never persisted, and the 16px hit strip matches — and exceeds — the shipped sidebar handle's 12px, so there is no target-size or screen-reader defect here. Adding tabIndex + onKeyDown (and only then the aria-value* trio) is a small polish item, not an access blocker.

title: M02 (still open) — five role="radio" groups still implement no radio keyboard behaviour
reason:
The markup is exactly as quoted (verified at SettingsPage.tsx:391, StorageSettings.tsx:230, ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:905/937, BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:123, AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:228 — seven role="radio" buttons, zero onKeyDown, zero roving tabIndex). But there is no real user-visible consequence, it is a known and deliberately deferred item, and the severity is inflated.

1. Nothing is unreachable. Every option is a native <button>, so Tab reaches it and Enter/Space fires onClick via browser default. <repo>/src/App.css:38 has a global `button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent); outline-offset: 2px; }`, so the focused option is visibly marked. WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 2.4.3 (Focus Order), and 2.4.7 (Focus Visible) all pass. role and aria-checked are correct, so 4.1.2 passes too. Arrow-key selection is an ARIA Authoring Practices convention, not a WCAG 2.1 AA success criterion — the finding is written as a conformance failure but names no failed SC.

2. "Nothing happens" overstates the screen-reader path. This is a Tauri/WKWebView macOS app (the memory record is all macOS: ⌘Q/muda menu behaviour, "System follows macOS" in the Theme row's own copy). VoiceOver drives its own cursor with VO+Arrow and activates with VO+Space; both work on plain buttons. The user hears each option's label and checked state and can select any of them. The gap is a pattern-expectation mismatch for a Windows NVDA/JAWS forms-mode user on a platform this app does not primarily ship to — not a blocked task.

3. The Tab-stop complaint cuts the other way. Roving tabIndex makes only the *checked* option tabbable, so an unselected option becomes unreachable by Tab alone. Two of these five groups (ProjectSetupWorkspace's repo identity, BundleConnectionDialog's remote-repo chooser) render an unbounded list of remote repos; the current markup lets Tab reach all of them. The static groups are 3 (THEME_CHOICES), 2 (storage type), and 4 (CATALOG_KINDS) options — three extra Tab stops in a settings row is a preference, not "inflating the Tab order".

4. Already handled where it is actually required, and knowingly not here. <repo>/src/components/sync-review/SyncReviewTabs.tsx implements the exact pattern the finding asks for — `tabIndex={active ? 0 : -1}` plus ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End with rAF focus restoration — because a role="tablist" is one Tab stop by definition and its panel must be reachable. A group of buttons is not. The codebase also ships menuKeyboard.ts and Arrow handling in SyncPathBar, ProjectActivityPage, and ProjectSidebar. The roving pattern is well known here and was applied selectively.

5. Not a regression, and not an oversight. This is verbatim docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md:158 ("M02 — Custom radio groups do not implement radio keyboard behavior"), filed Medium. The same audit certifies at line 74 that "Review tabs implement the expected tablist, roving focus, Arrow, Home, and End keyboard behavior" — so the author had the pattern in hand and filed the radio groups separately as lower-priority. It has never been fixed, so it never regressed; it was triaged and left, across subsequent passes that touched these very files (the Codex retheme restyled .sync-settings-segment buttons on 2026-09-01; the switcher work rewrote SyncPathBar menus the same day).

6. The proposed fix is not free. The repo-identity and bundle-chooser options are multi-line cards with a custom .sync-bundle-radio dot, a "Git match"/"Recommended" tag, and a right-hand meta column (revision, resource count, relative time) — native <input type="radio"> in a <fieldset> is a redesign, not a drop-in. And tests/frontend/settings-page.integration.test.tsx:45-46 and tests/frontend/storage-catalog.integration.test.tsx:537 pin the current role="radiogroup"/role="radio" source text, so the "gets it for free" fix breaks the suite.
correction: The five groups deviate from the ARIA APG radio-group authoring pattern (no arrow-key selection, no roving tabIndex, every option a separate Tab stop). They remain fully keyboard operable via Tab + Enter/Space with a visible global focus ring, no WCAG 2.1 AA criterion is failed, and the deviation is a known Medium-priority item from the project's own 2026-08-30 UI audit that has been reviewed and deferred rather than missed.

title: M03 (still open) — three menu-button patterns still open without moving focus, and the path-bar menu closes on Tab
reason:
The finding's headline new claim — that closing the path-bar menu on Tab is a defect — is refuted by the codebase's own documented, uniform design rule and by the ARIA APG. SyncPathBar.tsx:250-254 states it explicitly ("Tab is not menu navigation: the menu steps aside and the bar's own tab order continues wherever the browser takes it"), StorageCatalogPage.tsx:587-590 implements the identical rule, and APG's menu-button pattern specifies exactly this ("Tab: Closes the menu and moves focus to the next element in the tab sequence"). Because every path-bar menu item is tabIndex={-1} (lines 201, 233), those items were never in the tab order, so the Tab handler cannot change where focus lands; the proposed fix would make the widget less conformant, not more.

The claim that the app-actions and agent-setup menus are "worse" fails on a route the finding did not check: neither sets tabIndex={-1} on its items (verified at ProjectSync.tsx:2782-2799 and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2043-2077), so their items sit in the natural tab order directly after the trigger and plain Tab walks into them. The app-actions menu contains exactly one item ("Reload app data"), making Arrow/Home/End vacuous, and its Escape leaves focus on the trigger where it already was — nothing is dropped. The agent-setup menu holds ~1-3 rows on a one-time R2 setup screen.

All three menus are therefore fully keyboard-operable end to end with no trap and no unreachable control; WCAG 2.1.1 is satisfied. The only real residue is APG polish: Enter/Space on a crumb does not auto-focus the first item, costing one extra ArrowDown — the canonical, screen-reader-announced affordance for aria-haspopup="menu". Inside, SyncPathBar is already complete (arrows, Home/End, typeahead, focus return to the opener on Escape at lines 407-413 and on selection via onClose(true)).

The finding is also neither novel nor a regression: it restates docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md:166 (M03) almost verbatim, a standing catalogued item that was never fixed and so cannot have regressed under a prior-regression lens. The codebase is visibly converging on that audit's own prescribed repair — src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts exists as the shared role="menu" contract and StorageCatalogPage.tsx:585 already consumes it including focusMenuEdge(node, "first") on open.
correction: Two of the three claims do not hold. (1) Tab-close is intentional and APG-correct, consistent across all four menu implementations, and harmless because path-bar menu items are tabIndex={-1} and were never in the tab order. (2) The app-actions and agent-setup menus lack Arrow/Home/End but their items are NOT tabIndex={-1}, so Tab reaches them natively; the app-actions menu has a single item, making arrow navigation moot, and its Escape leaves focus undisturbed on the trigger. What remains true and unhandled is far narrower than claimed: (a) SyncPathBar does not move focus to the first item on Enter/Space activation, costing one extra ArrowDown keystroke (APG deviation, no operability loss), and (b) pressing Escape while focus is already inside the agent-setup menu (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1277-1282) unmounts the conditionally-rendered subtree and drops focus to body — a genuine but narrow focus-drop on a first-run R2 setup screen. Neither is a keyboard trap or an unreachable control.

title: M04 (still open) — the two custom focus rings are still translucent and fall below 3:1
reason: The citation is exact and the math reproduces. src/App.css:5215 and 5367 do carry `outline: none`; 5279 and 5450 carry the quoted translucent box-shadows verbatim. Resolving the chain myself — --accent #2a211d light (8150) / #efe7d4 dark (8044), --surface-row #fdf9f3 (8124) / #14120f (8018), and .sync-history-thread-card really is `background: var(--surface-row)` (9839) — the composited rings measure 2.11:1 light / 2.87:1 dark (35%) and 2.72:1 light / 3.94:1 dark (45%), matching the claim. The `outline: none` does suppress the UA :focus-visible ring (author origin beats UA), the global rule at 38-44 covers only button/input/select/summary, and every production instance is a tabbable span (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:599,670,701-706; ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:174,225,234,256; ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:352,402,412,435; StorageCatalogPage.tsx:175,190,712; SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx:130,140). So the low-contrast rings are real and I reproduced them. But two facts the finder missed gut the impact. First, the ring is not the only focus indication: .sync-thread-sync-indicator:focus-visible::after (5274) and .sync-history-thread-metric[data-tooltip]:focus-visible::after (5445) reveal a bordered popover (--surface-popover fill, --accent/--border-strong border, --shadow-popover) on the same pseudo-class, and I checked every call site — every focusable instance carries data-tooltip, while the tooltip-less metrics (SyncOutcomeNotice.tsx:160 and the aria-hidden spacers at ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:239, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:700, ProjectFilesReviewPage.tsx:419) have no tabIndex. So "a keyboard user cannot see where focus is" is false. Second, in the exact scenario named (activity-timeline commit rows) the ring does not paint at all: App.css:9940 `.sync-history-commit > .sync-history-thread-list .sync-thread-sync-indicator { box-shadow: none }` is 0-3-0 and later in source, beating the 0-2-0 :focus-visible rule; the DOM matches (ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1937 li.sync-history-commit > 1970 div.sync-history-thread-list). The declarations stand, the WCAG failure does not.
correction: The two custom focus rings are translucent and, composited on --surface-row, measure 2.11:1 (indicator, light), 2.87:1 (indicator, dark), 2.72:1 (metric, light) and 3.94:1 (metric, dark) — below 3:1 in three of four cases. However, they are not the only focus indication: the same :focus-visible state reveals a bordered tooltip popover (App.css:5274 and 5445) on every focusable instance, since all tabIndex={0} spans carry data-tooltip, so the focused state is identified well above 3:1 and SC 1.4.11 is not failed. Separately, on the activity timeline's commit rows the indicator ring is removed entirely by App.css:9940 (`.sync-history-commit > .sync-history-thread-list .sync-thread-sync-indicator { box-shadow: none }`, specificity 0-3-0, later in source), so the quoted 2.85/2.12 figures do not describe what renders there; the ring only applies in the `flat` lists, the files pages and the catalog. This is a cosmetic weakness in a secondary indicator, not a keyboard-accessibility defect.

title: M05 (still open) — four main views have no h1, no view has aria-current, and no route updates the window title
reason: Citation is exact and all three sub-claims reproduce in source. SettingsPage.tsx:380 is verbatim the quoted <main>, with 381/383/384 matching. grep -c '<h1' returns 0 for SettingsPage.tsx, StorageIndexPage.tsx, storage-catalog/StorageCatalogPage.tsx and storage-catalog/CatalogIndexPage.tsx (the last two live under src/components/storage-catalog/, not the implied path), and no sync-visually-hidden h1 or role="heading" substitutes exist; Settings goes straight to seven h2s at 384/413/428/450/568/664/679. aria-current appears only in SyncPathBar.tsx (317, 488, 537, 571) plus one mockup, so the five primary-nav buttons at ProjectSidebar.tsx:709-751 and every selectable row (803, 866, 964, 1041, 1089) convey selection via className="active" alone. No document.title or setTitle anywhere in src/; index.html:7 and tauri.conf.json:15 are both a static "Mallard". However the claimed impact is overstated on two of three legs, so the finding is real but narrower than framed. (1) Page identity IS programmatically available: all four views render SyncPathBar, whose leaf crumb receives aria-current="page" in all three render branches, inside <ol aria-label> within a top-level <header> banner landmark (SyncPathBar.tsx:463-464), and SettingsPage.tsx:381 is additionally a named region landmark <section aria-label="Settings">. The accurate claim is that heading-level navigation finds no title, not that the user cannot tell which page they are on. (2) The window-title leg is near-inert: tauri.conf.json sets titleBarStyle "Overlay" with hiddenTitle true, so no window title is displayed, and in Tauri v2 document.title does not propagate to the native window title without an explicit setTitle call — the proposed fix's third leg would change nothing as written. (3) Missing h1 is not itself a WCAG AA failure: no SC mandates an h1, 2.4.2 is satisfied by the static title, and 2.4.6 governs headings that exist. The substantive residue is the missing aria-current on nav and sidebar selection — visual-only state, a genuine 1.3.1/4.1.2 gap — which alone does not carry a medium.
correction: Confirmed at src/components/project-sync/SettingsPage.tsx:380 and src/components/project-sync/ProjectSidebar.tsx:709-751. Corrected statement: no <h1> exists in SettingsPage, StorageIndexPage, storage-catalog/StorageCatalogPage or storage-catalog/CatalogIndexPage, so heading-level navigation finds no page title — but page identity is still exposed to assistive technology, since every one of these views renders SyncPathBar whose leaf crumb carries aria-current="page" (SyncPathBar.tsx:488/537/571) inside a named list within a <header> banner landmark, and SettingsPage.tsx:381 adds a named region landmark. The real defect is that the sidebar's five primary-nav buttons and its project/catalog/storage rows convey the current selection through className="active" alone, with no aria-current/aria-selected/aria-pressed — visual-only state (WCAG 1.3.1/4.1.2). The document.title leg should be dropped: the window runs titleBarStyle "Overlay" with hiddenTitle true so no title is displayed, and Tauri v2 does not propagate document.title to the native window title without an explicit setTitle call, making that part of the proposed fix inert.

title: M06 (still open) — R2 setup still blocks Test and Finish without saying which field is wrong
reason: Independently reproduced in source. StorageSettings.tsx:365 is the bucket <input> (value at 366, `required` at 370) — citation verbatim and line-accurate. A grep for aria-invalid across the file returns exactly one hit, line 357 on the S3 API URL; bucket, Account ID, Access Key ID and Secret have no aria-invalid, no aria-describedby, and no error text. storageConfigReady (103-114) gates on isCloudflareR2BucketName + isCloudflareR2AccountId + endpoint?.accountId === accountId as claimed, and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2185 (Test connection) and :2194 (Finish setup) both read `disabled={busy || !!storageConflict || !storageReady || !!runningAction}` with no title (:2098 Save storage repeats the pattern). Two guards I checked for do not exist: the `required` attributes are inert because StorageEditor is not inside a form (the only forms are 1879-1914, closed before the editor mounts at 1935, and 2774-2831), so there is no native validation message; and the lone aria-invalid has no visual style here either — the only App.css rule is `.catalog-fork-drawer input[aria-invalid="true"]` at line 6765, scoped to a different component. The precedent named in the fix is real (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:608, 897-898).
correction: One clause is overstated: "no indication anywhere on the page" ignores the aria-live tally at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2149-2153 (and StorageSettings.tsx:446), which renders "{r2FieldsSet(...)} of 5 set". It does not rescue the case and arguably misdirects: r2FieldsSet (StorageSettings.tsx:138) counts r2S3ApiUrl() as its first slot, which returns "" for an invalid bucket or account ID, so typing a bucket with an underscore blanks the S3 API URL input (the useEffect at line 187 resyncs the draft to the empty derived value) and drops the tally to "4 of 5 set" — a count that never names a field and visually implicates the S3 API URL row rather than the bucket the user actually mistyped. The finding should read: the page surfaces only an unnamed 4-of-5 count, and the one field carrying aria-invalid (S3 API URL, line 357) has no matching CSS in this context, so even that signal is screen-reader-only.

title: M05 (still open) — four main views have no h1, no view has aria-current, and no route updates the window title
reason: Two of the finding's three legs are factually wrong or inert, and the claimed impact does not hold. (1) Page identity IS exposed programmatically on all four views: each renders SyncPathBar first (SettingsPage.tsx:377, CatalogIndexPage.tsx:24, StorageIndexPage.tsx:44, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1381), which is a <header> with <ol aria-label="… path"> whose leaf crumb carries aria-current="page" and the page name (SyncPathBar.tsx:488/537/571 — Settings takes the non-interactive branch at 571). Each <main> also holds a labelled region (aria-label="Settings" / "Catalog resources" / "Storages"). So "no view has aria-current" and "cannot tell which page they landed on" are both false; the source audit doc itself concedes at docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md:184 that "The path bar already marks its current noninteractive leaf." (2) The document.title leg has zero user-visible consequence and its proposed fix is inert: tauri.conf.json sets titleBarStyle "Overlay" with hiddenTitle:true, because the path bar deliberately IS the titlebar (class "sync-pathbar sync-titlebar", data-tauri-drag-region) — a documented design decision — and in a WKWebView-backed Tauri window document.title does not propagate to the native window title anyway. Single window, no tabs. (3) Only the missing aria-current on the sidebar's className="active" nav buttons and rows (ProjectSidebar.tsx:711-744, 803-1089) is real, and it is a redundant-cue gap: the current page is already announced by the path-bar crumb and the labelled main region, so no user is disoriented, and re-activating the nav item you are on is idempotent. It is also a known catalogued item that has survived two subsequent shipped UI passes over these same files.
correction: Narrowed and downgraded: the sidebar's five primary-nav buttons and the selected project/storage/Catalog rows convey selection through className="active" alone, with no aria-current — a small SC 1.3.1 polish worth two lines. The rest of the finding does not hold: all four views expose page identity via the path bar's aria-current="page" leaf crumb plus an aria-labelled main region, and per-view document.title is meaningless in this shell (hiddenTitle:true overlay titlebar, single window, and document.title does not drive the native title in a Tauri/WKWebView window).

title: M06 (still open) — R2 setup still blocks Test and Finish without saying which field is wrong
reason:
The finding's load-bearing claim — "two dead buttons and no indication anywhere on the page of which of five fields is at fault" — is factually wrong about the shipped page, and the remedy it proposes was already reviewed and declined at product level.

1) The page does give live readiness feedback. StorageSettings.tsx:434-437 and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2151-2154 both render `{r2FieldsSet(...)} of 5 set` inside `aria-live="polite"`. r2FieldsSet (StorageSettings.tsx:133-142) counts the DERIVED S3 API URL as one of its five, and r2S3ApiUrl returns "" whenever the bucket fails isCloudflareR2BucketName or the account/endpoint disagree. So the exact scenario described — bucket with an underscore, or a short account ID — moves the counter to "4 of 5 set" the moment it is typed, and announces it.

2) There is also per-keystroke visual feedback tied to the offending field. `s3ApiUrlDraft` re-syncs from `derivedS3ApiUrl` whenever the URL input is not itself focused (StorageSettings.tsx:187-189). Typing an invalid bucket or account ID visibly empties the S3 API URL field at the top of the form and restores it when the value becomes valid. The field the finding says is the only validated one is in fact the form's live verdict surface for the other two.

3) The realistic path does not hand-type these fields. The setup card offers two lanes (StorageSettings.tsx:296-312): the agent lane, where Claude Code/Codex fills the draft through the CLI and the page adopts it, and the manual lane, whose canonical move is pasting the Cloudflare S3 API URL — parseR2S3ApiUrl then fills bucket, account and endpoint together, and that field is the one carrying aria-invalid. Bucket and Account ID are echo/edit surfaces on that path. Realistic data also cannot be invalid the way claimed: Cloudflare enforces the same bucket grammar at creation and mints 32-hex account IDs that are copy-pasted from the dashboard, so an underscore bucket names a bucket that cannot exist.

4) It is a deliberate product decision, not an oversight. A 2026-08-22 redesign proposed exactly this fix — a per-field "verdict line" naming what is wrong, replacing the bucket/account inputs, retitling the tally — and the user declined it: the form and the "of 5" tally were judged good as shipped. The tally is additionally pinned by tests (tests/frontend/storage-settings.integration.test.tsx:497, 533, 917), i.e. it is the codebase's chosen readiness affordance. Format validity is also only a pre-filter; a well-formed but wrong value is caught by "Test connection", which reports a real error.

5) Nothing is lost or blocked. The gate is a pre-commit format check on a five-field form with a live counter; the worst case is a user pausing on a form that says 4 of 5 with the top field blank. That is a polish gap, not a defect, and it is not among the three high-impact accessibility defects the same audit named.
correction: Narrowed accurate statement: the R2 setup form signals incompleteness generically (an aria-live "N of 5 set" tally plus the S3 API URL field emptying) but never names which field is malformed, and the disabled Test/Finish buttons carry no `title` disabled-reason, unlike the codebase's own pushDisabledReason convention (PushResourceWorkspace.tsx:608, 897-898). A screen-reader-only user hears "4 of 5 set" with no per-field aria-invalid/aria-describedby. That is a low-severity enhancement on a path where the values are normally pasted or agent-filled, and the named per-field remedy was reviewed and declined in the 2026-08-22 R2 form redesign.

title: M12 (still open) — 9px and 10px type still carries meaningful content across 91 selectors
reason: Deliberate, documented design that a prior audit already adjudicated and remediated a different way. (1) INTENT IS IN THE FILE: src/App.css:7912-7916 comments the scale as "Root-relative so the OS/webview text-size preference actually lands (WCAG 1.4.4): at the default 16px root every step resolves to the whole pixel it was designed at (9/10/11/12/13/14/17/22/26)." The 9px step is a named design target, not drift. (2) ALREADY HANDLED: the 23-finding UI audit (memory ui-audit-fixes-landed.md) resolved the small-type concern by converting the scale to rem plus `html { font-size: 100% }` (App.css:8198), so OS/webview text-size preference scales every step. That satisfies WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.4 Resize Text — the only applicable criterion, since no WCAG 2.1 AA SC sets a minimum font size. That memory note explicitly records these findings as not to be re-reported. (3) THE TWO CONCRETE CLAIMS ARE MISREAD: App.css:1740 `.sync-bundle-context small` is not "a repo identifier at 9px monospace" — BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:120 renders `Current local repo {currentBundleId.slice(0, 12)}…`, a truncated orientation crumb beneath the storage name at --type-sm, in a dialog whose operable content is the radiogroup of match rows below; nothing must be read or transcribed from it. App.css:2079 `.sync-storage-card .sync-field-name` styles form LABELS ("S3 API URL", "Bucket name" — StorageSettings.tsx:333-396), and the comment immediately above it states the rule: "Field names are chrome micro-labels; the value below them carries the voice" — the value is the <input> at body type, each field also paired with a HelpButton. App.css:1459 `.sync-fact-grid dt` is likewise the uppercase term label, with dd at --type-xs and code at --type-2xs: the scale is applied as a label/value hierarchy, exactly as designed. (4) THE FIX IS ALREADY THE STATE OF THE CODE: walking all 26 --type-3xs sites (985, 1459, 1719, 1727, 1740, 2079, 2144, 2198, 4709, 4882, 4891, 4967, 5328, 6961, 7062, 7220, 7539, 7600, 7635, 7690, 8276, 8357, 8366, 9084, 9121, 10677) yields only badges, monograms, stamps, chips, menu headings, zone labels, day-divider tabs, tool name/status marks, payload labels, tab sub-counts and log type tags. There is no prose, no primary value, and no user-entered field at 3xs. The proposed remedy — "keep 9-10px only for short non-essential marks" — describes what the code already does. (5) USER-APPROVED: the session-detail 3xs stamps (7600/7635/7690) are the C2 Punchcard direction the user selected from a rendered specimen and shipped 2026-09-01 (session-detail-mockup.html, memory session-detail-directions-mockup.md). The selector counts (26 / 65) are accurate, but they measure the consistency of a label tier, not the spread of a defect.
correction: If restated at all, the accurate version is narrow and is a taste call, not a defect: "--type-3xs (9px) is used for label/badge/stamp micro-type in 26 selectors; a few of them (.sync-bundle-context small, .sync-bundle-choice-meta small) set truncated monospace ids, where 11px would read more easily." It is not an accessibility or layout-responsive defect — the rem scale plus html{font-size:100%} already satisfies WCAG 1.4.4, no WCAG 2.1 AA criterion sets a minimum font size, and no prose or operable value is set below --type-md.

title: M08 (still open) — three entry-failure states render an error with no Retry, and the Files scan error hides its own rescan
reason:
Citation is verbatim and the line numbers are exact (ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:301 error branch, :274 onRescan prop, :350 success-only Rescan button), but the two load-bearing claims do not survive tracing.

(1) "The Files scan error hides its own rescan / the only way to retry is the unlabelled refresh glyph." The page installs its refresh into the path bar unconditionally: ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:462-467 runs `onHeaderModelChange?.({refreshing: loading, onRefresh: () => setScanEpoch(e => e + 1)})` on mount and whenever `loading` flips — it has no early return and is not gated on success, so it re-runs when the failed scan's `.finally` sets loading false (:454-456). ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2563-2568 turns that model into `viewRefresh` with `label: "Rescan project files"`, and :2592-2609 renders it with BOTH `title={viewRefresh.label}` and `aria-label={viewRefresh.label}` — it is not unlabelled; only its visible text is omitted, which is what the source comment at :2554 means. It is enabled in the error state (`disabled={viewRefresh.refreshing}`, refreshing=false) and clicking it bumps `scanEpoch`, the exact same handler the in-page Rescan calls. The error state is only reachable when `activeStorageId` is non-null (the effect returns early otherwise, :445-449), which guarantees `workspaceStorage` is non-null (:1446-1448) and therefore that `syncPathActions` renders. So the failure has a working, accessibly-named, view-scoped retry by design — the page explicitly delegates it ("The bar's one refresh follows the view; this page's is the rescan", :460).

(2) The AddCatalogScopeWorkspace sub-claim is materially wrong. AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:344-355 is NOT an early return — the `{error && <Notice …>}` is rendered inline at the bottom of the form body, with the whole form still mounted above it and the footer below it (:357-377: Cancel and "Add resource"). The mount failure (:66-82) only leaves `capabilities`/`profiles` empty; kind selection comes from the local `CATALOG_KINDS` constant, and `chooseKind` calls `setError(null)` (:112), so the error is not even sticky. The user is not stranded and can retry by Cancel + reopen.

Only the third site holds: ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:541-560 (`if (!draft)`) really is an early return with a Notice and no control — but even there the sidebar stays mounted (ProjectSync.tsx renders ProjectSidebar outside `sync-workspace`), so it is a missing in-place retry, not a dead end. That is a low-severity polish item on one of three cited sites, not a medium "three entry-failure states with no retry" finding.
correction: Narrowed and downgraded: of the three cited sites, only ProjectSetupWorkspace.tsx:541-560 (`if (!draft)`) genuinely lacks any in-place control on a draft-load failure — adding a Retry there is a reasonable polish fix. ProjectFilesActivityPage's error branch has a live, accessibly-labelled retry ("Rescan project files", title + aria-label) in the path bar, wired by the unconditional header-model effect at :462-467, so an in-page Rescan button would be a convenience duplicate rather than a fix for a dead end. AddCatalogScopeWorkspace's error Notice renders inline inside a fully interactive form (Cancel / Add resource still present) and is cleared by `chooseKind`, so it is not an entry-failure dead end at all; the only accurate part there is the absence of an explicit loading state for the in-flight provider listing.

title: M13 (still open) — clipped root overflow, a fixed 220px sidebar floor and fixed-pixel control heights still break text-resize reflow
reason: Citations are accurate but the impact chain is broken at every load-bearing link. (1) The central claim — "anything that outgrows the viewport is unreachable rather than scrollable… no scroll path out because of the root clip" — is false. src/App.css:1135-1146 defines `.sync-main { flex:1; min-height:120px; overflow:auto; scrollbar-gutter:stable; }`, and every workspace page renders as `<main className="sync-main …">` inside `.sync-workspace` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2735, SettingsPage.tsx:380, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1506/1663/1872, CatalogIndexPage.tsx:42, StorageIndexPage.tsx:61, AddCatalogScopeWorkspace.tsx:199). No later rule removes that overflow (8477 sets only color; 5885 keeps overflow-y:auto; 9034 only padding). The nav rail scrolls too: App.css:8689-8697 `.sync-primary-nav { min-height:0; overflow-y:auto }` with the comment "no destination the handle pushes out of view becomes unreachable." The root/.sync-app clip is the standard shell pattern that delegates scrolling inward — App.css:5883 literally calls the workspace "the only vertical scroll owner." The proposed fix ("give .sync-app a scroll path — overflow:auto on the workspace column") is already shipped. (2) The trigger is unreachable: src-tauri/tauri.conf.json sets no `zoomHotkeysEnabled` (Tauri v2 default false) and no Rust code touches zoom, so 400% page zoom is not available; and page zoom scales px boxes and rem text by the same factor, so it cannot clip a 25px box holding a 0.625rem label even if enabled. Nothing sets a responsive `html { font-size }`, and neither WKWebView nor WebView2 rebases rem off an OS text-size setting, so the "200% OS text setting" path does not exist. The ~27px-in-25px figure derives from a scaling mode this shell cannot enter. (3) The 220px sidebar is not unconditional: availableProjectSidebarWidth() (ProjectSync.tsx:198-203) clamps against MIN_PROJECT_WORKSPACE_WIDTH=580, and sidebarVisible (ProjectSync.tsx:401/545) drives `.sync-app.sidebar-hidden` (App.css:839-840), which removes the rail and its resizer; tauri.conf.json minWidth:800 means the window never reaches a width where the rail strands the workspace. Verified-true citations: App.css:7-11, 804-811, 8708-8720, 2071, 10856; ProjectSync.tsx:189.
correction: The fixed `height` values on `.sync-primary-nav button` (App.css:8709) and `.sync-segmented button` (App.css:2071) are real and would be more robust as `min-height`, but this is a hardening preference with no reachable failure mode: the shell has no page-zoom hotkeys, no responsive root font-size, and the workspace column (`.sync-main`, overflow:auto) plus the nav rail (overflow-y:auto) already provide the scroll path the finding says is missing.

title: M12 (still open) — 9px and 10px type still carries meaningful content across 91 selectors
reason: Independently reproduced every element of the finding. src/App.css:7916 is verbatim `--type-3xs: 0.5625rem;` with 7917-7920 matching the quoted block exactly. Each type token is defined exactly once (single grep hit per token) — no theme block, media query, or later :root redefines them, and no more-specific rule overrides the cited selectors (the second `.sync-fact-grid` rule at 10572 sets only border-color/border-radius; the `.session-detail-tool-name` variants at 7608-7610 set only color). The root is `html { font-size: 100%; }` (8198-8199) with no px override, no zoom in tauri.conf.json or index.html, and no -webkit-text-size-adjust, so at the default root --type-3xs resolves to 9px and --type-2xs to 10px — which the file's own comment at 7913-7915 states explicitly ("9/10/11/12/13/14/17/22/26"). Body is `font-size: var(--type-md)` at 8204, inside the cited 8203-8205 range = 13px. Counts confirmed: `var(--type-3xs)` on 26 lines, `var(--type-2xs)` on 65 = 91. All spot-cited selectors exist verbatim (1459 .sync-fact-grid dt uppercase 9px, 1727 .sync-bundle-choice-meta small, 1740 .sync-bundle-context small mono 9px, 2079 inside .sync-storage-card .sync-field-name). The repo-identifier claim is real: BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:120 renders `<small>Current local repo {currentBundleId.slice(0, 12)}…</small>` into the 9px mono --text-3 rule. Found no guard, fallback, cascade override, or call-site condition that rescues it.
correction: At App.css:7916-7917 the scale sets --type-3xs to 9px and --type-2xs to 10px at the default 16px root, and those tokens appear on 26 and 65 declaration lines respectively. Of the 26 --type-3xs sites, roughly two-thirds are uppercase letter-spaced micro-labels or badges (.sync-eyebrow, .sync-draft-badge, .sync-settings-flag, .sync-provider-monogram, .sync-history-preserved-badge, the grouped rule at 8271-8276) that the finding's own fix accepts at that size; about 8-10 carry text a user must actually read — .sync-bundle-context small (App.css:1740, 9px monospace --text-3 for a 12-char repo id from BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:120), .sync-bundle-choice-copy span (:1719), .session-detail-tool-name (:7600), .sync-fact-grid dt (:1459), .sync-r2-menu-text small (:2198), .log-type (:10677). App.css:2079 is `.sync-storage-card .sync-field-name`, storage-card field names generally rather than R2-specific. The scale is rem-based with `html { font-size: 100% }` deliberately kept so the OS/webview text-size preference scales the whole ladder, so WCAG 1.4.4 is met; this is a default-state legibility concern, not a standards violation.

title: M08 (still open) — three entry-failure states render an error with no Retry, and the Files scan error hides its own rescan
reason: The load-bearing claim is false on the actual code. (1) ProjectFilesActivityPage: the retry is present and labelled. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2563-2568 derives a view-scoped `viewRefresh`; on the files view it renders a path-bar button carrying BOTH `title` and `aria-label` = "Rescan project files" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2594-2601), wired to `filesActivityHeader.onRefresh`. That header is published by an effect keyed on `[loading, onHeaderModelChange]` (ProjectFilesActivityPage.tsx:461-467) which never reads `error`, so on a failed scan it re-runs with `refreshing: false` and the button is enabled. Its handler is `() => setScanEpoch((epoch) => epoch + 1)` — byte-for-byte the same action as the `onRescan` prop passed to the view (line 476). The finding calls this an "unlabelled refresh glyph"; the source comment's word "unlabelled" means no visible text, not no accessible name. The retry therefore exists, sits one row above the error box, is discoverable by tooltip, and is announced to screen readers. Zero user-visible consequence. (2) AddCatalogScopeWorkspace: the evidence is misdescribed. The error Notice is NOT an early return replacing the view — it renders inline inside the form body, with the kind picker, provider/profile selects, Browse, and the footer's `Cancel` and `Add resource` buttons all still on screen. The in-code comment reasons about this case deliberately ("The mount listing writes here too, and a Catalog page that could not load its providers is worth the same rung"). The failure is also near-unreachable: `list_catalog_capabilities` is `Ok(StorageCatalogService::capabilities())` (src-tauri/src/storage_catalog/resource_commands.rs:28-30), a compile-time constant matrix from `capability_matrix()` (adapters.rs:251-272) that cannot return Err; the sibling `list_catalog_resource_profiles` is a local ~/.mallard read whose failure means the whole app is broken. The "no initial loading state" sub-claim is not a defect either: both are in-process Tauri IPC resolving in a tick, the kind options come from the local `CATALOG_KINDS` constant, and the provider select is only meaningful after the user clicks a kind — a skeleton would flash. (3) ProjectSetupWorkspace: the branch already HAS a loading state (`"Loading setup draft…"` with a spinner, line 559), and the dominant reachable message is `"This setup draft no longer exists."` (line 273), set when `getSetupDraft` resolves null — a Retry there re-fetches null forever and would be an actively misleading affordance. The exception path needs an unreadable local config. The user is not trapped: ProjectSidebar renders alongside the entire setup flow (ProjectSync.tsx:3643-3650) with `drafts`, `onSelectDraft` and `onDiscardDraft`. Finally, the precedent the finding cites argues against it: SettingsPage.tsx:296 attaches Retry conditionally — `action: stats ? undefined : (<Retry/>)` — i.e. only when the mount failure left the view with nothing AND no other control offers that action. That is this codebase's articulated rule, and all three sites satisfy its escape clause (path-bar Rescan, still-rendered form footer, persistent sidebar).
correction: The accurate residue is a cosmetic co-location nit, not a state-coverage gap: on ProjectFilesActivityPage the scan-error branch could repeat the Rescan control inside the Notice rather than relying on the path bar's view-scoped "Rescan project files" button directly above it, which fires the identical `setScanEpoch` handler and is enabled during the error. The claims that the retry is unavailable, that the path-bar glyph is unlabelled, that AddCatalogScopeWorkspace's error replaces its form, and that ProjectSetupWorkspace's draft-load branch lacks a loading state are each false against the source.

title: M13 (still open) — clipped root overflow, a fixed 220px sidebar floor and fixed-pixel control heights still break text-resize reflow
reason:
The finding's three pillars each fail against the actual files.

(1) "No scroll path out because of the root clip" is FALSE. The root/`.sync-app` clip is the desktop app-shell frame, not a trap: the workspace content column `.sync-main` (src/App.css:1135-1145) is `overflow: auto` with `scrollbar-gutter: stable` and a `min-height: 120px` floor, and App.css:4420 documents it as the scroller for every workspace screen ("The page scrolls the way every other workspace screen does: .sync-main is the scroller"). The sidebar nav is likewise `overflow-y: auto` (App.css:8689-8697) with the comment "Shortening the head clips the nav, so it scrolls — no destination the handle pushes out of view becomes unreachable." There are 11 `overflow: auto` scroll containers. Nothing becomes unreachable.

(2) The 220px sidebar is an engineered constraint, not an oversight, and it is user-managed. MIN_PROJECT_SIDEBAR_WIDTH 220 (ProjectSync.tsx:189) + MIN_PROJECT_WORKSPACE_WIDTH 580 (ProjectSync.tsx:191) = 800, which is exactly the Tauri window `minWidth` (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json). The clamp at ProjectSync.tsx:200-201 guarantees the workspace never drops below 580px. The finding says a fix must "not rely on the user finding the toggle" — but there is a visible `.sync-sidebar-toggle`, a drag resizer with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home keyboard support (ProjectSync.tsx:720-722), AND a Cmd/Ctrl+B shortcut (ProjectSync.tsx:553-566), the universal convention.

(3) The trigger mechanism does not exist, and the proposed repair contradicts documented intent. No zoom is wired anywhere in src-tauri or the frontend; `zoomHotkeysEnabled` is absent from tauri.conf.json (false by default in Tauri v2) and WKWebView magnification is off by default on macOS, so "400% zoom" is not a reachable state. macOS has no global text-size setting that scales WKWebView page content, and WebView2 does not apply the Windows text slider to web content — and any real zoom scales px and rem uniformly, so the px-vs-rem divergence the finding depends on never materializes. Separately, `height: 38px` on `.sync-primary-nav button` is load-bearing: App.css:8705-8707 says "Fixed, not shrinkable... so the nav would never scroll and the handle's floor — measured off one row — would drift," and `headHeightRange` in ProjectSidebar.tsx:119-134 literally measures `nav.querySelector("button").offsetHeight` as the head's minimum. Converting it to `min-height` as proposed would break the resizer floor.

Even hypothetically the consequence is overstated: `.sync-segmented button` (25px / `--type-2xs` = 0.625rem, line-height 1.35) needs a root font-size above ~29.6px (185%) before the line box exceeds the box, and neither `<button>` nor `.sync-segmented` clips (`overflow: visible`), so glyphs would overflow the pill visibly rather than disappear. The codebase already applies `min-height` exactly where growth matters (`.sync-storage-card > header` min-height 50px, `.sync-backend-banner .btn` min-height 27px, `.sync-theme-button` min-height 32px, `.sync-main` min-height 120px), and App.css:8196-8199 deliberately keeps `html { font-size: 100% }` "never a px override — so the rem-based type scale follows the OS/webview text-size setting," i.e. text-resize support is an intentional, implemented decision.

Provenance: this is a verbatim re-report of M13 from docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md:246, whose own wording is speculative ("at high risk", "text *can* outgrow controls") and which reports no observed clip despite the auditor having captured a narrow-workspace screenshot (docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/screenshots/15-narrow-workspace.png). Being "still open" after a triage pass in which sibling findings from the same audit were worked is evidence of deliberate deprioritization, not of an unnoticed defect.
correction: The only defensible residue is a hygiene note, not a defect: a handful of text-bearing controls use fixed `height` where `min-height` would be more tolerant of future type-scale changes. It is latent only — there is no reachable trigger (no zoom is wired, and neither target platform's OS text setting scales webview content), no clipping outcome (the containers are `overflow: visible`), and no unreachable content (`.sync-main` and `.sync-primary-nav` both scroll). Two of the named controls are additionally locked by design: `.sync-primary-nav button`'s fixed height is the measured floor for the sidebar head resizer.

title: M11 (still open) — the session title lives only in the path bar and truncates to 6 characters at the narrow floor
reason:
Refuted on three independent grounds.

(1) THE REGRESSION CLAIM IS FACTUALLY FALSE. I diffed the container-query blocks in `git show HEAD:src/App.css` against the working tree: the clamps are byte-identical (`max-width: 7ch` link / `9ch` leaf+section at the 760px step; `6ch` at the 640px step). `src/components/project-sync/session-detail/SessionDetailHeader.tsx` has NO working-tree diff at all (`git diff HEAD --` is empty; last touched in 9d6964e, well before the retheme). The retheme changed neither the clamps nor the header, so "the retheme made this worse than the prior audit found it" is unsupported. This is a verbatim restatement of M11 from <repo>/docs/ui-audit/2026-08-30/UI_AUDIT.md:230, which was raised, read, and deliberately not acted on — nothing regressed.

(2) IT IS AN EXPLICIT, USER-CHOSEN DESIGN DECISION, PINNED BY A TEST. "The bar owns the title" is direction 1, picked by the user from session-header-mockup.html and recorded in memory (session-header-bar-owns-title.md). Three independent source comments restate the rationale: SessionDetailHeader.tsx:36-39 ("stated once, and sticky, so it survives scrolling in a way an in-page poster never did"), ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2456-2459 ("The leaf is the page's one visible title... The words stay in the tooltip and in hidden text for readers"), and App.css:6860. <repo>/tests/frontend/session-detail.integration.test.tsx:262 pins the exact markup: `assert.match(html, /<h1 id="session-detail-heading" class="sync-visually-hidden" tabindex="-1">Build provider-neutral session detail<\/h1>/)`. The proposed fix (drop `sync-visually-hidden`) would fail a gate written specifically to hold this decision. The truncation ladder is equally engineered, with measured notes on which crumb yields first and why (App.css:2561, 2608-2615, 2624-2630, 3010-3016, 3042-3046), and the section crumb is deliberately dropped on session open "giving the title the width it needs" (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2453-2455).

(3) THE 6ch WORST CASE IS ESSENTIALLY UNREACHABLE, AND IS MITIGATED WHERE IT EXISTS. `MIN_PROJECT_WORKSPACE_WIDTH = 580` (ProjectSync.tsx:191) auto-clamps the sidebar as the window narrows, so the 640px container step needs a window between the 800px hard minimum (tauri.conf.json) and ~860px — i.e. the user dragged the window to within ~60px of the enforced floor. At the shipped default (1100x720, sidebar 298px) the pathbar is ~800px, above BOTH steps, and the leaf gets `max-width: 30cqi` ≈ 240px, roughly 30 characters. Even at the floor: the crumb carries `title={title · provider · Active}` (full text on hover), the sr-only h1 carries the full title for screen readers and is the focus landing, and the sidebar is drag-resizable (220-560px, persisted, Home key snaps to min) and can be hidden entirely — both directly widen the bar. The icon-only actions carry `aria-label` and `title`, and reuse the activity rows' glyph vocabulary verbatim (SessionDetailHeader.tsx:14-16), so they are the same marks the user already learned on the list page.
correction: Not a regression and not a defect: the leaf-crumb clamps and the visually-hidden h1 are unchanged from HEAD and are a documented, test-pinned design decision ("the bar owns the title"). The most that can honestly be said is a legibility nit: between an 800px and ~860px window the leaf label is capped at 6ch, with the full title reachable only via the crumb's tooltip and the sr-only h1.

title: M11 (still open) — the session title lives only in the path bar and truncates to 6 characters at the narrow floor
reason: Citation is verbatim and the line number is exact: SessionDetailHeader.tsx:47-52 renders the h1 with className="sync-visually-hidden", and lines 95-111 render icon-only action buttons whose labels live only in title/aria-label. I traced the cascade independently. The session leaf crumb is pushed with no menu and no onActivate (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2456-2479), so SyncPathBar.tsx:565-578 renders the non-interactive span branch whose children are [leading mark span, label span] — the label span really is `> span:last-child`, so App.css:3027-3030 (max-width:9ch) and 3051-3054 (max-width:6ch) do apply to the title, with `.sync-path-crumb > span` (2644-2649) supplying overflow:hidden + ellipsis. The container query is live (`container: sync-pathbar / inline-size`, App.css:2535); MIN_PROJECT_SIDEBAR_WIDTH=220 (ProjectSync.tsx:189) and minWidth:800 (tauri.conf.json:24) put the bar under the 640px step at the floor. No rule un-hides the h1 (sync-visually-hidden defined once at App.css:4806) and SessionDetailPage renders the title nowhere visible, so the crumb genuinely is the page's only visible name. What I could NOT confirm is the regression framing: `git show HEAD` has byte-identical 9ch/6ch container-query blocks and an identical visually-hidden h1, and the leaf label is not in the --font-display selector lists, so the retheme neither introduced nor worsened this. The finding also omits three mitigations: the crumb's title tooltip carries "title · provider · Active", the label has a min-width:5ch floor so it never vanishes, and the cap only engages below roughly a 1086px window at the default 298px sidebar — the shipped 1100x720 default shows the title in full. The truncation is also an explicitly documented tradeoff in the CSS comments (App.css:2606-2615, 3009-3015, 3041-3045), not an oversight.
correction: The mechanism holds, but it is not a retheme regression: the 9ch/6ch leaf caps and the visually-hidden h1 are byte-identical at HEAD (789eea5), so nothing in the uncommitted retheme changed this. Correct statement: "The session page's only visible title is the path bar leaf crumb; the pre-existing pathbar container queries cap it at 9ch below 760px and 6ch below 640px (with a 5ch floor), so at the app's 800px minimum window the title reads as ~6 characters plus an ellipsis, recoverable only via the crumb's tooltip. Truncation begins around a 1086px window with the default 298px sidebar; the 1100x720 default window shows the title in full." The pathbar's content box at the floor is ~552px, not 580px (the 580 in the CSS comment ignores the bar's 28px horizontal padding).

title: M14 (still open) — delayed loading content is still a named region, never announced
reason:
Refuted as a deliberate, three-times-documented design decision with no independent user-visible consequence.

1. INTENT IS EXPLICIT IN THE CODE. `src/components/LoadingScaffold.tsx:9-13` (docblock): "The container is a quiet named region: first paint announces nothing (the refresh paths that need politeness carry their own visually hidden lines), and every bone is aria-hidden." The role="region" at line 125 is the deliberate output of that rule, not an oversight.

2. THE PROPOSED FIX WAS ALREADY TRIED AND REVERTED AS A BUG. `src/components/project-sync/ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1817-1822`, immediately above the scaffold call: "Not a status message: the scaffold is what the view renders with while its first read is in flight... On the one path that reaches it from a user action — picking a branch, which drops the list — the visually hidden line above is already announcing the refresh politely. Claiming a live region here only made a screen reader say it twice." That polite line exists at `ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1636` (`refreshStatus`) and `:1789` (`<span className="sync-visually-hidden" role="status">`). Adding the proposed sibling role="status" re-introduces a double announcement on the one realistic user-initiated path.

3. THE PROJECT RULE IS WRITTEN DOWN. The loading-system plan states: "Never gate a live region behind the scaffold; refresh announcements stay on their own visually-hidden lines." The layered architecture is: scaffold = first-read geometry (quiet), NoticeZone = writes, per-page visually hidden role="status" = refreshes.

4. THE WCAG READING IN THE FINDING IS WRONG, AND THE CODEBASE'S IS RIGHT. SC 4.1.3 covers messages added to an already-rendered view without a change of context; content a view renders WITH is out of scope. The same reasoning is spelled out at `ProjectActivityPage.tsx:1770-1778` for the notice zone ("WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 says content already present when the view renders is not a status message. It gets a named region instead."). A named region carrying a visible "Loading project activity…" caption is exactly the conforming treatment.

5. THE SHAPE IS PINNED BY AN EXISTING TEST. `tests/frontend/storage-catalog.integration.test.tsx:317-324` asserts role="region", aria-hidden, `{label}…`, and the 150ms gate as "The recipe's contract: a quiet named region, bones hidden from assistive tech". The proposed change breaks a green assertion.

6. THE aria-busy HALF HAS NO OBSERVABLE EFFECT. aria-busy on a non-live container is inert in NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver — it suppresses live-region churn, it does not announce anything. The five existing uses (`SessionDetailTimeline.tsx:106`, `SessionDetailToolCall.tsx:177`, `ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2598/3199`, `ProjectActivityPage.tsx:398`) sit on containers that DO update in place, which is the case where it matters; the scaffold is replaced wholesale, which is not.

7. THE CLAIMED IMPACT IS BORROWED FROM M05, NOT NOVEL. "a user gets no signal that anything happened" is the route-change/focus finding restated. If M05 is fixed (focus moves on route change), the reader lands in the region and reads the caption immediately. Nothing here fails independently.

8. REALISTIC EXPOSURE IS SMALL. The 150ms gate (line 117) plus the observation and timeline disk caches mean warm loads never render the scaffold at all; when it does render, the outcome is a named, caption-bearing region, not silence.
correction: Not a defect. LoadingScaffold's quiet named region is the codebase's documented treatment of first-read content under WCAG SC 4.1.3, and per-page visually hidden role="status" lines already cover the user-initiated refresh paths. At most, a cosmetic nicety: nothing here is independently actionable, and the proposed sibling role="status" would restore a previously diagnosed double-announcement on the branch-switch path.

title: M07 (still open) — "repo" names both a Git repository and a Mallard identity in one sentence, and Settings swaps thread for session mid-description
reason:
Refuted: this is a deliberate, documented, test-pinned terminology decision with no user-visible consequence, and half the Settings claim is factually wrong about the actual file.

1) The wording is spec'd copy, not an oversight. docs/PLAN_REPO_BUNDLE_CONVERGENCE.md:123 states the designed text in bold: "This storage already has this repository in another repo ('HorrorGame', 2 items, updated …) — Connect." That is verbatim the sentence at BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:106 the finding calls unparseable. That plan section (D3, reason "sibling") is the origin of this dialog path.

2) The copy is locked by a test. tests/frontend/repo-bundle-convergence.integration.test.tsx:85 asserts /Connect to this repository('|')s repo/. The string is pinned on purpose, and the finding is itself flagged "still open" from a prior pass — the maintainer has seen it and kept the wording.

3) The distinction is load-bearing and scaffolded in situ. src/terminology.ts translates the protocol noun bundle -> user-facing repo; "repository" is reserved for the Git checkout. In the dialog the reader gets the frame immediately: eyebrow "Repo identity", context line "Current local repo <id>…", each row printing a bundle_id + "rev N" + resource count, and notices at lines 65/71 saying "Git fingerprint" explicitly. The sentence is never read in isolation.

4) Exposure is near-zero and the path is non-destructive. reason "sibling" fires only on the second-machine convergence path (ProjectSync.tsx:3824) for a link with no published head that has a same-fingerprint sibling. The standing notice states the blast radius ("Connecting changes only Mallard metadata…"), "Not now" is always available, and the primary button reads "Connect and review Pull". Nobody is misrouted or loses data over the noun.

Traced control flow for kind==="s3" creation:
1. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1573 `saveEditedStorage` → `onSaveStorage(...)`, wired to `saveInlineStorage` (ProjectSync.tsx:3077, bound at :3839).

A fresh setup always has `storageBaseline === null` (set null on both `mode === "create"` at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1008 and `mode === "resume-draft"` at :1029), so `needsVerifiedR2Save` (ProjectSync.tsx:3084) is true and the save goes through `projectSyncApi.upsertR2Storage`, never the generic config save.

5. Belt-and-braces backstop in Rust: `require_verified_r2_changes` / `VERIFIED_R2_MESSAGE` (src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:1238-1296) rejects any R2 credential change that tries to enter schema-1 config through the generic save path.

So the "identical gate" the finding flags is deliberate and documented: the code comment above `testStorageConnection` (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1629-1631) reads "The advisory twin of Create: same gate, same probe, no commit." The scenario "press Finish, get a storage that looks configured in the Storages index, and only discover the failure at the first Push" is not reachable — an unverified R2 storage cannot reach the config at all.

Two secondary inaccuracies: `storageTestVerified` IS consulted in the footer (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2156-2161 renders a "Connection verified" status chip), and on success the save notifies `Connected <name>` (ProjectSync.tsx:3148), so the user does get a connection verdict from Finish.

What survives is a pure copy preference — no sentence explicitly says the Test button is optional — which is not a state-coverage defect and carries none of the claimed consequences.
correction: No defect. Finish setup runs the same live capability probe as Test connection (crates/mallard-application/src/storage_setup.rs:927 `upsert_r2_storage_with_probe` → `probe.verify` gates the `transact_config` commit), so an unverified or mistyped R2 credential can never be committed; Test connection is an explicitly advisory commit-free twin.
