title: M09 (still open) — R2 setup still finishes without a successful connection test, and never says the test is optional
reason:
REFUTED — "Finish setup" already performs the identical live connection probe, and refuses to commit when it fails. The two buttons sharing `!storageReady` is not the whole story; the divergence is on the backend.

Trace:
1. `src/components/project-sync/ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1596` — Finish calls `onSaveStorage(...)`, wired to `saveInlineStorage` (`src/components/project-sync/ProjectSync.tsx:3077`).
2. `ProjectSync.tsx:3084` — `const needsVerifiedR2Save = storage.kind === "s3" && (!expectedBaseline || !sameR2Connection(...))`. A new R2 storage (the exact case in the claim) always takes this branch and goes through `projectSyncApi.upsertR2Storage(...)`, not the generic config save.
3. `src-tauri/src/project_sync/service.rs:1252` — `require_verified_r2_changes` doc: R2 credentials "enter the schema-1 config only through a focused operation that completes the exact capability probe. The generic config save ... cannot create, replace, or convert an R2 connection and bypass verification."
4. `crates/mallard-application/src/storage_setup.rs:927` `upsert_r2_storage_with_probe` → `probe_r2_upsert` (line 864). At line 913: `probe.verify(pending.storage(), setup_id.as_str()).and_then(|()| on_verified(...))` — the config transaction that commits the storage lives *inside* `on_verified` and only runs after the probe succeeds.
5. `storage_setup.rs:512` documents `test_r2_storage` as "the exact upsert pipeline ... minus the config transaction." Test connection is upsert minus commit — not a stronger check that Finish skips.

So a mistyped secret cannot produce a saved-but-broken storage. `upsertR2Storage` returns an error, `saveInlineStorage` surfaces it, `saveEditedStorage` returns early, and the comment at `ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1618-1620` confirms the typed secret is deliberately retained "for correction and retry." The claimed impact — "a storage that looks configured in the Storages index, discovered only at the first Push" — cannot occur; the storage is never written.

The remaining two sub-claims are also weak:
- "Nothing consults storageTestVerified": correct but by design. The code comment at `ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1629` names the button "The advisory twin of Create: same gate, same probe, no commit." Identical gating is the stated intent — the receipt (`Connection verified`, line 2156) is a convenience so the user can validate fields before spending a commit, and the invalidation-on-edit half was implemented deliberately.
- "No copy tells the user the test is optional": the app says so twice in user-facing text — the post-agent-handoff status at `ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:365` ("Review or edit them, optionally test the connection, then finish setup yourself") and the copied agent instruction at line 402 ("I will ... optionally test the connection, and personally click Finish setup").

Implementing the proposed fix would be a regression: gating Finish on `storageTestVerified` would add a mandatory extra round-trip to the bucket before every save, and a "warning beside Finish" would tell the user something untrue about the risk they are taking.
correction: The only true residue is cosmetic: on the purely manual R2 path (no agent handoff) the footer does not state in words that Test connection is optional, while Finish silently performs the same probe. That is a UX-copy nicety, not a state-coverage defect — there is no reachable state in which an unverified R2 connection is committed.

title: Path-bar switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard — every route into it closes the menu
reason:
The mechanics are roughly right but the impact is not. Nothing is unreachable and nothing is blocked.

1) The function the field serves is already keyboard-operable, in the same component. `<repo>/src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:274-300` implements ArrowUp/Down (wrapping), Home/End via `moveMenuFocus` (`<repo>/src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts:22-34`), and a purpose-built typeahead — 500ms buffer, repeated-first-letter cycling, longer prefixes narrowing from the focused row. With an empty `query`, `matches()` (line 175-177) passes every item, so arrows and typeahead reach all N targets. "Jump to the project named X by typing its name" is available from the keyboard; the search pill is a filter accelerator over an already-navigable list, not a gate. WCAG 2.1.1 is about functionality, not about every redundant control.

2) The Tab contract is deliberate and documented in three places: the code comment at line 256-257 ("Tab is not menu navigation: the menu steps aside and the bar's own tab order continues"), the ARIA APG menu-button pattern it implements, and the design memo (`switcher-menu-directions-mockup.md`, which records the shipped rule as "ArrowDown/Up step into the list, Enter activates the first .target, typeahead skips the input"). The proposed fix changes that contract for every menu in the bar, including the ⋯ overflow that has no input at all.

3) Screen-reader users are unaffected. An `<input>` is not a permitted child of `role="menu"`; in menu-reading mode AT exposes only the menuitem family, so the field is not announced-but-unusable — there is no trap. The only affected persona is a sighted keyboard-only user, and for them the keystrokes still produce the intended result with visible feedback: typeahead moves focus to the matching row and `button:focus-visible` (App.css:38-43) paints a 2px outline on it.

4) Two pieces of the evidence overstate the case. The file has an explicit `const typing = event.target instanceof HTMLInputElement` branch (line 262-273) that routes characters to the input and lets only ArrowUp/Down/Enter through — the two mechanisms were separated on purpose, not conflated. And `.sync-path-menu-search:focus-visible` (App.css:3202) is not styling for an impossible state: it is a local override of the global `input:focus-visible` rule, and the field is focused on every mouse click, which is the interaction the design was drawn for.

5) The trigger is rare. `searchable` counts only labelled "Switch to" groups against `SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR = 6`, so it needs 7+ projects in one workspace, 7+ storages, or 7+ catalog scopes. The view switcher has exactly one other target (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2537-2544) and storage switchers list 1-3 in practice; only a heavy user of the project switcher ever paints the box at all.

Residual worth a polish ticket, not a medium a11y defect: the accelerator is pointer-only, and a text input inside `role="menu"` is a pattern smell. One-line fix if wanted — focus the input rather than the first menuitem in `focusMenuOption` (line 422-431) when the menu is `searchable`, since the exit path from the field (arrows out, Enter on first target) is already written.
correction: The switcher's search pill can only be focused with a pointer, so keyboard users lose the filter accelerator — but not access: arrows, Home/End and the menu's own typeahead reach and activate every switch target, and the field is not exposed to screen readers inside role="menu". Cosmetic/polish, only on switchers with 7+ targets.

title: Path-bar switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard — every route into it closes the menu
reason: Independently reproduced in source. src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:328-337 renders the search input verbatim as quoted, with no autoFocus and no role attribute. menuKeyboard.ts's MENU_OPTION_SELECTOR is only '[role="menuitem"], [role="menuitemcheckbox"], [role="menuitemradio"]', so menuOptions() excludes the input — focusMenuOption (line 422-430) and moveMenuFocus can never focus it, and the file contains no other .focus() call that could. Every menuitem is tabIndex={-1}, making the input the only tabbable node inside an open menu, but it precedes the lists in DOM order, so only Shift+Tab from the first menuitem could reach it — and the menu-root onKeyDown at line 258 intercepts key === "Tab" without checking shiftKey and calls onClose(false). The three opener handlers (516, 551, 618) do the same. Closing genuinely removes it from tab order: hidden={!open} (line 254) plus .sync-path-menu[hidden]{display:none} at App.css:3080, with no later override (only .sync-path-menu.switcher{width:380px} at 3158). I checked the one theoretical escape — Shift+Tab backward from crumb.scope's BranchPicker, whose crumb has no menu so line 550 returns before the Tab branch — but focus can only get there via mouse or a Tab press that closes the menu first. The overflow menu is passed no header (630-638) so searchable is always false there. Trigger condition confirmed: ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2432 maps otherProjects into a "Switch to" group (targetCount = totalProjects - 1, so searchable at 7 projects) and ~2296 does the same for otherStorages. No test references sync-path-menu-search.

(1) Forward Tab from a menuitem could not reach the input even with the handler removed, because the input is rendered BEFORE the lists (line 328 vs 338+); only Shift+Tab from the first menuitem is the blocked route, so the fix at line 258 must specifically preserve backward Tab, not Tab generally. (2) ".sync-path-menu-search:focus-visible ... for a state that cannot occur" is wrong — browsers match :focus-visible on text/search inputs focused by pointer, which is the one working route today. Also worth noting for the fix: the handler at lines 264-274 already anticipates the input having focus (the `typing` branch correctly suppresses typeahead and steps arrows into the list), so only the missing initial focus and the unconditional Tab-closes rule are defective.

title: Activity log drawer's resize handle is mouse-only; the identical sidebar handle beside it is fully keyboard-operable
reason:
Citation and control flow both check out; I could not refute it.

VERIFIED VERBATIM. <repo>/src/components/project-sync/ActivityLogDrawer.tsx lines 190-199 contain exactly the quoted block: `{open && (` at 190, `<div` at 191, `className="log-resizer"` 192, `role="separator"` 193, `aria-label="Resize log"` 194, `aria-orientation="horizontal"` 195, `onMouseDown={onStartResize}` 196, `onDoubleClick={onResetHeight}` 197. No tabIndex, no onKeyDown, no aria-value* anywhere in the file (the only tabIndex in it is `tabIndex={-1}` on the drawer region at 187).

COMPARISON IS REAL. ProjectSync.tsx:3701-3716 is the sidebar separator with `aria-valuemin={MIN_PROJECT_SIDEBAR_WIDTH}` (3706), `aria-valuemax` (3707), `aria-valuenow={sidebarWidth}` (3708), `tabIndex={0}` (3709), `onKeyDown={resizeSidebarWithKeyboard}` (3714), and that handler (718-727) implements ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End. So the pattern exists in the same codebase.

NO MISSED PATH. I grepped every `setLogHeight` caller in src/: ProjectSync.tsx:589 (a window-resize clamp that can only SHRINK: `Math.min(current, Math.max(140, innerHeight - 120))`), :676 (inside `startLogResize`, reachable only from the mousedown handler), and :3890 (`onResetHeight={() => setLogHeight(240)}`, wired only to the resizer's onDoubleClick). There is no keyboard, no menu, and no settings route to logHeight, and no localStorage key for it (contrast PROJECT_SIDEBAR_WIDTH_KEY at :185, which persists the sidebar). `const [logHeight, setLogHeight] = useState(240)` is at :398 as claimed. No test references "Resize log" or `.log-resizer`, so there is no encoded design position either.

CORRECTIONS (why I would not call this medium):
1. The ARIA sub-claim is wrong. A `role="separator"` without tabIndex is a valid STATIC separator per ARIA, and static separators do not take aria-valuenow/min/max — those are required only for the focusable (widget) form. So the missing value attributes are a consequence of the missing tabIndex, not an independent defect, and nothing is mis-announced as a broken slider. The genuine smell is the action-promising `aria-label="Resize log"` on an element that offers no keyboard action.
2. The impact overstates content loss. `.log-panel-body` is `overflow-y: auto` (App.css:731-736), so the full log scrolls inside the fixed 240px drawer and nothing becomes unreadable — a screen reader reads the whole list, and pointer/trackpad scrolling works. What a keyboard-only user loses is the ability to enlarge the viewport, i.e. a convenience, not access to content. (A narrower real gap sits nearby: the scroll container itself has no tabIndex and usually holds no focusable child, so arrow-key scrolling of the body is awkward in WKWebView — but that is a different finding.)
3. "a few rows tall" is only true on an unusually short window; at 240px with `line-height: 1.6` on `--type-sm` the body shows roughly ten rows, and ProjectSync.tsx:589 already caps the height against short windows.

Net: the keyboard-inoperable resize handle is real and confirmed, the inconsistency with the sidebar separator is real, and the proposed fix is the right shape — but this is a lost enhancement on a control whose content stays fully reachable, so low, not medium.
correction: ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:191-198 renders the log drawer's `role="separator"` resize handle with only onMouseDown/onDoubleClick — no tabIndex and no onKeyDown — so keyboard-only users cannot resize or reset the drawer, while the sibling sidebar separator at ProjectSync.tsx:3701-3716 implements the full tabIndex/ArrowKey/Home/End pattern. logHeight (ProjectSync.tsx:398) stays at its 240px default for the session (it is never persisted, and only the shrink-only window clamp at :589 can change it without a mouse). Content is NOT lost: `.log-panel-body` is `overflow-y: auto` (App.css:734), so the log still scrolls within the fixed height — this is an inconsistent, mouse-only enhancement, not blocked access. The missing aria-valuemin/max/now is not itself an ARIA violation, since a non-focusable separator is a valid static separator; the value attributes only become required once tabIndex={0} makes it a widget.

title: Activity log drawer's resize handle is mouse-only; the identical sidebar handle beside it is fully keyboard-operable
reason:
The markup is quoted accurately (ActivityLogDrawer.tsx:190-198), but the claimed consequence does not survive the actual code.

1) No content or functionality is lost. `.log-panel-body` (LogPanel.tsx:333) is a scrolling container with follow-tail pinning, a ResizeObserver, a "Load older" button, and Type/Level/Search filters — every line the drawer can show at 440px it also shows at 240px, just fewer rows at a time. Drawer height is presentation, not access. For a screen-reader user the framing is inverted: virtual-cursor reading is unaffected by the pixel height of a scrolling region, so "a screen-reader user cannot resize the log" costs them nothing at all.

2) The ARIA is conformant as written, not an omission. `role="separator"` without `tabIndex` IS the static separator role; `aria-valuemin`/`valuemax`/`valuenow` are required only for the focusable window-splitter variant. The drawer has a legal non-focusable separator; the sidebar (ProjectSync.tsx:3701-3716) has the legal focusable one. Nothing here is an aria-required-attr violation, and the "announced as Resize log, separator with no valuenow" description is of a valid pattern.

3) The worst-case window math is wrong. tauri.conf.json pins `minHeight: 560`, and the drag clamp is `Math.max(140, Math.min(520, window.innerHeight - 120))` (ProjectSync.tsx:670-673) — at the smallest window the app permits, the mouse ceiling is 440 against the keyboard-fixed 240. The 140px floor cited as "a few rows tall" needs a sub-260px window, which the app forbids. The delta a keyboard user forgoes is ~200px of extra simultaneously-visible rows in an auto-scrolling list, not access to the log.

4) The two handles are different classes of control, which reads as a decision rather than a lapse. `sidebarWidth` is a persisted layout dimension (localStorage at ProjectSync.tsx:537, restored at :400) rewritten during the sidebar collapsible-sections work with pointer capture, operation-keyed gutters and inert/aria-disabled states — deliberate investment. `logHeight` is ephemeral session state that is intentionally NOT persisted and whose double-click "reset" just snaps back to the 240 default (:3890); its handle is a hover-revealed 4px pill (`background: transparent` until `:hover`/`:active`/`.resizing-log`, App.css:10618-10630) — a control drawn to be invisible until a pointer is over it is designed as a pointer affordance. The nearby "Manage logs" button (→ Settings) is the keyboard route to the log store anyway.

Real remaining nit: an unfocusable separator carrying the action-y label "Resize log" is slightly misleading in a screen reader's element list. That is a copy/polish issue, not a keyboard-operability defect, and "medium" is inflated for a convenience affordance that gates zero content on a desktop app with a 560px minimum window.
correction: Accurate minimal version: the log drawer's separator is announced with the action label "Resize log" but is not focusable, so its label overstates what keyboard users can do with it; no log content or function is unreachable, since the panel body scrolls and the height is ephemeral, non-persisted presentation state. Fix is either dropping/neutralizing the label or, optionally, mirroring the sidebar's focusable-splitter pattern.

title: Every custom radiogroup in the app ignores arrow keys and puts all five radios in the tab order
reason: The code claim is exact and I reproduced it. BundleConnectionDialog.tsx:123 carries the quoted `role="radiogroup" aria-label="Available remote repos"` verbatim at that precise line, and the `<button role="radio" aria-checked={active}>` at lines 129-137 matches the quoted evidence. `grep -n tabIndex` over all five cited files returns nothing (exit 1), and no arrow-key handling appears in any of them; there is no document- or window-level keydown listener in src/ that could supply the behavior from outside, and no CSS or call-site condition is relevant to a keyboard-handler omission. All four sibling citations resolve correctly at the stated lines with the identical shape. The house convention the finding appeals to genuinely exists and is applied elsewhere: SyncReviewTabs.tsx:78 uses `tabIndex={active ? 0 : -1}` with a Home/End/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight handler at lines 49-61, and menuKeyboard.ts does the same for menus, so these five radiogroups are an inconsistency rather than a deliberate style. The only test coverage is source-text matching (settings-page.integration.test.tsx:45, storage-catalog.integration.test.tsx:537), which asserts the role string and nothing about behavior. However, the finding's central impact claim is factually wrong: the radios are native `<button type="button">` elements with onClick, so Tab reaches each and Space/Enter fires setSelectedId, which populates `selected` (line 45) and enables the primary button (line 177). The dialog is never a dead end and WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard is satisfied.
correction: Corrected statement: all five custom radiogroups omit roving tabindex and arrow-key handling, so they violate the WAI-ARIA radiogroup pattern that this codebase already implements for its tablist (SyncReviewTabs.tsx:78 and its handler at lines 49-61) and for menus (menuKeyboard.ts). The real consequences are (a) a screen reader announces "radio button, 1 of N" and switches to radiogroup navigation, after which arrow keys do nothing, and (b) each radio is its own tab stop, so a storage holding 12 repos costs 12 Tab presses instead of one. Strike the claim that BundleConnectionDialog "appears to have no way forward": the radios are native buttons with onClick, so Tab plus Space/Enter selects a repo, sets `selected` (line 45), and enables the "Connect and review Pull" button (line 177). Keyboard operability is preserved, so this is an ARIA pattern-conformance and navigation-friction defect, not a keyboard trap or a WCAG 2.1.1 failure. The proposed fix (a shared roving-focus helper beside menuKeyboard.ts) remains correct, and it should skip `disabled` radios since four of the five groups disable their buttons on a busy/working flag.

title: Every custom radiogroup in the app ignores arrow keys and puts all five radios in the tab order
reason: Refuted on novelty and on the load-bearing impact claim. title: Catalog row action menu drops focus onto <body> both when it is dismissed and when an option is chosen
reason: Confirmed against the real file. StorageCatalogPage.tsx:955-961 (closeOnEscape) and :1751-1758 (onChoose) are verbatim as quoted and at the exact line numbers; line 577 is `{action.expanded && (` so the menu is unmounted, not hidden, and line 585's `ref={(node) => focusMenuEdge(node, "first")}` calls menuKeyboard.ts:38-43, which unconditionally focuses options[0] on open (mouse or keyboard). title: App-actions menu loses focus to <body> on Escape and offers no arrow-key navigation
reason: The citation and mechanism hold up under direct reading. title: App-actions menu loses focus to <body> on Escape and offers no arrow-key navigation
reason:
Both halves of the finding collapse against the actual file.

(1) The arrow-navigation half has zero possible user-visible consequence. `#sync-app-actions-menu` (ProjectSync.tsx:2784-2806) contains exactly ONE `role="menuitem"` — "Reload app data" — with no conditional siblings. `moveMenuFocus` on a single-option menu re-focuses the same button for ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Home/End alike; a screen-reader user in menu mode has nowhere to navigate. The codebase is in fact consistent, not negligent: every MULTI-item `role="menu"` implements the arrow contract — SyncPathBar.tsx:277, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:591, and ProjectActivityPage.tsx:241-256 (a hand-rolled copy). The one menu without it is the one menu with one item. That reads as proportionate, not as a missed contract.

(2) The blast-radius claim is factually wrong. `windowActions` renders only at ProjectSync.tsx:3733, inside `{showsPathBar ? null : (...)}`. `showsPathBar` (line 792) is true for Settings (`settingsOpen`), Storages (`storageIndexOpen`), catalog index/scope, storage settings and any selected project — all of which render `SyncPathBar` with `overflowLabel="App actions"`, the fully-implemented menu the finding itself cites as the good example. The fallback titlebar appears only on the empty Projects index (zero projects) and the setup/draft/add-scope screens. And the startup effect at line 1219-1226 auto-selects `nextProjects[0]`, so any user with at least one project never sees this titlebar at all on launch — the affected screen is essentially first-run/empty state, where "Reload app data" has nothing to reload.

(3) The Escape path described is not the realistic one. Opening the menu leaves focus on the `.storage-link-more` trigger (there is no auto-focus-into-menu effect), so Tab → Enter → Escape returns nothing to <body> and behaves correctly. Reaching the described state requires Tab → Enter → Tab onto the single actionable item → then pressing Escape instead of Enter. On that contrived path the consequence is that the next Tab restarts from the top of a screen whose only prior stops are the sidebar and the theme toggle: a couple of extra Tab presses, no trap, no lost functionality, no unreachable action. Moreover the identical focus-to-body occurs on the PRIMARY path — the menuitem's own `onClick` calls `setAppMenuOpen(false)` (line 2802) — so framing this as an Escape-handler defect is arbitrary; the Escape handler's actual, documented job there is the `stopPropagation` that keeps the Push/Pull review from discarding itself.

No WCAG SC is failed: nothing is keyboard-inaccessible or trapped, and focus order is not "meaningful sequence"-broken. Returning focus to the opener is APG guidance, not a conformance requirement.
correction: The residue worth stating, if anything: on the empty Projects index and setup screens only, dismissing the single-item app-actions menu (by Escape or by activating "Reload app data") leaves focus on <body> rather than the ⋯ trigger, costing a keyboard user a few extra Tab presses. The arrow/Home/End claim should be dropped entirely — the menu has one item.

title: Agent-launcher split menu declares role="menu" with no arrow keys, no label, no focus move, and stays open when the user tabs past it
reason: Independently reproduced in source. ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2044 is verbatim `<div className="sync-path-menu end" role="menu">` with `role="menuitem"` children, and the dismissal effect at 1271-1289 registers only `mousedown` (outside-press, gated on `agentSplitRef.current?.contains`) and `keydown`/Escape. I searched for every escape hatch: `grep -c onKeyDown` over the full 3384-line file returns 0, so no parent handler can supply arrow keys by bubbling; the file never imports `../sync-review/menuKeyboard`; the only ref is `agentSplitRef` on the wrapper div, so there is no `focusMenuEdge` call, no `autoFocus`, and no focus-restore target; there is no `focusin` listener anywhere. The shared helper `src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts` exists and its own header comment names this exact failure, and `StorageCatalogPage.tsx:580-592` applies the full recipe (aria-label, `ref={(node) => focusMenuEdge(node, "first")}`, onKeyDown with Tab-close plus `moveMenuFocus`) to the identical `.sync-path-menu end` markup — so sub-claims 1, 2 and 3 hold and the site is a genuine divergence from an in-repo convention. Sub-claim 4 is stated wrongly, see correction. Severity lowered because the defect is narrower than claimed: the items are native buttons rendered after the trigger, so every route stays reachable and activatable with Tab+Enter (no trap, no blocked path); `role="menu"` requires no accessible name under ARIA and the trigger already carries aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-label="More agent setup routes"; and the surface is one transient S3 storage-setup panel whose menu usually holds one or two items (`agentLaunchers` minus the default, plus the fixed Copy item), so with a single launcher-bearing provider it is a one-item menu.
correction: Sub-claim 4 is wrong on the ordinary path and contradicts sub-claim 2: because focus never enters the menu, pressing Escape leaves focus where it already was — on the `.sync-r2-split-arrow` trigger — so nothing is dropped to `<body>`. Focus falls to `<body>` only in the narrower case where the user first Tabs into a menu item and then presses Escape, unmounting the focused element. The accurate finding is: `role="menu"` is declared at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2044 without the keyboard half of the contract the repo's own `menuKeyboard.ts` exists to supply — no ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End, no focus move on open, no Tab/focusin dismissal (tabbing past the last item leaves the popover floating over the setup form until a click or Escape), and no focus restore in the Escape path for the tabbed-in case. The proposed fix (mirroring StorageCatalogPage.tsx:580-592) is correct as written.

title: Agent-launcher split menu declares role="menu" with no arrow keys, no label, no focus move, and stays open when the user tabs past it
reason: The code is as described and the refutation attempts fail. The menu div at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2044 really is bare `role="menu"` with no aria-label, no onKeyDown, no focus move and no focus restore, and the effect at lines 1271-1289 really has only mousedown+Escape. It is not a deliberate choice: menuKeyboard.ts (src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts) exists specifically to satisfy this contract and its header comment names this exact failure mode; it landed 2026-08-21 in 2ecfac1, while this menu was added 2026-08-26 in 8a11bbf/e7c1d60, so it is a miss, not a precedent. It is not handled elsewhere: all four other shipped role="menu" popups comply — SyncPathBar.tsx:252, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:583, ProjectActivityPage.tsx:239, and even the single-item ProjectSync.tsx:2787 which has aria-label plus a focusin dismissal at line 1315 — making this the only non-conforming menu in the app. No test covers it (only storage-catalog.integration.test.tsx asserts menu keyboard behavior). However, the claimed severity is inflated. Every menu item is a native <button> in DOM order right after the trigger with no tabIndex={-1}, so a keyboard-only user Tabs from the chevron into both items and activates them normally — the widget is fully operable, nothing is blocked or trapped. The trigger already carries aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-label="More agent setup routes", and each item's accessible name is its full visible text, so no information is actually lost; "announced as a bare menu" and "appears without any focus cue" (focus visibly remains on the chevron) overstate the case. In production the menu holds exactly two items (claude and codex are the only providers with cli_launcher), on a once-per-storage R2 setup screen. Real consequence, but polish/consistency-grade: low.
correction: The menu at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2044 is the app's only role="menu" that omits the shared keyboard contract from src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts: no arrow/Home/End handling for its two menuitems, no aria-label on the container, no focusin dismissal, and Escape unmounts it without returning focus to the .sync-r2-split-arrow trigger. It is not, however, inoperable or unlabelled in practice — the items are native buttons in tab order directly after the trigger, so Tab reaches and activates both, and the trigger supplies aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-label so the popup's purpose is announced. The defect is degraded menu semantics and a popover that lingers after Tab-out on a once-per-storage setup screen, not a blocked task. The proposed fix (mirror StorageCatalogPage.tsx:581-592) is still the right one.

title: Catalog row menu re-focuses its first option on every parent re-render because focusMenuEdge is called from an inline ref callback
reason: Independently reproduced in source. Line 585 of src/components/storage-catalog/StorageCatalogPage.tsx is verbatim `ref={(node) => focusMenuEdge(node, "first")}` on the `role="menu"` div (581-585), rendered under `action.expanded &&` so the element stays mounted across re-renders. focusMenuEdge (src/components/sync-review/menuKeyboard.ts:38) calls `options[0].focus()` with no activeElement guard and returns undefined (so no React 19 ref cleanup). ResourceCard (line 477) is a plain function component with no React.memo, so every parent render re-renders it. React's reconciler confirms the re-attach: node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.development.js markRef (10115) sets the Ref flag whenever `current.ref !== ref` — always true for an inline arrow — and safelyDetachRef (13505) invokes `ref(null)` (refCleanup is null) before safelyAttachRef (13498) re-invokes the new callback with the same node, re-running focusMenuEdge. Triggers verified: setRemotePreviews (line 987) fires once per row inside the sequential await loop whose targets (`!local_present && remote_present && !preview_png`, lines 977-978) are exactly the remote-only rows a pet Pull review lists; and the outside-click handler (950-953) only dismisses on clicks outside pullListRef entirely, so setPullSelected (1736) or setPullAcks (1772) from another row inside the list also re-render with the menu still open. No guard, fallback, or call-site condition prevents the focus reset.
correction: Accurate as written, with two sharpenings: (1) the re-focus happens on every commit that includes this fiber, not literally every render call (a bailed-out render commits nothing) — immaterial in practice; (2) the trigger surface is wider than the pet-preview stream. Because the outside-click handler at lines 950-953 only closes the menu when the click falls outside the whole pullListRef list, clicking another row's include checkbox (setPullSelected, line 1736) or an AckChip (setPullAcks, line 1772) re-renders the page with the menu still open and yanks focus back to the first option, with no slow network involved.

title: Switcher mistakes a lone "Add storage…" group for the object's verbs and renders it as a bare "+" glyph
reason: The mechanism is real but the impact is cosmetic and partly mis-stated. (1) The item does NOT lose its name: renderPill's verb branch sets aria-label={item.label} and title=verbTitle(item), so both the screen-reader name and the hover tooltip read "Add storage…" — only the visible text is suppressed, which is the intended verb-pill treatment. (2) An icon-only "+" for add-storage is an established affordance in this very app (ProjectSidebar.tsx:1019-1020 and ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2925-2926 both ship plus buttons with title/aria-label "Add storage"), so it is not a mystery glyph. (3) Blast radius is one crumb in one state: every other switcher opens with a genuine unlabelled verbs group and is unaffected at any storage count — workspace storage crumb (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2273, settings/unlink first), catalog storage crumb (StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1225, settings/unlink first), project crumb (:2384). Only the deliberately verb-less storage-editor crumb, and only at storages.length === 1, can hit it. (4) Positional role assignment is a deliberate, documented design shipped 2026-09-01 (switcher-menu-directions-mockup: "reads the existing PathBarMenuGroup[] by position — first unlabelled group = verbs → 32px icon pills … trailing unlabelled groups = text pills"), chosen specifically so no caller had to change; the proposed fix reverses part of that contract for a visual wobble. (5) Nothing is broken: onSelect fires, the menu closes, Add storage opens — no dead-end, no data risk, no keyboard or focus regression. The before/after shape comparison is also barely observable, since adding a second storage simultaneously introduces an entire "Switch to" list, so the menu looks different regardless.
correction: Accurate, narrower statement: on the storage-editor crumb only, and only when exactly one storage exists, the "Add storage…" command renders as a left-aligned icon-only 32px verb pill instead of a right-aligned text pill, because the conditional "Switch to" group is omitted and the trailing group falls into the positional verbs slot. Its accessible name and tooltip remain "Add storage…" and activation works normally; the defect is a visual-label/placement inconsistency, not a lost or unusable control.

title: Switcher mistakes a lone "Add storage…" group for the object's verbs and renders it as a bare "+" glyph
reason: Independently reproduced. The cited code at SyncPathBar.tsx:168-172 is verbatim and at the exact line, and git diff shows it is newly introduced by this change (pre-diff, every menu item rendered a visible {item.label}). The call site at ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:1707-1731 is exactly as described: the "Switch to" group is spread in conditionally on `storages.some(c => c.id !== editedStorageConfig.id)`, and the unlabelled add-storage group is the only other group. With one storage, `populated[0]` is that unlabelled group, so it is claimed as `verbs`; `lists` is empty and `caption` is empty (add-storage has no `detail`). I rendered the real SyncPathBar through renderToStaticMarkup with both storage counts: one storage emits `` (icon only, no text node), two storages emit ``. CSS confirms the shapes (.sync-path-menu.switcher width:380px; .sync-path-menu-verb height:32px/min-width:32px/padding:0; .sync-path-menu-tail margin-left:auto/padding:0 12px). The state is reachable: the storage editor is opened from the sidebar (ProjectSidebar.tsx:1046) or the Storages index (StorageIndexPage.tsx:84) with any saved storage, so a user with exactly one storage hits it on first run. The three other switcher call sites (ProjectLinksWorkspace.tsx:2312, StorageCatalogPage.tsx:1226 and 1292) all lead with an unconditional unlabelled verbs group and are unaffected, so the defect is confined to this one crumb.
correction: The item does not lose its name entirely — only its visible text. renderPill(item, false) still emits aria-label={item.label} and title={verbTitle(item)}, and the menu's typeahead falls back to aria-label (SyncPathBar.tsx:293), so screen readers, the tooltip and keyboard search all still say "Add storage…". Accurate statement: with exactly one storage, the storage-editor crumb's switcher footer renders "Add storage…" as an unlabelled 32px "+" icon pill instead of the text pill it becomes once a second storage exists — a visible-label and discoverability regression, not an accessible-name or functional loss.

title: The new switcher search field cannot be reached by keyboard at all
reason:
The mechanics are described correctly (the `<input>` at src/components/sync-review/SyncPathBar.tsx:328 carries no menuitem role, so `menuOptions()` skips it, and Tab closes the menu at both line 516/551 and line 258) — but the claimed user-visible consequence does not exist, one load-bearing evidence claim is false, and the shape is a deliberate, recorded design decision.

1) No functionality is keyboard-inaccessible. Everything the filter pill does — narrowing a long switch list to reach a target — is already served for keyboard users by the type-ahead the same handler implements (SyncPathBar.tsx:283-299): printable keys accumulate for 500ms, a repeated first letter cycles matches, a longer prefix narrows from the focused row, plus ArrowUp/Down/Home/End wrapping via `moveMenuFocus`. That is the ARIA menu pattern's own mechanism for long menus. A keyboard-only user with 6+ projects can reach and activate every target; nothing is blocked. WCAG 2.1.1 is a functionality-level criterion ("all functionality operable through a keyboard interface"), not a per-widget focusability rule, and an equivalent keyboard mechanism is present and working.

2) The claim that the Enter branch at line 268 is "likewise unreachable" is simply wrong. `typing = event.target instanceof HTMLInputElement` is true on the ordinary pointer path — click the crumb chevron, click into the filter pill, type, press Enter → `options.find(o => o.classList.contains("target"))?.click()`. Same for the ArrowDown/ArrowUp step-out at line 270. That code is live on the path it was written for; it is not dead.

3) It is intentional. The shipped B·Switcher record states the contract verbatim: search pill appears at >= SWITCHER_SEARCH_FLOOR (6) targets, "ArrowDown/Up step into the list, Enter activates the first .target, typeahead skips the input" — pointer affordance layered over a keyboard mechanism that already exists. The file also explicitly documents the constraint the proposed fix would violate (line ~305): "A `role=\"menu\"` admits only the menuitem family." Adding `role="searchbox"`/`tabIndex={0}` and folding the input into the roving order would break the menu's ARIA contract this codebase deliberately maintains — a searchbox is not a permitted child of `role="menu"`, and AT in menu-navigation mode would not expose it as a valid child even if it were focusable. The proposed fix is worse than the status quo; only the finding's own alternative (route type-ahead into `setQuery`) is coherent, and that is a refinement, not a defect fix.

The only genuine residue is a cosmetic asymmetry of power, not of access: type-ahead prefix-matches the label, while the pointer filter substring-matches label + detail (path). Worth a polish note, not a high-severity keyboard-access defect.
correction: Accurate statement: the switcher's search input is a pointer-only affordance — it is not in the menu's roving focus order and Tab closes the menu, so keyboard users reach targets through the existing type-ahead/arrow contract instead. This is the documented shipped design, not an access failure; the residual gap is that type-ahead prefix-matches labels only, whereas the pointer filter substring-matches label + detail (path). Also, the finding's claim that the Enter-takes-first-match branch (line 268) is unreachable is false — it fires whenever a pointer user focuses the field and presses Enter.
